analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 focus-fire on Indeedee (Moonblast + Draco Meteor) removed Psychic Terrain and the Follow Me/Trick Room support immediately, exactly as the coach rule demands. Turn 2 switching the -2 SpA Dragonite out instead of firing again respected the 'Draco Meteor once, then pivot' rule and dodged the Glimmora Power Gem OHKO. Milotic did excellent cleanup work, KOing both Sneasler and Mega Glimmora with Scald, and the Whimsicott Moonblast + Milotic Scald focus on the -1 Def Sneasler was a correct kill-the-threat line.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) 'Vs Indeedee terrain teams, focus both attacks on Indeedee turn 1' — done, Indeedee died T1. (2) 'At -2 SpA Dragonite is a pivot: switch it out' — done on T2. (3) 'Focus Mega Glimmora the turn it Megas' — partially; we focused it on T5 and killed it, but 3 turns late. VIOLATED: (a) 'Sneasler Dire Claw OHKOs Whimsicott — Protect or bench Whimsicott turn 1 vs Sneasler' — Whimsicott was led into a revealed open-sheet Sneasler and was at 1 HP after T2, then died T4. (b) 'Basculegion Last Respects snowballs with our faints: KO it before our third Pokemon dies / never trade chip' — Basculegion was on the open sheet, we let 3 of ours faint before it even got targeted once, and it then swept with 3 consecutive Last Respects. (c) 'Renew: vs psyterrain sheets containing Sneasler plus a Rock partner, leave Drogon home' — followed, but the deeper issue was we brought a Last Respects-vulnerable team instead.
analysis.whatFailed: The game was lost on team selection and on the Turn 3 Garchomp line, not on the Basculegion turns. (1) Preview: the open sheet showed Sneasler + Glimmora + Basculegion. We brought four Pokemon that all lose to that trio's endgame. Basculegion with Last Respects was NEVER targeted a single time across the whole game — it did 4 attacks, all KOs or near-KOs (87%, 80%, 100%). (2) Turn 3 was the catastrophic turn: we clicked Protect with a 1 HP Whimsicott and Earthquake with Garchomp while Sneasler (faster, Close Combat, Fighting on a Ground/Dragon) was staring at Garchomp. Garchomp died before moving; the Earthquake never happened. We should have switched Garchomp to Milotic (which later tanked Sneasler) or Protected Garchomp instead. We traded our Protect onto the wrong slot. (3) Turn 6: Protecting Milotic while Dragonite ate Last Respects for an OHKO — both mons were in KO range, we had no Tailwind-based speed to 'outrun Scarf Basculegion next turn' because Tailwind had already expired on turn 5. We should have attacked Basculegion with Dragonite (Heat Wave/Draco) and Protected the slot that dies, or simply double-attacked Basculegion. (4) Overall: Whimsicott took 2 turns of Tailwind that never produced a single KO, and Tailwind expired before we needed it.
analysis.howToImprove: Rule 1 (hard): When Basculegion is on the sheet, it is the opponent's ONLY win condition in the late game and must be removed before our second Pokemon faints. Every turn Basculegion is on the field with 2+ of our mons fainted, both of our actions go into Basculegion. Rule 2: When a foe with Close Combat / a Fighting STAB is on the field and our Garchomp/Kingambit is active and would be OHKO'd, Protect THAT slot — never Protect the 1 HP support mon that is already dead weight. Rule 3: Check Tailwind remaining turns before basing a Protect on 'next turn we outspeed'; Tailwind set on T2 ends after T5. Rule 4: Preview vs psyterrain + Basculegion sheets — bring Kingambit (Sucker Punch priority OHKOs the frail Basculegion, Dark resists Ghost Last Respects) instead of Garchomp, and bench Whimsicott if Sneasler is revealed.

proposals.change: Vs any sheet containing Basculegion, mandatorily bring Kingambit (Dark type resists Last Respects/Ghost and Sucker Punch priority OHKOs frail Basculegion) and treat Basculegion as the must-kill win condition; do not bring a team of four mons that all die to Last Respects.
proposals.evidence: Basculegion attacked 4 times for 87%, 80%, 100%, 100% and was never targeted once; it 3-0'd our back half after our 2nd faint.

proposals.change: Never Protect a sub-10% support mon (Whimsicott at 1 HP) while an active attacker threatens an OHKO on the partner — Protect the threatened attacker or switch it. On T3 Garchomp died to Close Combat before Earthquake fired, wasting both actions.
proposals.evidence: T3: Whimsicott (1 HP) Protected, Garchomp was OHKO'd by Sneasler Close Combat, our Earthquake never executed.

proposals.change: Before using Protect justified by 'next turn we outspeed thanks to Tailwind', verify Tailwind turns remaining. Tailwind set T2 expires at end of T5; T6 Protect was based on a Tailwind that no longer existed.

lessons: Basculegion must be targeted BEFORE our second Pokemon faints — Last Respects scales with our faints and becomes an unanswerable OHKO machine.
Vs Basculegion sheets bring Kingambit: Dark resists Ghost Last Respects and Sucker Punch OHKOs it through its frailty.
Never Protect a 1 HP support mon while the partner attacker is about to be OHKO'd — Protect or switch the attacker.
Count Tailwind turns before justifying a Protect with 'we outspeed next turn'; Tailwind lasts 4 turns from the turn it is set.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Adopt their late-game 'cleaner' concept: keep one Pokemon whose power scales with the game going long, and always bring Kingambit as our Ghost/Psychic sponge + Sucker Punch revenge killer. Consider Kingambit EV shift to max HP / Adamant with Life Orb retained so it survives a Last Respects at 2 faints and Sucker Punches back.
teamInspiration.reason: Basculegion with Last Respects did zero work early and won them the game from turn 5 onward; they simply traded pieces and let it scale. A Dark-type revenge killer completely invalidates that plan.

analysis.whatWorked: Very little. The only correct reads were recognizing that Mega Staraptor's Close Combat threatened everything and that Drogon needed Protect to survive. Whimsicott did get Tailwind up turn 1 and chipped Grimmsnarl.
analysis.lessonsApplied: VIOLATED the core 'never let the opponent have BOTH speed and power' rule: Staraptor-Mega was handed +1/+1 Atk/SpA by TWO Parting Shots and +2 Atk by Charm (Defiant-style?) while we Protected and switched, then they added Tailwind on T5. We also repeated Protect on Drogon three turns in a row (T6/T7/T8) with no plan to remove the threat, directly violating the 'never double/triple Protect while a foe boosts' and 'Protect-stalling a booster gives it a free sweep' rules. We also switched Milotic into +2 Close Combat and lost it instantly.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Lead: Whimsicott + Drogon into a sheet with Staraptor-Mega (Flying/Fighting) + Grimmsnarl (screens/Parting Shot) is the worst possible pairing — both leads lose to Close Combat/Brave Bird and Light Screen blunted our special attacks. 2) T2 we attacked Grimmsnarl (a support mon) instead of pressuring Staraptor, letting it Parting Shot-boost twice. 3) T3-T5 we burned four actions on pure switching/Protect while Staraptor stacked +4 def/spd and +2 atk; by T5 we had dealt almost no damage and lost Milotic for free. 4) Our remaining Pokemon (Garchomp, Kingambit) that actually threaten Staraptor (Rock Slide / Sucker Punch) were LEFT HOME. 5) Encore on Staraptor at T6 was useless because Close Combat was already its KO move, and it was never going to be punished.
analysis.howToImprove: Against Mega Staraptor (Reckless Brave Bird / Close Combat), Garchomp is mandatory: Rock Slide is 4x and OHKOs it, and Scarf Garchomp outspeeds it. Kingambit Sucker Punch also revenge-kills it. Never bring a Whimsicott+Charizard+Milotic+Dragonite squad where all four lose 1v1 to the same mon. On the board, the moment a Parting Shot / Intimidate / Charm chain starts stacking boosts on one foe, switch into our Rock/Dark answer and KO it rather than cycling Protects. Three consecutive Protects on Drogon with zero offensive progress is a surrender.

proposals.change: Mandatory: if the opponent sheet contains Staraptor (especially with Staraptite), ALWAYS bring Garchomp (Rock Slide 4x OHKO) and Kingambit (Sucker Punch revenge, resists nothing but outprioritizes). Never bring a four-mon squad where no member has a Rock or Electric move.
proposals.evidence: vs joaquinpug: brought Whimsicott/Drogon/Dragonite/Milotic — zero Rock/Electric coverage; Mega Staraptor +2/+4 swept all four without ever being below 100% HP.

proposals.change: Boost-chain alarm: if a single foe accumulates +2 or more total stat stages from ally support (Parting Shot, Charm, Helping Hand, Howl) in two consecutive turns, stop Protect/switch cycling and immediately focus both actions on that foe or switch in our hard counter. Three consecutive Protects on the same mon is banned.
proposals.evidence: T3-T8: Staraptor reached +2 Atk/+1 SpA/+4 Def/+4 SpD while we used Protect on Drogon on T3, T6, T7, T8 and never damaged it once the whole game.

proposals.change: Never switch a bulky non-resist (Milotic) into an active +1 or higher Fighting attacker. Milotic is NOT a Close Combat sponge; it is 2x weak-neutral and died from full HP in one hit.
proposals.evidence: T5 Milotic switched in at 202/202 and was OHKO'd by +1 Close Combat.

proposals.change: Test Choice Scarf Garchomp loadout for this metagame window: Scarf Garchomp outspeeds Mega Staraptor (178) and Mega Raichu-Y and immediately Rock Slides them; the current Sitrus loadout is 0-2.

lessons: Mega Staraptor sheets are mandatory-Garchomp (Rock Slide 4x) and mandatory-Kingambit (Sucker Punch) — never bring four mons with no Rock/Electric answer.
Parting Shot chains stack boosts on one foe: treat 2+ stacked support boosts as a setup sweeper and KO/counter it immediately, not with Protect cycling.
Three Protects in a row on the same Pokemon with no damage dealt is a surrender — attack or switch to our counter instead.
Milotic is not a Close Combat sponge; never switch it into an active boosted Fighting attacker.
Light Screen from Grimmsnarl halves our special attacks — prioritize physical answers (Garchomp/Kingambit) on screen teams.

itemExperiment.reason: Mega Staraptor (178 Spe) and Mega Raichu-Y (200) have outsped and swept us repeatedly; Scarf Garchomp at 231 outspeeds both and Rock Slide is a 4x OHKO on Staraptor.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'boost-funnel' concept in a defensive form: run Whimsicott with Helping Hand or keep Encore but, more importantly, add a Rock-move holder that is always brought vs Flying Megas. Concretely: switch Garchomp back to Choice Scarf and consider Milotic EVs shifted to max HP / +Def to actually survive one Close Combat.
teamInspiration.reason: They won purely by stacking Parting Shot/Charm boosts onto one Mega sweeper behind Light Screen; the only counterplay is a faster Rock attacker or priority Dark, which we left at home.

analysis.whatWorked: The team-preview read was sound: Kingambit is the correct anti-Psychic-Terrain piece (immune to Expanding Force, Psychic-resistant) and it did kill Indeedee-F, removing Follow Me/Psychic Terrain. Whimsicott got Tailwind up turn 1. Garchomp's Earthquake correctly spread-KO'd the grounded Psychic-Seed Sneasler on the last turn.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed the psyterrain lead rule (Kingambit + Whimsicott) and avoided Sucker Punch into Psychic Terrain. Correctly identified Indeedee as the Follow Me/terrain source. However the core coach note 'Psyterrain + Fighting coverage: bench Kingambit entirely, lead Drogon + Whimsicott' was contradicted by the chosen plan, and more importantly the rule 'never let the opponent have both speed AND power' was ignored — Mega Gardevoir (Pixilate Hyper Voice, spread, faster) was never targeted at all until it had already removed three of our Pokémon.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) We never attacked Mega Gardevoir, their single win condition. Turn 1 and Turn 2 both actions went into Indeedee behind Follow Me — Follow Me redirected Kingambit's Iron Head on T2, so the 'Iron Head OHKOs Mega Gardevoir' plan was impossible by construction and the pilot's own calc line was a lie: with Follow Me up, any single-target move is forced into Indeedee. 2) T2 Whimsicott Protect at 14% was a wasted action in a game where Hyper Voice (spread) hits through Protect's partner slot anyway and Kingambit was dying — we should have Moonblasted Gardevoir or Encored it into Hyper Voice. 3) Three turns of double-action spent on a Follow Me support while the Mega killed Kingambit through chip. 4) Bringing Drogon into a board with Mega Gardevoir (Expanding Force 56-104%) + Sneasler (Dire Claw) was a death sentence; Drogon was slept and KO'd without ever acting. 5) The real Hyper Voice damage source was spread chip onto Kingambit (55% T1) which no one accounted for — Kingambit died to residual spread damage, not a direct attack.
analysis.howToImprove: Against Follow Me + a Mega sweeper: Follow Me means single-target moves cannot touch the sweeper, so the only correct lines are (a) spread moves (Heat Wave/Earthquake/Hyper Voice-class) which hit both and ignore redirection, (b) KO the redirector in ONE action and spend the second on the sweeper, or (c) Encore/Taunt the redirector. We had Earthquake-Garchomp and Heat Wave available and brought neither to the front. Concretely vs Indeedee+Gardevoir: lead Garchomp (Scarf, spread EQ ignores Follow Me, hits Indeedee and Gardevoir) + Whimsicott (Encore Follow Me / Tailwind). Never spend both actions turn after turn on a redirector. And never Protect a 14% support when the partner is the one about to faint.

proposals.change: FOLLOW ME / RAGE POWDER RULE: while an opposing Follow Me/Rage Powder user is active and healthy, treat all single-target moves as targeting the redirector. Either use a SPREAD move (Earthquake, Heat Wave, Hyper Voice-class) to hit the real threat, or commit exactly one action to killing the redirector and the other to a spread move — never both actions into the redirector two turns in a row.
proposals.evidence: T1 and T2 both actions went into Indeedee behind Follow Me; Mega Gardevoir took zero damage all game and KO'd Kingambit, Drogon, Whimsicott and Garchomp.

proposals.change: Vs Indeedee/Gardevoir psyterrain sheets, mandatorily bring Garchomp (Scarf Earthquake is our only spread move that ignores Follow Me and hits grounded Psychic Seed Sneasler + Indeedee + Gardevoir) and lead it, not bench it.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp entered on turn 4 as our last mon and immediately spread-KO'd Sneasler and did 57% to Mega Gardevoir — the exact move that would have won the early game.

proposals.change: Ban Protect on a support mon below 20% HP when the partner slot is in KO range from a SPREAD move: Protect does not save the partner, and spread moves still chip through. Attack or switch instead.
proposals.evidence: T2 Whimsicott Protect at 14% did nothing; Hyper Voice chipped Kingambit to 0 anyway and we lost a full action.

proposals.change: Do not bring Drogon against sheets containing BOTH a Mega Psychic (Gardevoir/Alakazam) and Sneasler — Expanding Force 56-104% plus Dire Claw status means Drogon will not act.
proposals.evidence: Drogon was Dire-Clawed to sleep then Expanding-Forced for 0 without ever using a move.

lessons: Follow Me / Rage Powder redirects ALL single-target moves: against it, only spread moves (Earthquake, Heat Wave) reach the real threat — never claim a single-target KO on the partner while Follow Me is up.
Never spend both actions two turns in a row on a redirector while the opposing Mega sweeper takes zero damage.
Never Protect a sub-20% support mon when the partner is dying to a spread move — Protect saves neither.
Vs Indeedee + Mega Psychic, lead Scarf Garchomp: spread Earthquake ignores Follow Me and hits grounded Psychic-Seed Sneasler.
Drogon must stay home when the opponent has a Mega Psychic plus Sneasler.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp's spread Earthquake is our only Follow-Me-proof answer to Indeedee/Gardevoir psyterrain cores and it needs the speed to fire before Hyper Voice; keep testing it rather than reverting to Sitrus.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their redirection+Mega funnel: pair a single unstoppable spread Mega with a Follow Me body. For us, that means always pairing Mega Charizard-Y's Heat Wave with Whimsicott and bringing Garchomp as the Follow-Me-proof spread option — and consider giving Whimsicott Helping Hand over Moonblast so the Mega's spread move is the win condition instead of chip damage.
teamInspiration.reason: Indeedee's Follow Me bought Mega Gardevoir two completely free turns; the only reason that worked is that our entire board was single-target. Spread offense plus redirection is the strongest structure in this meta.

analysis.whatWorked: Focus-firing Arcanine-Hisui on turn 1 with Scald + Dragon Pulse was the right target priority (it was the Head Smash threat to Mega Dragonite), and Dragonite's Dragon Pulse cleanly removed Sneasler on turn 3 before it could Close Combat. Whimsicott's Moonblast finished a weakened Rillaboom.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The team-preview rule to shelter Mega Dragonite was followed, and we did not click Tailwind into Trick Room or Sucker Punch into a blocker. However the explicit coach lesson 'Milotic is not a Close Combat/ Wood Hammer sponge' was effectively violated in spirit: we led Milotic directly into a Grassy-Terrain-boosted Rillaboom whose Wood Hammer was calculated at 139-183% GUARANTEED OHKO, and we still left it in to attack instead of Protecting or switching. We also ignored the 'Protect Mega Dragonite's Multiscale' rule by Mega-evolving and attacking into a visible Head Smash OHKO range.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1 catastrophe: our own calc printed 'Milotic threatened by Rillaboom Wood Hammer (139-183% OHKO)' and 'Dragonite threatened by Head Smash (96-173% OHKO 95%)' — BOTH our leads were in guaranteed/near-guaranteed OHKO range and we attacked with both. We lost Milotic for free on turn 1 and Multiscale on Dragonite in the same turn. The correct line was Protect on Milotic (or switch) while Dragonite fired, or double-Protect-equivalent repositioning. 2) Turn 2 Earthquake into an obvious Protect from a 31% Arcanine wasted half our action economy. 3) Turn 4: we let Mega Salamence enter unanswered at full health and clicked Dragon Pulse into a faster Draco Meteor without Tailwind up — Dragonite at 36% HP, no Multiscale, died before moving. Tailwind was never set until turn 5 when only Whimsicott remained. 4) We gave the opponent BOTH speed and power all game (Grassy Glide priority + Mega Salamence) while never establishing our own speed control.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: if the pre-turn calc shows a lead in >=100% guaranteed OHKO range from a foe that moves first, that slot must Protect or switch — never attack. Second: set Tailwind on turn 1 or turn 2, not turn 5; with Whimsicott benched, Dragonite's own Tailwind should be clicked the turn Multiscale is already broken instead of a chip Dragon Pulse. Third: never attack a foe that already Protected last turn with the same predictable KO move while it sits at low HP — target the partner. Fourth: vs Rillaboom + Grassy Terrain, Milotic must never lead; bring Garchomp/Dragonite as the Grass-resist-ish front and keep Milotic as a back-side pivot.

proposals.change: GUARANTEED-OHKO LEAD RULE: if the engine's threat calc shows our active Pokemon takes >=100% minimum damage (guaranteed OHKO) from a foe that moves before it, that slot is BANNED from using an attacking move — it must Protect or switch. Attacking with a slot that is dead before/after a guaranteed OHKO with no KO of its own is a free loss of a Pokemon.
proposals.evidence: T1: calc printed 'Milotic threatened by Rillaboom Wood Hammer (139-183% OHKO)'; we clicked Scald and lost Milotic for 83% chip on a different target.

proposals.change: TAILWIND DEADLINE: when Whimsicott is not on the field but Mega Dragonite is, and no speed control is active by turn 2-3, Dragonite must click Tailwind instead of a non-KO Dragon Pulse once Multiscale is already broken. Never finish a game with 0 Tailwind turns while the foe has a Mega sweeper.
proposals.evidence: Tailwind turns: us 0, them 0. Dragonite died to Mega Salamence Draco Meteor having never set Tailwind; Whimsicott set it on turn 5 as the last mon.

proposals.change: ANTI-REPEAT-PROTECT TARGETING: never aim a spread or single-target KO attempt at a foe that used Protect on the previous turn and is the obvious focus target at low HP; redirect to the partner slot instead.
proposals.evidence: T2 Arcanine Protected at 31% HP; T3 we again aimed Earthquake/Dragon Pulse at that slot — it switched to Sneasler and our EQ hit a +1 Def switch-in.

proposals.change: Vs sheets with Rillaboom (Grassy Surge) + Arcanine-Hisui + Salamence, do NOT lead Milotic. Lead Whimsicott (Tailwind) + Garchomp, keep Mega Dragonite in back as the late-game cleaner after Rillaboom is gone.
proposals.evidence: Milotic was OHKO'd turn 1 by Grassy-boosted Wood Hammer; our lead gave up a mon for zero KOs and no speed control.

lessons: If the threat calc shows a guaranteed OHKO (min damage >=100%) on our slot from a faster foe, that slot Protects or switches — it never attacks.
Never lead Milotic into Rillaboom with Grassy Terrain: Wood Hammer is a guaranteed OHKO.
Finishing a game with 0 Tailwind turns while the opponent has a Mega sweeper is a loss by default — set speed control by turn 2.
Don't aim the same KO attempt at a foe that Protected last turn; hit its partner instead.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 0-2 and its speed did nothing against Grassy Glide priority and Mega Salamence; Sitrus gives Garchomp a second Wood Hammer/Close Combat survival and lets it pick EQ vs Rock Slide freely instead of being locked.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'terrain + priority + Mega cleaner' structure: their Grassy Surge Rillaboom made Grassy Glide a turn-1 priority KO tool AND healed their whole side, while Mega Salamence sat in the back as the unanswered cleaner. For us: shift Milotic's spread to max HP / max Def (Calm, Leftovers) so it actually survives one Grassy-boosted Wood Hammer, and strongly consider bringing Dragonite with Tailwind as the mandatory turn-1 click whenever Whimsicott is benched.
teamInspiration.reason: Milotic's current bulk dies in one hit to the single most common attack in the format, which removes our Competitive pivot before it ever triggers; and their Mega stayed safe in the back while ours was exposed and chipped from turn 1.

analysis.whatWorked: Switching Milotic out of Electric Terrain into Electric-immune Garchomp on T2 was correct, and Mega Dragonite's Dragon Pulse removed Pincurchin (terrain + Discharge source) on schedule. Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum/Earthquake chipping was the only consistent damage source and eventually took Raichu-Y and Incineroar. Recognising Raichu-Mega-Y as the single win condition was the right macro read.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Partly. We correctly avoided Earthquake into our Flying ally, correctly identified the Raichu win-con, and correctly refused to Protect with a Choice-free Milotic when it was a dead slot. But we violated the ANTI-REPEAT-PROTECT TARGETING rule twice: Raichu Protected on T4, and we aimed at it again on T5 and again on T7 immediately after it Protected on T4 — on T7 both of our actions were eaten by a second Protect, a full wasted turn in the 2-action economy. We also violated the GUARANTEED-OHKO rule in reverse on T3: Dragonite was in OHKO range of Zap Cannon (41-71%, already at 78/168 and paralysed) and still clicked an attack instead of Protect/switch, and it died.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) The lead itself. We led Milotic + Dragonite into an Electric Terrain team with Pincurchin + Raichu; Milotic was flinched by Fake Out and then Discharge paralysed Dragonite, breaking Multiscale and costing it the game before it ever threatened. 2) Zero Tailwind turns for the fifth straight game — Whimsicott came in on turn 5 as a sacrifice, never set speed control, and we spent the whole match being outsped by a Mega. 3) T3: with Dragonite at 46% HP and paralysed, facing a guaranteed-ish Zap Cannon KO, we attacked instead of Protecting or switching; Dragonite (our Mega, our win-con) died on turn 3 having dealt one KO. 4) T7: double-targeted a Raichu that had Protected on T4 and was the obvious focus target at 22% — it Protected, both actions wasted, and Incineroar Parting Shot stacked another -1/-1 on Garchomp for free. 5) Incineroar's Parting Shot chain dropped Garchomp to -3 Atk over the game and we never switched Garchomp out to reset it (Choice-free Scarf still resets on switch).
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: never attack with a slot that is at or below ~50% HP, paralysed, and facing a listed KO threat from a faster foe — Protect or switch. Hard rule: a foe that used Protect last turn gets at most ONE of our two actions, never both. Hard rule: when our attacker reaches -2 or worse from Parting Shot/Intimidate chains, switch it out to reset. Preview: vs Electric Terrain (Pincurchin/Tapu Koko/Raichu) lead Garchomp (Ground immunity) + Whimsicott (Tailwind on turn 1), keep Milotic and Dragonite in the back; Dragonite must never be the lead into a paralysis-spreading Discharge board.

proposals.change: PROTECT-REPEAT TARGET CAP: if an opposing Pokemon used Protect on the immediately preceding turn, at most ONE of our two actions may target it this turn; the other action must target the partner slot or set up. Never double-target a just-Protected foe.
proposals.evidence: T7: both Stomping Tantrum and Moonblast aimed at 22% Raichu which had Protected on T4 and Protected again — entire turn wasted, Incineroar got a free Parting Shot.

proposals.change: PARALYSED/CHIPPED MEGA RULE: our Mega (Dragonite/Charizard) must Protect or switch instead of attacking whenever it is paralysed or below 55% HP AND the threat calc lists an incoming move with max damage >= its current HP from a foe that moves first.
proposals.evidence: T3 Dragonite at 78/168 paralysed, threat line 'Raichu Zap Cannon 41-71% (KO 83%)' — we attacked and lost our Mega on turn 3.

proposals.change: Vs Electric-Terrain sheets (Pincurchin/Tapu Koko/Raichu-Mega) lead Garchomp (Electric-immune) + Whimsicott (turn-1 Tailwind). Milotic and Dragonite go to the back: Discharge paralysis breaks Multiscale and Competitive never triggers against Electric teams.
proposals.evidence: T1 Discharge hit both leads, paralysed Dragonite and chipped Milotic to 44%; Milotic was Fake-Out flinched and contributed 0 damage all game.

proposals.change: STAT-DROP RESET RULE: if our attacker is at -2 or worse Attack/SpA from Intimidate or repeated Parting Shot and we have a healthy switch, switch it out instead of attacking at reduced power.
proposals.evidence: Incineroar Parting Shot twice plus two Intimidates left Garchomp at -3 Atk; its Stomping Tantrum fell from 59-86% to 30-36% on the same target.

lessons: Never double-target a foe that Protected on the previous turn — give it one action at most.
Our Mega must Protect or switch (never attack) when paralysed or below 55% HP with a listed KO threat from a faster foe.
Vs Electric Terrain (Pincurchin/Raichu-Mega-Y), lead Garchomp + Whimsicott; Discharge paralysis ruins Dragonite's Multiscale and Milotic's bulk.
Repeated Parting Shot is a stat-drop chain: switch the debuffed attacker out to reset instead of attacking at -2 or worse.
Five straight games with zero Tailwind turns — Whimsicott or Dragonite must click Tailwind by turn 2 or the Mega sweeper simply outspeeds us all game.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 0-3 and this loss featured a Parting Shot/Intimidate chain stacking -3 on our only attacker; Clear Amulet Kingambit blocks Parting Shot and Intimidate drops entirely and gives us a Dark-type that is immune to Fake Out-chip strategies and ignores Electric Terrain.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'terrain + Fake Out + Mega special nuke' funnel: Pincurchin existed only to put Electric Terrain + Discharge paralysis down so Mega Raichu-Y's Zap Cannon became an unavoidable OHKO machine, while Incineroar's Fake Out/Parting Shot bought free turns and permanently debuffed our attacker. For us: give Whimsicott Helping Hand over Moonblast is NOT the fix — instead run Milotic at max HP / max SpD with Leftovers so it actually survives Zap Cannon, and bring Kingambit (immune to nothing electric but fully immune to Prankster/Psychic and unaffected by Parting Shot with Defiant) as the mandatory 4th vs any Fake Out + pivot team.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Milotic was OHKO'd by Zap Cannon at 50% and contributed zero damage; their support pieces generated two free turns and -3 on our attacker without ever taking a hit.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 Prankster Tailwind went up before Mega Alakazam could act, and Dragon Pulse cleanly removed Alakazam on T4. Garchomp's Dragon Claw finished the +1 Dragon Dance Dragonite on T7, and Garchomp's Protect on T6 blanked both Extreme Speed and Drain Punch. Mega Dragonite absorbed the early Ice Spinner instead of Whimsicott taking an Expanding Force.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Tailwind-by-turn-2 rule was followed (3 Tailwind turns, our best in several games). Drogon correctly stayed home vs Delphox/Alakazam special pressure. The chipped-Mega rule was partly honored (Dragonite switched out at 44% on T5). However the Sucker Punch discipline rule was violated on T7 and the anti-setup rule was violated on T4.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) MASSIVE action waste: Dragonite's T1 Tailwind FAILED (ally had just set it) — a completely dead action with our Mega. 2) Whimsicott then clicked Encore on THREE consecutive turns (T2, T3, T4) and it FAILED every time (no foe had used a move / foes switched) — four total dead actions across the first four turns, i.e. half our action economy gone with zero damage. 3) On T4 the foe Dragonite used Dragon Dance completely unpunished while we Encore-whiffed; a +1/+1 Dragonite then Extreme Speed-chipped Garchomp to 13% and forced bad turns. 4) T7 Sucker Punch FAILED into a foe that used Extreme Speed (priority, resolves before Sucker Punch so the 'foe attacks' condition still should have hit — but it whiffed because Dragonite moved first in the priority bracket), another wasted action while Kingambit was being OHKO'd by Drain Punch (threat calc showed 99-145% OHKO 97% — that slot should have Protected or switched, violating the GUARANTEED-OHKO rule). 5) Heat Wave missed twice (T3, T8) at 90% in a game decided by chip. 6) Mega Chesnaught (Drain Punch) was never answered: we had no sustained Fairy/Flying pressure left after Whimsicott was chipped, and it ended with 4 of our mons dead.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block Encore when no opposing active Pokémon has a recorded lastMove this turn-cycle or when the foe just switched in — Encore has failed 3x in one game. Hard-block Tailwind when our own side already has Tailwind active. Enforce the guaranteed-OHKO rule as an actual move block: a slot facing >=100% min damage from a faster foe may only Protect/switch. Punish Dragon Dance immediately: on the turn a foe boosts, the next turn must be a focus-fire or Encore on that exact mon, never a second whiffed status. Finally, prefer Dragon Pulse/Moonblast (100% acc) over Heat Wave when the spread doesn't gain a KO.

proposals.change: HARD-BLOCK Tailwind if our side already has Tailwind active, and HARD-BLOCK Encore when neither opposing active Pokémon has a lastMove from the previous turn (fresh switch-in) or the target is a Dark type.
proposals.evidence: T1 Dragonite Tailwind |-fail|; T2/T3/T4 Whimsicott Encore |-fail| three times in a row — four dead actions in four turns lost the game before it started.

proposals.change: GUARANTEED-OHKO ENFORCEMENT: convert the existing proposal into a code block — if the threat table lists an incoming move with min damage >= our slot's current HP from a foe that moves first, that slot may only Protect or switch.
proposals.evidence: T7 Kingambit was shown taking Chesnaught-Mega Drain Punch 99-145% (OHKO 97%) and still clicked a failing Sucker Punch, dying for free.

proposals.change: SETUP PUNISH LOCK: when a foe used Dragon Dance/Swords Dance/Calm Mind/Nasty Plot last turn, at least one of our two actions must be an attacking move aimed at that foe on the following turn.
proposals.evidence: Foe Dragonite Dragon Danced on T4 unpunished; +1 Speed Extreme Speed then dictated turns 5-7.

proposals.change: Vs sheets containing Mega Chesnaught / bulky Grass-Fighting, bring Drogon (Charizard-Y) — Heat Wave/Weather Ball in sun is our only clean answer; Kingambit is a free KO for Drain Punch.
proposals.evidence: Mega Chesnaught Drain Punch OHKO'd Kingambit and Garchomp and ended the game at full board control.

lessons: Never click Tailwind when our side already has Tailwind up — check the side condition first.
Encore fails against a Pokémon that just switched in or has no last move: only Encore a foe that actually used a move last turn.
Three failed status moves in four turns is a self-inflicted loss — if a status move failed last turn, do not repeat it.
Sucker Punch loses to foes with higher-priority moves (Extreme Speed): it only connects if the foe's attack is in the same or lower priority bracket.
When the threat calc shows a 97%+ OHKO on our slot, that slot Protects or switches — never attacks.
Mega Chesnaught (Drain Punch) requires Charizard-Y/Dragonite Flying-Fire pressure; Kingambit and Garchomp are free KOs for it.

itemExperiment.reason: Mega Dragon Dance Dragonite and +1 Extreme Speed dictated the midgame; Scarf Garchomp outspeeds +1 setup sweepers before they snowball and gives a turn-1 revenge option that Sitrus does not.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'pivot-and-boost' structure: they switched twice on turns 2-3 purely to invalidate our status moves, then set up Dragon Dance behind the chaos. For us: give Whimsicott Helping Hand in place of Encore is the wrong fix — instead keep Encore but add a hard usage condition, and shift Whimsicott's spread toward max HP/Def so it survives one Brave Bird/Shadow Claw and can keep refreshing Tailwind. Also bring Charizard-Y (not Dragonite) against Grass/Fighting Megas like Chesnaught.
teamInspiration.reason: Their double-switch on T2 made our Encore and Heat Wave read dead; a bulkier Whimsicott converts those wasted turns into a second Tailwind cycle, and Charizard-Y's Fire STAB is the only thing on our team that threatens Mega Chesnaught.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead vs Indeedee-F was correct and executed perfectly: Kowtow Cleave OHKO'd the Psychic Terrain/Trick Room setter on turn 1 while Whimsicott Protected the guaranteed Hurricane OHKO. Whimsicott Moonblast finished Kommo-o before it could Clangorous Soul sweep. Those were the only two clean turns of the game.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: 'KO the Psychic Terrain/TR setter immediately with Kingambit', 'Protect the slot facing a 94%+ OHKO'. Violated: 'Set speed control by turn 2' (0 Tailwind turns all game while they had 3), 'Never let the opponent have both speed AND power' (Pelipper Tailwind + Gyarados Dragon Dance went completely unpunished), 'After Wide Guard, stop clicking spread moves' (Rock Slide was blocked by Wide Guard FOUR consecutive turns, T4-T7, a total surrender of the action economy), and the Dragon Dance setup-punish rule (T5 Gyarados danced freely while we Protected and spread into Wide Guard).
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Choice Scarf Garchomp locked into Rock Slide against a Wide Guard Pelipper = four dead turns, ~0 damage from our best attacker for the entire back half. The Choice lock should have been reset by switching Garchomp out the first time Wide Guard appeared. 2) Turn 4 Tailwind with a 1 HP confused Whimsicott was a coin flip that lost — it hit itself and died with zero Tailwind turns. The real error was turn 2 (engine fallback) where we Protected into Pelipper's free Tailwind instead of attacking it or setting our own. 3) Turn 3 we split Iron Head + Moonblast onto Kommo-o while Pelipper (the Tailwind/Wide Guard engine) took zero damage all game until turn 6. 4) Drogon was brought into a rain team with Gyarados-Mega and died to two Waterfalls having dealt 70% total; T6 attacking at full HP with a listed 99% Waterfall threat, then T7 attacking at 1 HP. 5) Mega evolved on turn 5 — far too late to matter.
analysis.howToImprove: Code a hard Wide Guard memory: once a foe uses Wide Guard, block all spread moves (Rock Slide/Heat Wave/Earthquake/Discharge) for the next 2 turns and, if our attacker is Choice-locked into a spread move, force a switch to reset the lock. Treat Pelipper as a priority target the moment it reveals Tailwind/Wide Guard — it is the whole support engine. Enforce a Dragon Dance punish: when Gyarados-Mega dances, every action must hit it (Rock Slide is blocked, so single-target Ancient Power / Dragon Claw). Never click Tailwind with a confused sub-10% Whimsicott; attack or let it die usefully. Against rain + Gyarados-Mega, Drogon is not the right Mega — Mega Dragonite (Multiscale + Tailwind) or keeping Drogon home is correct.

proposals.change: WIDE GUARD MEMORY: if an opposing active Pokémon used Wide Guard within the last 2 turns, hard-block all spread moves (Rock Slide, Heat Wave, Earthquake, Blizzard, Discharge, Make It Rain). If our Pokémon is Choice-locked into that spread move, the only legal actions are switch or Protect.
proposals.evidence: T4-T7 vs DinFinn: Scarf Garchomp clicked Rock Slide four consecutive turns into Pelipper's Wide Guard for literally zero damage while Gyarados Dragon Danced and swept.

proposals.change: SUPPORT-ENGINE TARGETING: a foe that has used Tailwind, Wide Guard, Follow Me or Trick Room becomes the designated priority target — at least one of our two actions must be a single-target attack aimed at it until it faints.
proposals.evidence: Pelipper set Tailwind T2, then Wide Guard T4/5/6/7 and took its first damage on turn 6; it survived the whole game and enabled the Gyarados sweep.

proposals.change: BLOCK Tailwind/status from a Pokémon that is confused AND below 15% HP — attack instead so the turn has value even if the self-hit happens.
proposals.evidence: T4: Whimsicott at 1 HP and confused clicked Tailwind, hit itself, fainted; we finished the game with 0 Tailwind turns vs their 3.

proposals.change: Vs rain sheets containing Gyarados-Mega + Pelipper, bring Mega Dragonite (Multiscale, Tailwind, Dragon Pulse) rather than Drogon; Drogon's sun is reverted and Waterfall/Stone Edge both OHKO it.
proposals.evidence: Drogon megaed turn 5, dealt 70% total and died to two Waterfalls; our sun never mattered because Gyarados was physical Water.

lessons: Wide Guard blocks every spread move: after it is used once, stop clicking spread moves for at least two turns — and if Choice-locked into one, switch to reset the lock.
A Choice-locked Pokémon whose move is being blocked/immune must switch out, not keep firing.
Pelipper-style support (Tailwind + Wide Guard) is a win condition: attack it with single-target moves the turn it reveals itself, don't let it live to turn 6.
Never click a status move with a confused Pokémon at under 15% HP.
Vs Gyarados-Mega, Rock moves are our answer but Wide Guard shuts Rock Slide down — Garchomp needs a single-target option or must be switched.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice Scarf Garchomp was locked into Rock Slide against Wide Guard for four turns and contributed nothing. Sitrus Garchomp can pivot between Earthquake and single-target Dragon Claw/Stomping Tantrum when spread moves are walled, and survives Ice Fang rolls.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'spread-proof support + Dragon Dance cleaner' structure: Pelipper's Wide Guard made our entire offense (Rock Slide, Heat Wave, Earthquake) illegal while Gyarados-Mega set up for free. For us: give Whimsicott a bulkier spread (max HP / +Def, Focus Sash kept) so it survives one Hurricane and can actually land Tailwind, and ensure at least two single-target attacks are always on the field (Garchomp Dragon Claw/Stomping Tantrum + Drogon Ancient Power) so a Wide Guard user cannot zero out our turn.
teamInspiration.reason: We lost 4 of 8 turns to a single Wide Guard user; our team leans heavily on spread moves (Heat Wave, Rock Slide, Earthquake) and had no plan when they were blocked.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Tailwind went up immediately and Drogon Mega-evolved to flip rain into sun. Turn 2 focus-fire (Moonblast chip + Weather Ball) cleanly removed Mega Gengar, the Shadow Tag/Perish Song trapper, before it could trap anything — that was the correct macro target. Turn 4 Dragon Claw finished Pelipper (support engine) rather than overkilling.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: KO the Shadow Tag trapper fast; set Tailwind by turn 1; target the support engine (Pelipper) with a single-target move. Violated: the hard rule that a slot facing a listed OHKO must Protect or switch — Drogon attacked on turn 3 with Archaludon's Electro Shot and Pelipper's Weather Ball both listed as KO threats and died. Also violated the 'burst Archaludon in one turn, never chip it' rain rule: Kowtow Cleave did 51% into Stamina +1 Def and gave it a free snowball.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1 Drogon attacked into a 100% certain Fake Out from Infernape and lost its action anyway (predictable Fake Out from a fresh Infernape lead — Protect or a non-committal move was better, or at minimum the Mega should not have been the Fake Out target of choice). 2) Turn 3 was the game-losing turn: both our mons were flagged with OHKO threats, Whimsicott was at 1 HP, and we attacked with both. Drogon (our Mega and only win condition) died to Electro Shot. The correct play was Drogon Protect (Archaludon had just switched in; Electro Shot charges in rain and is instant) while Whimsicott chips. 3) We let Archaludon charge Electro Shot unopposed and gain +1 SpA, then Stamina +1 Def — the opponent achieved speed (Pelipper could have had Tailwind) AND power with zero resistance. 4) Kingambit chipped Archaludon for 51% instead of us focus-firing it with both actions on T4; Archaludon then 1-shot Kingambit and Garchomp. 5) Garchomp was Choice-locked into Dragon Claw against a Steel/Dragon wall with +1 Def and had no out.
analysis.howToImprove: Against Archaludon rain: Archaludon is THE win condition — it must be double-targeted the turn it appears, never chipped across two turns. On T4 the correct line was Kowtow Cleave + Dragon Claw both into Archaludon (51% + ~35% = KO) and let Pelipper live at 14%. Second: enforce the OHKO rule mechanically — any slot with a listed min-damage>=current-HP threat from a faster foe may only Protect or switch; that single rule saves Drogon on T3 and likely the game. Third: vs a fresh Infernape/Incineroar lead, assume Fake Out on the Mega and do not spend the Mega's turn-1 action on a committal attack when a Protect or support line exists.

proposals.change: ARCHALUDON BURST LOCK: when Archaludon is on the field, both of our actions must target it until it faints (never split damage between Archaludon and a chip target); never leave it alive after a turn where we could have double-targeted it.
proposals.evidence: T4 we did Kowtow Cleave (51%) into Archaludon and Dragon Claw into a 14% Pelipper. Archaludon survived at 49% with +1 Def Stamina and then KO'd Kingambit and Garchomp on consecutive turns.

proposals.change: HARD OHKO GUARD (code-enforced): if the threat table lists an incoming move with min damage >= our slot's current HP from a foe that moves first, that slot may only select Protect or a switch. Applied to Drogon this would have blocked the T3 Ancient Power.
proposals.evidence: T3 Drogon was listed as threatened by Pelipper Weather Ball (90-158% KO) and still attacked; Archaludon Electro Shot finished it. Our Mega and only sun-abuser died turn 3.

proposals.change: FAKE OUT ANTICIPATION: on turn 1, if an opposing active has Fake Out (Infernape/Incineroar/Rillaboom/Hariyama) and is faster than our Mega, the Mega's damaging attack is penalised; prefer Protect or a support action.
proposals.evidence: T1 Infernape Fake Out flinched Drogon; the whole Weather Ball turn was lost while Gengar freely Sludge Bombed Whimsicott to 1 HP.

proposals.change: Vs rain sheets containing Archaludon, bring Milotic over Kingambit: Milotic resists nothing relevant but survives Electro Shot/Aura Sphere far better and Scald+Competitive pressures the whole rain core, while Kingambit is 1-shot by Aura Sphere.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit took 90% from Aura Sphere and died in one hit after doing 51% chip; Garchomp was 89%'d by Dragon Pulse. Our back half contributed 65 damage total.

lessons: Archaludon is a one-turn burst target: double-target it the turn it lands or it snowballs via Electro Shot (+1 SpA) and Stamina (+1 Def).
Never let our Mega attack on a turn where the threat table lists an OHKO on it from a faster foe — Protect or switch, even if that forfeits a KO.
Assume Fake Out from a fresh Infernape/Incineroar/Rillaboom lead on turn 1 and do not spend the Mega's action on a committal attack.
A Choice-locked Garchomp facing a +1 Def Steel wall must switch, not keep clicking a resisted move.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice Scarf Garchomp was locked into Dragon Claw against a +1 Def Archaludon and had zero outs as our last Pokemon; Sitrus Berry gives move freedom (Earthquake into Archaludon) and survives one Dragon Pulse.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'disruption lead into charging nuke' structure: Gengar+Infernape existed purely to burn our turn-1 and turn-5 actions (Fake Out, Sludge Bomb) while Archaludon came in free and charged Electro Shot in Pelipper's rain. For us: keep Milotic as the mandatory 4th vs any rain sheet (max HP / max SpD, Leftovers) so Electro Shot and Aura Sphere are 3HKOs rather than OHKOs, and give Drogon a bulk-leaning spread (enough HP to survive one unboosted Electro Shot in rain) so it is not deleted before sun pays off.
teamInspiration.reason: Every one of our Pokemon was OHKO'd or near-OHKO'd by a single Archaludon; we had no body that could take two hits from it, so it never had to respect our offense.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead vs Indeedee logic was sound in principle, and Whimsicott's Moonblast chip plus Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum did eventually remove Incineroar. Drogon's Mega + Weather Ball finally pressured Indeedee, and Whimsicott's Protect on T7 correctly dodged a listed KO threat.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Several durable lessons were VIOLATED. (1) 'If the threat calc shows a guaranteed/97%+ OHKO on our slot from a faster foe, that slot Protects or switches — it never attacks': T1 the calc listed Raichu Focus Blast 71-108% on Kingambit and we still attacked into it, losing our Psychic-immune anchor on turn 1 for ~28% chip. (2) 'Never double-target a foe that Protected on the previous turn / don't aim the same KO attempt at a foe that Protected last turn': T2 Raichu Protected, and on T3 we aimed Stomping Tantrum at Raichu again (it switched out, wasting the Scarf lock). (3) 'Encore fails against a Pokémon that just switched in' and 'if a status move failed last turn, do not repeat it': Encore was clicked 3 separate turns, failing on T3. (4) 'Punish setup immediately': Milotic used Coil SIX times unpunished, reaching +6/+6/+6 — we never once attacked it, never switched a counter in, and Encore'd it INTO Coil (which just lets it keep boosting). Encoring a setup move is a non-punish.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T1 Kingambit attacked into a listed 71-108% OHKO and died immediately — a 1-for-0 trade that handed them the whole game and left Drogon exposed to Zap Cannon. 2) We Encored Milotic into COIL on T2 and T5 — Encore on a boosting move locks the foe into continuing to boost. That is the opposite of punishment. Milotic ended at +6 Atk/+6 Def/+6 accuracy and killed two of our Pokémon with Icy Wind. 3) Garchomp was Choice-locked into Stomping Tantrum and we kept firing it at a target that Protected, then switched; 3 of its actions produced nothing. 4) Only 2 Tailwind turns the whole game; Whimsicott spent its turns on Encore/Moonblast instead of the one move that mattered. 5) Drogon Mega'd on turn 7 — our win condition sat on the bench while Raichu-Y farmed, then got OHKO'd by Zap Cannon at full HP. 6) Damage calcs were off three times (Weather Ball predicted 8-12% actually did 64%), meaning our engine's assumed sets were wrong and our 'this won't KO' reasoning was unreliable.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: never Encore a foe whose last move was a self-boosting setup move (Coil, Calm Mind, Swords Dance, Dragon Dance, Iron Defense, Bulk Up, Nasty Plot, Quiver Dance, Shell Smash, Clangorous Soul) — Encore locks them into continuing to boost. Punish setup with damage, or switch in a body that walls it. Hard rule: a slot facing a listed >=90% OHKO from a faster foe may only Protect or switch; on T1 Kingambit should have Protected (Raichu Focus Blast wasted) while Whimsicott set Tailwind. Hard rule: do not re-aim at a foe that Protected last turn. Hard rule: Whimsicott's first action of the game is Tailwind unless Trick Room is up. Finally, Mega by turn 2 at the latest — Drogon Mega'd on turn 7 and contributed almost nothing.

proposals.change: ENCORE SETUP BAN: hard-block Encore when the target's last move was a self-targeting stat-boosting move (Coil, Calm Mind, Swords Dance, Dragon Dance, Nasty Plot, Bulk Up, Iron Defense, Quiver Dance, Shell Smash, Clangorous Soul, Agility, Work Up). Encore in that case locks them into boosting further. Punish with damage or switch instead.
proposals.evidence: vs RahliCahli T2 and T5: Whimsicott Encored Milotic into Coil; Milotic reached +6/+6/+6 and KO'd Whimsicott and Garchomp with Icy Wind.

proposals.change: HARD OHKO GUARD (code-enforced, raise priority): if the threat table lists an incoming move with max damage >= 100% of our slot's current HP from a faster foe, that slot may only Protect or switch. Enforce in shouldBlockMove for all damaging moves on that slot.
proposals.evidence: T1 Kingambit attacked into Raichu Focus Blast listed at 71-108% and was KO'd before acting, costing our only Psychic-immune body.

proposals.change: PROTECT MEMORY: block any move aimed at a foe that used Protect/Detect/Spiky Shield on the immediately preceding turn; redirect to its partner.
proposals.evidence: T2 Raichu Protected; T3 we re-aimed Scarf-locked Stomping Tantrum at Raichu, which switched out — the action was wasted.

proposals.change: WHIMSICOTT TAILWIND FIRST: Whimsicott's first action of a battle must be Tailwind unless Trick Room is active or Tailwind is already up. Tailwind turns were 2 this game and have been 0-3 in five straight losses.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott spent T2-T6 on Encore/Moonblast; we only got Tailwind up late and never had speed advantage over Raichu-Mega-Y.

proposals.change: Vs sheets with Raichu-Mega-Y (Zap Cannon/Focus Blast), do not lead Kingambit — Focus Blast OHKOs it. Lead Garchomp (Scarf, outspeeds and Stomping Tantrum KOs Raichu) + Whimsicott Tailwind, Kingambit in the back for Indeedee/Gholdengo.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit died turn 1 to Focus Blast; Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum was listed at 87-127% KO on Raichu-Mega-Y.

lessons: Never Encore a foe that just used a self-boosting setup move — Encore locks them INTO the boost. Attack it or switch a wall in instead.
A slot facing a listed max-damage >= 100% OHKO from a faster foe may only Protect or switch, never attack.
Never re-target a foe that Protected on the previous turn; hit its partner.
Whimsicott's first action of the game is Tailwind unless Trick Room is up.
Do not lead Kingambit into Raichu-Mega-Y: Focus Blast is a clean OHKO.
Mega Evolve by turn 2; a Mega that evolves on turn 7 contributes nothing.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 0-6. Choice lock wasted three actions this game (locked Stomping Tantrum into a Protect, then a switch). Sitrus gives move freedom (Rock Slide vs Raichu, Dragon Claw vs Dragonite, EQ) and longevity against Icy Wind chip.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'boost behind a redirecting/bulky partner' plan: Coil Milotic became unkillable because Incineroar then Indeedee (Follow Me) absorbed every action while it boosted six times. For us: give our Milotic Coil-proof pressure by running Ice Beam + Scald with max HP/max SpD Leftovers AND bring Kingambit in the back (not the lead) so Sucker Punch punishes setup turns; additionally consider swapping Whimsicott's Encore for Helping Hand is wrong — keep Encore but add Taunt consideration on a future variant, since Taunt (not Encore) is the real anti-Coil tool.
teamInspiration.reason: Encore cannot stop a self-boosting foe (it locks them into boosting), but Taunt does. Their entire win condition was a +6 Milotic we had no tool to stop; one Taunt or one focused double-attack turn would have ended it.

analysis.whatWorked: Whimsicott clicked Tailwind on its first action (coach rule honoured) and we got 3 Tailwind turns. Kingambit was an excellent mid-game cleaner: Kowtow Cleave KO'd the 8% Raichu on T4 and finished Pelipper on T5, removing the rain/Tailwind/Wide Guard engine. Drogon's Protect on T5 correctly dodged the listed Weather Ball/Scald OHKO threat. Mega evolution of Charizard flipped rain to sun at the right moment.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: Whimsicott Tailwind first; Protect on our Mega when the threat table listed an OHKO (T5); switched Garchomp out at 9% instead of attacking into Wide Guard (T3). Violated: the explicit 'after Wide Guard, stop clicking spread moves for at least two turns' rule — Rock Slide was used into Wide Guard on T1 AND repeated on T2, burning both of Garchomp's actions, and Heat Wave (spread) was clicked on T4 and T6 into the same Wide Guard user's side. Also violated: Drogon attacked on T6 with Milotic Scald listed at 58-102% KO on it — that slot should have Protected or switched.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Two full Garchomp turns wasted on Rock Slide into Wide Guard (T1, T2) while Milotic free-fired Icy Wind, dropping Garchomp to 9% and Whimsicott to 33% before we had done anything. That single Wide Guard user effectively won the action economy 4-0 in the first two turns. 2) Garchomp's whole kit in this matchup was spread/Ground — against a Flying rain setter with Wide Guard it had no safe button, so it contributed 0 damage all game. 3) T6 Drogon attacked into a listed 58-102% Scald KO and died; Kingambit Protected instead (it was the one at 24% but also the one that could have taken the hit behind Protect order). We should have Protected Drogon and attacked with Kingambit or switched Drogon out. 4) Lead choice: Garchomp + Whimsicott into a sheet with Pelipper (Wide Guard + Hurricane) meant our lead's only moves were spread moves Pelipper blocks and Icy Wind-vulnerable. 5) Icy Wind spam completely neutralised our Tailwind — three consecutive -1 Speed drops meant Tailwind bought nothing.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-code a Wide Guard memory: once a foe uses Wide Guard, block ALL spread moves (Rock Slide, Heat Wave, Earthquake, Dazzling Gleam) for the next 3 turns and force single-target options or a switch. Against any sheet containing Pelipper/Mandibuzz-style Wide Guard, prefer Dragon Claw / Stomping Tantrum / Weather Ball / Ancient Power targeting. Enforce the OHKO guard for Drogon (T6) — if max damage >= current HP from a faster foe, Protect or switch, never attack. Against Icy Wind rain cores, Tailwind is a trap after the first drop: prefer switching the speed-dropped piece out to reset. Lead Whimsicott + Drogon (not Garchomp) vs Pelipper rain so Weather Ball/Ancient Power are available turn 1 and sun is up immediately.

proposals.change: WIDE GUARD MEMORY (code-enforced): once any opposing Pokémon uses Wide Guard, hard-block every spread move (Rock Slide, Heat Wave, Earthquake, Dazzling Gleam, Blizzard, Discharge, Icy Wind) from our side for the following 3 turns while that Pokémon is alive. Force single-target attacks or a switch.
proposals.evidence: T1 and T2 Garchomp Rock Slide were both fully blocked by Pelipper Wide Guard; T4 and T6 Heat Wave were also spread moves into the same side. Four of our actions in a 7-turn game produced ~0 value.

proposals.change: SPREAD-ONLY KIT CHECK: if our active Pokémon's only non-blocked damaging options are spread moves and a Wide Guard user is active, switch that Pokémon out instead of attacking.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp's Rock Slide and Earthquake were both dead vs Pelipper; it dealt 0% damage the entire game and died at 9%.

proposals.change: ICY WIND / SPEED-DROP RESET: when our Tailwind is up and a slot has taken 2+ Speed drops, switch that slot out (resets stages) rather than keep attacking — Tailwind is otherwise fully neutralised.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp took -3 Speed over turns 1-3 from Milotic Icy Wind, negating all 3 Tailwind turns.

proposals.change: Vs rain sheets containing Pelipper, do NOT lead Garchomp (Rock Slide/EQ both answered by Wide Guard + Flying). Lead Whimsicott (Tailwind) + Charizard-Y so Drought cancels rain turn 1 and Ancient Power/Weather Ball are single-target answers to Pelipper.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp lead produced zero damage and died; Drogon only entered on T3 and megad on T4, by which point Pelipper had Tailwind and Wide Guard established.

lessons: Wide Guard memory is absolute: after a foe uses Wide Guard once, every spread move on our side is banned for 3 turns — switch or use single-target instead.
If a Pokémon's entire usable kit this turn is spread moves and a Wide Guard user is active, switch it out; do not click a blocked move twice.
Repeated Icy Wind negates Tailwind: switch the speed-dropped Pokémon out to reset stages instead of attacking at -2 or worse Speed.
Never lead Garchomp into a Pelipper rain sheet — its Rock Slide and Earthquake are both dead moves there.

For us: drop Garchomp's Rock Slide reliance by switching to Sitrus Berry (move freedom), and give Milotic Icy Wind in place of Ice Beam on a test variant so WE can deny opposing Tailwind/speed. Additionally run Whimsicott at max HP/Def with Focus Sash so it survives one Icy Wind + Hurricane cycle and can refresh Tailwind.

analysis.whatWorked: Whimsicott Tailwind on turn 1 (coach rule) followed by Mega Charizard-Y Drought gave us both speed and power immediately and we never lost that advantage. Weather Ball in sun 2HKO'd Golurk through Protect-stall and OHKO'd Aromatisse; Whimsicott's Moonblast cleaned three Pokemon (Hydrapple, Pangoro, Golurk) because Tailwind kept it moving first. Encore on Golurk (locked into Protect) was a clean, correct disruption that neutralised their Protect-stalling slot. Opponent set Trick Room turn 1 and we correctly did NOT click Tailwind again into it — we kept attacking and let the 5 turns burn while still winning the damage race.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Whimsicott's first action was Tailwind (active proposal) — applied. Mega evolved on turn 1, satisfying 'Mega Evolve by turn 2'. We did not click Tailwind into Trick Room. We did not re-target the slot that Protected on the previous turn with our whole team (Heat Wave spread still hit Golurk through its Protect only by splash, Moonblast was redirected onto the partner Hydrapple — correct Protect-memory behaviour). No Sucker Punch whiffs, no spread moves into Wide Guard, no status move repeated after a fail.
analysis.whatFailed: Three of seven turns fell back to the engine due to HTTP 429 rate limiting — a quarter of our decisions were made blind. On turn 5 Drogon attacked into an active Golurk with Rock Slide available (4x super-effective on Charizard-Y); the threat table had already listed Golurk Poltergeist on Drogon and Golurk had revealed nothing but Protect/Rock Slide risk — our Mega win-con died to a 2%-HP Pokemon because the fallback engine clicked an attack instead of Protect. That is a direct violation of 'never let our Mega attack on a turn where a Rock user is active'. Also, turn 4 Encore was aimed at a freshly switched-in Aromatisse (which had used Trick Room earlier but had just been re-sent); the Encore landed but on a Pokemon that was about to be KO'd anyway, a wasted half-action.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Hard-code: while any Rock-capable foe (Golurk, Tyranitar, Excadrill, Garchomp, Rhyperior, Terrakion) is on the field, Charizard-Y may not use a damaging move if it is not guaranteed to KO that foe this turn — Protect or switch instead. Golurk at 2% HP is still lethal to a 4x Rock weakness. 2) When ahead 4v2 or more, the safe line is Protect on the Mega and attack with the expendable slot. 3) Reduce rate-limit exposure by making the fallback engine inherit the last Claude directive (e.g. 'Protect Drogon vs Rock') rather than re-deriving from scratch.

proposals.change: ROCK-WEAK MEGA GUARD (code-enforced): while Charizard(-Mega-Y) is active and any opposing active Pokemon knows or plausibly carries a Rock move (Golurk, Tyranitar, Excadrill, Rhyperior, Garchomp, Terrakion, Tyrantrum, Aerodactyl, Archeops), block all damaging moves from Charizard unless that move guarantees the KO on the Rock user this turn; force Protect or switch. Applies even if the Rock user is at 1-5% HP.
proposals.evidence: T5: Golurk at 2% HP used Rock Slide and OHKO'd our Mega Charizard-Y (49% listed, 4x effective) while we clicked an attack. We were winning 4v3 and threw our win condition to a nearly-dead Pokemon.

proposals.change: LOW-HP LETHAL FOE RULE: a foe below 15% HP is still a full-power attacker. Never treat it as 'free'. If it has a move that OHKOs one of our actives, that slot Protects or we KO the foe with the slot that moves first — never both slots attacking the other target.
proposals.evidence: Golurk at 2% HP got a full-power Rock Slide off and killed Drogon on T5.

proposals.change: FALLBACK DIRECTIVE INHERITANCE: when the Claude call fails (HTTP 429), the engine fallback must still honour the hard guardrails in shouldBlockMove (Rock guard, OHKO guard, Wide Guard memory). Ensure shouldBlockMove is consulted on the fallback path too.
proposals.evidence: 3 of 7 turns were engine fallbacks and the losing-our-Mega decision on T5 was one of them.

proposals.change: Keep Whimsicott + Charizard-Y as the default lead vs 'standard' archetypes: 13-10 and this game's clean win. Whimsicott scored 3 KOs under Tailwind.
proposals.evidence: Tailwind turns us 3, them 0; Whimsicott dealt 144% and 3 KOs.

lessons: A foe at 2% HP deals 100% of its damage — never leave our 4x-weak Mega exposed to a low-HP Rock user; Protect or KO it with the faster slot.
While a Rock-move user is on the field, Charizard-Y only attacks if that attack guarantees the KO on it; otherwise Protect or switch.
Encore is wasted on a Pokemon that is about to faint or has just switched in — spend that action on damage instead.
Tailwind turn 1 + Mega Drought turn 1 is our strongest opening vs 'standard' teams: we out-sped and out-powered them every turn.
When the Claude call rate-limits, the engine fallback must still be bound by the hard move guardrails, or it will throw the game on one turn.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 focus-fire removed Mega Raichu-Y (the Zap Cannon OHKO threat) before it ever attacked, and turn 2 Moonblast+Weather Ball removed Staraptor. Two KOs in two turns with Drogon, and the damage calcs were all inside predicted ranges (3/3).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Mega evolved turn 1 (rule followed). Focus-fired the biggest threat instead of splitting. BUT the two most important standing rules were violated: (1) Whimsicott's first action of the game must be Tailwind — it clicked Moonblast twice instead, so we had 0 Tailwind turns in a game where speed decided everything; (2) 'Assume Fake Out from a fresh Rillaboom lead and do not spend the Mega's action on a committal attack' — Drogon at 18% attacked into a freshly switched-in Rillaboom and died to Fake Out.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) No Tailwind at all: Whimsicott opened Moonblast, then Moonblast again, then died. Our only speed control never happened. 2) Drogon at 27/153 HP attacked into a brand-new Rillaboom instead of Protecting or switching — Fake Out (a guaranteed-hit priority move from an unused Pokemon) deleted our Mega for free; that is a textbook 'threatened slot must Protect or switch' violation. 3) Primarina got FOUR free Calm Minds. Nobody ever threatened it meaningfully: we spent turn 1 and 2 on the other slot and then only chipped with Stomping Tantrum (a 33-52% roll) while it boosted to +4/+4 and Moonblasted Garchomp for an OHKO. Unpunished setup = the game. 4) Milotic was brought in at turn 3 into a Rillaboom with Grassy Terrain and Wood Hammer and was OHKO'd — the wrong switch-in; Kingambit (Dark, resists nothing relevant but survives Wood Hammer far better) or simply Protect-cycling was better. 5) 4-turn loss with zero Protects clicked all game.
analysis.howToImprove: Whimsicott must click Tailwind turn 1 unless Trick Room is up — hard-code it. A fresh (activeTurns===0) Fake Out user on the field means any of our sub-40% Pokemon in the targetable slot must Protect or switch, never attack. Calm Mind/Coil/Dragon Dance on the field: the boosting slot becomes the mandatory focus-fire target for BOTH our actions from the turn it first boosts, not a chip target. Against Primarina/Rillaboom/Staraptor rain-less balance, Milotic is not a safe pivot into Wood Hammer in Grassy Terrain; send Kingambit instead.

proposals.change: HARD RULE (code-enforced): Whimsicott's first action of the battle is Tailwind unless Trick Room is active or Tailwind is already up. Block all other Whimsicott moves on its first turn out in that case.

proposals.change: FAKE-OUT GUARD: if an opposing Pokemon has activeTurns===0 and plausibly carries Fake Out (Rillaboom, Incineroar, Infernape, Mienshao, Hariyama, Raichu, Kangaskhan, Scrafty), any of our actives below 35% HP must Protect or switch — block their damaging moves.
proposals.evidence: Drogon at 18% attacked a freshly-switched Rillaboom and was KO'd by Fake Out before acting, losing our Mega for nothing.

proposals.change: SETUP FOCUS-FIRE: once a foe has +2 or more in any offensive stat (Calm Mind/Coil/DD/NP/SD), both our actions must target that foe (or Protect) until it is KO'd; ban attacks aimed at its partner while we have 2 live actives.
proposals.evidence: Primarina reached +4/+4 Calm Mind over 4 turns while we attacked Raichu, Staraptor and Rillaboom; its Moonblast then OHKO'd Garchomp to end the game.

proposals.change: SWITCH-IN SAFETY: never bring Milotic in while Rillaboom is active with Grassy Terrain up (Wood Hammer 139-183% OHKO listed). Prefer Kingambit or Dragonite as the replacement body.
proposals.evidence: T3 engine switched Milotic into Rillaboom and it was OHKO'd by Wood Hammer on T4 without doing anything.

lessons: Whimsicott's very first action is Tailwind — no exceptions outside Trick Room; a game with 0 Tailwind turns is a game we lose on speed.
A freshly switched-in Fake Out user (Rillaboom/Incineroar/Infernape) means our low-HP slots Protect or switch; never attack into a guaranteed priority flinch at <35% HP.
Calm Mind / Coil setup must be answered with BOTH actions the turn it starts; chip damage from one slot never beats a +1-per-turn booster.
Do not switch Milotic into an active Rillaboom under Grassy Terrain — Wood Hammer OHKOs it.
Two early KOs mean nothing if the opponent's setup sweeper is untouched: count win conditions, not knockouts.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Protect on Kingambit vs Sneasler Close Combat was correct, and Mega Drogon evolving turn 1 set sun immediately and later KO'd Sneasler and Swampert-Mega (172% damage, 2 KOs). Switching Drogon out at 27% on turn 3 to bring Milotic in against Waterfall was a clean defensive reposition. Milotic's Protect/Scald stall cycle burned Trick Room turns correctly and eventually KO'd Indeedee. Damage calcs were accurate (6/6 inside predicted range).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Mega by turn 1: yes. Did not click Tailwind into Trick Room: correct (Tailwind was set on T3 BEFORE Trick Room went up, which was still a wasted resource because the opponent's TR immediately inverted it). Protect-stalling TR turns with Milotic/Whimsicott was correct per the TR playbook. VIOLATED: Kingambit was led into a Sneasler sheet — Close Combat is a guaranteed 153-222% OHKO on it, the same class of error as 'do not lead Kingambit into Raichu-Mega-Y'. Also violated 'a slot facing a listed max-damage >=100% OHKO from a faster foe may only Protect or switch' — on T2 Kingambit clicked Iron Head into a listed 153-222% OHKO and died for 0 damage.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) LEAD: Kingambit into a sheet containing Sneasler (Fighting, faster, Close Combat) is an auto-loss for that slot; it died turn 2 having dealt 0 damage. 2) T2 Kingambit attacked into a guaranteed OHKO instead of Protecting or switching — a wasted action AND a lost Pokemon; the Weather Ball KO'd Sneasler anyway, so Protect would have cost nothing and saved Kingambit. 3) Whimsicott spent its Tailwind on T3, one turn before Indeedee set Trick Room, so all 3 Tailwind turns were actively harmful (we moved LAST). Against an Indeedee-F sheet, Tailwind must be withheld until Trick Room is confirmed expired. 4) We never pressured Indeedee, the TR setter and the eventual game-winner with Slowking-G's Expanding Force; it lived until turn 13. 5) Whimsicott was left at 1 HP and then clicked Moonblast into a guaranteed Ice Punch KO instead of switching out — another slot lost for ~25% chip.
analysis.howToImprove: Never lead Kingambit when the opposing sheet shows Sneasler, Raichu-Mega-Y, Great Tusk, or any fast Fighting/Fire attacker. Against an Indeedee-F / Slowking-G / Trick Room sheet, Whimsicott's first action is NOT Tailwind — it is Encore/Moonblast on the setter or Protect; Tailwind only goes up once TR has visibly ended with >=3 turns of usable field. Any slot with a listed >=100% incoming OHKO from a faster foe may only Protect or switch — enforce in code, no exceptions. Focus-fire Indeedee the turn it lands: it is the win condition enabler for Expanding Force + TR.

proposals.change: HARD RULE (code-enforced): block all damaging moves from a slot whose listed max incoming damage from a FASTER foe is >=100%. That slot may only Protect or switch. Kingambit T2 Iron Head into a 153-222% Close Combat is the exact failure.
proposals.evidence: T2: Kingambit clicked Iron Head (58-114%) into a listed 153-222% OHKO, died before moving, dealt 0 damage; Drogon's Weather Ball KO'd Sneasler on its own.

proposals.change: ANTI-SNEASLER LEAD BAN: never lead Kingambit when the opponent sheet contains Sneasler, Raichu-Mega-Y, Great Tusk, Urshifu-Single, or Koraidon. Lead Milotic/Whimsicott + Charizard instead and keep Kingambit in the back.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit has now been the first Pokemon lost in 3 of the last 5 games, twice to a lead Fighting/Focus Blast OHKO (Raichu-Y T1, Sneasler T2).

proposals.change: ANTI-TR TAILWIND DELAY: if the opposing sheet contains a Trick Room setter (Indeedee-F, Hatterene, Farigiraf, Porygon2, Dusclops, Slowking-G, Bronzong) and TR has not yet been used, Whimsicott's first action is Encore/Moonblast/Protect, NOT Tailwind. Only set Tailwind after TR has expired or the setter is KO'd.
proposals.evidence: T3 Tailwind went up; Indeedee set Trick Room the same turn; we then moved LAST for 3 turns with our own speed control active.

proposals.change: Give Whimsicott Taunt over Encore on a test variant: Prankster Taunt pre-emptively blocks Trick Room AND Calm Mind/Coil, the two archetypes that have beaten us most (TR 13/37, setup sweepers in the last 3 losses). Encore cannot stop either.
proposals.evidence: Indeedee freely clicked Trick Room and Helping Hand all game; Encore was never a useful answer, and in two prior losses Encore would have locked a booster INTO boosting.

lessons: Never lead Kingambit into a sheet with Sneasler, Raichu-Mega-Y or any faster Fighting-type attacker — Close Combat/Focus Blast is a guaranteed OHKO and the slot dies with 0 damage dealt.
A slot facing a listed >=100% incoming OHKO from a faster foe may ONLY Protect or switch — never attack, even if its attack 'might' KO.
Against an Indeedee-F / Slowking-G / Hatterene sheet, do NOT set Tailwind until Trick Room has been used and expired; a Tailwind set one turn before TR makes us move last for 4 turns.
Focus-fire the Trick Room setter (Indeedee) the turn it lands — leaving it alive until turn 13 let Expanding Force win the game.
A Pokemon at 1-5% HP that is guaranteed to be KO'd should switch out, not trade ~25% chip for the slot.

analysis.whatWorked: Lead choice (Milotic + Mega Dragonite) was correct vs a Gholdengo/Volcarona/Garchomp/Incineroar/Rillaboom/Raichu sheet: Milotic's Competitive punishes Incineroar Intimidate and Dragonite gets Tailwind/Dragon Pulse. analysis.lessonsApplied: Mega evolved turn 1 (rule followed). Focus-fired the single most dangerous foe instead of splitting damage (Wolfe win-con denial). Structurally, the larger issue is the standing record: scarf_garchomp loadout sits at 2W-9L and the 14-game team window is 2-12, so the sample of real failures lies outside this battle.
analysis.howToImprove: Keep the Milotic + Mega Dragonite lead as the default vs Incineroar/Rillaboom/Gholdengo 'standard' sheets — it is our best-performing plan (standard / Dragonite|zw = 17-9). Continue focus-firing the one foe that both outspeeds us and threatens an OHKO on the Mega on turn 1. Given the 2-12 window, the priority is not micro play but the structural fixes already proposed: Whimsicott Taunt variant for anti-setup/anti-TR, bulk on Drogon so it survives one unboosted Rock Slide, and benching Kingambit against Fighting-coverage leads.

proposals.change: TURN-1 MEGA-THREAT FOCUS FIRE (code-enforced): on turn 1, if exactly one opposing active is listed as dealing >=100% max damage to our Mega-evolving slot and we can reach a combined KO on it with both actions, both actions must target that foe. Boost scores for moves aimed at it by +1.5.
proposals.evidence: T1 vs mach greninja: Mega Garchomp-Z threatened 67-121% on Mega Dragonite; Dragon Pulse + Ice Beam focus-fire removed it before it could fire a second time, and the opponent forfeited on the spot.

Default 'standard'-archetype lead is Milotic + Mega Dragonite (65% win rate), not Whimsicott + Charizard (57%).
Struggle Bug / Intimidate / any opposing stat-drop on Milotic is a gift: Competitive turns it into +2 SpA — never switch Milotic out after it gets the boost.

Sitrus Berry restores move freedom and extra bulk, which the Dragonite-lead plan values more than raw speed now that Dragonite's Tailwind covers speed control.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their sheet (Gholdengo + Volcarona + Incineroar + Rillaboom + Raichu + Mega Garchomp-Z) is the 'bulky pivots + one fast Mega nuke' shell that keeps beating us. Mirror the pivot half: give Milotic max HP / max SpD with Leftovers (already our single best performer — it tanked Struggle Bug and healed back to 96%), and test Incineroar or Amoonguss in Kingambit's slot, since Kingambit has died first with near-zero output in 3 of the last 5 games.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Mega Dragonite + Mega Charizard core needs a body that survives turns rather than a slow glass attacker; Milotic is the only piece that consistently generates value (Competitive +2 from any Intimidate/Struggle Bug) and a second bulky pivot would let the Megas enter on a clean board.

analysis.whatWorked: Focus-firing with Milotic Ice Beam + Mega Charizard Weather Ball removed Wyrdeer (the Skill Swap/TR enabler) on turn 1 and Sneasler on turn 2 — two clean KOs in two turns with zero wasted actions. Mega evolved turn 1 as required. Milotic was again our best piece (2 KOs, tanked Poison Jab + poison). Dragonite's Heat Wave finished their Whimsicott and kept chipping Swampert, and the endgame Whimsicott Moonblast cleanup sealed a win despite a +3 Bulk Up Swampert-Mega. Overall a win where we denied their Trick Room entirely (Farigiraf never came).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: no Kingambit lead into a Sneasler sheet (preview ban honored); Mega by turn 1; Whimsicott's Tailwind delayed correctly while a TR sheet threatened; focus fire instead of splitting damage. Violated: the core 'Calm Mind/Bulk Up setup must be answered with BOTH actions the turn it starts' rule — Swampert used Bulk Up on T1, T2 and T5 completely unpunished while we KO'd passive targets; and on T3 Charizard-Y attacked into an active Swampert-Mega listed at 124-201% OHKO on us instead of Protecting/switching, which is a direct breach of the '>=100% incoming from a faster foe = Protect or switch only' hard rule.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T1-T2: Swampert-Mega got two free Bulk Ups. We treated Wyrdeer/Sneasler as the win condition when the real win condition was the Mega that was visibly boosting. 2) T3: Drogon attacked (Heat Wave) with a listed 124-201% Liquidation OHKO on the board and died for 20-36% chip; the Mega was our second-best damage source and it contributed nothing after turn 2. 3) T4: Milotic at 42% stayed in against a listed 71-94% High Horsepower and died instead of switching; Whimsicott re-set a Tailwind we already had. 4) T5-T8: our Whimsicott got Encored into Tailwind and spent FOUR consecutive turns failing a move — four dead actions in the 2-action economy — because we never switched it out of the Encore. 5) We won on a coin-flip endgame vs a +3 Swampert that should never have been +3.
analysis.howToImprove: (a) Treat a foe that uses Bulk Up/Calm Mind/Coil as the primary target immediately, even over a 'free' KO on a frail support — Wyrdeer/Sneasler could have been handled one turn later. (b) Enforce the hard rule: any slot facing a listed >=100% hit from a faster foe may only Protect or switch; Drogon must have Protected or pivoted to Milotic on T3. (c) Encore/Taunt/Disable on our side: if our Pokémon is Encored into a move that FAILS (Tailwind already up), switch it out next turn — never re-click a failing move twice, let alone four times. (d) Milotic below 50% facing a listed KO should Recover or switch, not trade chip.

proposals.change: ENCORE-FAIL ESCAPE (code-enforced): if our active Pokémon is under Encore and the locked move failed last turn (e.g. Tailwind already active, Protect spam), it must switch out on the next available turn. Block the Encored move from scoring.
proposals.evidence: Orakcaj game T5-T8: Whimsicott clicked Tailwind four consecutive turns, all |-fail|, while Swampert Bulk Up'd to +3. Four dead actions.

proposals.change: SETUP-FOE PRIORITY: when a foe uses Bulk Up / Calm Mind / Coil / Iron Defense / Swords Dance, mark it as the primary target for the rest of the game; add +2.0 to moves aimed at it and refuse to spend both actions on a non-boosting foe unless that foe is a confirmed OHKO threat to our Mega this turn.
proposals.evidence: Swampert-Mega got 3 unanswered Bulk Ups (+3/+3) while we KO'd Wyrdeer and Sneasler; it then solo-KO'd Drogon, Milotic and Dragonite.

proposals.change: Reaffirm the >=100% incoming guardrail for Charizard-Y specifically: with a Water/Rock/Electric Mega active and a listed OHKO on Drogon, Drogon's only legal actions are Protect or switch.
proposals.evidence: T3 calc line: 'Drogon threatened by Swampert-Mega Wave Crash (124-201% OHKO)' — we clicked Heat Wave for 20-36% chip and lost the Mega.

proposals.change: Proceed with the Whimsicott Taunt-over-Encore test variant; Taunt would have shut down Swampert's Bulk Up chain and Farigiraf's Trick Room, both of which Encore cannot stop.
proposals.evidence: 3 of the last 5 games were decided by an unpunished self-boosting foe (Bulk Up Swampert, Calm Mind Primarina, Coil Milotic).
