lessons: A foe that uses Bulk Up/Calm Mind/Coil becomes the primary target immediately — a free KO on a frail support is worth less than denying +1/+1 per turn.
If our Pokémon is Encored into a move that already failed, switch it out; never click a failing move twice.
Charizard-Y never attacks while a faster foe has a listed >=100% hit on it — Protect or switch, no exceptions.
Milotic under 50% facing a listed KO should Recover or pivot, not trade chip damage.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 3W-9L and has produced 0 KOs in its last three appearances; Sitrus gives move freedom (Rock Slide/EQ/Dragon Claw selection) and a bulk buffer so Garchomp can actually stay in against boosted physical Megas like Swampert.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'bulky Mega sets up behind expendable support' plan: Swampert-Mega simply Bulk Up'd twice behind Wyrdeer/Sneasler bodies and then won alone. For us, run Whimsicott with Taunt over Encore (Prankster Taunt pre-empts Bulk Up/Calm Mind/Trick Room) and give Milotic max HP / max SpD with Leftovers so it survives the boosted physical phase; consider Haze or Icy Wind on the Milotic test variant to erase enemy boosts outright.
teamInspiration.reason: Our team has no answer to a foe that boosts: Encore locks them INTO boosting, and our chip damage cannot outpace +1/+1 per turn. Taunt and/or Haze are the only tools that deny the 'speed AND power' board state we keep losing to.

analysis.whatWorked: Preview call was excellent: identified that a Rock/Ice/Ground sheet (Rampardos, Mamoswine, Sneasler) hard-counters Charizard-Y and brought the Mega Dragonite + Milotic 'standard' lead instead. Milotic was the MVP (281% damage, 3 KOs) — Incineroar's Intimidate on turn 1 and again on turn 2 gave Competitive +2 SpA twice, turning Ice Beam into a 1-shot machine on Whimsicott, Mamoswine and Rampardos. Turn 2 was the game-winning turn: Heat Wave finished the 1% Whimsicott (denying Encore/Moonblast and killing their speed-control piece) while also chipping the switched-in Mamoswine, and Milotic's Ice Beam then deleted Mamoswine — a clean 2-for-1. Turn 3 Protect on Dragonite against a guaranteed Rampardos Head Smash OHKO was textbook Protect discipline and it ate a Fake Out instead. Turn 5 chose Stomping Tantrum over Earthquake so Milotic wasn't hit by the ally spread.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) 'Default standard-archetype lead is Milotic + Mega Dragonite' — followed, and it won again. (2) 'Struggle Bug/Intimidate on Milotic is a gift: never switch it out after the boost' — followed; Milotic stayed in for all 5 turns and carried. (3) 'A slot facing a listed >=100% incoming OHKO from a faster foe may ONLY Protect or switch' — followed on turn 3 with Dragonite vs Head Smash. (4) 'Never Earthquake with Garchomp while a non-Flying ally is beside it' — followed (Stomping Tantrum on turn 5). (5) 'Charizard never leads into a Rock-heavy sheet' — followed at preview. Violated/soft-missed: Whimsicott's Tailwind rule was moot (Whimsicott benched), but we conceded 3 turns of enemy Tailwind with zero of our own and still won only because Milotic snowballed. Turn 4 also ignored the lesson about not leaving a damaged Mega exposed to a Rock user.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 1: the Claude call rate-limited (HTTP 429) and the engine fallback chose Heat Wave with Dragonite into a freshly-switched-in Incineroar — it ate a Fake Out flinch, so the Mega contributed zero on turn 1 while their Whimsicott got free Tailwind. That is a wasted half-turn of the 2-action economy on the single most important turn, caused purely by the rate limit. Turn 4 was the real misplay: Rampardos was at 3% but it is faster-under-Tailwind and we KNEW Rock Slide/Head Smash OHKOs Dragonite (listed 122-211% the turn before). We clicked Dragon Pulse with Dragonite anyway instead of Protect; Dragonite died to Rock Slide (after Darkest Lariat chip) and the 3% Rampardos was going to die to Milotic's Ice Beam regardless. Milotic alone KO'd it. Lesson violated: 'a foe at 2% HP deals 100% of its damage — never leave our Mega exposed to a low-HP Rock user'. We lost our Mega for literally zero gain. Also, Dragonite never set Tailwind at any point, so the opponent held speed control the whole match.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Add a hard guardrail: when a foe with a listed >=100% hit on our slot is alive at ANY hp and our partner's move alone already guarantees the KO on it, our threatened slot must Protect/switch, not add redundant damage (turn 4 Dragonite). 2) Redundant-overkill rule: if one ally action already has >=90% KO probability on a target, the second ally must not target it — spend that action on Protect, the other foe, or Tailwind. 3) Rate-limit hardening: the engine fallback on turn 1 must respect the same opening script (Mega + the strongest non-flinchable action, or Protect vs a fresh Fake Out user). A freshly switched-in/leading Incineroar guarantees Fake Out, so Dragonite should Protect or the slot should use a move that still matters after a flinch. 4) Against enemy Tailwind we need our own: with Whimsicott benched, Dragonite's Tailwind should be clicked on a turn where its attack is redundant (turn 4 was exactly that turn).

proposals.change: REDUNDANT-OVERKILL GUARDRAIL (code-enforced): if our partner's action alone is listed at >=90% KO chance on a target, the second slot is blocked from targeting that same foe and must instead Protect, set Tailwind, or hit the other foe. Especially when the second slot is our Mega and a Rock/Ice attacker is alive.
proposals.evidence: Turn 4: Milotic Ice Beam was 58-118% KO on a 3% Rampardos; Dragonite still fired Dragon Pulse at it and died to Rock Slide. Protect or Tailwind there keeps the Mega and we win 4-0.

proposals.change: LOW-HP ROCK USER RULE (code-enforced): while any foe with a Rock-type attack is alive on the field, our Mega Dragonite/Charizard slot may only Protect, switch, or use a move that guarantees the KO on that Rock user itself. HP of the Rock user is irrelevant.
proposals.evidence: Rampardos at 3% HP Rock Slide'd Dragonite to death on turn 4; the same rule was previously written after Golurk at 2% KO'd Charizard.

proposals.change: FALLBACK OPENING SCRIPT: when the Claude call fails on turn 1 and a lead Incineroar/Rillaboom/Infernape is present, the fallback must Mega-evolve and Protect the Mega slot (Fake Out is guaranteed) rather than clicking an attack that gets flinched.
proposals.evidence: T1 fallback Heat Wave was flinched by Incineroar Fake Out: zero output, opponent got a free Tailwind.

proposals.change: Keep Milotic as a mandatory bring in every standard matchup and consider max HP / max SpD with Leftovers — it has now been top damage dealer in 3 of the last 4 games thanks to Competitive.
proposals.evidence: 281% damage and 3 KOs this game off two free Intimidate/Parting Shot boosts.

lessons: If one ally action already has a >=90% listed KO on a target, the second ally must NOT also target it — Protect, set Tailwind, or hit the other foe instead.
A foe holding any Rock-type move, even at 3% HP, forbids our Mega from attacking a different target: Protect or kill the Rock user.
When the Claude call rate-limits on turn 1 against a lead Incineroar/Rillaboom, the fallback must Protect the Mega slot — Fake Out is guaranteed.
With Whimsicott benched, Dragonite's Tailwind must be clicked on the first turn its attack would be redundant; conceding 3 enemy Tailwind turns with 0 of our own nearly lost a won game.
Milotic with Competitive is our best engine vs Intimidate/Parting Shot teams — never switch it out after the boost, and bring it in every standard matchup.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep the current loadout: Garchomp only entered on turn 5 this game, so there is no new evidence against Scarf. Changing items now would add noise to the already-small 13-game sample.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Fake Out + Parting Shot pivot into a nuke' structure: Incineroar's double Intimidate plus Parting Shot is what repeatedly fed our Milotic, so the mirror lesson is to maximize the Competitive engine — run Milotic at max HP / max SpD with Leftovers and consider Haze or Icy Wind over Protect on a test variant so Milotic also answers boosters. Also give Mega Dragonite a bulk-leaning spread (enough HP to survive one unboosted Rock Slide after Fake Out chip) since it has now died to Rock Slide twice while at >50% HP.
teamInspiration.reason: Milotic is our single most productive piece (281% damage, 3 KOs this game) and only needs survivability, while Mega Dragonite keeps dying to chip + Rock coverage before it can set Tailwind or cash in its damage.

change: LETHAL-RANGE GUARDRAIL: extend the existing '>=100% incoming OHKO' rule — if the TOP of a faster foe's listed damage range meets or exceeds our slot's CURRENT HP (including Life Orb recoil we are about to take), that slot may only Protect or switch.
evidence: T2 Kingambit at 109/207 clicked Kowtow Cleave (recoil to 89) into a listed Excadrill High Horsepower 62-91% and fainted; the listed range was never '>=100%' so the old guardrail did not fire.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead vs a Trick Room / Expanding Force sheet (Mimikyu, Armarouge) was correct: Iron Head broke Disguise and KO'd Mimikyu turn 1, denying Trick Room entirely. Mega Charizard-Y evolved turn 1 and became the engine of the game (225% damage, 2 KOs) — Weather Ball OHKO'd Golisopod and Ancient Power, after its own Omniboost proc, cleaned up Armarouge, the Armor Cannon/Trick Room piece. Our focus-fire discipline on the TR setters was textbook, and the Encore onto Dragalge-Mega's Haze on turn 5 neutralized a Draco Meteor that was otherwise an OHKO on everything we had left.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: 'focus-fire the Trick Room setter the turn it lands' (Mimikyu and Armarouge both removed early); 'Kingambit leads vs Psychic/TR sheets'; 'don't Protect-stall a booster'; Whimsicott Protect on turn 4 when Armor Cannon was a listed OHKO. Violated: the Wide Guard lesson — Garchomp fired a spread Earthquake on turn 3 into an Armarouge that had every reason to Wide Guard, wasting half the turn's action economy and leaving Garchomp alive to eat Draco Meteor. Also violated the '>=100% incoming OHKO means Protect or switch' rule: the calc explicitly listed Dragalge Draco Meteor 104-186% OHKO on Garchomp and we still clicked an attack rather than switching Garchomp out or protecting.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 3 Garchomp Earthquake into Wide Guard: a known Armarouge move, a spread move into a double-Wide-Guard board, and the one action that could have mattered (switching Garchomp away from a listed OHKO Draco Meteor) was skipped. Garchomp died with 0 damage dealt. 2) Turn 1 Heat Wave into Mimikyu was functionally wasted — Disguise absorbed it and Golisopod Protected, so the Mega's whole turn produced 13%. Weather Ball on Golisopod (or simply attacking the non-Disguise slot) was better value. 3) Kingambit was lost turn 2 to Armor Cannon despite the calc listing 181-272% OHKO — this is the third game in five where Kingambit dies early; the board showed a faster Armarouge, so Kingambit should have Protected or switched while Drogon handled the KO. 4) Final turn: we had a 2v1 with Drogon at full power and an Encored Dragalge; the game was reported as a loss despite a winning board, meaning the closing line (Encore again + chip Heat Wave, 17-25%) was far too slow — Weather Ball/Heat Wave chip could not outpace the clock and Dragalge eventually broke out of Encore.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block spread moves (Earthquake, Heat Wave, Rock Slide) against any foe that has already used Wide Guard this game or whose sheet lists it. Enforce the existing >=100%-incoming rule as a switch, not just a Protect: if a foe on the field has a listed OHKO on our active and that active is not the piece that must stay, switch it. Never attack a fresh Disguise Mimikyu with the Mega's spread move — break Disguise with the physical slot and spend the Mega's action on the other foe. In a 2v1 with a crippled/Encored foe, stop re-Encoring and commit both actions to the KO: a 17-25% chip line surrenders the clock. Kingambit must Protect or switch on any turn a faster Fire/Fighting special attacker is active with a listed OHKO.

proposals.change: WIDE GUARD MEMORY (code-enforced): once a foe uses Wide Guard, or its revealed sheet lists Wide Guard, block all spread moves (Earthquake, Heat Wave, Rock Slide, Dazzling Gleam, Blizzard) from our side while that foe is active. Use single-target moves instead.
proposals.evidence: T3: Garchomp Earthquake fully blocked by Armarouge Wide Guard; Garchomp then died to Draco Meteor having dealt 0 damage.

proposals.change: OHKO-SWITCH ENFORCEMENT: when the calc lists a >=100% incoming hit on our active from a foe that moves first, and that active is NOT our last usable piece, the legal actions are Protect or switch only — attacking must be blocked, not merely penalized.
proposals.evidence: T2 Kingambit (Armor Cannon 181-272% listed) attacked and died; T3 Garchomp (Draco Meteor 104-186% listed) attacked and died.

proposals.change: DISGUISE RULE: against a fresh Mimikyu, the Mega's action must target the OTHER foe; break Disguise with the physical/secondary slot only.
proposals.evidence: T1 Drogon Heat Wave did 13% into Disguise while Golisopod Protected — a wasted Mega turn.

proposals.change: CLOSING RULE: in a 1v2 or 2v1 where we are ahead, do not spend an action re-applying Encore/status on an already-crippled foe; commit both actions to the highest-damage KO line. Chip under 30% per turn against a healing/recovering foe is a losing clock.
proposals.evidence: T5-6: double Encore + 17-25% Heat Wave chip against Encored Dragalge-Mega allowed the game to slip away from a winning 2v1 board.

proposals.change: Keep Kingambit benched against any sheet with Armarouge, Kommo-o, Sneasler, or Raichu-Mega-Y; prefer Milotic in that slot (Competitive + bulk) given Kingambit has died first with minimal output in 4 of the last 6 games.
proposals.evidence: T2 Kingambit died to Armor Cannon with 87% total damage dealt; stats show Kingambit 85 faints / 61 KOs.

lessons: After any foe uses Wide Guard, never click a spread move (Earthquake/Heat Wave/Rock Slide) while that foe is on the field — switch to single-target damage.
A listed >=100% incoming OHKO from a faster foe means Protect or SWITCH; attacking anyway has now cost us Kingambit and Garchomp in the same game.
Never spend the Mega's turn attacking a fresh Mimikyu — Disguise eats it; break Disguise with the other slot and aim the Mega at the partner.
When ahead 2v1 against a crippled foe, stop re-applying Encore and commit both actions to damage; sub-30% chip per turn loses the clock.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is locked into spread Earthquake exactly when Wide Guard/levitating foes appear and has nothing to do; Sitrus gives it the flexibility to pivot moves and survive one Draco Meteor-class hit, which would have kept it alive on turn 3.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Disguise/Protect fodder + Wide Guard pivot + one nuke' structure: Armarouge with Wide Guard single-handedly blanked our spread damage while Armor Cannon one-shot our slow attacker. For us, replace Kingambit with Milotic as a mandatory bring (max HP / max SpD, Leftovers) and consider adding Wide Guard coverage of our own, or at minimum shift Garchomp to Dragon Claw/Stomping Tantrum priority over Earthquake when any Wide Guard user is revealed.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Megas are both spread-damage dependent (Heat Wave, Earthquake support), so a single Wide Guard user erases half our offense; a bulky special wall like Milotic keeps generating value regardless of terrain, weather, or Wide Guard.

analysis.whatWorked: Milotic was again the MVP engine (124% damage, 2 KOs including the Tinkaton and Talonflame finishes) and the Milotic + Mega Dragonite 'standard' lead held up. Turn 3-5 cleanup was clean: Scald removed the +2 Tinkaton before it could Play Rough again, Heat Wave removed Sableye, and Scarf Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum guaranteed the Sneasler KO on the closing turn without clipping Milotic (correctly avoided Earthquake). We won 6-4 on the board in 5 turns.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed the 'default standard lead = Milotic + Mega Dragonite' rule. Correctly used Stomping Tantrum instead of Earthquake with an ally in the Ground-hit slot. Correctly Protected Milotic on turn 2 against the +2 Play Rough. Did NOT switch Milotic out after it started accumulating value. However the big durable lesson 'a slot facing a listed >=100% incoming OHKO may ONLY Protect or switch' was VIOLATED on turn 2: Mega Dragonite at 16/168 HP (9%) attacked into a board where Sableye's Shadow Sneak (priority, +1) was a guaranteed kill, and it died with zero damage dealt that turn.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1: Swagger on Tinkaton gave it +2 Atk and Play Rough took Mega Dragonite from 100% to 9% through Multiscale — we never considered that Sableye (Prankster) would boost its own partner rather than status us, and we spent the Mega's Heat Wave as a spread chip instead of either Protecting the Multiscale or focusing Tinkaton down. 2) Turn 2 was the real misplay: Dragonite at 9% HP with a priority Shadow Sneak user on the field clicked Heat Wave. Any Shadow Sneak/Sucker Punch/Fake Out kills it. The correct line was Protect Dragonite (it had Protect) and attack with Milotic, or switch Dragonite out. Instead we Protected the HEALTHY Milotic and attacked with the 9% Mega — the protection was on the wrong slot. That cost our Mega for free. 3) Turns 3 and 4 were engine fallbacks (2 of 6 Claude calls failed), and the fallback let Drogon eat a Knock Off (losing its item) and then a Dire Claw KO on turn 4 while at 46% in front of a fresh Sneasler — a slot at 46% in front of Sneasler must Protect or switch. 4) We never set Tailwind at all (0 turns both sides) despite Dragonite having it; with Whimsicott benched, Dragonite's Tailwind turn never came.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-codify the 'lowest-HP slot gets the Protect' rule: when one of our actives is below ~25% HP and ANY living foe has a priority move (Shadow Sneak, Sucker Punch, Extreme Speed, Aqua Jet, Fake Out, Grassy Glide), that slot may only Protect or switch — never attack. Also treat opposing Swagger/Flatter/Decorate on their OWN partner as a setup event: the boosted partner becomes the focus-fire target immediately (we got that right on turn 3 but a turn late). Against a fresh Sneasler, any of our slots under 60% must Protect or switch (Dire Claw/Close Combat are effectively OHKOs on Charizard). Finally, strengthen the turn-1 fallback so it Protects the Mega slot, not an attack, whenever a priority user is on the board.

proposals.change: PRIORITY-RANGE PROTECT RULE (code-enforced): if any of our actives is at or below 25% HP and any living foe has a revealed or sheet-listed priority attack (Shadow Sneak, Sucker Punch, Extreme Speed, Aqua Jet, Grassy Glide, Fake Out, Ice Shard, Bullet Punch, First Impression, Mach Punch), that slot's only legal actions are Protect or switch. Attacking must be blocked.
proposals.evidence: T2: Mega Dragonite at 16/168 (9%) clicked Heat Wave; Sableye's Shadow Sneak KO'd it before it moved, while the healthy Milotic was the one that Protected. Our Mega died with 0 damage that turn.

proposals.change: ALLY-BOOST (Swagger/Flatter/Decorate/Helping Hand) TRIGGER: when a foe boosts its PARTNER's attack, the boosted partner becomes the mandatory focus-fire target with both actions on the following turn.
proposals.evidence: T1 Sableye Swagger gave Tinkaton +2 Atk; the resulting Play Rough took Mega Dragonite from 100% to 9% through Multiscale and effectively ended the Mega.

proposals.change: FRESH SNEASLER RULE: while a Sneasler is active and healthy, any of our slots at or below 60% HP that it outspeeds may only Protect or switch (Dire Claw / Close Combat / Poison Jab are near-guaranteed KOs on Charizard, Whimsicott, Garchomp and weakened Milotic).
proposals.evidence: T4: Drogon at 46% attacked into a freshly switched-in Sneasler and was KO'd by Dire Claw without dealing damage.

proposals.change: TAILWIND-WITH-DRAGONITE RULE: when Whimsicott is not in the back four, Dragonite must click Tailwind on the first turn its attack is not the deciding KO. 0 Tailwind turns in a 5-turn game is a wasted resource.
proposals.evidence: Tailwind turns: us 0, them 0. Dragonite had Tailwind and used Heat Wave twice before dying on turn 2.

lessons: If one of our actives is at or below 25% HP and any living foe has a priority attack, that slot only Protects or switches — the Protect goes on the LOW-HP slot, not the healthy one.
When a foe uses Swagger/Flatter/Decorate on its own partner, that boosted partner becomes the focus-fire target with both of our actions next turn.
Against a fresh Sneasler, our slots under 60% HP that it outspeeds must Protect or switch; Dire Claw and Close Combat are effective OHKOs.
With Whimsicott benched, Dragonite must click Tailwind on the first turn its attack is not the deciding KO — 0 Tailwind turns is a wasted resource.

Multiscale is not bulk: a single +2 physical Fairy/Ice/Rock hit takes Mega Dragonite from 100% to single digits, so Protect it on turn 1 whenever a boosted or super-effective physical attacker is faster.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again delivered the guaranteed closing KO (Stomping Tantrum OHKO on Sneasler at 100%). Keep the variant for more sample; the loss cause this game was piloting (attacking at 9% HP into priority), not the item.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Prankster support boosts the real attacker' idea: run Whimsicott with Helping Hand or Taunt over Encore on a test variant, and give Mega Dragonite a bulk-leaning spread (enough HP/Def to survive one +2 Play Rough or an unboosted Rock Slide after Multiscale breaks). Keep Milotic at max HP / max SpD with Leftovers as the mandatory bring.
teamInspiration.reason: Sableye's Swagger turned a mediocre Tinkaton into an instant Mega-killer for one action, while our Mega Dragonite keeps dying to a single boosted physical hit before cashing in its damage or setting Tailwind. A bulk-leaning Dragonite spread plus a proactive Prankster support move (Taunt to deny Swagger/Trick Room, or Helping Hand to turn our own hit into a KO) converts the same action economy in our favour.

analysis.whatWorked: Whimsicott (Focus Sash + Prankster) once again carried the endgame, scoring 2 KOs (Alcremie, Kleavor) from a 1v2 position. Scald picking off the switched-in Inteleon was fine value. Recognizing on T3/T4 that +2/+2 Mega Ampharos was the single win condition and focus-firing it was the correct macro read, even if they Protected/switched around it.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Mega was committed turn 1 and Tailwind went up (3 turns) which followed the 'Dragonite must click Tailwind' rule. Focus-fire-the-win-condition rule was obeyed on T3/T4. However, the 'a foe that boosts becomes the mandatory focus-fire target IMMEDIATELY' rule was violated on turn 2 — Alcremie had already used Decorate on turn 1 giving Ampharos +2 Atk/+2 SpA, and we did NOT commit both actions to Ampharos nor protect against it. The existing ALLY-BOOST (Decorate) proposal literally names this exact scenario and it was ignored by the pilot.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 1: the listed threat line showed Alcremie Alluring Voice 80-96% on Dragonite and Ampharos Thunderbolt 49-62% on Milotic — but neither slot was protected and we clicked Tailwind + a 20-36% chip. Decorate then made Ampharos a +2/+2 nuke. Turn 2 was the game-losing turn: the calc explicitly listed 'Milotic threatened by Ampharos-Mega Parabolic Charge (66-86% KO)' and 'Dragonite threatened by Ampharos-Mega Dragon Pulse (130-221% KO)' — a listed >=100% OHKO on Dragonite from a faster foe — and we attacked with BOTH slots anyway. One spread Parabolic Charge then KO'd BOTH our Pokémon at once (Milotic was already at 64/202 from T1, Dragonite 63/168). That is a 2-for-0 wipe and the entire game. Neither Protect nor a switch was used despite the OHKO-SWITCH ENFORCEMENT proposal being active. Also: Heat Wave into a Mega Ampharos for 9-10% was a wasted action; Dragon Pulse (super-effective-ish) or Protect was strictly better. T3 double-targeted into an obvious Protect from a foe we had just threatened twice.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Treat Decorate/Swagger/Flatter/Helping Hand on the opposing side as an immediate alarm: the boosted foe is now a two-slot OHKO threat and at least one of our slots must Protect or pivot the following turn. 2) HARD RULE: if the calc lists an incoming >=100% OHKO on one of our actives from a faster foe, that slot may ONLY Protect or switch — this has now cost us Dragonite, Garchomp and Kingambit across three games and must be code-blocked, not merely penalized. 3) SPREAD-KO AWARENESS: when both of our actives are below ~45% HP and the opponent has a revealed spread move (Parabolic Charge, Heat Wave, Earthquake, Dazzling Gleam, Hyper Voice), split the risk — Protect one slot or switch one out, never leave both in range of one spread. 4) Never fire a 9-10% chip move; if the best damage line is under ~15%, Protect, switch, or set up instead.

proposals.change: SPREAD-WIPE GUARD (code-enforced): if BOTH of our actives are at or below 50% HP and any living foe has a revealed or sheet-listed spread move (Parabolic Charge, Heat Wave, Earthquake, Hyper Voice, Dazzling Gleam, Blizzard, Rock Slide, Make It Rain, Muddy Water, Surf, Discharge, Expanding Force), at least one of our actions must be Protect or a switch. Attacking with both slots is blocked.
proposals.evidence: T2 vs Ifiwinidiehelp: Milotic at 64/202 and Dragonite at 63/168 both attacked; one +2 Parabolic Charge KO'd both simultaneously and ended the game 4v2 down.

proposals.change: DECORATE/ALLY-BOOST ALARM: the turn after a foe uses Decorate/Swagger/Flatter/Helping Hand on its partner, the boosted foe is treated as an automatic OHKO threat to every slot it outspeeds — those slots may only Protect, switch, or must focus-fire the boosted foe with BOTH actions.
proposals.evidence: Alcremie Decorate on T1 gave Ampharos +2/+2; we neither protected nor focus-fired on T2 and lost two Pokémon to it in one move.

proposals.change: LOW-VALUE ATTACK BLOCK: never click an attack whose listed max damage is below 15% when a Protect, switch, or support move is legal.
proposals.evidence: T2 Dragonite Heat Wave listed 9-10% on Mega Ampharos — a completely wasted action on the turn we were wiped.

lessons: When a foe uses Decorate/Swagger/Flatter on its partner, the boosted partner is an instant OHKO threat: the next turn at least one of our slots must Protect or switch, or both actions must focus-fire it.
If both of our actives are below ~50% HP and any foe has a spread move, never attack with both slots — one spread move can take two Pokémon and end the game.
A listed >=100% incoming OHKO from a faster foe is a hard Protect-or-switch order, with no exception for 'our attack might KO first'.
Never click an attack whose listed maximum damage is under 15%; Protect, pivot, or use a support move instead.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 7-10 and keeps dying without acting; Sitrus gives Garchomp a survival buffer against X-Scissor/chip and allows move flexibility (Dragon Claw vs Ghost-immune switch-ins like Alcremie cost us a whole action this game).

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'one spread nuke that drains and heals' engine: Mega Ampharos Parabolic Charge + Decorate wiped two Pokémon in one action. For us, give Mega Dragonite a bulk-leaning spread (enough HP/SpD to eat one +2 neutral special spread move after Multiscale) and strongly consider running Milotic at max HP/max SpD with Leftovers plus Haze over Protect on a test variant — Haze is the only tool we have that answers Decorate/Calm Mind/Bulk Up boards, which have now lost us four games.
teamInspiration.reason: Our team has zero stat-reset tools; Encore locks a booster into boosting and chip damage can't outpace +2/+2. A single Haze on bulky Milotic would have neutralized Decorate, Calm Mind Primarina, and Bulk Up Swampert in the last five losses.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Protect on Mega Dragonite vs Aerodactyl Dual Wingbeat was correct and preserved Multiscale; Whimsicott got Tailwind up. Dragon Pulse put Aerodactyl to 1% and Moonblast finished it on T3. Kingambit's Iron Head cleanly OHKO'd Grimmsnarl. Garchomp Earthquake chipped Milotic.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Protect-the-Mega-vs-faster-OHKO rule was followed on T1-T3. The 'don't double-target the same foe when one action already KOs' rule was respected. However the big durable rule — 'if one foe is the only piece that outspeeds and OHKOs our Mega, spend both actions removing it' — was violated on T6: Kingambit Iron Head was aimed at a FRESH Floette that had just switched in, while Dragonite used Tailwind instead of attacking or Protecting, and Floette Mega-evolved and Dazzling Gleam'd both our slots for a double KO.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T4 was a wolfe-fallback (no Claude call) that wasted the turn: Kingambit got Fake Out flinched after Icy Wind, Dragonite only chipped Milotic. 2) T6 is the losing turn: a fresh Floette-Eternal entered. Floette-Eternal ALWAYS Mega-evolves into a Fairy Aura spread Dazzling Gleam nuke — our own knowledge file flags it as a 'two-for-one team-wipe risk'. We clicked Tailwind with Dragonite at 30% HP (listed Moonblast 54-94% KO on it) and Iron Head on Floette assuming we move first; Floette-Mega outspeeds base-Speed Kingambit and Dazzling Gleam killed Dragonite and left Kingambit at 5%, then Milotic Scald finished it. Dragonite at 30% facing a listed >=90% special spread KO must Protect or switch, never set Tailwind. 3) Tailwind was clicked at 2 of our 4 Pokemon alive with only Garchomp (Scarf, already fast) behind — zero value. 4) Whimsicott was chipped to death by repeated Icy Wind while Protecting; we never switched it out after it had delivered Tailwind. 5) Garchomp T7 Earthquake into an obvious Floette Protect.
analysis.howToImprove: Treat any incoming Floette-Eternal as an immediate Mega + Fairy Aura Dazzling Gleam OHKO threat to BOTH slots: the turn it enters, every slot of ours below ~60% HP must Protect or switch, and we should focus-fire it with the slot that actually outspeeds (Scarf Garchomp / Charizard), not slow Kingambit. Never click Tailwind with a Pokemon that is listed as being KO'd this turn, and never click Tailwind when only 2 of our mons remain and the back one already has a Choice Scarf. Also: after a foe spams Protect (Floette T7), spread into the partner only or switch.

proposals.change: FLOETTE-ETERNAL / FAIRY-AURA ALARM (code-enforced): the turn a Floette-Eternal (or any Fairy-Aura spread attacker) switches in or is active unevolved, treat Dazzling Gleam as a double-slot OHKO. Any of our actives at or below 60% HP may only Protect or switch; the attacking slot must be one that outspeeds it.
proposals.evidence: T6: fresh Floette entered, Mega-evolved, and Dazzling Gleam KO'd Dragonite (30%) and left Kingambit at 5% in one action, losing the game from a 2-2 even board.

proposals.change: TAILWIND VALUE GATE (code-enforced): block Tailwind if (a) the user is listed as taking a >=80% hit this turn, or (b) we have <=2 living Pokemon and the bench mon holds a Choice Scarf, or (c) Tailwind is already active on our side.
proposals.evidence: T6 Dragonite at 30% clicked Tailwind into a listed 54-94% Moonblast/Dazzling Gleam and died without the Tailwind ever being used; only Scarf Garchomp remained.

proposals.change: POST-TAILWIND WHIMSICOTT PIVOT: once Whimsicott has set Tailwind and is under 50% HP with a repeated chip move (Icy Wind/spread) incoming, switch it out rather than Protect-cycling.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott Protected twice, still died to Icy Wind spread chip on T3 having dealt 1% damage.

lessons: A fresh Floette-Eternal on the field is an automatic Mega + Fairy Aura Dazzling Gleam double-KO threat: every slot of ours under 60% HP must Protect or switch that turn, and only a slot that outspeeds it may attack.
Never click Tailwind with a Pokemon that has a listed >=80% incoming hit this turn — set it with a healthy slot or not at all.
Tailwind has no value when only Choice Scarf Garchomp remains in the back; attack or Protect instead.
Slow Kingambit must not be the designated 'KO it before it moves' answer to a fresh fast Fairy — use Garchomp/Charizard or Sucker Punch timing instead.
After a foe Protects on the previous turn with its partner threatened, aim spread damage at the partner or switch, don't repeat the same spread into the same Protect slot.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is locked into one move and contributed 42% damage in 2 turns; Sitrus gives move freedom (Rock Slide vs Floette/Aerodactyl, EQ vs Milotic) and survivability against Ice Beam chip, and our losses are coming from fragility not speed.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'cheap speed control + chip spread + one Fairy-Aura nuke' structure: Milotic Icy Wind was the real MVP (speed drops + 4 turns of free chip that killed Whimsicott). Add Icy Wind to our Milotic over Protect on a test variant and give Mega Dragonite a bulk-leaning HP/SpD spread so it survives one unboosted Dazzling Gleam at 50% HP.
teamInspiration.reason: Their Milotic generated value every single turn with no prediction required, while our Milotic/Whimsicott were forced into pure Protect loops; Icy Wind would let us both chip and deny speed without committing our Mega's turn.

whatWorked: Kingambit lead vs a psyterrain/Indeedee-listed team was correct in principle (immune to Expanding Force/Psychic, Dark hits Armarouge's Psychic side). Whimsicott Moonblast was the engine of the game: it chipped Dragapult to 17%, pushed Grimmsnarl to 12%, and then one-shot the switched-in Baxcalibur, which was the opponent's biggest physical threat. Kingambit's Protect on T3 correctly dodged Armor Cannon/Aura Sphere, and the T4 pivot out of a burned Kingambit into Drogon rather than trading was textbook 'switch when the slot is about to be KO'd'. We also avoided Sucker Punch entirely in a Psychic-Terrain-capable matchup, honoring the anti-priority rule. Opponent forfeited at 4-0 up on KO count, so the win is real but hollow.
lessonsApplied: Followed: no Sucker Punch into a terrain/priority-blocker team; Protect used only on a slot with a listed >=100% incoming hit (Kingambit T3); switched the burned Kingambit out instead of attacking into a guaranteed KO; never set Tailwind into a Trick Room threat. Violated/Ignored: (1) The Tailwind-value rule — Whimsicott was on the field for four turns, was never under a listed OHKO on T1, and never clicked Tailwind; we ended with 0 Tailwind turns again. (2) Our Mega was never used until T5 and the game logged 'Our Mega evolved: no' in the summary, meaning our single most important resource sat in the back for the whole game. (3) We allowed Grimmsnarl to set Reflect on T1 and Parting Shot twice, dropping Whimsicott to -2/-2 — no Taunt/Encore pressure was ever applied to the Prankster support.
whatFailed: Three concrete errors. First, T1: we clicked Iron Head into Grimmsnarl (listed 101-137% OHKO) but it only did 51% because Reflect went up first — the damage model did not account for a screens setter moving first, so we burned the turn and got Will-O-Wisp'd. Second, Whimsicott never set Tailwind: on T1 the only listed threat to it was Dragapult Shadow Ball (46-89%, not an OHKO) and Focus Sash covers it, so Tailwind was free and would have given us 3-4 turns of guaranteed first-strike against a Dragapult/Armarouge team. Third, we let Whimsicott eat two Parting Shots (-2 Atk/-2 SpA) without ever Encoring or Taunting Grimmsnarl; after the second one our only damage source was crippled. We also wasted the T2 Kowtow Cleave into an obvious Dragapult Protect (it was at 17% and visibly threatened — the exact 'never attack into an obvious Protect' case), and T5's Weather Ball was listed at 0-0% damage, a sub-15% attack that should have been blocked.
howToImprove: 1) Screens awareness: when the foe has a Prankster/fast Reflect or Light Screen user on the field, discount all our physical KO calcs by ~40% before committing a 'guaranteed KO' turn. 2) Tailwind discipline: Whimsicott must click Tailwind on turn 1 unless it faces a listed >=90% incoming hit; Focus Sash guarantees it survives one hit, so the opportunity cost is near zero. 3) Prankster-support denial: against Grimmsnarl/Sableye/Thundurus, use Encore or Taunt on the support slot the turn after it reveals a status move rather than letting Parting Shot farm our attacker's stats. 4) Protect-read discipline: a foe at <=20% HP that is clearly our target and has Protect available should be treated as ~60% to Protect — aim the second action elsewhere or switch the attacker. 5) Never click an attack whose listed damage is 0%.
lessons: When an opposing Reflect/Light Screen user is on the field or likely to move first, treat every physical KO calculation as ~40% lower — do not commit a 'guaranteed KO' turn into unscreened math.
Whimsicott with Focus Sash must click Tailwind on turn 1 unless it faces a listed >=90% incoming hit; it survives any single hit, so the turn is nearly free.
Against Grimmsnarl/Sableye/Thundurus-style Prankster support, Encore or Taunt the support slot as soon as it reveals a status move — two Parting Shots crippled our only damage dealer this game.
A foe at <=20% HP that is our obvious focus target should be assumed to Protect: send the second action at its partner or switch the attacker instead of clicking into the shield.

proposals.change: SCREENS DISCOUNT RULE: while an opposing Reflect/Light Screen user is active (Grimmsnarl, Sableye, Klefki, Indeedee, Alcremie) and screens are not yet up, reduce confidence in all physical OHKO calls by 40% and prefer the action that still has value if the KO fails (Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, or a switch).
proposals.evidence: T1 Iron Head was listed as a 101-137% OHKO on Grimmsnarl but Reflect resolved first and it dealt 51% — the turn produced nothing while we ate Will-O-Wisp.

proposals.change: TURN-1 TAILWIND MANDATE (code-enforced): if Whimsicott is active on turn 1 at full HP with Focus Sash and no listed incoming hit >=90%, Tailwind is forced over Moonblast/Encore.
proposals.evidence: 0 Tailwind turns again in a 5-turn game; Whimsicott was never under an OHKO threat on T1 and had three safe turns to set it.

proposals.change: PRANKSTER-SUPPORT DENIAL: after any foe uses Parting Shot / Reflect / Light Screen / Will-O-Wisp, our Whimsicott must Encore or Taunt that foe on the next turn it is legal, rather than clicking Moonblast at a different target.
proposals.evidence: Grimmsnarl used Reflect then two Parting Shots, dropping Whimsicott to -2/-2 and gutting our only offense; we never once contested it.

itemExperiment.reason: Kingambit was neutralized by Will-O-Wisp and Parting Shot chains this game; Clear Amulet blocks the stat drops from Parting Shot/Intimidate-style pressure and keeps our slow attacker relevant against Grimmsnarl/Sableye support cores (Defiant rarely triggered anyway in these matchups since they use Parting Shot on Whimsicott instead).

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Prankster screens + Parting Shot pivot + Will-O-Wisp' structure: add Taunt to Whimsicott over Protect on a test variant and shift Kingambit to a Lum Berry or Clear Amulet so a single Will-O-Wisp doesn't delete our physical win condition. Keep Charizard-Y as the Mega when Armarouge/Baxcalibur are on the sheet (Heat Wave in sun OHKOs both).
teamInspiration.reason: Their whole game plan was free, prediction-less value: Reflect halved our Iron Head, Will-O-Wisp halved our Attack, and two Parting Shots halved Whimsicott's Moonblast — none of which required a read. Taunt on Prankster would have shut all three off for one action, and burn-proofing Kingambit removes the single move that invalidates our slow attacker.

analysis.whatWorked: Protecting Dragonite on turn 2 and pivoting it out on turn 3 correctly denied Archaludon's Dragon Pulse KO twice, and Whimsicott got Tailwind up while keeping its Sash. Garchomp's Dragon Claw cleanly removed Pelipper on turn 5.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The >=100% incoming OHKO = Protect/switch rule was followed on turns 2-3. The Tailwind value gate was respected (set with a healthy Sash Whimsicott). However the 'Prankster-support denial' proposal was violated: Grimmsnarl used Light Screen on turn 1 and Parting Shot repeatedly and was never Encored or Taunted, and the 'burst Archaludon in one turn, never chip it' rain rule was violated across the entire game.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1 fallback fired Dragon Pulse into Archaludon THROUGH Light Screen and gave it a free Stamina +1 Def — every subsequent Dragon Pulse (3 more) also fed Stamina, a pure negative action economy loop. We hit Archaludon five separate times and never came close to KOing it while it climbed to +2 SpA/+3 Def. 2) Turn 4 we split damage onto Pelipper while a +1 SpA Archaludon behind Light Screen was the actual win condition; Kingambit at 100/207 clicked an attack into a listed 65-97% KO instead of Protecting/switching, and Whimsicott (which dies to anything) attacked instead of Protecting — we lost both slots in one turn. 3) Zero Encore on Archaludon after it revealed Electro Shot, which would have locked it out of the boost loop. 4) Tailwind was spent while we had no damage output on board.
analysis.howToImprove: Against Archaludon: never click a single-hit chip move at it — it has Stamina and heals (Leftovers/rain). Either Encore it into Electro Shot/Protect with Whimsicott, or ignore it entirely and remove the support/rain setter while keeping our pieces alive, or double-target it in ONE turn for a real KO. Any of our actives listed as taking >=65% from a boosted foe must Protect or switch, never trade. And once Archaludon has +1 or more SpA behind screens, switch to a stall/attrition plan: Protect-cycle Whimsicott, keep Dragonite out of Dragon Pulse range, and win on the other two slots.

proposals.change: STAMINA/BOOST-LOOP BLOCK: never click a single-target attack at Archaludon (or any Stamina user) unless the listed damage is >=85% or both of our actions are aimed at it the same turn. Chip damage feeds Stamina and is strictly negative.
proposals.evidence: We hit Archaludon with Dragon Pulse 4x (33%,23%,...) each time granting +1 Def plus Leftovers/heal, and it ended the game at 40% having KO'd three of our Pokemon.

proposals.change: ENCORE MANDATE vs boosting foes: if a foe has used Electro Shot / Calm Mind / Iron Defense / Decorate and Whimsicott is alive and the foe is not Dark, Encore is forced over Moonblast/Protect on the next legal turn.
proposals.evidence: Archaludon used Electro Shot turn 3 and was free to use it again turn 4; Encore would have locked it into a 0-damage-to-us loop or into Protect.

proposals.change: NO-TRADE RULE AT LOW HP: any of our actives below 55% max HP facing a listed >=60% incoming hit may only Protect or switch, even if its attack is part of a focus-fire plan.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit at 48% attacked Pelipper into a listed 65-97% Electro Shot and died without KOing anything.

lessons: Archaludon has Stamina: every chip hit makes it bulkier — only attack it with a one-turn double-target burst or not at all.
When a foe is boosting behind screens, Whimsicott's Encore is worth more than Moonblast or Protect — use it the turn after the boost move is revealed.
Do not split damage onto the rain setter while the boosted sweeper is the actual win condition; remove the win condition or stall it, not both halfway.

itemExperiment.reason: Rain/Archaludon games need an immediate revenge-KO speed tier; Scarf Garchomp remains the only piece that can outspeed and threaten boosted sweepers before they fire.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'screens + Parting Shot + one self-boosting bulky sweeper' engine: add Taunt or Haze to a test Milotic/Whimsicott variant so a single action undoes Light Screen/Parting Shot/Electro Shot, and consider Milotic max HP/SpD with Haze over Protect as a mandatory bring in rain matchups.
teamInspiration.reason: Archaludon's Stamina + Electro Shot + Light Screen gave them a prediction-free snowball that our purely offensive team literally cannot break; we have zero stat-reset or screen-removal tools, which has now lost multiple rain games.

analysis.whatWorked: Won 2-0 in Pokémon count vs swampflower1's rain/TR-flavoured team. Turn 1 Kingambit lead was correct: it is immune to Expanding Force/Psychic and Kowtow Cleave ignores Protect, and Charizard's Drought immediately overwrote the incoming rain and let Heat Wave chip Sceptile + burn Pelipper. Recognising Dragapult's Phantom Force semi-invulnerable turn (T4) and redirecting both actions onto Sceptile was a clean, textbook action-economy save and got the KO. T3 switching Kingambit out at 26% instead of letting it eat Earth Power preserved our endgame win condition — Kingambit later KO'd Inteleon and Dragapult and closed the game 1v1. Sucker Punch on the final turn vs an attacking Dragapult was legal (no Psychic Terrain, no Armor Tail) and converted.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: switch-out-when-about-to-be-KO'd rule (Kingambit T3), no Tailwind into a TR-ish board, no spread move into Wide Guard, Sucker Punch legality check, Protect on Dragonite only when an actual OHKO was listed (T6). Violated/partially: Drogon stayed in on T4 with a listed Draco Meteor threat and two attackers able to combine for a KO — it died to Sceptile Dragon Pulse + Phantom Force. Also the T2 fallback (Kingambit Protect + Ancient Power) was an engine fallback, not a deliberate line; it luckily produced an Ancient Power omniboost but spent the Mega's turn on a 60 BP move instead of pressuring Sceptile.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Drogon lost at T4: we committed both of our actions to Sceptile while Drogon was at 16% HP after Sceptile Dragon Pulse was clearly in range; the low-HP slot should have Protected (our own rule: slot at/below 25% HP with threats on board only Protects or switches). 2) Two misses (Weather Ball T3, Moonblast T5) cost tempo — both were sub-100% accuracy clicks while we were ahead; the safe-play accuracy bias exists in code but did not stop a 100%-accurate Moonblast miss (Moonblast is 100, so that was pure luck) while Weather Ball missing was the real damage. Actually Weather Ball is 100% too — the misses came from Phantom Force/evasion timing, not accuracy choices. 3) Repeated Phantom Force cycling by Dragapult burned 3 of our turns; we never used Kingambit's Sucker Punch pressure or a Protect-cycle to deny the emerging Phantom Force turn. 4) Rate-limit fallback on T2 meant one of ten turns was piloted blind.
analysis.howToImprove: Add an explicit 'semi-invulnerable / Phantom Force cycle' handler: when a foe is in Phantom Force/Dig/Fly/Dive/Bounce, never target it; and on the turn it is due to RESURFACE, the slot it threatens should Protect or we should pre-position Sucker Punch (Phantom Force is an attack, so Sucker Punch connects). Enforce the <=25% HP Protect rule on the Mega: Drogon at 16% with two live attackers must Protect, not attack. Against Dragapult specifically, treat Draco Meteor/Phantom Force as a 100% OHKO flag on Charizard.

proposals.change: SEMI-INVULNERABLE TURN RULE (code-enforced): if a foe used Phantom Force/Shadow Force/Dig/Fly/Dive/Bounce last turn and is currently charging, (a) block all moves targeting that slot, and (b) on the resurfacing turn, the slot it is most likely to hit (lowest HP / super-effective target) must Protect or switch, or Kingambit must click Sucker Punch (which connects into an attacking charger).
proposals.evidence: T3-T6 vs swampflower1: Dragapult used Phantom Force four times, cost Drogon its life on T4 and wasted a Weather Ball on an invulnerable target on T3.

proposals.change: MEGA LOW-HP PROTECT MANDATE: any of our actives at or below 25% max HP with at least two living foes on the field may only Protect or switch, with no exception for 'our action is part of a focus-fire KO'.
proposals.evidence: Drogon at 25/153 (16%) attacked into Sceptile with Ancient Power on T4 and was KO'd by Dragon Pulse + Phantom Force before our action mattered.

proposals.change: Test Milotic with Icy Wind or Haze over Protect in a variant: both recent losses (FencyWill, Ifiwinidiehelp) and this win's close turns were decided by speed control / stat resets we do not own.
proposals.evidence: Opponent Milotic Icy Wind generated free chip + speed denial every turn in the FencyWill loss; we have zero stat-reset tools across 196 games.

lessons: Never click an attack at a foe that is in a semi-invulnerable turn (Phantom Force/Dig/Fly/Dive/Bounce) — the move auto-fails and surrenders half the turn.
A Pokémon in Phantom Force/Dig/Fly will attack on the turn it resurfaces: that is the turn to Protect the threatened slot or to click Sucker Punch with Kingambit, not the turn to attack it.
Our Mega at or below 25% HP with two live foes must Protect or switch; focus-fire plans do not override the low-HP rule.
Kingambit switched out at low HP early can still close a game 1v1 — preserving the slow Dark attacker is a real win condition, not a sacrifice piece.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep the current loadout; the game was decided by semi-invulnerable turns and HP management, not by item choice, and scarf_garchomp remains our best-performing variant at 45%.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Phantom Force / U-turn evasive pivot' tempo idea by giving Mega Dragonite a bulk-leaning HP/SpD spread (survive one Inteleon Ice Beam at full HP after Multiscale) and testing Milotic with Icy Wind over Protect; Icy Wind both chips and denies the speed that Dragapult/Inteleon used to dictate every turn.
teamInspiration.reason: Dragapult cycled Phantom Force to dodge our damage and dictate timing while Inteleon's Ice Beam deleted both Whimsicott and Mega Dragonite in consecutive turns — a single Icy Wind would have flipped the speed order and let our bulkier pieces cash in damage before dying.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 Tailwind mandate with Whimsicott + Protect on Drogon was textbook: Raichu-Y's Fake Out hit the shield, Tailwind went up for free, and we held speed control for 6 turns. Kingambit was the MVP (219% damage, 3 KOs including the Raichu-Y Mega and Rillaboom) — the slow Dark attacker closing out games is now a repeated winning pattern. Garchomp correctly used Stomping Tantrum instead of Earthquake while Whimsicott was beside it (no ally chip, 114% damage onto Incineroar/Rillaboom). Protecting Whimsicott at 27% HP against Grassy Glide/Parting Shot priority followed the low-HP rule exactly and blanked Incineroar's Parting Shot. Drogon pivoting out at 46% rather than trading with Flare Blitz preserved it to finish Milotic on turn 15.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: Turn-1 Tailwind mandate; Protect Drogon vs a faster electric nuke; low-HP Protect rule for Whimsicott; no Earthquake next to a non-Flying ally; Mega evolved turn 1; switched a threatened Mega out rather than trading. Violated: Whimsicott clicked Encore into Incineroar on T6 — Prankster is immune on Dark types (a known, written team rule) and the whole action was wasted; Encore was also clicked on T3 into an empty slot/switch and failed. That is two wasted halves of the 2-action economy in a 15-turn game.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Two failed Encores: T3 Encore fizzled (Raichu switched out, no last move to lock), T6 Encore into Incineroar was a hard Prankster-vs-Dark immunity — both were free turns given to the opponent while Rillaboom set Grassy Terrain and Wood Hammered Whimsicott to 21%. 2) T2 double-attacked into an obvious Raichu Protect: Raichu was the clear focus target after surviving turn 1 unharmed, and both of our actions hit the shield — the playbook says send at least one action at the partner when the target's Protect is obvious. 3) Garchomp was chipped to 5% and then KO'd by Grassy Glide because we kept attacking at <55% HP into a Rillaboom that 1-shots it (NO-TRADE RULE violation). 4) Damage estimates on Drogon's Heat Wave/Weather Ball were repeatedly optimistic (the game was won anyway, but Milotic needed many turns).
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block Encore (and all Prankster status) onto Dark-type foes in code, and block Encore onto a slot whose lastMove is empty/just switched in. Respect the obvious-Protect rule: after a foe Protects or is the clear focus target at full HP, split actions. Enforce the NO-TRADE rule for Garchomp specifically: at <=55% HP facing Rillaboom/any priority-Grass user, Protect or switch rather than click a third Stomping Tantrum. Keep leaning on Kingambit as the late-game closer — it is now our highest-value piece in standard matchups.

proposals.change: PRANKSTER-DARK BLOCK (code-enforced): block Encore/Taunt/Tailwind-at-foe/any Prankster status move from Whimsicott when the chosen target is a Dark type, and block Encore when the target has no lastMove or switched in this turn.
proposals.evidence: T6 Whimsicott Encore -> Incineroar: '-immune|p2a: Incineroar' (Prankster vs Dark). T3 Encore failed outright after Raichu switched out. Two wasted actions.

proposals.change: OBVIOUS-PROTECT SPLIT: if a foe is at full HP, is the clear focus-fire target, and we move first under Tailwind, send only one action at it and the other at the partner or at setup; never double-target a healthy foe that has an unused Protect.
proposals.evidence: T2 Moonblast + Weather Ball both hit Raichu's Protect, giving them a free Snarl turn.

proposals.change: GARCHOMP NO-TRADE: Garchomp at <=55% HP with a Rillaboom/Grassy Glide or any priority user alive must Protect or switch instead of attacking.
proposals.evidence: T7 Garchomp attacked at 100%->5% then died to Grassy Glide on T8; its 114% of damage stopped there.

lessons: Whimsicott's Prankster Encore/Taunt is IMMUNE on Dark types (Incineroar, Kingambit, Grimmsnarl, Tyranitar, Hydreigon) — never click it at a Dark foe.
Encore fails if the target has no last move (just switched in): only Encore a foe that actually used a move last turn and is still in.
Do not spend both actions on one healthy foe that has an unused Protect while we hold Tailwind — split one action to its partner.
Kingambit is our best standard-matchup closer: preserve it to clean up after Tailwind expires rather than trading it early.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again out-tempoed Incineroar/Rillaboom all game and is the only piece that reliably revenge-kills Raichu-Y; keep the loadout stable while we fix the Encore/Protect misplays.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Snarl + Parting Shot + Grassy Terrain' value engine by testing Milotic with Haze or Icy Wind over Protect: Snarl cut Drogon's and Whimsicott's SpA twice for free, and we had no reset. Also consider shifting Whimsicott to Taunt over Encore in matchups with 2+ Dark types, since Encore is dead weight there.
teamInspiration.reason: Their whole early game was prediction-free chip and stat drops (Snarl x2, Parting Shot, Fake Out) while our only answer, Prankster Encore, was immune on their Dark pivot — a stat-reset or Taunt gives us a working response to that structure.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 Whimsicott Tailwind with Focus Sash intact was free value — it survived their Mega Charizard Heat Wave at 1% HP and still provided speed control for the rest of the (very short) game. Mega-evolving Drogon turn 1 set Sun, which both powered our own Heat Wave and denied them nothing but importantly matched their Zard-Y weather war. Turn 2 was textbook: Whimsicott at 1% HP was a free action, so we cashed its damage in immediately (Moonblast KO on the 57% Garchomp) instead of Protecting, and Ancient Power (Rock, 4x into their Mega Charizard-Y) deleted their Mega. Double KO on turn 2 ended the game. Ancient Power selection over Weather Ball/Heat Wave was the key macro call: their Zard-Y was their win condition and Rock is the one move that one-shots it.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed the 'Whimsicott with Focus Sash must click Tailwind on turn 1' mandate. Followed 'damaged Pokemon do not deal less damage' — Whimsicott at 1 HP still fired Moonblast for the KO rather than wasting the slot on Protect. Followed 'deny their win condition' by targeting the opposing Mega Charizard-Y with the 4x Rock move. Followed 'no overkill / pick the move that actually KOs' and Mega-Zard-Y vs Zard-Y mirror handling. No Sucker Punch, no Tailwind-into-TR, no Prankster-into-Dark errors.
analysis.whatFailed: Very little, but two process issues: (1) The preview call fell back to the engine due to an HTTP 429 rate limit — this has now happened in 4 of the last 5 games, meaning our team selection and lead are frequently being made without the Claude macro layer. That is a systemic risk, not a tactical one. (2) Our turn-1 damage calc for Heat Wave into their Charizard-Mega-Y predicted 14-24% but the actual was 31% — we are under-modelling foes that Mega evolve on the same turn (their Zard-Y's new stats/Drought weren't accounted for), which could cause us to misjudge an incoming threat in a closer game. (3) Minor: Whimsicott was left in Heat Wave spread range on turn 1 when their lead pair (Zard + Venusaur) both had spread moves — only their miss on Drogon and Sash saved full value; the result was fine but the risk was real.
analysis.howToImprove: Treat an opposing Charizardite/mega stone holder as already Mega-evolved for threat calculation on the turn it is on the field at full HP. Keep prioritising the opposing Mega as the single win condition and reach for 4x-effective coverage (Ancient Power) even when a STAB spread move looks bigger on paper. Resolve the rate-limit fallbacks so preview/lead selection always gets a macro call; vs sun mirrors the plan is settled: Mega Charizard + Whimsicott Tailwind lead, Ancient Power reserved for the opposing Zard.

proposals.change: OPPOSING-MEGA PRE-COMPUTE: when a foe holds an unused mega stone and is at full HP on its first active turn, evaluate its threat range and our damage against its MEGA forme stats, not its base forme.
proposals.evidence: T1 Heat Wave -> Charizard predicted 14-24%, actual 31% because they mega-evolved the same turn; the same error in reverse could leave a slot in an unforeseen OHKO range.

proposals.change: ZARD MIRROR RULE: vs an opposing Charizard-Y (or any 4x Rock-weak Flying/Fire lead), Drogon's Ancient Power is the forced target-the-mega move over Heat Wave/Weather Ball, even when the spread looks like more total damage.
proposals.evidence: Ancient Power did 69% and KO'd their Mega Zard-Y on T2; Heat Wave had only done 31% in a full turn.

proposals.change: Keep the Charizard + Whimsicott Tailwind lead locked for sun archetype (now 16-3).
proposals.evidence: sun / Charizard|zw record 15-3 before this game, 16-3 after.

lessons: Treat an opposing Pokemon holding an unused Mega Stone as already in its Mega forme when calculating both its damage output and our damage into it.
Against an opposing Charizard-Y, Drogon's Ancient Power (4x Rock) is the win-condition-denial move — use it over Heat Wave/Weather Ball even if the spread option looks bigger.
A Focus Sash Pokemon at 1 HP is a free full-power action, not a liability: click its best attack, never Protect with it unless it must survive to set field control.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their Charizard-Y + Venusaur + Greninja sun/weather core shows why a dedicated Rock option matters: keep Ancient Power on Drogon permanently (do not swap for Solar Beam), and consider giving Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so we own both a Rock answer and speed denial vs weather mirrors.
teamInspiration.reason: The whole game was decided by owning a 4x-effective move against the opposing Mega; conversely their team had no answer to our Rock coverage and folded in two turns.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 focus fire removed Hisuian Arcanine (Head Smash/Rock threat) before it could fire a second time, immediately denying their fastest burst. Preview pick (Milotic + Dragonite lead, Whimsicott/Scarf Garchomp back) correctly used Competitive bait and Scarf Garchomp as the late-game speed insurance. Turn 3 pivot of Milotic out of Grassy Glide range preserved our eventual closer. Turn 4 double-target on Mega Garchomp-Z removed their only remaining win condition (Power Gem had already deleted Mega Dragonite). Turn 5 Protect on Whimsicott vs Incineroar Flare Blitz was textbook; Whimsicott then traded itself to KO Rillaboom, and Scarf Garchomp + Milotic closed a clean 2v1.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: 'Tailwind has no value when only Scarf Garchomp remains' (T6 correctly skipped Tailwind for Moonblast). Followed: Protect the slot facing a listed OHKO (T5 Whimsicott vs Flare Blitz). Followed: never Earthquake next to a non-Flying ally (EQ never clicked next to Milotic/Whimsicott in range). Followed: focus fire the opposing Mega rather than splitting. Violated: the OPPOSING-MEGA PRE-COMPUTE rule — on T2 we double-Protected while their Garchomp mega-evolved for free, and on T3 we left Mega Dragonite in against a Mega Garchomp-Z Power Gem (Rock, 4x-relevant special) that the calc itself listed as a likely KO; Dragonite died for nothing.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 2 was a wasted 2-action turn: engine fallback double-Protect with no live Mega-stone threat already resolved — it gave Garchomp a free Mega Evolution and a free positioning turn. 2) Turn 3 Mega Dragonite at 59/168 stayed in against Mega Garchomp-Z whose Power Gem is super-effective special damage; the correct line was Protect or switch Dragonite, not attack. We traded our Mega for 0 KOs and ~65% total damage. 3) Damage-calc model is systematically under-rating our own hits vs. this opponent (4 of 6 checks over-performed), meaning we Protected/pivoted on turns where a straight attack KO'd — a conservatism cost. 4) Whimsicott died to a predictable Flare Blitz on T6 when Protect was available and Garchomp alone could finish Rillaboom the next turn.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: any of our Pokémon that is at or below 40% HP and faces a foe with a revealed super-effective move must Protect or switch — Mega Dragonite at 35% into Power Gem is an automatic pivot to Kingambit/Milotic. Second: never double-Protect when the only 'threat' is an unmegaed foe about to mega — attack the mega-stone holder on the turn it evolves instead of giving it a free turn. Third: Milotic should pivot out earlier against Grassy Glide priority rather than Protect-cycling into chip. Fourth: trust the damage model's upper roll vs Rillaboom/Incineroar-class bulk — our Dragon Claw consistently hit ~32% not 27%, so two-turn KO plans were actually one-turn-plus-priority plans.

proposals.change: LOW-HP SUPER-EFFECTIVE MANDATE: any of our actives at <=40% max HP facing a foe with a revealed (or obvious, e.g. Power Gem on Rock/Ground mega) super-effective move must Protect or switch; attacking is blocked.
proposals.evidence: T3 Mega Dragonite at 35% attacked into Mega Garchomp-Z Power Gem (listed as KO) and died, losing our Mega for zero KOs.

proposals.change: NO FREE MEGA TURN: forbid double-Protect on a turn where an opposing Pokemon holds an unused mega stone and nothing on our side has a listed >=80% incoming hit — spend at least one action attacking the stone holder.
proposals.evidence: T2 engine fallback double-Protect gave Garchomp-Z a free mega evolution and a free turn; it then OHKO'd Mega Dragonite on T3.

proposals.change: GRASSY GLIDE PIVOT: Milotic/Whimsicott/Garchomp below 50% with a Rillaboom alive must switch rather than Protect-cycle, since Grassy Glide priority ignores our speed control.
proposals.evidence: Milotic took 77% from turn-1 Grassy Glide and spent two further turns Protecting/healing instead of pivoting to a resist.

proposals.change: Continue Milotic Icy Wind-over-Protect test: this game's only speed control was a Scarf, and Tailwind was never set.
proposals.evidence: Tailwind turns us 0, them 0 — we won on raw trades; an Icy Wind would have flipped the Garchomp-Z and Rillaboom speed checks.

lessons: A Pokemon at or below 40% HP facing a foe with a revealed super-effective move must Protect or switch — no 'our attack might KO first' exception, and this applies doubly to our Mega.
Never spend both actions on Protect when the only pending threat is an opposing Pokemon that has not mega-evolved yet: that turn hands them a free Mega and free positioning.
Against Rillaboom's Grassy Glide, switching beats Protect-cycling: priority re-threatens the same slot every turn regardless of our speed control.
When our damage rolls repeatedly over-perform against a given opponent's bulk, trust the top of the range and take the attacking line instead of an extra conservative Protect.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp was the game-winning piece (181% damage, closed the 2v1) in a game where we set zero Tailwind turns; keep the loadout for continued sample.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Grassy Terrain + Grassy Glide priority + Mega Garchomp-Z Power Gem' structure by giving Milotic Icy Wind over Protect and testing a bulkier Mega Dragonite spread (survive one Power Gem at full HP through Multiscale); priority and a Rock special move were the two things that beat our speed control.
teamInspiration.reason: Rillaboom's Grassy Glide ignored every speed tool we own and their Garchomp-Z used a 4x-relevant special Rock move to delete our Mega — we own neither a priority answer nor a speed-drop tool, so Icy Wind plus Multiscale-preserving bulk directly patches both holes.

analysis.whatWorked: Won in 6 turns vs SunnySleepy's sun team (Torkoal/Vileplume/Raichu-Y/Ditto). Turn-1 Weather Ball into Mega Raichu-Y was the correct win-condition denial: No Guard Zap Cannon would have OHKO'd Drogon and paralyzed the rest of the team, and sun-boosted Weather Ball OHKO'd it before it acted. Drogon's Drought flipping the field to sun also powered our Fire/Weather Ball damage. After Drogon died, the Milotic + Scarf Garchomp back half closed it cleanly: double-targeting Vileplume (the fast Chlorophyll special attacker) on T3 removed their real damage output, then Garchomp picked off Ditto over two turns while Milotic Recovered back into safety. Garchomp Choice Scarf again paid for itself (outspeeding transformed Ditto and Torkoal).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Whimsicott turn-1 Tailwind mandate was followed (Sash user, nothing listed >=90% to OHKO it). Zard-mirror / Rock-weak-mega rule applied in spirit: Weather Ball at the opposing Mega rather than a spread. Low-HP rule applied on T5: Milotic at 26% Recovered instead of attacking. Safe-play-when-ahead directive applied from T3 onward: 100% accurate Dragon Claw/Ice Beam focus fire, no gambles. No Tailwind into Trick Room, no Sucker Punch into a blocker, no Earthquake beside Kingambit (Kingambit not brought).
analysis.whatFailed: Two avoidable losses of our own pieces. (1) T1: Whimsicott died immediately — Raichu-Y Fake Out flinch + Vileplume Acid Spray broke through the Sash in the same turn. The Sash only guarantees survival of ONE hit; a Fake Out user plus a second attacker is a two-hit turn, so the 'Sash makes Tailwind free' assumption is wrong when the opposing lead has Fake Out. Tailwind turns ended up 0. (2) T2: Drogon was KO'd by Ditto's Ancient Power. Ditto had just switched in on T1's faint — it transformed into one of our Pokemon (it copied Drogon's Charizard-Y data, giving it Ancient Power, 4x effective into our Drogon). Our listed 'Threats' line only showed Vileplume Sludge Wave 22-42% and completely ignored Ditto; we clicked Heat Wave instead of Protect/retreating the 4x-Rock-weak Mega against a fresh Ditto that mirrors our own team. That is a free Mega loss. (3) Minor: T2 Heat Wave was predicted to OHKO both and instead we lost the attacker before it resolved — the sequencing was never checked against Ditto's post-transform speed (Ditto copies stats and our Drogon is Speed 138, so a speed tie/loss was always possible).
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Treat Ditto as a MIRROR of our own active Mega: on the turn Ditto enters, assume it has our fastest/strongest active Pokemon's exact moveset and stats (including the 4x-effective Ancient Power against Drogon) and either Protect the mirrored Pokemon, switch it out, or KO Ditto before it moves. Never leave Drogon in front of a freshly-transformed Ditto. 2) Focus Sash does NOT make a turn free when the opposing lead holds Fake Out: Fake Out breaks the Sash and flinches, and the partner's attack then kills. Against a Fake Out lead, either Protect Whimsicott turn 1 or set Tailwind only if the Fake Out user is the ONLY opposing attacker. 3) Always re-read the threat list for the newly-switched-in foe; a blank threat entry for an unknown mon (Ditto, Imposter, unrevealed set) should be treated as 'maximum threat', not 'no threat'.

proposals.change: DITTO MIRROR RULE: when an opposing Ditto/Imposter is active or just switched in, assume it has transformed into our strongest active Pokemon and owns all of that Pokemon's moves/stats. Our 4x-weak Mega (Drogon) must Protect or switch on that turn; never attack through it.
proposals.evidence: T2 Ditto transformed into our Charizard-Y and OHKO'd Drogon with Ancient Power while our threat list listed only Vileplume (22-42%).

proposals.change: FAKE OUT + PARTNER SASH RULE: Whimsicott's turn-1 Tailwind mandate is suspended when an opposing lead has Fake Out AND its partner has any damaging move — Fake Out breaks the Sash and flinches, so the partner's hit kills. Protect or lead differently instead.
proposals.evidence: T1 Raichu-Y Fake Out broke Whimsicott's Sash, flinched it, and Vileplume's Acid Spray finished it; we ended with 0 Tailwind turns.

proposals.change: UNKNOWN-FOE THREAT FLOOR: if an active foe has zero listed threat damage because its set is unknown (Ditto, Zoroark, unrevealed), treat it as capable of a super-effective OHKO on our frailest active and bias that slot toward Protect/switch.
proposals.evidence: The engine threat list showed nothing for Ditto on T2; it then dealt 100% to Drogon.

lessons: Ditto/Imposter copies OUR active Pokemon: on the turn it enters, assume it mirrors our strongest active (same speed, same moves, including moves that are super-effective against our own Mega) — Protect or switch the mirrored piece, never trade with it.
Focus Sash does not survive a Fake Out plus a partner attack in the same turn: against a Fake Out lead with a damaging partner, Whimsicott's 'free Tailwind' turn is not free.
A foe with no listed threat damage (unknown/unrevealed set) must be treated as a maximum threat, not as harmless.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again outsped and cleaned a transformed Ditto and Torkoal; keep the current loadout while the Ditto/Fake Out guardrails are tested.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their Fake Out + spread-damage opening (Raichu-Y Fake Out into Vileplume Acid Spray) by testing Milotic with Icy Wind over Protect so we own a non-priority speed-denial action; and consider that their Ditto proves our team is weak to its own mirror — a bulkier Mega Dragonite HP/SpD spread (survive one mirrored Draco/Ice attack at full HP via Multiscale) is a better Mega choice than Drogon versus any team carrying Ditto or Rock coverage.
teamInspiration.reason: They won both of our Pokemon losses this game with a two-action turn-1 burst (Fake Out breaks Sash, partner kills) and with a mirror Pokemon exploiting Drogon's 4x Rock weakness — we have no speed-drop tool and no safe Mega into Rock coverage.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 switch of Milotic into Kingambit correctly dodged a Wood Hammer OHKO. Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum cleanly removed Sneasler before Unburden/Grassy Seed could snowball. Milotic's Ice Beam finished Rillaboom and Competitive triggered +2 SpA off Salamence's Intimidate. Protect discipline on Dragonite turn 2 correctly dodged Draco Meteor range.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Low-HP switch rules were respected (Garchomp pivoted out at 36%). Protect-vs-OHKO discipline was followed on Dragonite T2. However the single most important standing lesson — PUNISH SETUP IMMEDIATELY — was violated: Goodra-Hisui used Shelter twice (+4 Def) completely unpunished, and we explicitly wrote it off as 'unkillable' and never Encored, Taunted, or special-attacked it after that. Whimsicott, our only Encore/Taunt answer to a Def-setup Body Press wall, was left at home.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Goodra-Hisui got +4 Defense for free on turns 1-2 and then Body Pressed Kingambit (100%), Garchomp (58%), and Milotic (50%) — Body Press scales with ITS Defense, so every Shelter was a direct Attack boost. We treated a boosting Pokemon as a wall to ignore instead of the win condition to deny. 2) We never set Tailwind the entire game (0 Tailwind turns) — Dragonite's Tailwind slot was never clicked, and Whimsicott (our actual speed control) was benched. The opponent therefore held speed AND power from turn 5 onward. 3) Dragonite was Fake Out flinched TWICE (T1 and T5) by the same Rillaboom, wasting two of our four actions, and Multiscale was broken on turn 1 as feared. 4) We kept firing Heat Wave into a +4 Def Goodra that regenerated with Life Dew — three turns of 15-26% chip into a healer is zero action economy. 5) Endgame: Mega Salamence came in fresh at turn 7 against Milotic 11%, Dragonite 13%, Garchomp 36% and Hyper Voice swept all three in two turns — we had no healthy piece left and no speed control.
analysis.howToImprove: Treat any repeated defensive setup (Shelter, Iron Defense, Cosmic Power, Acid Armor) on a Body Press / Stored Power user as a SWEEPER, not a wall: Encore it, Taunt it, or switch to a special attacker and remove it immediately on the turn the second boost lands. Against a Grassy Terrain Rillaboom with Fake Out, never lead Mega Dragonite (Multiscale is guaranteed broken by Fake Out and priority Grassy Glide); lead Whimsicott for Tailwind + Encore instead. Click Tailwind on the first turn Dragonite is not under an OHKO threat — three Protect/Heat Wave turns passed while we had no speed control. Reserve one healthy answer for the fourth Pokemon (Mega Salamence here) rather than spending all four of our mons down to <40% against a healing wall.

proposals.change: DEFENSE-SETUP WIN-CON RULE: if a foe uses Shelter/Iron Defense/Cosmic Power/Acid Armor/Bulk Up twice, or reaches +2 or more Def while holding Body Press/Stored Power, it is flagged as the opponent's win condition: Encore/Taunt it, or focus-fire with special moves — never declare it 'unkillable' and chip it with a spread move while it heals.
proposals.evidence: Goodra-Hisui reached +4 Def unpunished on T1-T2 and then Body Pressed Kingambit for 100%, Garchomp 58%, Milotic 50%; we spent T3/T6/T7 Heat Waving it for 15-26% into Life Dew healing.

proposals.change: Never bring Mega Dragonite as a lead against a revealed Rillaboom (Fake Out + Grassy Glide priority + Grassy Terrain healing). Multiscale is guaranteed broken turn 1 and the flinch costs an action.
proposals.evidence: Rillaboom Fake Out flinched Dragonite on T1 and again on T5, breaking Multiscale and wasting 2 of our 8 early actions; Dragonite ended at 13% without ever setting Tailwind.

proposals.change: TAILWIND DEBT RULE: if we have a Tailwind user on the field and have not set Tailwind by turn 3 while no Trick Room exists, Tailwind becomes the mandatory action on the first turn that user is not facing a listed >=70% incoming hit.
proposals.evidence: 0 Tailwind turns this game; we lost the endgame to a fresh Mega Salamence that outsped all three of our remaining mons.

proposals.change: Always bring Whimsicott against any team with a defensive setup move or a Life Dew/Recover wall — Prankster Encore is the only tool we own that reverses a +4 Def Body Press user, and it was benched this game.
proposals.evidence: We benched Whimsicott and then had literally no answer to Shelter spam; the game report notes Whimsicott is never worth cutting (every replacement lost 7+ points).

lessons: Body Press and Stored Power turn DEFENSIVE boosts into offense: a foe spamming Shelter/Iron Defense is a sweeper gaining Attack every turn, not a wall to ignore.

Never label a boosting foe 'unkillable' and chip it with spread damage while it heals — Encore it, Taunt it, or switch to a piece that threatens it; otherwise we donate the whole game's action economy.
Do not lead Mega Dragonite into a revealed Rillaboom: Fake Out guarantees Multiscale breaks and steals an action, and Grassy Glide re-threatens every turn regardless of speed control.
If we own a Tailwind user and reach turn 3 with 0 Tailwind turns and no Trick Room on the field, Tailwind is mandatory on the next safe turn — speed control deferred forever is speed control lost.
When three of our four Pokemon are under 40% and the opponent still has an unrevealed fourth (especially a Mega), stop trading and preserve one healthy answer for it.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp remains our only reliable answer to fresh Mega Salamence/Raichu late-game; it is the loadout with a winning record (13-12) and this loss was caused by strategy, not item choice.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Shelter + Body Press + Life Dew' self-sufficient wall concept by giving Milotic Haze over Protect (or Icy Wind) so we own a stat-reset answer to defensive setup; and never bench Whimsicott — its Prankster Encore is our only lock on a repeated boosting move.
teamInspiration.reason: Goodra-Hisui won the game alone by converting free Shelter turns into Body Press KOs while healing with Life Dew and Grassy Terrain; we had zero stat-reset and zero Encore on the field, so every boost was permanent.

analysis.whatWorked: Drogon's Ancient Power correctly targeted Armarouge turn 1 (a Fire/Psychic that is weak to Rock) and the Weather Ball KO on Indeedee turn 3 removed Psychic Terrain and Follow Me. Protecting Dragonite on turn 3 was correct given Gardevoir-Mega's Expanding Force threat.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Kingambit was correctly led into a Psychic Terrain team (immune to Expanding Force) and the setter-denial rule was applied (targeting Armarouge before Trick Room). However the 'treat an unused Mega Stone as already Mega' rule was VIOLATED: Gardevoir was holding Gardevoirite at preview and we calculated/led as if it were base Gardevoir, so we never accounted for a Fairy Aura-free but 165-SpA Mega Gardevoir Expanding Force spread move that would two-for-one us every single turn. The Tailwind debt rule was also violated: Whimsicott came in on turn 3 and we never set Tailwind at all.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) The real win condition was Mega Gardevoir, not Armarouge. We spent turn 1 and turn 2 focus-firing Armarouge (which then switched out untouched-ish) while Gardevoir Protected turn 1 and Mega Evolved turn 2 completely unpunished, then fired spread Expanding Force every turn from behind Psychic Terrain and Follow Me. 2) Kingambit was fed into Armor Cannon — Kingambit is 4x-relevant frail vs Fire special and we knew Armarouge's Armor Cannon was listed as a 121-182% OHKO on it, yet we attacked instead of Protecting or positioning; we traded our Psychic-immune anchor for 57% chip. 3) Turn 2 we double-targeted a slot the opponent switched out of (Armarouge left, Indeedee entered), so both attacks landed on a fresh 100% Indeedee — a classic double-into-switch. 4) Zero Tailwind the whole game; Whimsicott entered at 3-1 down and immediately died. 5) Game ended turn 4 at 0-4; spread Expanding Force took 3 of our 4 Pokemon.
