analysis.howToImprove: Against Psychic Terrain teams the kill order is Indeedee FIRST (it is the terrain + Follow Me + redirection engine and the frailest piece), not the Armarouge/Armor Cannon attacker. Removing terrain restores Sucker Punch, un-boosts Expanding Force by 1.5x, and stops Follow Me redirection. Second: never leave Kingambit in front of a revealed Armor Cannon user when the threat table already says OHKO — Protect or switch it; its value is as a late-game closer, not a turn-1 trade. Third: when a foe Protects turn 1 with a Mega Stone unused, assume it Mega Evolves next turn and becomes the primary threat — reprioritize onto it immediately. Fourth: when an opponent has a 100% HP healthy partner and the target slot is at low HP with an obvious KO pending, split damage or expect a switch rather than double-targeting.

proposals.change: PSYCHIC TERRAIN KILL ORDER: against a team with Indeedee/Indeedee-F (or any Psychic Surge setter) plus an Expanding Force user, the terrain setter is the primary target on turn 1-2, ahead of the Expanding Force attacker. Killing the setter removes terrain, the 1.5x spread boost, Follow Me redirection, and restores our Sucker Punch/Fake Out.
proposals.evidence: We focus-fired Armarouge turns 1-2 while Indeedee entered untouched, set terrain, used Follow Me, and Mega Gardevoir's spread Expanding Force then took three of our Pokemon in two turns.

proposals.change: KINGAMBIT PRESERVATION RULE: never leave Kingambit in front of a revealed Fire/Fighting/Ground super-effective attacker whose listed damage is >=100% when Kingambit cannot KO it first and the partner cannot remove it. Protect or switch; Kingambit is a closer, not a turn-1 trade piece.
proposals.evidence: Turn 1 threat table read 'Kingambit threatened by Armarouge Armor Cannon (121-182% OHKO)' and we clicked Kowtow Cleave into a 16% miss-the-KO line; Gardevoir Protected, Armarouge survived and KO'd Kingambit for free.

proposals.change: DOUBLE-TARGET SWITCH HEDGE: do not commit both actions into a single damaged foe when the opponent has a healthy benched answer and the foe is at <=50% HP with an obvious incoming KO — split one action onto the other active slot or onto a likely switch-in.
proposals.evidence: Turn 2 both Dragon Pulse and Ancient Power were aimed at 43% Armarouge; the opponent switched to a full-HP Indeedee and absorbed both attacks at no cost while Mega Evolving Gardevoir.

proposals.change: Against Gardevoir + Indeedee-F + Armarouge + Gallade (psyterrain hyper-offense), bring Whimsicott as a LEAD, not a back piece: Prankster Tailwind is unaffected by Psychic Terrain (targets our own side) and it is the only way to out-speed Mega Gardevoir before it fires spread Expanding Force.
proposals.evidence: We placed Whimsicott third; it entered at turn 3 with the game already lost and never set Tailwind. Zero Tailwind turns in a game decided by a faster spread attacker.

lessons: Against Psychic Terrain teams, kill the TERRAIN SETTER (Indeedee/Indeedee-F) first — not the Expanding Force attacker. Removing terrain cuts Expanding Force to single-target non-boosted and restores our priority moves.

Mega Gardevoir's Expanding Force in Psychic Terrain is a spread move that hits BOTH our slots for ~80% each: it is a two-for-one team-wipe threat and must be the win-condition target the moment the Gardevoirite is revealed at preview.
Never leave Kingambit in front of a revealed Armor Cannon / Close Combat / Earthquake user listed as a 100%+ OHKO on it; Kingambit's value is as a late-game Dark closer, not a turn-1 damage trade.
Do not aim both actions at one damaged foe when the opponent still has healthy switch-ins: a switch absorbs the whole turn for free and gains them a Mega Evolution turn.
A foe that Protects on turn 1 while holding an unused Mega Stone is telegraphing a Mega Evolution next turn — reprioritize targeting onto it immediately, do not finish the already-chipped partner.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp remains the only piece that outspeeds Mega Gardevoir (and Mega Alakazam) without Tailwind; keep it while we test the psyterrain kill-order fix.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Mirror their 'terrain + redirection + spread nuke' engine by permanently pairing Whimsicott as a LEAD on psyterrain matchups and testing Milotic with Icy Wind over Protect; additionally consider Garchomp over Kingambit as the psyterrain anchor, since Scarf Earthquake outspeeds and OHKOs Indeedee/Gardevoir while Kingambit is walled by Armor Cannon and Psycho Cut.
teamInspiration.reason: Their win came entirely from Indeedee's Follow Me + Psychic Terrain protecting a Mega Gardevoir that spread-nuked both our slots each turn. Our 'Kingambit is Psychic-immune' plan failed because their Fire and Fighting coverage (Armor Cannon, Gallade) deletes Kingambit instantly; speed control and a fast Ground attacker beat that structure, not a slow Dark type.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 focus fire on Mega Garchomp-Z with Milotic Ice Beam + Mega Dragonite Dragon Pulse was the textbook play: we correctly treated the unused Garchompite Z as already mega-evolved, identified it as the only piece that could OHKO our Dragonite (Dragon Claw 67-121%), and removed it before it ever got a second action. The opponent forfeited immediately afterward. Milotic's Competitive also converted Volcarona's Struggle Bug SpA drop into +2 SpA, which is exactly why Milotic is in the lead slot on standard matchups. The Milotic+Dragonite lead has now compiled 20W-12L on 'standard' archetype and is our most reliable plan.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) 'Treat an opposing Pokemon holding an unused Mega Stone as already in its Mega forme when calculating damage' — we calc'd against Mega Garchomp-Z and focus-fired it. (2) 'Don't split damage when one foe is the only real threat' — both actions on Garchomp rather than chipping Volcarona. (3) Mega'd Dragonite turn 1 rather than holding the Mega (avoids 'never spend both actions on Protect when only threat is a non-mega'). (4) No Protect spam, no unnecessary prediction while even on count. Not tested this game: Tailwind debt rule, psyterrain kill order, Kingambit preservation — the battle ended turn 1.
analysis.whatFailed: Nothing material failed; the game was a 1-turn forfeit and generates almost no data. The only micro-note: Dragon Pulse rolled 83% and Ice Beam only needed 17% to finish — a small overkill risk existed in the other direction (if both rolled low, Garchomp survives at ~5% and Rock Slide flinch-threatens Dragonite). A marginally safer line was Milotic Ice Beam (56-102%) + Dragonite Tailwind, banking speed control for the rest of the match, but with Dragonite at risk of a 39% OHKO roll from Dragon Claw the double-KO line was defensible. Broader concern from the window: 14W-17L over 31 games, with psyterrain (13/35) and sand (2/10) still the bleeding matchups, and Whimsicott leading all faint counts (128) — our Tailwind piece dies more than it sets.
analysis.howToImprove: Keep the Milotic+Dragonite standard lead. When the opponent's only threatening active is already in lethal range from ONE of our attacks, consider spending the second action on Tailwind rather than overkill — that converts a guaranteed KO turn into a KO plus 4 turns of speed control, which is the single highest-EV conversion available to this team (Whimsicott dying before Tailwind lands is our #1 structural loss cause). Codify a 'KO-overkill to Tailwind' conversion check: if our first attacker's minimum roll already KOs the sole threat, the partner should set Tailwind/Protect rather than duplicate the hit, unless the partner is itself at OHKO risk from the other slot.

proposals.change: OVERKILL-TO-SPEED CONVERSION: if one of our attacks' MINIMUM damage roll already KOs the only threatening foe, the partner must not duplicate the attack — spend that action on Tailwind (if no Trick Room), Protect (if the partner is itself in OHKO range), or a hit on the second foe.
proposals.evidence: T1 vs Haruhi15k: Milotic Ice Beam alone was 56-102% into Garchomp-Mega-Z while Dragon Pulse did 83% — Dragonite's action could have been Tailwind, banking 4 turns of speed control for free.

proposals.change: WHIMSICOTT SURVIVAL RULE: Whimsicott has fainted 128 times across 203 games (most of any mon). Never lead Whimsicott into a revealed Fake Out user paired with a damaging partner (Sash does not survive both); in those matchups lead Milotic+Dragonite and bring Whimsicott as the back-half Tailwind setter.
proposals.evidence: Running stats: ourFaints Whimsicott 128 vs ourKOs 81; SunnySleepy game lost Whimsicott turn 1 to Fake Out-equivalent + Acid Spray.

proposals.change: Keep Milotic+Dragonite (team 6235) as the default lead vs 'standard' archetype — now 20W-12L, our best-performing plan in the stats table.
proposals.evidence: byPlan: standard/Dragonite|zw 20-12 (62.5%) vs standard/Charizard|zw 14-10 (58%).

lessons: When a single one of our attacks already guarantees the KO on the opponent's only threatening Pokemon at its MINIMUM roll, the partner's action should buy field advantage (Tailwind) or safety (Protect) instead of duplicating the kill — overkill converts a free speed-control turn into nothing.
Treating an unused Mega Stone as the Mega forme and focus-firing that piece on turn 1 continues to be correct: it removed Garchomp-Mega-Z before it ever acted.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp remains the only loadout with a winning record (14-13, 52%) while standard and clear_amulet sit at 0-2 each; no reason to switch off it on a 1-turn sample.

teamInspiration.suggestion: They built around a Mega Garchomp-Z special attacker (Dragon Pulse off a Ground/Dragon) paired with Volcarona's Struggle Bug SpA drops — a 'lower their special output, then nuke' engine. Mirror the disruption half: test Milotic with Icy Wind over Protect so we own a non-priority speed-denial action that also feeds nothing to Competitive-style punishers, and keep Ice Beam as the mandatory Garchomp/Salamence/Dragon answer.
teamInspiration.reason: Volcarona's Struggle Bug was a free two-target SpA drop that would have crippled a Drogon lead; we have no equivalent spread-debuff and our only speed control (Whimsicott Tailwind) dies more often than it fires. Icy Wind on Milotic gives a second, bulkier speed-control source that survives Fake Out leads.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Milotic Protect correctly dodged the Rillaboom Wood Hammer/Grassy Glide OHKO threat, and the Mega Charizard-Y Drought immediately flipped Grassy Terrain's utility into our favor. Focus-firing Dragapult on T2 with Ice Beam + sun Weather Ball removed the fastest foe cleanly. Recognizing that Whimsicott at 1 HP should cash its action into Tailwind rather than Protect was the right application of the Focus Sash rule, and Tailwind did let Kingambit outspeed Flareon late. Kingambit's late Iron Head finally removed Flareon.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: 'Focus Sash mon at 1 HP is a free action — click the best move' (Whimsicott Tailwind on T5). Applied: 'A Pokemon at or below 40% must Protect or switch' (Milotic Protect T3, switch T4). Applied: don't chip-stall — we did focus-fire Dragapult. VIOLATED: the durable lesson 'If we own a Tailwind user and reach turn 3 with 0 Tailwind turns, Tailwind is mandatory on the next safe turn' — Whimsicott only entered on T4 and set Tailwind on T5 at 1 HP, after Drogon had already eaten a Fake Out and two Flare Blitzes. VIOLATED: 'never leave our Mega in front of a revealed super-effective attacker at <=40% HP' — Drogon sat at 80%→ate Flare Blitz on T5 from a Flareon we had already seen Flare Blitz three times, instead of Protecting or switching.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) MISREAD THE FLASH FIRE SWITCH: on T1 they switched Flareon in on our Heat Wave, activating Flash Fire. From that moment Drogon's Fire STAB (Weather Ball in sun, Heat Wave) was dead weight against half their team, yet we kept Drogon in as the primary attacker for four more turns with only Ancient Power as real coverage. 2) DROGON DIED TO A FORESEEN ATTACK: Flareon Flare Blitz was listed in our own threat line as 43-72% from 'Last Resort' — we mis-scouted the moveset and left a 80% Drogon exposed to a Flash-Fire-boosted Flare Blitz that OHKO'd. We had Protect available. 3) TAILWIND DEFERRED TO TURN 5: three full turns of no speed control against a Scarf-feeling Flareon and a Primarina; by the time Tailwind landed, Whimsicott was at 1 HP and Drogon died the same turn, so we got exactly 3 Tailwind turns with only Kingambit and a 40% Milotic to use them. 4) WHIMSICOTT BURNT AS A PIVOT: switching Milotic→Whimsicott into a Flare Blitz turn put our Sash setter at 1 HP before it ever acted — the exact 'Whimsicott survival rule' we wrote. The correct pivot was Kingambit (resists nothing of Fire but is far bulkier and immune to the Grass priority in Grassy Terrain). 5) T6-T7 OVERKILL/WHIFF: we spent two turns aiming Kowtow Cleave at a 14-31% Flareon that Detected once and then switched out, while Rillaboom freely re-set Grassy Terrain; no action was ever directed at Rillaboom, which then killed Milotic and Kingambit.
analysis.howToImprove: A) FLASH FIRE / IMMUNITY AUDIT: the moment an opposing mon activates Flash Fire (or Water Absorb / Volt Absorb / Levitate), hard-flag Drogon's Fire moves as dead against that slot and re-evaluate whether Drogon should remain the primary attacker at all. Against a Flash Fire Flareon, Drogon is a liability, not a win-con — pivot to Garchomp/Milotic/Kingambit. B) TAILWIND BY TURN 3: never let three turns pass with a Tailwind user on the bench and no field control. If Whimsicott is on the bench at the end of turn 2 with no Trick Room up, bring it in on turn 3 at full HP, not at 1 HP on turn 5. C) PIVOT TARGET SELECTION: when switching away from a threatened slot, send in the piece that survives the incoming attack, not the most 'useful' piece. Whimsicott should never be the pivot into a revealed Fire/spread attacker. D) MEGA PRESERVATION: with a revealed 4x-or-boosted threat on the field and our Mega above 40%, if our Mega cannot KO it this turn, Protect it rather than click a 38-69% attack. E) TARGET THE SUPPORT ENGINE: Rillaboom re-set Grassy Terrain twice and was never attacked after turn 3; against Rillaboom, attacking it is what shuts off both terrain and Grassy Glide priority.

proposals.change: FLASH-FIRE / ABSORB AUDIT: when an opposing Pokemon's ability absorbs one of our Mega's STAB types (Flash Fire vs Drogon, Water Absorb/Storm Drain vs Milotic, Volt Absorb vs Raichu etc.), immediately demote that Mega from primary attacker: block its absorbed-type moves against that slot entirely and prefer switching it out or Protecting rather than chipping with its weak coverage move.
proposals.evidence: Flareon got Flash Fire on T1 via a switch-in to Heat Wave; Drogon then had only Ancient Power (38-69%) and spent T4-T5 doing nothing meaningful before being OHKO'd by a Flash-Fire-boosted Flare Blitz.

proposals.change: TAILWIND-BY-TURN-3 HARD RULE: if we own Whimsicott/Dragonite with Tailwind, no Trick Room is up, and we reach the start of turn 3 with 0 Tailwind turns, the next action for that Pokemon must be Tailwind (bring it in on turn 3 at full HP if benched). Never set Tailwind from a 1 HP Sash user as a last resort.
proposals.evidence: Tailwind landed on T5 from a 1 HP Whimsicott; Drogon and Whimsicott both fainted the same turn, so only 3 Tailwind turns existed and only for a chipped Milotic and Kingambit.

proposals.change: PIVOT SURVIVABILITY FILTER: when switching a threatened slot, never select a switch-in whose listed incoming damage is >=90% of its HP. Whimsicott must never be the pivot into a revealed spread/Fire attacker; prefer Kingambit or Garchomp.
proposals.evidence: T4 Milotic->Whimsicott ate Flare Blitz for 136/137 damage, leaving our only speed-control setter at 1 HP before it acted.

proposals.change: TERRAIN-SETTER RE-TARGET: against Rillaboom (Grassy Surge + Grassy Glide + Fake Out), at least one action per turn must be directed at Rillaboom whenever it is on the field; do not spend two consecutive turns aiming at a <35% foe that has already Protected/Detected.
proposals.evidence: Rillaboom re-set Grassy Terrain on T6 and was never attacked after T3; it then KO'd Milotic (Wood Hammer) and Kingambit (High Horsepower).

lessons: Flash Fire (and Water Absorb / Storm Drain / Volt Absorb / Lightning Rod) activating on a switch-in permanently kills that STAB line: re-plan the whole game immediately — Drogon with its Fire moves absorbed is a liability, not a win condition.
Never pivot into a revealed spread or super-effective attacker with Whimsicott: pick the switch-in that survives the hit, not the one with the best move.
If turn 3 arrives with a benched Tailwind user and no field control, bring it in and set Tailwind at full HP — Tailwind set from 1 HP on turn 5 is worth almost nothing.
Do not spend two consecutive turns attacking a sub-35% foe that has already Protected/Detected while its partner freely re-establishes terrain; re-target the support engine.
When our Mega is above 40% and cannot KO the revealed threat in front of it this turn, Protect it instead of clicking a sub-70% coverage move.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 14-14 and was left on the bench entirely this game; a Sitrus Garchomp can take a Grassy-Glide/Wood Hammer turn and stay in as a Rillaboom answer with move freedom (EQ into Flareon/Rillaboom, Rock Slide into Volcarona/Charizard), which is what this loss actually needed.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'immunity ability + priority terrain' engine: give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect for a second speed-control source that is not Prankster-dependent, and seriously test Rotom-Heat or Gholdengo over Whimsicott in Fire-heavy matchups — Whimsicott has now fainted 129 times in 204 games and is the single most fragile piece we own.
teamInspiration.reason: Flareon's Flash Fire turned Drogon off and Rillaboom's Grassy Surge gave permanent priority; we had no non-Prankster speed tool and no Fire-immune body. A Fire-immune/Flash-Fire pivot plus Icy Wind would have let us keep the Mega alive and still move first after Whimsicott died.

analysis.whatWorked: Vs popandpop (WIN, 4 turns): the Kingambit + Drogon lead into a Trick Room/Armor Tail team was correct. Turn 1 Protect on Drogon against a Glimmora holding an unused Mega Stone (Power Gem is 4x on Charizard-Y) was textbook win-con preservation, and Kingambit's Iron Head — chosen over Sucker Punch because Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks priority — put Glimmora to 27% before Toxic Debris/Spiky Shield healed it. Turn 2 Weather Ball in sun OHKO'd Farigiraf, simultaneously removing the Trick Room setter AND the Armor Tail priority blocker, which is the exact 'kill the engine, not the attacker' directive. Turn 3 Iron Head punched through Clefable's Follow Me for the KO and Weather Ball chipped it to 4% first — focus fire on the redirector worked. Opponent forfeited at 2-0 down with us having lost nothing.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) 'A foe that Protects/holds an unused Mega Stone is telegraphing a Mega next turn — reprioritize onto it' — Glimmora was the designated kill target every single turn. (2) 'Protect Drogon turn 1 vs a 4x Rock threat' — exactly what happened, and it also absorbed the Mortal Spin poison attempt. (3) 'Never click Sucker Punch into Armor Tail (Farigiraf)' — the pilot used Iron Head/Kowtow instead for all four turns. (4) 'Kill the support engine' — Farigiraf (TR + Armor Tail) and Clefable (Follow Me) died before the attackers. (5) 'Don't double-Protect with no threat' — only one Protect per turn, always on the genuinely threatened slot.
analysis.whatFailed: Minor: Turn 2 Kingambit's Iron Head hit Glimmora's Spiky Shield — a wasted action plus 25 HP contact recoil. Glimmora at 52% after Toxic-Debris healing had already shown it was the Protect-prone slot, and the Wolfe rule 'the more obvious their Protect is, the more likely they Protect that slot' applied: the correct line was Iron Head into Farigiraf (or Clefable's eventual slot) while Weather Ball handled the other, converting their Protect into a free turn for us instead of for them. Turn 4 double-committed Drogon to Protect again while Kingambit attacked a 52% Glimmora that had Spiky Shielded once already — a second likely-wasted action, saved only by the forfeit. Also, Farigiraf's Trick on turn 1 swapped an item onto Kingambit (likely Choice-locking it); the pilot never accounted for the possible Choice lock in subsequent turns, which was pure luck that Iron Head stayed the right move. Finally, Tailwind was never relevant (Whimsicott/Garchomp unused), fine in a 4-turn win but note 0 Tailwind turns again.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Track Trick: when a foe uses Trick/Switcheroo on our Pokemon, assume that Pokemon is now Choice-locked into its next move and verify the move is still correct for the rest of the game. 2) Anti-Protect-cycling: a foe that has used Protect/Spiky Shield/Detect/King's Shield on turn N should be de-prioritized as a target on turn N+1 only if it already Protected twice; but a foe holding Toxic Debris/Spiky Shield that healed back to >50% should be hit with the spread/secondary slot while the primary attacker handles the other foe. 3) When our Mega is at full HP and the only threat is a sub-50% foe that already Protected, attack instead of Protecting a second consecutive turn. 4) Keep the Kingambit lead vs Armor Tail / Trick Room teams — it is now 4W-2L on 'Charizard|zk' plans and it blanks Psychic/Prankster.

proposals.change: TRICK/SWITCHEROO AUDIT: if an opposing Pokemon used Trick or Switcheroo on one of our Pokemon, treat that Pokemon as potentially Choice-locked from the next turn on; prefer its single best move and re-evaluate switching it out to reset the lock if that move becomes bad.
proposals.evidence: T1 Farigiraf used Trick on Kingambit; the pilot never mentioned or accounted for a possible Choice lock in turns 2-4 and only coincidentally kept clicking Iron Head.

proposals.change: PROTECT-CYCLE TARGETING: do not aim the same attacker at a foe that used Protect/Spiky Shield/Detect last turn when a second live foe exists; redirect that action to the other slot (or to the support/redirection piece) so their Protect costs them a turn instead of us.
proposals.evidence: T2 Kingambit Iron Head hit Glimmora's Spiky Shield for 0 damage plus 25 HP recoil, wasting half our action economy.

proposals.change: SECOND-CONSECUTIVE-PROTECT BAN ON OUR MEGA: if our Mega is above 70% HP and the only threatening foe is below 55% and has already Protected once, attack rather than Protect.
proposals.evidence: T4 Drogon Protected a second time against a 52% Glimmora that had already Spiky Shielded, risking another fully wasted turn.

lessons: When a foe uses Trick or Switcheroo on our Pokemon, assume that Pokemon is now Choice-locked: confirm its best move is repeatable, or switch to reset the lock.
Never aim a contact move at a foe that Protected/Spiky Shielded the previous turn when a second live foe exists — redirect to the other slot so their Protect wastes their turn, not ours.

Killing the support engine (Armor Tail / Trick Room setter, then the Follow Me redirector) before the attackers wins Trick Room games outright: Farigiraf then Clefable went down before Toxapex or Glimmora could do anything.
Protect on Drogon turn 1 against an unused Mega Stone holder with 4x Rock coverage (Glimmora Power Gem) remains a mandatory, game-winning play.

teamInspiration.suggestion: They ran a hazard/chip + redirection + Armor Tail shell (Glimmora Toxic Debris/Spiky Shield, Farigiraf Trick + Armor Tail, Clefable Follow Me). Mirror the redirection half: test Whimsicott with Helping Hand or keep Encore, but more importantly give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so we own a non-Prankster speed-control action that still works when Whimsicott is dead or blocked — and consider Clear Amulet on Kingambit so Trick/Intimidate/stat shenanigans cannot cripple our lead piece.
teamInspiration.reason: Farigiraf's turn-1 Trick onto Kingambit could have Choice-locked our main lead into a bad move for the whole game; a Clear Amulet does not stop Trick but an item we care about losing does matter, and their redirection/disruption engine (Follow Me + Spiky Shield) bought them free turns that only a second speed-control source or an Encore would have punished.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 2 Heat Wave into the 1% opposing Whimsicott secured the KO on their Tailwind setter and the Gallade Protect was correctly ignored by the spread move. Whimsicott's Moonblast finished Mega Gallade on T4. Drogon's Sun Heat Wave again produced the most damage on the team (176%).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Partially. We correctly treated the Mega-Stone holder (Gallade/Galladite) as the primary threat, and we did not click Sucker Punch into anything blocking. But the T1 lead decision was made by the engine fallback (Claude was rate-limited), which violated the hard coach rule 'Never leave Kingambit in front of a revealed Close Combat/Drain Punch Fighting user listed as a 100% OHKO on it' — Kingambit died on turn 1 before acting for the second game in a row. The Tailwind-by-turn-3 rule was also violated: we only clicked Tailwind on T5 from a 1 HP Whimsicott, the exact 'last resort Tailwind' the rule forbids.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Lead Kingambit vs Gallade (Fighting) = instant 0-for-1 action economy loss; Kingambit is 4x-pressured by Drain Punch/Close Combat and contributed zero damage all game. 2) Three consecutive Claude fallbacks (HTTP 429) meant T1, T3 and T4 were engine-piloted: T3 was a DOUBLE PROTECT with no real threat to Whimsicott, donating a free Tailwind turn and a free Mamoswine switch-in; T4 Drogon attacked into a Psycho Cut it could not survive instead of Protecting or switching. 3) We let them hold BOTH speed (Tailwind) and power (Mega Gallade) from T2 onward while we had zero speed control. 4) Whimsicott burned its Sash on Flamethrower and then died to Ice Shard with Tailwind only just set — speed control effectively never existed for us.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block Kingambit as a lead whenever the opponent's revealed team contains a Fighting-type attacker (Gallade, Mamoswine Superpower, Urshifu, Lucario); lead Drogon + Whimsicott or Milotic instead. Ban double-Protect when neither active slot has a listed threat >=60% of its HP. Enforce Tailwind on the first turn Whimsicott is on the field above 50% HP when no Trick Room is up. When the opponent sets Tailwind and we have none, our Mega must prioritize Protect/switch over trading into a faster Mega attacker.

proposals.change: NEVER lead Kingambit when the opponent's preview team contains a Fighting-type attacker (Gallade, Lucario, Urshifu, Conkeldurr, Hariyama) or Mamoswine/Great Tusk with Superpower/Close Combat. Lead Drogon + Whimsicott instead and hold Kingambit for the late game.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit died on turn 1 to Gallade Drain Punch (100%) having done nothing, the second game in a row a Kingambit lead was deleted on turn 1 (Armarouge Armor Cannon vs derek is king).

proposals.change: DOUBLE-PROTECT BAN: forbid Protect on both slots on the same turn unless both actives have a listed incoming threat >= 60% of max HP or we are stalling the final turn of an opposing field effect.
proposals.evidence: Turn 3's engine double Protect gave the opponent a free Mamoswine entry turn and burned one of our only pre-Tailwind turns while neither slot was actually in KO range.

proposals.change: TAILWIND-AT-FULL-HP: the first turn Whimsicott is on the field above 50% HP with no Trick Room active and 0 Tailwind turns, Tailwind is mandatory unless it would be KO'd through Sash that same turn by a spread move.
proposals.evidence: We set Tailwind on turn 5 from 1 HP, it provided zero turns of value, and the opponent held Tailwind from turn 2.

lessons: Never lead Kingambit into a revealed Fighting-type attacker (Gallade, Urshifu, Lucario) or a Superpower/Close Combat user — it dies before acting and surrenders half the turn's action economy.
Double Protect with no listed OHKO threat on either slot is a donated turn: it gave the opponent a free switch-in and a free Tailwind turn.
When the opponent gains Tailwind and we have none, stop trading with our Mega into their faster Mega — Protect or pivot until their 4 turns expire.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 15-15 and provides no speed control when Whimsicott dies early; Sitrus gives a bulkier Ground attacker that survives Fighting/Ice chip and can stay in as the late-game answer in matchups where our Tailwind never lands.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Beat Up + Mega Gallade' burst engine conceptually: the key is that their support Pokemon (Whimsicott) spent turn 1 making their attacker stronger instead of setting Tailwind. Give our Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so we own a non-Prankster speed-control action, and consider swapping Kingambit for a Fighting-resistant pivot (Gholdengo or Corviknight) in matchups with Gallade/Urshifu/Mamoswine.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Kingambit has now been turn-1 KO'd by Fighting and Fire coverage in back-to-back games; and our only speed control (Whimsicott Tailwind) failed to fire again, losing the speed-and-power race from turn 2.

whatWorked: Turn-1 focus fire on Runerigus was correct and decisive: Kowtow Cleave + Dragon Pulse removed the Body Press/Trick Room-capable Ghost before it could act, and the opponent forfeited immediately (win in 1 turn). Mega Dragonite evolved turn 1 at full HP with Multiscale intact, and Kingambit was correctly positioned as a Dark attacker against a Ghost lead (immune to Runerigus's likely Psychic/Normal utility). The preview call (Kingambit + Dragonite front, Whimsicott/Garchomp back) was a reasonable anti-Trick Room shell even though it came from the engine fallback after a rate-limit error.
lessonsApplied: Applied: 'focus fire the Trick Room setter / the foe that threatens our lead before it moves' — Runerigus was the Body Press threat listed at 56-83% on Kingambit and died first. Applied: Mega evolved on turn 1 to bank the Multiscale/stat boost. Applied: no Sucker Punch clicked (Kowtow Cleave is the correct, unblockable pick). Not tested this game: Tailwind timing, Protect discipline, double-Protect ban — the game ended too early. One standing rule was unverified rather than violated: the preview call was a FALLBACK because of an HTTP 429 rate limit, meaning our lead was chosen without reading that Lucario (Fighting) was on their preview team — the 'never lead Kingambit into a revealed Fighting attacker' rule would have flagged Lucario, and Clawitzer's Ice Beam was listed as an 86-152% OHKO on Dragonite.
whatFailed: Nothing in-game failed — the opponent conceded on turn 1. The real failure is infrastructural and preview-level: (1) the Preview Claude call fell back to the engine due to a rate limit, so Kingambit was led into a team containing Lucario (Fighting) in direct violation of our own standing preview rule; we got lucky that they led Runerigus + Clawitzer instead. (2) Dragonite was exposed on turn 1 to a listed 86-152% OHKO from Clawitzer Ice Beam — our Mega win-condition was in front of a 79% OHKO chance on turn 1, which contradicts 'shelter the win-con in the back.' (3) We also learned nothing about the matchup: a 1-turn win provides no scouting data, so no behavioural adjustment is possible. (4) Clawitzer used Flip Turn + Skill Swap — a Mega Launcher Skill Swap pattern we should log, since Skill Swap near Malamar-style teams signals Contrary shenanigans.
howToImprove: 1) Harden the preview path: when the Claude preview call fails (HTTP 429), the engine fallback must still apply the hard preview rules — never lead Kingambit when a Fighting-type (Lucario, Gallade, Urshifu, Conkeldurr) is in opponent preview, and never lead the Mega into a listed turn-1 OHKO. 2) Prefer Charizard-Y or Whimsicott alongside Kingambit against mixed Ghost/Water teams rather than exposing Mega Dragonite to Ice Beam on turn 1. 3) Against Clawitzer specifically (Mega Launcher: Aura Sphere / Dark Pulse / Water Pulse / Ice Beam) treat it as a special nuker that OHKOs Dragonite — Kingambit resists Dark Pulse but dies to Aura Sphere; Milotic is the safe pivot. 4) Keep the Kowtow-Cleave-over-Sucker-Punch default under Trick Room and against Armor Tail (Farigiraf was on their bench).

proposals.change: FALLBACK PREVIEW GUARDRAILS: when the Claude preview call errors out, the engine fallback must still enforce (a) no Kingambit lead if any Fighting-type is in opponent preview, (b) no Mega lead into a foe with a listed >=90% OHKO. Encode as a hard filter in getLeadPreference rather than relying on the LLM.
proposals.evidence: vs graffetti the preview was a 429 fallback; Kingambit was led into a team with Lucario and Mega Dragonite was led into Clawitzer Ice Beam (86-152%, 79% OHKO). We won only because they led Runerigus + Clawitzer and conceded.

proposals.change: SKILL SWAP WATCH: when an opposing Pokemon uses Skill Swap (Clawitzer did on turn 1), flag a possible Contrary/ability-transfer plan and record which ally received it; never assume the receiving Pokemon's stat-drop moves are drawbacks.
proposals.evidence: T1 log: |-activate|p2b: Clawitzer|Skill Swap| followed immediately by a switch to Lucario — the ability transfer was hidden by the ally-swap hint.

proposals.change: MEGA-LAUNCHER THREAT TAG: tag Clawitzer as a special nuker whose Ice Beam/Aura Sphere OHKOs Dragonite and Kingambit respectively; route Milotic or Charizard-Y in front of it instead of our Mega.
proposals.evidence: Threat line: Dragonite threatened by Clawitzer Ice Beam (86-152% (OHKO 79%)).

lessons: When the preview LLM call fails and the engine fallback picks the lead, the hard preview rules (no Kingambit into Fighting types, no Mega into a listed turn-1 OHKO) must still be enforced in code — a lucky concession is not validation of the lead.
Clawitzer (Mega Launcher) OHKOs Mega Dragonite with Ice Beam and Kingambit with Aura Sphere: it is a win-condition-level special attacker, not a support Water type.
An opposing Skill Swap aimed at an ally is an ability-transfer tell (Contrary/Mega Launcher/Flash Fire); log it and re-evaluate that ally's stat-drop moves as boosts.

teamInspiration.suggestion: They paired Runerigus (Body Press / possible Trick Room) with Clawitzer running Flip Turn + Skill Swap — a pivot that both chips, repositions, and hands out Mega Launcher/abilities. Mirror the pivot half: give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so we own a non-Prankster speed-control action AND a momentum tool when Whimsicott is dead; and keep Garchomp on Choice Scarf since it is our only answer to fast special pivots once Tailwind is gone.
teamInspiration.reason: Our only speed control is Prankster Tailwind on a Focus-Sash Whimsicott that has now fainted 130 times in 207 games. Clawitzer's Flip Turn showed how cheaply a team can generate free positioning; Icy Wind on bulky Milotic gives us a second speed source that survives Fake Out and works against Dark types where Prankster fails.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Kingambit lead into Psychic Terrain was textbook: Kingambit is immune to Expanding Force/Psychic and Iron Head OHKO'd the Follow-Me'd Indeedee-F (terrain setter) immediately, removing Psychic Terrain. Turn 2 under their own Trick Room, our slow Kingambit moved FIRST and Iron Head OHKO'd Mega Gardevoir (the flagged two-for-one Expanding Force win-con) while Drogon's sun Weather Ball OHKO'd their Kingambit — a double KO that put us 4v2. Endgame Milotic (Leftovers + Recover + Scald) out-sustained Torkoal and closed the game; Whimsicott Protect-cycling at 1 HP correctly preserved a body and avoided feeding Eruption.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) kill the TERRAIN SETTER first, not the Expanding Force attacker — Indeedee died turn 1; (2) treat a revealed Gardevoirite as the win condition and delete it the moment it Megas — done turn 2; (3) Kingambit thrives under Trick Room, use Iron Head/Kowtow rather than Sucker Punch — Sucker Punch was correctly never clicked into Psychic Terrain; (4) no double-Protect donation turns; (5) Protect the 1 HP Whimsicott only when a listed OHKO threat (Eruption) existed. Violated: the turn-3 line left BOTH Kingambit and Drogon in front of a freshly-switched Torkoal whose Eruption was explicitly listed as a 100-152% KO on Kingambit and a spread move — that is the 'never leave a piece in front of a listed OHKO' rule, and it cost us two Pokemon in one action.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 3 was the only real misplay and it was large: Torkoal switched in at full HP under THEIR Trick Room, meaning Torkoal (base 20 Spe) moved first with a full-power spread Eruption. Our calc explicitly showed Eruption 100-152% KO on Kingambit, yet we chose to focus-fire Torkoal with Kowtow Cleave (37-54%) + Ancient Power (50-78%) — a range that only KO'd on a high-high roll, i.e. a coin flip for the whole board. Because Eruption is a SPREAD move and we moved second, the wrong roll lost Kingambit AND Drogon simultaneously (a two-for-one in their favour, the exact pattern we flag against Expanding Force). The safe line was Drogon Protect (Eruption is only 23-41% on it anyway after the KO we had already banked) or switching Kingambit out while Drogon Ancient Power chipped. Also, Drogon took 67% from their Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave on turn 2 — acceptable trade, but it is what put Drogon into Eruption range. Minor: Whimsicott again never set Tailwind the whole game (0 Tailwind turns in a won game, but the pattern repeats).
analysis.howToImprove: Rule: under an ACTIVE opposing Trick Room, any freshly-switched-in slow foe moves FIRST — treat its biggest spread move as guaranteed damage and never leave two of our Pokemon in its spread range on a non-guaranteed-KO turn. If combined damage on the slow foe is under ~100% at MINIMUM roll, Protect the piece that dies or pivot it out instead of gambling. Specifically: when a Fire type with Eruption/Heat Wave/Blizzard switches in under TR, Protect the lower-HP slot. Second: when the opponent is reduced to one Pokemon and we are ahead 4v1, zero risk lines only — Protect + chip, never a 50% KO roll that loses two mons on failure. Third: Whimsicott must fire Tailwind the first safe turn it is on the field; it entered on turn 3 and never used it.

proposals.change: SPREAD-UNDER-TRICK-ROOM GUARD: while an opposing Trick Room is active and a slow foe (base Spe <= 60) just switched in with a known/likely spread move (Eruption, Heat Wave, Blizzard, Earthquake, Hyper Voice, Make It Rain), do not leave both our actives in range. If the combined damage of our two attacks on that foe does not KO at MINIMUM roll, Protect or switch the slot listed as being KO'd.
proposals.evidence: T3 vs Akromancer: Torkoal switched in, moved first under their TR, and Eruption KO'd both Kingambit (100-152% listed) and Drogon (23-41% but Drogon was at 33%) in one action because our focus-fire only did 87-132% (non-guaranteed).

proposals.change: NO-GAMBLE-WHEN-AHEAD: when we have >= 3 alive and the opponent has <= 2 alive, forbid any line whose KO is not guaranteed at minimum roll if failing that roll exposes two of our actives to a spread OHKO. Prefer Protect + single-target chip.
proposals.evidence: We were 4v1-equivalent on T3 (they had Torkoal + one benched) and still took a coin-flip KO line that cost two Pokemon.

proposals.change: ERUPTION/WATER SPOUT HP RULE: a Torkoal/Volcarona-style Eruption user at full HP deals full power; chipping it even 20-30% materially reduces the spread threat. Prefer a guaranteed-chip + Protect turn over an unguaranteed KO turn against Eruption users.
proposals.evidence: Torkoal at 100% did ~81% to Kingambit and ~100% of Drogon's remaining HP; after chip to 66% its Eruption was survivable by Milotic (19-24%).

lessons: Under an opposing Trick Room, a slow foe that just switched in moves FIRST next turn — treat its spread move as guaranteed and never leave two of our actives inside it on a coin-flip KO turn.
If our combined damage on a threatening foe is not lethal at the MINIMUM roll, do not focus-fire it when the failure case is a spread two-for-one; Protect the threatened slot instead.
When ahead 4v2 or better, every line must be variance-free: no 50% KO rolls that cost two Pokemon if they fail.
Eruption/Water Spout users at full HP are spread OHKO threats; chip them first, then attack — the power scales with their current HP.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep the current loadout: Scarf Garchomp remains our only non-Prankster speed answer and this loss pattern was a Trick Room spread issue, not an item issue.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Follow Me + Trick Room + full-HP Eruption' engine conceptually: the Torkoal slot alone nearly reversed a 4v2. Give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so we own a non-Prankster speed-control action AND a way to undo Trick Room speed order pressure, and consider Heat Wave -> Protect is already present on Drogon; most importantly keep a Fire-resistant body (Milotic/Garchomp) on the field whenever a Torkoal/Eruption user is alive.
teamInspiration.reason: Indeedee Follow Me bought Gardevoir a free Trick Room turn, and Torkoal's full-HP Eruption under TR took two of our Pokemon in a single action. Our team has no spread-damage insurance and no second speed-control source once Whimsicott is sidelined (it has fainted 130 times in 208 games).

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Protect on Drogon against Aerodactyl (4x Rock, faster) was correct in isolation, and Kingambit's Iron Head guaranteed the KO on Sylveon. Identifying Lucario-Mega-Z as the win condition was correct.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Protect-Drogon-vs-Rock-turn-1 rule was followed. The 'focus the Mega Stone holder' rule was partially followed (Lucario targeted). But the double-Protect ban and the 'never Earthquake next to Kingambit' standing rule were both violated, and Tailwind was set 3 turns too late.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 2: Drogon stood in front of a revealed Aerodactyl Rock Slide (listed 268-367% OHKO) and used Heat Wave instead of Protecting or switching — Kingambit Protected the slot that was NOT threatened and Drogon died. This is a pure slot-assignment blunder: the Protect went on the wrong Pokemon. 2) Turn 3: Garchomp Earthquake was clicked with Kingambit adjacent, violating the hard team rule; Lucario Detected, Aerodactyl was immune, and the ONLY thing EQ hit was our own Kingambit, killing it. That turn produced -1 of our own Pokemon and 0 damage to them. 3) Turn 4: Earthquake clicked again next to Whimsicott, chipping our own Tailwind setter 30% while Aerodactyl stayed immune. 4) Tailwind was set on turn 4 with 2 mons left instead of turn 1-2. 5) Garchomp was Choice-locked into Earthquake, the single worst move on a board with a Flying-type Aerodactyl.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block Earthquake whenever a Ground-immune foe (Flying/Levitate) is active AND an ally is grounded — it is strictly a self-damage move. Assign Protect to the slot that is actually listed as being OHKO'd, never to its partner. Against a faster Rock/Flying attacker like Aerodactyl, pivot Drogon out rather than trading. Lead Whimsicott for turn-1 Tailwind when the opponent has Aerodactyl/Staraptor-tier speed.

proposals.change: EARTHQUAKE SELF-HARM BAN: block Garchomp Earthquake entirely when (a) any grounded ally is on the field AND (b) every live opposing active is Ground-immune (Flying/Levitate/Air Balloon) or protected-likely. Use Dragon Claw/Rock Slide/Stomping Tantrum instead.
proposals.evidence: T3 EQ hit only our own Kingambit (Aerodactyl immune, Lucario Detected) and killed it; T4 EQ chipped our own Whimsicott 30% for 0 relevant value.

proposals.change: PROTECT-THE-THREATENED-SLOT RULE: Protect must be assigned to the active listed with the highest incoming OHKO percentage. Never Protect a slot whose listed threat is lower than its partner's while the partner stays exposed.
proposals.evidence: T2 Kingambit (threatened 118-180%) Protected while Drogon (threatened 268-367% OHKO by Aerodactyl Rock Slide) attacked and died.

proposals.change: When the opponent's preview contains Aerodactyl / Staraptor-Mega / any Rock Slide + Flying user, do not lead Drogon at all — lead Whimsicott (turn-1 Tailwind) + Kingambit and keep Drogon in the back.
proposals.evidence: Drogon was Protected turn 1 then immediately OHKO'd turn 2 by Rock Slide; it contributed 0 damage all game.

lessons: Earthquake into a board where the only live foes are Ground-immune (Aerodactyl) or likely to Protect is a pure self-KO: it hit only our own Kingambit and lost us the game.
Protect belongs on the Pokemon listed with the largest incoming OHKO, not on its partner — Kingambit Protected while Drogon ate a 268-367% Rock Slide.
Choice-Scarf Garchomp locked into Earthquake against a Flying-type is dead weight; switch to reset the lock instead of re-clicking the immune move.
Set Tailwind on turn 1-2 while Whimsicott is at full HP; Tailwind on turn 4 at 2-mons-left changed nothing.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice-lock on Earthquake into a Flying-type foe directly lost this game; Sitrus Garchomp keeps move freedom (Rock Slide vs Aerodactyl) and survives a hit.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'fast Rock Slide Flying + Mega Fighting closer' pressure: give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect for a non-Prankster speed source, and strongly consider Rock Slide-proofing by leading Whimsicott + Kingambit with Drogon in the back whenever Aerodactyl/Staraptor is previewed.
teamInspiration.reason: Aerodactyl alone invalidated Drogon (4x Rock, faster) and forced two Protect turns, while Lucario-Mega-Z Detect blanked our only offensive turn. A second speed-control action and a Drogon-free lead would have denied them both speed and power.

analysis.whatWorked: Won in 2 turns vs wally123 (psyterrain/rain hybrid). Both Claude overrides were correct: T1 Kowtow Cleave guaranteed the KO on Ceruledge at minimum roll (108-164%) even through its Swords Dance, denying a +2 sweeper, while Whimsicott set Tailwind at FULL HP on turn 1 — exactly the standing coach rule ('set Tailwind turn 1-2 while Whimsicott is at full HP'). Kingambit's Poison immunity blanked Glimmora's Sludge Wave entirely, a free action-economy win from the lead choice. T2 correctly pivoted a 1-HP Whimsicott out rather than donating it, while Kowtow Cleave targeted the Trick Room setter Sinistcha (75% OHKO) — killing the support engine first.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) punish setup immediately — Ceruledge used Swords Dance and was KO'd that same turn rather than being Protect-stalled; (2) Tailwind on turn 1 at full HP; (3) switch out a Pokemon about to be KO'd (1 HP Whimsicott -> Garchomp); (4) kill the support/TR engine (Sinistcha) before the attackers; (5) Drogon kept in the back away from Glimmora Power Gem / Politoed rain, per the standing anti-Rock preview rule; (6) no Mega was burned early, keeping the option open.
analysis.whatFailed: Almost nothing in-game. Minor: the lead exposed Whimsicott to a Glimmora spread (Sludge Wave took it to 1 HP) — the preview note anticipated Sludge Bomb OHKO yet we still led Whimsicott beside a Poison spread attacker, so the Focus Sash was consumed turn 1 and Whimsicott could only ever provide one more action. A Kingambit + Garchomp or Kingambit + Drogon-in-back lead with Whimsicott entering later would have preserved the Sash. Also the T1 calc preview underestimated Glimmora: it listed Sludge Bomb, not the spread Sludge Wave, so our threat model under-counted the spread damage.
analysis.howToImprove: When the opposing lead contains a known spread attacker (Glimmora Sludge Wave/Bomb, Gardevoir Hyper Voice, Torkoal Eruption), treat Whimsicott's Focus Sash as already spent for threat purposes: either lead Whimsicott only when we expect single-target pressure, or accept the Sash trade only if Tailwind turn 1 is genuinely needed. Also add Glimmora to the explicit spread-threat tag list, and keep the rule that a Poison/Ground-immune body (Kingambit) beside Whimsicott absorbs half the spread.

proposals.change: SPREAD-ATTACKER SASH GUARD: when an opposing lead has a revealed/likely spread move (Sludge Wave, Hyper Voice, Heat Wave, Eruption, Dazzling Gleam, Make It Rain, Blizzard, Earthquake, Rock Slide), treat Whimsicott's Focus Sash as consumed on turn 1. Only lead Whimsicott if Tailwind turn 1 is the game plan; otherwise bring it in later.
proposals.evidence: Glimmora Sludge Wave dropped Whimsicott 137->1 on turn 1; it could never act again and had to be pivoted out on turn 2.

proposals.change: GLIMMORA TAG: treat Glimmora as a 4x-Rock-coverage Power Gem + spread Poison threat and a Mega Stone candidate — never lead Drogon into it, and prefer Kingambit (Poison-immune) in the slot beside our support.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit was immune to Sludge Wave, converting Glimmora's whole turn into a half-action.

proposals.change: Keep the 'KO the setup user at min-roll instead of Protecting' rule as a hard scoring boost: Ceruledge Swords Dance was punished same-turn and the game ended immediately.
proposals.evidence: T1 Kowtow Cleave 108-164% min-roll OHKO on a +2 Ceruledge.

lessons: Kingambit beside Whimsicott absorbs Poison spread moves (Sludge Wave/Bomb) for free — a strong lead pairing vs Glimmora/Toxapex cores.
Against a revealed spread attacker on their lead, Whimsicott's Focus Sash should be considered already spent; plan its Tailwind for turn 1 or keep it in the back.
Punishing setup (Swords Dance Ceruledge) with a guaranteed min-roll KO on the same turn remains the highest-value line — it ended the game in two turns.

teamInspiration.suggestion: They paired Glimmora (spread Poison + hazards + Power Gem) with Ceruledge Swords Dance behind Politoed/Sinistcha — a 'chip everything, then one setup sweeper closes' shell. Mirror the chip half: give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect for a non-Prankster speed-control action that survives spread damage, and consider Safety Goggles or a bulkier item test on Whimsicott in spread-heavy metas since its Focus Sash is consumed by any spread move on turn 1.
teamInspiration.reason: Whimsicott has now fainted 131 times in 210 games, usually after its Sash is popped by a spread attack on turn 1, leaving us with one speed-control action per game. A second speed source on a bulky body (Milotic Icy Wind) would survive the spread chip that erases Whimsicott.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 Protect on Drogon against Mega Garchomp's 4x-effective Power Gem/Rock Slide was correct and saved the Mega for the endgame. Switching Drogon out on turn 2 instead of trading into a faster Mega Garchomp was right. Garchomp Stomping Tantrum removed Slowking-Galar (the Trick Room/Helping Hand support) cleanly, and Drogon's Weather Ball in restored Sun eventually removed Pelipper, cancelling Drizzle.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Protect-the-threatened-slot was followed (Drogon, not Kingambit). The Drought-resets-rain plan from preview was sound. However the 'spread-attacker Sash guard' lesson was violated in spirit: Whimsicott was led into Toxicroak (Fake Out + Gunk Shot) and spent turn 1 flinched, then died on turn 2 before Tailwind mattered — exactly the failure mode flagged in the last five reviews (Whimsicott 132 faints / 211 games).
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Lead: Whimsicott + Drogon into a Fake Out user (Toxicroak) and a Mega Garchomp meant our only speed control was Fake-Out-blanked on turn 1 and dead on turn 2; Tailwind was set at the cost of Whimsicott's entire life for 3 turns of mostly-wasted speed. 2) Turn 3: we attacked the freshly switched-in Slowking with BOTH attackers (Stomping Tantrum + Iron Head) leaving Pelipper completely free to set Tailwind — we handed the opponent speed AND power simultaneously, the single rule we must never break. Pelipper was the win condition (rain + Tailwind + Weather Ball), not Slowking. 3) Turn 5: Garchomp was choice-locked-equivalent into Stomping Tantrum against Levitate Garchomp and a Flying Pelipper, firing a 0% move — a fully wasted action (the engine even predicted 0-0%). 4) Turn 6: same thing again — Stomping Tantrum listed at 0-0% into Pelipper was clicked a second time while Garchomp sat in front of a Draco Meteor OHKO; we should have switched Garchomp out (Scarf lock reset) or clicked Rock Slide which hits both Pelipper and nothing-immune. That is two donated turns in a row against a 0% move.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-ban any move whose computed damage range is 0-0% against every legal target — switch or pick a different move instead. Against rain, kill the rain/Tailwind engine (Pelipper) first even if a chip target looks juicier: Kowtow Cleave + Stomping Tantrum on Pelipper turn 3 would have removed Drizzle, Tailwind and Weather Ball in one action pair. Do not lead Whimsicott when a Fake Out user (Toxicroak, Incineroar, Rillaboom) is previewed alongside a faster Mega — bring Whimsicott as the third/fourth slot and lead Kingambit + Drogon or Kingambit + Milotic.

proposals.change: ZERO-DAMAGE MOVE BAN: block any attacking move whose predicted damage is 0% (type immunity: Ground into Flying/Levitate, Normal/Fighting into Ghost, Electric into Ground) against the chosen target; if all targets are immune, force a switch or a different move.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp clicked Stomping Tantrum into Pelipper (Flying) on T5 and again on T6 with the calc showing 0-0% — two consecutive donated turns in a 2-mon endgame.

proposals.change: RAIN ENGINE PRIORITY: when the opponent has an active Drizzle setter (Pelipper/Politoed) that has not yet used Tailwind, focus-fire the setter, not a switched-in support Pokemon. Removing Drizzle also halves Weather Ball and restores our Sun.
proposals.evidence: T3 both attackers hit Slowking (freshly switched in) while Pelipper set Tailwind unopposed; Pelipper then Weather-Balled Kingambit from 100% to 30% to 0% and we never recovered.

proposals.change: Do not lead Whimsicott when the opponent previews a Fake Out user (Toxicroak, Incineroar, Rillaboom, Mienshao) together with a faster Mega. Lead Kingambit + Drogon/Milotic and hold Whimsicott for turn 3+.
proposals.evidence: Toxicroak Fake Out flinched Whimsicott turn 1, Gunk Shot KO'd it turn 2; Tailwind existed for 3 turns but we had no fast attacker alive to use it.

lessons: Never click a move the damage calc lists at 0-0% — type immunity makes it a donated action; switch (resetting any Choice lock) or pick a move that can hit something.
Against rain, the Drizzle setter (Pelipper/Politoed) is the win condition: focus-fire it before any switched-in support, because it carries weather, Tailwind and Weather Ball at once.
Do not lead Whimsicott into a previewed Fake Out user plus a faster Mega — the Sash and the turn are both spent before Tailwind can pay off.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp spent the endgame locked-in-practice into a Ground move against two Ground-immune foes (Levitate Mega Garchomp, Flying Pelipper). A Sitrus set keeps move flexibility (Rock Slide hits both) and extra longevity against rain Weather Ball chip.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'weather setter also carries the speed control' efficiency: give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so a bulky, Fake-Out-proof body owns a second speed-control action, and consider Rock Slide staying mandatory on Garchomp as the anti-Flying/anti-rain click.
teamInspiration.reason: Pelipper provided Drizzle, Tailwind and a STAB-boosted Weather Ball from one slot while our single speed source (Focus Sash Whimsicott) was deleted by Fake Out + Gunk Shot in two turns. Whimsicott has now fainted 132 times in 211 games; we need speed control that survives spread damage and priority.

analysis.whatWorked: Won in 3 turns vs savaqa's sand team. The Mega Charizard + Whimsicott Tailwind lead (the simulation-confirmed 70.7% plan vs sand) was correct. Turn 1 Weather Ball in Drought sun OHKO'd Sneasler (the Fake Out/Dire Claw threat) despite the damage preview badly underestimating it. Turn 2 Protect on Drogon at 37% denied Mega Garchomp's Dragon Pulse and bought the Tailwind turn. Turn 3 focus-fire (Dragon Claw + Weather Ball) removed Mega Garchomp-Z, the only remaining Power Gem OHKO threat on Drogon, before it could act under Tailwind.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) 'Protect Drogon vs sand / 4x-Rock coverage' — Protect on turn 2 saved the Mega; (2) 'set Tailwind turn 1 while Whimsicott is at full HP' — attempted turn 1, succeeded turn 2; (3) 'focus-fire the foe that OHKOs our Mega' — Mega Garchomp was double-targeted and removed; (4) PROTECT-THE-THREATENED-SLOT — Protect went on Drogon (75-125% listed) not Whimsicott (21-42%). Violated/ignored: the SPREAD-ATTACKER SASH GUARD and 'don't lead Whimsicott into a revealed Fake Out user' guidance — Sneasler's Fake Out was previewed and it wasted Whimsicott's turn-1 Tailwind, then Rotom Overheat killed it on turn 2 after the Sash was already burned by Fake Out chip.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn-1 Tailwind was blanked by Sneasler Fake Out: Whimsicott lost its action and its Sash buffer, then died to Overheat on turn 2 — our only speed source gone by turn 2 for the 133rd time in 213 games. Leading a Fake-Out-vulnerable Prankster setter opposite a previewed Fake Out user is the known failure pattern. 2) Severe damage-calc miscalibration again: Weather Ball on Sneasler was predicted 13-25% and dealt 100%. A 4x-underestimated calc means our move selection is running on bad numbers; if the engine had believed the real number it would never have considered an alternative. 3) Turn 2 we left Whimsicott exposed with no Protect while it was the slot with the lower listed threat but the actual fatal one (Rotom Overheat was not in the threat list at all because Rotom had switched out and back). Threat lists built only from currently-active foes under-report switch-back attackers.
analysis.howToImprove: Against previewed Fake Out users (Sneasler, Toxicroak, Incineroar, Rillaboom, Mienshao), either lead Whimsicott with the expectation that Tailwind lands on turn 2 and plan the Protect accordingly, or lead Kingambit/Drogon and bring Whimsicott in once the Fake Out is spent. Second: when a foe that was previously active switched out, keep its revealed moves in the threat model for the slot it can return to. Third: treat the internal damage preview as a lower bound when the mon is our Mega in its own weather (Drought Weather Ball, sun Heat Wave) — the sun/Mega boost appears to be missing from some calc paths, so never pass up a Weather Ball in sun because the calc says 13%.

proposals.change: FAKE-OUT-SPENT TRACKING: once a previewed Fake Out user is on the field opposite Whimsicott on turn 1, assume Whimsicott's turn-1 action is lost. Either (a) lead Whimsicott only if Tailwind on turn 2 still wins, or (b) have the partner Protect and Whimsicott set Tailwind turn 1 anyway, but plan Whimsicott's Protect for turn 2 when its Sash is already chipped.
proposals.evidence: Sneasler Fake Out flinched Whimsicott turn 1 (Tailwind lost), chip removed the Sash buffer, Rotom Overheat KO'd it turn 2 before Tailwind landed a second time.

proposals.change: SWITCH-BACK THREAT MEMORY: include revealed moves of foes that are benched but can return (especially Volt Switch/U-turn pivots that just left) in the threat list for both our slots, so Protect allocation isn't driven only by currently-active foes.
proposals.evidence: Rotom-Heat Volt Switched out turn 1 and came back in turn 2; its Overheat (which KO'd Whimsicott) never appeared in the turn-2 threat list, so Whimsicott was left unprotected.

proposals.change: SUN WEATHER-BALL CALC FLOOR: when Drogon is in its own Drought sun, never discard Weather Ball on the grounds of a low predicted roll — treat the predicted damage as at least 2x the listed value (Fire-type 100 BP STAB + 1.5x sun + Mega SpA).
proposals.evidence: T1 Weather Ball -> Sneasler predicted 8-25%, actual 100% OHKO; identical miscalibration appeared vs Indeedee (predicted 8-12%, actual 68%).

lessons: Against a previewed Fake Out user, Whimsicott's turn-1 Tailwind is a coin flip: either accept the delay and protect it turn 2, or bring it in after the Fake Out is spent.
A foe that Volt Switched/U-turned out is still a live threat to the slot it returns to — keep its revealed moves in the Protect calculus.
Our internal damage preview badly underestimates Charizard-Y Weather Ball in its own Drought sun; treat sun Weather Ball as a likely OHKO on anything neutral and frail.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again provided the decisive second attack on Mega Garchomp-Z under Tailwind; 19-17 record remains the best variant. Keep it while we test Whimsicott survivability fixes.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their Rotom-Heat used Volt Switch to pivot freely and then came back to delete Whimsicott with Overheat — one slot provided chip, momentum and a KO. Mirror this by giving Milotic Icy Wind over Protect: a bulky, Fake-Out-proof, Dark-immune-proof second speed-control source that survives the spread/pivot chip that erases Whimsicott (133 faints in 213 games).
teamInspiration.reason: Our only speed control is a Focus Sash Prankster that dies on turn 1-2 to Fake Out + any chip; a second non-Prankster speed source on a bulky body would keep speed control alive after Whimsicott falls.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 was correct: Protect on Kingambit denied Torkoal's Eruption OHKO while Mega Drogon's Heat Wave took Venusaur to 1 HP (Sash) and chipped Torkoal, and Drought flipped the weather to sun so Politoed's rain had to be re-set. Turn 2's engine fallback Sucker Punch did pick up the Venusaur KO. Turn 4 focus-fire on Torkoal (Stomping Tantrum + Ancient Power) removed the Eruption threat exactly as the 'kill the spread engine' rule prescribes.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: Protect the Eruption-threatened slot; Kingambit lead vs a previewed Indeedee/Trick Room team; focus-firing a full-HP Eruption user; chipping the Drizzle setter. Violated: we never set Tailwind at all (0 Tailwind turns in a 7-turn game) despite Whimsicott being in the back untouched until turn 6 — our only speed control sat unused while Mega Dragonite outsped and Hurricane'd three of our Pokemon. We also let the opponent hold BOTH speed and power: Mega Dragonite (faster, 110 BP spread Hurricane in rain = 100% accurate) was never pressured even once, and we never considered switching Drogon out instead of Protect-cycling it at 37%.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Target selection collapse: Mega Dragonite was the opponent's single win condition from turn 3 onward (Flamethrower KO'd Kingambit, Hurricane KO'd Garchomp, Drogon and Whimsicott) and we never attacked it once. Every turn from 4-6 we spent actions on Torkoal/Politoed — passive supports — while the sweeper boarded free KOs. 2) Drogon was Protect-cycled at 37% on T3 and T5 instead of being switched out to preserve it; it died anyway on T6 for zero value. 3) Turn 6 we split Moonblast + Weather Ball into a 32% Politoed (overkill by a wide margin — Moonblast alone was lethal) instead of putting Drogon's Weather Ball into Mega Dragonite in sun. 4) No Tailwind the entire game, so in rain with Hurricane 100% accurate we were slower and weaker simultaneously. 5) The engine-fallback turn 2 (rate limit) wasted the only window to click Kowtow Cleave into Politoed before the rain re-set.
analysis.howToImprove: Rule: once an opposing Mega evolves and scores a KO, it becomes the designated win condition — all subsequent focus-fire goes there unless a lethal spread (full-HP Eruption) is live this exact turn. Rule: if Whimsicott is on the bench and no Tailwind has been set by turn 3 while a faster foe is scoring KOs, bring Whimsicott in on a Protect turn instead of Protect-cycling a 37% Drogon. Rule: never spend two actions on a target one action already KOs (Politoed at 32% vs Moonblast). Rule: a Mega with 4x-neutral spread Flying STAB in rain (Hurricane) should be assumed 100% accurate — do not Protect-stall a 37% Mega against it, switch instead.

proposals.change: MEGA WIN-CON FOCUS: once an opposing Pokemon has Mega Evolved AND scored at least one KO, flag it as the designated win condition; add a large scoring bonus to moves targeting it and a penalty to moves targeting any non-boosted, non-spread-threat support foe, unless a full-HP Eruption/Water Spout user is active this turn.
proposals.evidence: Mega Dragonite KO'd Kingambit (T3), Garchomp (T5), Drogon (T6) and Whimsicott (T7) and we never targeted it a single time; all four of our Pokemon died to the same foe.

proposals.change: UNUSED-TAILWIND ESCALATION: if Whimsicott is alive on the bench, we have 0 Tailwind turns, and turn >= 3 with an opposing foe faster than our active slots, prefer switching the threatened slot to Whimsicott over Protect-cycling it.
proposals.evidence: 0 Tailwind turns in a 7-turn loss; Whimsicott entered on turn 6 only as a forced replacement and died immediately.

proposals.change: NO-OVERKILL SPLIT: block/penalize assigning a second attacker to a target that the first attacker's listed minimum roll already KOs; redirect the second action to the other foe.
proposals.evidence: T6: Moonblast (21-30%) alone KO'd 32% Politoed, yet Drogon's Weather Ball was also aimed there instead of hitting Mega Dragonite in sun.

proposals.change: LOW-HP MEGA PRESERVATION: Drogon below 45% facing a faster foe with a listed KO should switch out (to Kingambit/Milotic/Whimsicott) rather than Protect a second time; Protect twice in three turns on the same mon is banned.
proposals.evidence: Drogon Protected T3 and T5 at 37% and still died on T6 having dealt no damage after T4.

lessons: Once an opposing Mega evolves and takes a KO, it is the win condition — focus-fire it; killing passive supports (Torkoal, Politoed) while it sweeps loses the game.
Never spend a second action on a foe the first action already KOs at minimum roll; redirect it to the live sweeper.
Protect-cycling a sub-40% Mega against a faster spread attacker only delays its death — switch it out and bring in the speed control instead.
In rain, Hurricane is 100% accurate: treat opposing Flying spread Megas as guaranteed, not as an accuracy gamble.
If Tailwind has not been set by turn 3 and Whimsicott is alive on the bench while a faster foe is scoring KOs, bringing Whimsicott in is worth more than another Protect turn.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their single-slot win condition: Mega Dragonite with a spread STAB (Hurricane) + Flamethrower coverage carried the whole game from behind. Give OUR Mega Dragonite Hurricane over Dragon Pulse (spread, rain-accurate, hits Grass/Fighting/Bug and Fairy-resists) and add Icy Wind to Milotic over Protect as the Fake-Out-proof second speed source.
teamInspiration.reason: Their Dragonite alone KO'd four of our Pokemon because it had a spread STAB that threatened both slots every turn; our Dragonite's single-target Dragon Pulse never forces that kind of two-for-one, and our only speed control (Whimsicott) has now fainted 134 times in 213 games.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 Kingambit Iron Head targeting Sylveon was the right win-condition call (Sylveon Hyper Voice was their whole game). Dragonite Mega + Tailwind turn 1 secured 5 Tailwind turns. Garchomp Earthquake was excellent: it KO'd Indeedee through Follow Me, then KO'd Mega Raichu-Y while chipping Sylveon twice — 185% damage and 2 KOs, with Dragonite's Flying immunity making EQ free. Turn-6 focus fire on 37% Incineroar got the KO at minimum roll.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: no Earthquake next to Kingambit (Kingambit was already dead); no Tailwind into Trick Room; Mega on turn 1; punished the spread threat rather than passive supports; did not predict wildly when behind. Violated: repeated Iron Head into a Sylveon that Protected on turn 2 and then switched on turn 3 — three consecutive turns aimed at the same slot that never connected, the exact 'remember what they keep doing' failure. Also Kingambit was left in at 8 HP on turn 3 instead of switching (our own rule: switch a mon that is about to be KO'd and can't Protect).
analysis.whatFailed: The decisive error chain was turns 2-3. T2: we clicked Iron Head into a Sylveon that was the single most obviously threatened mon on the field (a 152-222% OHKO was listed) — a textbook Protect read we ignored — and Dragonite Protected instead of attacking, so BOTH our actions produced zero damage while Incineroar Flare Blitz took Kingambit from 142 to 8. That is a double-wasted turn in the 2-action economy. T3: Kingambit at 8/207 should have switched out (Milotic was never brought... actually Milotic was left home; Whimsicott was the pivot) or at minimum we should have expected the Sylveon switch; instead it died to recoil-free chip after Iron Head hit a Sash-less Indeedee for 99% without KOing. We also never KO'd Sylveon all game — the one mon that killed Garchomp, Dragonite and Whimsicott. Team choice compounded it: we brought Garchomp+Whimsicott over Milotic into a Sylveon/Incineroar/Indeedee board where bulky Milotic (Competitive +2 from Incineroar Intimidate, Ice Beam/Scald) would have walled Hyper Voice far better than a Focus-Sash Whimsicott that contributed 48% damage.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) When a foe is listed at a guaranteed OHKO from our attack and it is their key piece, assume Protect on the turn immediately after it has already been threatened — either double-target the partner or use the turn to remove the second threat (Incineroar) instead of re-clicking into a near-certain Protect. 2) Never spend both actions on non-damage when the opponent's spread attacker is alive: on T2 Dragonite should have Dragon Pulsed Incineroar while Kingambit hit Incineroar too, likely removing the Flare Blitz that killed Kingambit. 3) Switch out a mon below 15% that cannot Protect and is not needed this turn. 4) Vs Fairy spread attackers (Sylveon Hyper Voice/Pixilate), bring Kingambit AND Milotic: Steel resist plus Competitive. 5) Count the enemy spread attacker as the win condition from preview and dedicate both actions to it on the first turn it can be hit without a Protect read.

proposals.change: PROTECT-READ ON REPEAT TARGET: if we attacked foe X last turn with a listed OHKO and X survived via Protect (or we attacked it and it Protected), apply a large penalty to attacking X again next turn — redirect both actions to its partner.
proposals.evidence: T2 Iron Head (152-222% OHKO listed) went straight into Sylveon Protect; T3 Sylveon switched out. Three turns aimed at Sylveon produced 0 damage to it while Incineroar Flare Blitz 65%+ chipped Kingambit to 8 HP and then killed it.

proposals.change: NO DOUBLE-NON-DAMAGE TURN: forbid a turn where neither of our actions deals damage (e.g. attack-into-likely-Protect + ally Protect) while an opposing spread attacker is active and healthy, unless we are stalling a field effect timer.
proposals.evidence: Turn 2: Kingambit Iron Head blocked by Protect + Dragonite Protect = 0 damage dealt; Incineroar hit Kingambit for 134 HP. Net loss of a full turn's action economy.

proposals.change: SUB-15% SWITCH RULE: a Pokemon at <=15% HP that has no Protect available this turn and faces any listed attack should switch rather than attack, unless its attack is a guaranteed KO on the opponent's win condition.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit at 8/207 on turn 3 stayed in, hit Indeedee for 99% (no KO due to Sash/bulk) and died to Flare Blitz, costing us our Dark/Steel wall vs Sylveon.

proposals.change: Against previewed Fairy spread attackers (Sylveon, Floette, Primarina) bring Milotic over Whimsicott when Incineroar is also previewed: Competitive gives +2 SpA off Intimidate and Milotic's special bulk absorbs Hyper Voice.
proposals.evidence: Sylveon Hyper Voice KO'd Garchomp, Dragonite and Whimsicott (3 of our 4). Whimsicott dealt only 48% all game and died to the same move.

lessons: If a foe Protected against our attack last turn, do not aim the same attack at that slot again next turn — redirect to its partner or expect a switch.
Never create a turn where both of our actions deal zero damage (attack-into-expected-Protect + ally Protect) while an enemy spread attacker is healthy; that hands them a free double-chip turn.
A Pokemon at or below 15% HP with no Protect available should switch out, not attack, unless its attack guarantees a KO on the opponent's win condition.
Pixilate/Fairy spread attackers (Sylveon Hyper Voice) are the win condition on balance teams: bring Kingambit (Steel resist) AND Milotic (Competitive) rather than Focus Sash Whimsicott.
Earthquake beside Mega Dragonite is free damage (Flying immunity) — it KO'd Indeedee through Follow Me and Mega Raichu; keep using Garchomp EQ when the ally is a Flying type.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again produced both KOs and 185% damage this game (outsped and EQ'd Mega Raichu-Y); the loss came from action-economy errors, not the item. Keep the variant to finish the sample.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their single-slot engine: one bulky Fairy spread attacker (Sylveon Hyper Voice) that threatens both of our slots every turn and is Protect-protected by a Follow Me redirector. For us, give Mega Dragonite Hurricane over Dragon Pulse (spread STAB that forces two-for-ones) and bring Milotic over Whimsicott whenever an opposing Fairy spread attacker + Intimidate user are previewed, so Competitive turns their Intimidate into our +2 SpA.
teamInspiration.reason: Sylveon alone KO'd three of our Pokemon with a single spread move while Indeedee's Follow Me and Incineroar's Parting Shot protected it. Our only spread option was Garchomp Earthquake; Dragonite's single-target Dragon Pulse can never force the same two-for-one, and Whimsicott (135 faints in 214 games) contributed 48% damage before dying to the same Hyper Voice.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 one-shot win vs I luv Politoed: Mega Charizard-Y evolved immediately, Drought overwrote Electric Terrain's irrelevance and powered sun Heat Wave into a double KO on Mega Raichu-X and Metagross while Whimsicott set Tailwind at full HP. The Claude override (Heat Wave over the engine's Protect) was correct: the damage preview listed Raichu 32-50% / Metagross 54-87% but real sun-boosted Heat Wave rolled 100% on both — exactly the known 'our preview underestimates sun Heat Wave' lesson, applied rather than ignored.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) set Tailwind turn 1 while Whimsicott is at full HP; (2) Mega Evolve turn 1 with Drogon; (3) treat sun Heat Wave as a likely OHKO on neutral frail targets instead of defaulting to Protect; (4) no unnecessary Protect with no real OHKO threat on the board (Zap Cannon was only a 22% OHKO roll and we were faster after Tailwind + we moved first anyway via the Heat Wave spread). (5) Spread move chosen over single-target because both foes were in KO range — correct no-overkill/two-for-one logic.
analysis.whatFailed: Nothing in-game; the win was clean in one turn. Process failures: the team-preview call fell back to the engine again due to an HTTP 429 rate-limit, so our lead/bring selection was not Claude-reasoned (this has now happened in 3 of the last 5 games). Also, the damage preview was materially wrong (54-87% predicted vs 100% actual on Metagross; 32-50% vs 100% on Raichu) — the calc is still under-rating Drought-boosted Weather Ball/Heat Wave, which risks the opposite error later (declining a line because the preview says 'no KO').
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Keep hard-coding a sun-Heat-Wave/Weather-Ball confidence bonus so the engine never Protects instead of taking a double KO. 2) Add retry/backoff for preview calls so rate-limits don't cost us the lead decision. 3) Against Electric Terrain Mega Raichu leads, Drogon's Drought + Heat Wave is now a proven turn-1 double-KO line — lead Whimsicott + Drogon and click it. 4) Continue the sun archetype plan (now 18-3 with Charizard|zw) and avoid Dragonite leads in sun.

proposals.change: SUN SPREAD CONFIDENCE: when our side has Sun (Drought active or Charizard-Y mega-evolving this turn), add a large score bonus to Heat Wave / Weather Ball and treat the listed damage range as ~1.5x for KO judgement; never choose Protect over a sun spread move when both foes are listed at >=45% max roll.
proposals.evidence: vs I luv Politoed T1: preview listed Raichu 32-50% and Metagross 54-87%; actual Heat Wave dealt 100% to both for an instant 2-for-0 and the game.

proposals.change: PREVIEW RETRY: on HTTP 429 during team preview, retry twice with 1.5s backoff before falling back to the engine; the preview decision is the highest-leverage call of the game.
proposals.evidence: 3 of the last 5 games (braborba, me when if the if, I luv Politoed) had fallback previews or fallback turns due to rate limits.

proposals.change: Keep Charizard-Y + Whimsicott Tailwind as the default lead vs sun/Electric-Terrain offense; record now 18-3 in the sun archetype with Charizard|zw.
proposals.evidence: LEARNED PREVIEW PLANS: sun / Charizard|zw 17W-3L before this game, now 18-3.

lessons: Sun-boosted Heat Wave from Mega Charizard-Y routinely OHKOs neutral targets our calc lists at only 50-85% — take the spread double-KO instead of Protecting.
Against a Mega Raichu (Electric Surge) + Metagross lead, Whimsicott Tailwind + Drogon Heat Wave is a proven turn-1 double KO.
Mega Evolving Drogon turn 1 overwrites opposing terrain-independent weather and immediately converts Heat Wave into a win condition; do it on turn 1 in sun matchups.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their lead stacked two Pokemon that are both neutral-to-weak to Fire spread (Mega Raichu-X and Metagross) with no Wide Guard and no Protect, losing on turn 1. Mirror the opposite lesson for us: keep a Wide Guard/Protect answer — specifically keep Protect on Drogon and consider Milotic over Whimsicott only when an opposing Fairy spread attacker plus Intimidate user are previewed. No change needed to the Mega Charizard-Y + Whimsicott Tailwind core, which is 18-3 in the sun archetype.
teamInspiration.reason: Our one-turn win came entirely from a spread move that threatened both slots at once; teams that lack a spread answer die to it. Protecting our own spread engine (Drogon) is therefore more valuable than adding a second single-target attacker.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 focus-fire on Indeedee removed Psychic Surge immediately and killed the Expanding Force win condition — the single best call of the game. Whimsicott's Moonblast chipping then finishing Kleavor, and Milotic's Ice Beam finally removing their Whimsicott, were correct target choices.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Setup/win-con denial was applied (Indeedee deleted turn 1). Kingambit was correctly led into Psychic Terrain (Psychic-immune). But the durable lesson 'Protect belongs on the Pokemon with the largest incoming OHKO' was violated twice: Kingambit was listed at 104-153% OHKO from Kleavor Close Combat on T2 and still attacked, and Drogon mega-evolved into a listed Kleavor Stone Axe (Rock, 4x) on T3 with Protect available. The 'set Tailwind turn 1-2 while Whimsicott is healthy' rule was also violated — Tailwind was not clicked until turn 4 at 2 mons left, exactly the failure mode flagged in coach notes.
