analysis.whatFailed: 1) T2: both actions dumped into Kleavor needing a 53% OHKO roll while Kleavor was guaranteed to move first under their Tailwind and OHKO Kingambit — we lost Kingambit for a non-KO. 2) T3: Drogon, a 4x Rock weakness, mega-evolved and Heat Waved into a live Kleavor whose Stone Axe was listed at 39-63% but actually OHKO'd (our calc badly underrates Stone Axe vs Charizard; Rock 4x) — Protect was the correct click and Drogon died before contributing anything. 3) Their Whimsicott had Tailwind up from turn 1 and we never denied or matched it: they had speed AND power the whole game. 4) Opposing Whimsicott was the real speed-control win condition and was left alive for 4 turns while we killed Kleavor/Indeedee. 5) Tailwind on T4 was a dead action — Whimsicott died the same turn it set it.
analysis.howToImprove: Against an opposing Prankster Whimsicott that sets Tailwind on turn 1, treat it as the enemy win condition alongside the terrain setter: split turn-1 damage so one action is aimed at it (Moonblast/Iron Head) rather than over-killing Indeedee. Never lead Drogon into a revealed Rock-type (Kleavor/Tyranitar) without Protecting on the turn it mega-evolves — 4x Rock means any listed Rock move is an OHKO regardless of printed range. When a foe is listed as a guaranteed OHKO on our slot and our two attacks only reach a ~50% OHKO roll, switch the threatened mon or Protect it instead of gambling both actions. Set Tailwind turn 1-2 or not at all.

proposals.change: ROCK-vs-CHARIZARD HARD RULE: if any opposing active Pokemon is a Rock-type or has a revealed Rock move and Drogon (Charizard) is active, Protect is mandatory on Drogon on the turn it mega-evolves unless the opposing Rock user is already guaranteed KO'd by our other action. Treat all listed Rock damage vs Charizard as 2x the printed range.
proposals.evidence: T3: Kleavor Stone Axe listed 39-63% actually dealt 100% and OHKO'd Drogon the turn it mega-evolved; Drogon contributed 0 damage all game.

proposals.change: COIN-FLIP FOCUS-FIRE BAN: if our combined damage on a target is below a guaranteed KO (OHKO chance < 85%) and that target is listed as a guaranteed OHKO on one of our actives, prefer Protect/switch on the threatened mon over double-attacking.
proposals.evidence: T2: Iron Head 72-131% (53% OHKO) + Moonblast into Kleavor; Kleavor moved first under Tailwind and OHKO'd Kingambit, leaving Kleavor at 16%.

proposals.change: ENEMY-TAILWIND SETTER PRIORITY: when an opposing Whimsicott/Tornadus/Prankster setter is active on turn 1 alongside a terrain setter, assign at least one of our two actions to the speed-control setter (it is Sash-breakable and re-sets Tailwind every 4 turns).
proposals.evidence: Their Whimsicott set Tailwind on T1 and again on T5, lived 4 turns, KO'd our Whimsicott, and gave them speed+power for the entire game.

proposals.change: Give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect as a Fake-Out-proof, Dark-proof second speed source; our only speed control (Whimsicott, 136 faints in 216 games) dies before Tailwind pays off in roughly half our losses.
proposals.evidence: T4-T5: Whimsicott died the same turn it clicked Tailwind; Milotic survived 2 extra turns with nothing but Ice Beam to click.

lessons: Charizard-Y has a 4x Rock weakness: any live Rock-type (Kleavor, Tyranitar, Lycanroc) on the field makes Protect mandatory on the turn Drogon mega-evolves — our calc under-reads Stone Axe/Rock Slide vs Charizard by roughly 2x.
Do not spend both actions on a target that only has ~50% OHKO chance when that target is a guaranteed OHKO on one of our slots and moves first — Protect or switch the threatened Pokemon instead.
An opposing Prankster Whimsicott with Tailwind is a co-win-condition with the terrain setter: break its Sash on turn 1 rather than over-killing the already-dying partner.
Tailwind clicked at 2 Pokemon remaining is a wasted action; set it turn 1-2 while Whimsicott is at full HP or keep Whimsicott benched entirely.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp: against Tailwind teams that out-speed us the whole game, the 231 Speed is our only natural answer once Whimsicott dies. No change warranted from this loss.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Prankster Tailwind + two physical Rock/Fighting breakers' shape: keep Whimsicott but pair it with Milotic running Icy Wind over Protect, and bench Drogon whenever a Rock-type (Kleavor/Tyranitar/Lycanroc) is previewed — bring Mega Dragonite instead, which resists nothing of theirs but is not 4x Rock weak.
teamInspiration.reason: Their Whimsicott set Tailwind twice and single-handedly gave Kleavor and Mega Tyranitar both speed and power; meanwhile our Charizard died to one Rock move without acting. A second speed source on a bulky body and a Mega choice that is not 4x Rock weak would both have changed this game.

analysis.whatWorked: Won 4-0 on KOs after a disastrous turn 1. Mega Charizard-Y's sun Heat Wave deleted Corviknight and Excadrill through sand-switching, and Choice Scarf Garchomp's Earthquake closed the game with a double KO on Mega Tyranitar + Sneasler (Flying ally already gone, so no friendly fire risk). Preview call (Kingambit + Whimsicott lead, Drogon sheltered in back, Garchomp for sand) was reasonable and the 'sand = Mega Charizard' plan held.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed the rule to Mega Drogon when it could convert Heat Wave into a win condition, and correctly Earthquaked only while the ally was Flying/absent. Followed 'don't attack into a guaranteed Protect twice' by shifting targets on T3-T4. However the hard Rock-vs-Charizard rule and the anti-sand lead rule were both violated: we led Whimsicott into Excadrill (a known Sash-breaking Iron Head/Rock Slide user) and we left Drogon in against a live Excadrill Rock Slide on T3 instead of Protecting.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 1 was a double loss: Whimsicott set Tailwind into Excadrill Iron Head (99% + sand residual = dead with Sash already consumed by sand damage) and Kingambit Iron Head into Tyranitar left it at 13% while Low Kick OHKO'd us. We traded 2 Pokemon for 0 on turn 1 — the worst action-economy turn possible. Our own coach note explicitly says 'vs sand: don't lead Whimsicott; Rock Slide/Iron Head double-KOs it' and 'sand chips Focus Sash to nothing'. Then on T3 the fallback engine kept Drogon in at full HP against an active Excadrill that had already revealed nothing but was obviously holding Rock Slide — Drogon died to a 1-HP Excadrill's Rock Slide. One Protect on Drogon would have kept our best piece alive and made the game a clean 4-2.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) In sand, treat Focus Sash as already broken (sandstorm residual damage removes it at end of turn 1) — never count on Whimsicott surviving. 2) Vs Excadrill/Tyranitar, Charizard must Protect on any turn both foes are live and either can click Rock Slide; our calc showed Rock Slide at 116-191% and we still attacked. 3) Turn 1 vs Mega Tyranitar: Kingambit Iron Head is not a KO — either Protect Kingambit or switch, and let Garchomp Earthquake handle TTar from the back. 4) Don't let the engine fallback pilot a turn where our Mega is one Rock move from death — add a hard guardrail.

proposals.change: Vs sand (Tyranitar/Excadrill/Hippowdon previewed), never lead Whimsicott. Lead Kingambit + Garchomp or Milotic + Kingambit and keep Whimsicott benched entirely; its Focus Sash is destroyed by sand residual on turn 1.
proposals.evidence: T1: Excadrill Iron Head left Whimsicott at 1 HP, sand upkeep killed it the same turn. Whimsicott has fainted 137 times in 217 games.

proposals.change: HARD RULE: if Charizard (Drogon) is active and ANY live opposing Pokemon is Rock-type or is Excadrill/Tyranitar/Lycanroc/Kleavor, Protect is mandatory unless both foes are guaranteed KO'd by our other action this turn.
proposals.evidence: T3: Drogon at full HP, Excadrill at 1% HP after EQ; engine fallback chose Heat Wave and Excadrill's Rock Slide (116-191% listed) KO'd Drogon before it could matter.

proposals.change: Turn-1 vs un-Megaed Tyranitar: do not click a non-KO Iron Head with Kingambit into a guaranteed Low Kick OHKO. Protect Kingambit or switch it to Garchomp/Milotic.
proposals.evidence: Calc listed Iron Head at 73-115% (OHKO 37%) vs Tyranitar Low Kick at 81-118% (OHKO 49%); we lost the coin flip and the Pokemon.

lessons: In sandstorm, Focus Sash is dead weight: sand residual breaks it at the end of the first turn, so Whimsicott must not lead into Tyranitar/Excadrill teams.
Never leave Charizard-Y in against a live Excadrill or Tyranitar, even at 1% HP — Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO and they will click it.
A turn-1 trade of two of our Pokemon for zero of theirs is unrecoverable on paper; when both our leads are listed as likely OHKO'd, at least one action must be Protect or a switch.
Engine fallback turns are the most dangerous turns in the game: if our Mega is one super-effective hit from death, the pilot must not defer.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again closed the game with a double KO through sand (immune to sand chip, resists Rock, outspeeds Excadrill). Keep the variant; the loss source was lead selection, not items.

teamInspiration.opponent: JJ1NE (sand: Mega Tyranitar + Excadrill + Corviknight + Sneasler)
teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'weather + Protect-cycling Sash sweeper' shape: give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so we have a sand-proof, Fake-Out-proof speed source that doesn't rely on a Focus Sash, and default to benching Whimsicott in every sand matchup. Also consider Yache/Sitrus over Focus Sash on Whimsicott specifically because residual weather deletes Sash value.
teamInspiration.reason: Their Excadrill survived at 1 HP behind Protect and still KO'd our Mega Charizard with Rock Slide, while our Sash Whimsicott died to chip + sand on turn 1 having contributed only Tailwind. Residual-damage weather teams invalidate our only speed control's item.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 was near-perfect: Kowtow Cleave (Dark, unblockable by Psychic Terrain) deleted Sash Indeedee and removed Psychic Surge, while Mega Dragonite's Dragon Pulse OHKO'd Mega Salamence before it could Draco Meteor. We went up 2-0 on turn 1 and Defiant converted Salamence's Intimidate into +2 Atk.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed the Psychic-Terrain rule (used Kowtow Cleave, never Sucker Punch), punished the terrain setter immediately, and led Kingambit into Expanding Force as prescribed. Mega evolved turn 1 to burst the biggest threat. But the 'never let the opponent have both speed and power' rule was violated on turn 2: their Tailwind was up and we answered with two attacks into a single already-not-lethal target instead of protecting/switching the piece that was a guaranteed OHKO victim.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 2 lost the game. After they sent in Sneasler + Basculegion under their own Tailwind, our calc explicitly flagged 'Kingambit threatened by Sneasler Close Combat (153-222% KO)' and we still clicked Iron Head (83% OHKO, i.e. a 17% whiff) plus a non-lethal Dragon Pulse into the same slot — the exact COIN-FLIP FOCUS-FIRE BAN we already wrote as an active proposal. Sneasler moved first in Tailwind, OHKO'd Kingambit, Iron Head never fired, and Basculegion's Last Respects (which scales with THEIR fainted count — already 2 dead, so ~100 BP+) OHKO'd Mega Dragonite the same turn. We also mis-evaluated Last Respects entirely: killing two of their Pokemon on turn 1 powered up Basculegion and it was never in our threat model. Turn 3 then wasted both actions (Tailwind at 2 mons left — another lesson we had already written — and a 22-42% Scald) while both our remaining mons died.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Against Last Respects users, every KO we score makes their Basculegion stronger: after KOing 2+ of their team, treat Basculegion as a guaranteed OHKO on everything we own and either KO it first or never leave a mon in range. 2) On turn 2, with their Tailwind up and Sneasler guaranteed to OHKO Kingambit before it moves, the correct line was Dragonite Protect + Kingambit switch to Milotic (or Kingambit Protect + Dragon Pulse into Basculegion); we must not spend both actions on an 83% roll against a mon that moves first and kills. 3) Never click Tailwind with 2 Pokemon left and a faster lethal board — Scald/Ice Beam into Basculegion was the only line.

proposals.change: LAST RESPECTS RULE: if an opposing Basculegion (or any Last Respects user) is on the field, count their fainted Pokemon; at 2+ fainted treat Last Respects as a guaranteed OHKO on every one of our Pokemon and make removing/blocking Basculegion the top priority action each turn (Protect, switch, or focus-fire it) before chipping anything else.
proposals.evidence: We KO'd Salamence + Indeedee on turn 1; Basculegion then OHKO'd full-HP Mega Dragonite (75%->dead through Multiscale) on T2 and Milotic on T3. It was never listed in our threat calc.

proposals.change: HARD ENFORCE the existing coin-flip focus-fire ban: if a foe moves before our mon (Tailwind/Scarf/faster) and is a listed guaranteed OHKO on it, and our combined damage on that foe is <95% OHKO chance, the threatened mon MUST Protect or switch instead of attacking.
proposals.evidence: T2 Iron Head at 83% OHKO vs Sneasler, which was listed as a 153-222% guaranteed OHKO on Kingambit under their Tailwind. Kingambit died without acting; Iron Head and Dragon Pulse both produced zero value.

proposals.change: TAILWIND END-GAME BAN: with 2 or fewer of our Pokemon remaining and a faster opposing board, Tailwind is forbidden — both actions must be damage or Protect.
proposals.evidence: T3 Whimsicott Tailwind + 22-42% Scald = zero progress; both our mons died that turn and Tailwind never got used.

lessons: Last Respects grows with the OPPONENT's fainted count — every KO we take powers up their Basculegion; after 2 KOs treat it as a guaranteed OHKO on our whole team and remove it first.
An 83% OHKO roll is not a KO: if the target moves first and guaranteed-OHKOs our attacker, Protect or switch instead of rolling the dice with both actions.
Under the opponent's Tailwind our slow pieces (Kingambit) cannot trade — they must Protect, switch, or be left on the bench until the Tailwind expires.
Never click Tailwind with 2 Pokemon remaining; it is a wasted action in a losing board.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp: in losses like this the only way to act before an opposing Tailwind Sneasler/Basculegion is raw Scarf speed; Sitrus does not solve being outsped by a +2 board.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'trade-bait + Last Respects payoff' shape: their Salamence/Indeedee were expendable because Basculegion gets stronger with each of their own deaths. For us, the equivalent is a mon that profits from a losing board — swap Whimsicott's Focus Sash for a Covert Cloak (Dire Claw/Fake Out/flinch-proof) and give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect so we still have a Fake-Out-proof, Dark-proof speed source once Whimsicott is gone.
teamInspiration.reason: Whimsicott again contributed only a Tailwind before dying to Dire Claw (138 faints in 218 games), and our entire speed plan collapsed the moment it was outsped. A second speed source on Milotic's bulky body would have let turn 3 be Icy Wind + Ice Beam into Basculegion instead of a wasted Tailwind.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 focus-fire on Annihilape was correct and won the game instantly: Kingambit Kowtow Cleave + Drogon sun Weather Ball removed the Bulk Up sweeper before it could snowball, and Mega-evolving Drogon on turn 1 set Sun so Weather Ball was a 150 BP Fire STAB. Leading Kingambit into a previewed psyterrain/Indeedee team was again the right preview call (Kingambit is immune to Expanding Force and Psychic-Terrain priority blocking does not matter to Kowtow Cleave). Altaria's Earthquake hit its own Annihilape for 12% and was fully immune on Drogon, confirming the rule that Flying-type Megas beside ground spread are free.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) 'punish setup immediately' — Annihilape clicked Bulk Up and we KO'd it that same turn rather than Protect-stalling; (2) 'never spend a second action on a foe the first action already KOs' was technically violated in direction but justified here because the damage calc wrongly printed Weather Ball as 0-0% so we could not know Kowtow alone was lethal; (3) Mega-evolve Drogon turn 1 in sun matchups; (4) 'focus-fire the foe that guaranteed-OHKOs our slot' — Annihilape Close Combat was 141-205% on Kingambit.
analysis.whatFailed: The damage calculator printed Drogon Weather Ball -> Annihilape as 0-0% when the actual hit was 59%. That is a hard calculator bug (likely Weather Ball typing not resolving to Fire before the Mega/Drought weather is applied in the pre-turn simulation) and it is dangerous: a 0% prediction can cause the pilot to discard the correct attack entirely in a future turn. We got lucky that the pilot overrode the engine anyway. Secondary issue: with Altaria active (Dragon/Flying, likely Earthquake + possible Rock coverage) we committed both actions to one slot and left Altaria completely untouched; against a less passive partner that is a free setup/Tailwind turn. The game was only 1 turn so there is little else to critique.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Treat any 0-0% calc line from Weather Ball / Terrain Pulse / Nature Power / Judgment as UNRELIABLE and recompute as the weather-appropriate STAB (Fire in Drogon's sun) rather than skipping the move. 2) When focus-firing a Bulk Up/Swords Dance user, check whether the first attack alone is lethal at minimum roll; if yes, redirect the second action to the untouched partner so we are not giving a free turn. 3) Keep leading Kingambit vs previewed Indeedee/psyterrain — it is now the highest-winrate psyterrain lead we have (Charizard|zk 5-4 vs Charizard|zw 10-12).

proposals.change: CALC-BUG GUARD: if the damage calculator reports 0-0% for a weather/terrain-variable move (Weather Ball, Terrain Pulse, Revelation Dance, Judgment, Nature Power) and the target is not immune by type to the move's weather-resolved type, ignore the 0% figure and treat the move as full-power STAB of the current weather type.
proposals.evidence: T1 Drogon Weather Ball -> Annihilape predicted 0%-0% but actually dealt 59% in sun; a pilot trusting the calc would have discarded the game-winning attack.

proposals.change: OVERKILL REDIRECT: before assigning both actions to one foe, verify the stronger attack's MINIMUM roll is not already lethal. If it is, send the second action at the untouched foe instead.
proposals.evidence: Kowtow Cleave (45-80%) plus Weather Ball (actual 59%) both hit Annihilape at 100%; Weather Ball alone left it at 41% and Kowtow finished it, so Kingambit's action could arguably have pressured Altaria.

proposals.change: Make Kingambit the default lead in every previewed Indeedee/Psychic Terrain matchup (psyterrain plan 'Charizard|zk'), with Drogon as the second slot for turn-1 Mega + sun Weather Ball/Heat Wave.
proposals.evidence: psyterrain record: Charizard|zw 10-12, Dragonite|zw 2-7, Charizard|zk 5-4 — the Kingambit lead is the only above-even psyterrain plan and won this game on turn 1.

lessons: A 0-0% damage-calc line on Weather Ball/Terrain Pulse is a calculator bug, not an immunity — in Drogon's sun, Weather Ball is a 150 BP Fire STAB and should be scored as such.
Against a foe that just used Bulk Up/Swords Dance, removing it this turn outranks spreading damage; Annihilape at +1/+1 would have OHKO'd both our active mons next turn.
Earthquake from an opposing Ground-move user beside our Flying Mega damages their own partner — leaving Drogon in beside an enemy EQ user is free value, not a risk.
Kingambit + Drogon is now the preferred lead pair vs previewed Indeedee/Psychic Terrain teams.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their Annihilape (Bulk Up + Close Combat, Rage Fist potential) is a single-slot snowball that beats our whole team if given one free turn; our answer was only a turn-1 double-target. Add insurance by giving Milotic Icy Wind over Protect (slows the boosted sweeper and is Fake-Out/Dark-proof speed control) and keep Kingambit as the mandatory psyterrain lead so Drogon can Mega safely behind it.
teamInspiration.reason: We won on turn 1 only because they led the Bulk Up user into two attackers; had they led Volcarona or Ninetales-A + Annihilape we would have had no way to slow a +1 Fighting sweeper, since Whimsicott Tailwind does nothing against a foe that is already faster and boosting.

whatWorked: Turn-1 Protect on Drogon against Kleavor's Stone Axe was correct and saved the Mega from an immediate 4x OHKO; the hard Rock-type rule worked. Whimsicott's Moonblast chip + finish removed Kleavor, and sun Heat Wave deleted Mega Metagross on turn 3, giving us a clean 4v2 board. Drogon's Mega on turn 1 set sun immediately and converted Heat Wave into a double-threat spread move.
lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) Protect Drogon on the Mega turn vs a live Rock-type; (2) don't re-aim into a slot that just Protected was VIOLATED on turn 3 (Whimsicott Moonblast went into Kleavor again — it worked only because they didn't double-Protect); (3) Earthquake/ally-safety rules not relevant. Violated: the 'never create a turn where both actions deal zero damage' rule on turn 2 (Moonblast into Protect + Heat Wave into double Protect = a fully wasted turn), and the Sucker Punch awareness rule — we repeatedly left Drogon and Dragonite in front of a healthy Kingambit at low/medium HP and lost both to Sucker Punch.
whatFailed: 1) Turn 2 was a complete 2-action waste: after turn 1 showed Kleavor was the aggressive Rock threat, we attacked the exact slot that had the strongest incentive to Protect while they double-Protected; we burned a turn with Whimsicott at 1%. 2) Turn 4 was the game-loser: we switched Whimsicott out (fine) but left Drogon at 45/153 HP in front of a freshly-entered Kingambit. Kingambit Sucker Punch is +1 priority and our listed threat line even said 'Kowtow Cleave 41-67% KO' — at 29% HP Drogon was dead to ANY Kingambit action. Drogon should have Protected or switched; Heat Wave only mattered if it OHKO'd both, and Sucker Punch beats it regardless of our speed. 3) Same mistake repeated turn 6: Dragonite at 48/168 clicked Heat Wave into a live Kingambit and died to Sucker Punch before resolving; Protect would have let Sucker Punch fail (it fails vs Protect) and we would still have had Dragonite + Milotic vs two chipped foes. 4) Milotic Protected turn 5 (fine) but then attacked into Grassy Glide priority at full HP range — Rillaboom's Grassy Glide outspeeds everything and we never accounted for it in the Milotic slot. 5) Whimsicott at 1% was kept on the field for three turns contributing one Moonblast instead of being pivoted immediately; it then died as our last mon.
howToImprove: Codify an explicit SUCKER PUNCH / PRIORITY GUARD: when an opposing Kingambit (Sucker Punch), Rillaboom (Grassy Glide), or any +1 priority attacker is active and one of our Pokemon is in KO range of that priority move, that Pokemon must Protect or switch instead of attacking — because Sucker Punch fails into Protect and Grassy Glide is unavoidable by speed. Also: never aim an attack at a slot that Protected last turn; and never spend a turn with a 1%-HP Pokemon attacking when a switch gives a healthy body. Finally, when ahead 4v2 after a double-KO, take the lowest-variance line (Protect the damaged Mega, attack with the healthy slot) rather than trying to spread-KO both replacements at once.

proposals.change: PRIORITY-KO GUARD: if an opposing Kingambit/Rillaboom/Arcanine-H/any revealed +1 priority attacker is active and our Pokemon's current HP is below the priority move's max roll, that Pokemon MUST Protect (Sucker Punch fails into Protect) or switch — never attack.
proposals.evidence: T4 Drogon at 45/153 and T6 Dragonite at 48/168 both died to Kingambit Sucker Punch before acting; both had Protect available.

proposals.change: NO-REPEAT-INTO-PROTECT: do not target a slot that used Protect on the previous turn; redirect to the partner or use a spread move only if the partner is also hit.
proposals.evidence: T2 Moonblast + Heat Wave both hit Protect for a 0-damage turn after a Protect-telegraphing board.

proposals.change: 1%-HP PIVOT RULE: a Pokemon at <=5% HP with a healthy teammate on the bench must switch, not attack, unless its attack is a guaranteed KO on the opponent's win condition.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott sat at 1/137 for turns 2-3, wasted a turn into Protect, and later died as our last mon with no Tailwind set.

lessons: Kingambit's Sucker Punch is +1 priority: any of our Pokemon in its KO range must Protect (Sucker Punch FAILS into Protect) or switch — attacking is strictly dominated.
Rillaboom Grassy Glide is +1 in Grassy Terrain: Milotic/Whimsicott in its KO range cannot win a speed race, so Protect or switch rather than trade.
Do not attack a slot that Protected on the previous turn; and never let both actions be aimed at an obviously Protect-incentivised slot.
After a double KO that puts us ahead 4v2, play the lowest-variance line: Protect the chipped Mega and attack with the healthy slot.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 22-22 and was not brought in this game; Sitrus gives Garchomp a bulk buffer to survive Grassy Glide/Sucker Punch chip and lets it click the correct move each turn against priority-heavy balance (Kingambit + Rillaboom), which is the archetype that just beat us.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'double priority back line' shape: Kingambit Sucker Punch + Rillaboom Grassy Glide meant our speed control was irrelevant. Give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect is NOT enough here — instead keep Protect on Milotic but swap Whimsicott's Focus Sash for Covert Cloak (Fake Out-proof) and consider running Dragonite with Extreme Speed over Heat Wave so our own +2 priority can finish chipped priority users before they fire.
teamInspiration.reason: Both of our Megas died to a +1 priority move at 25-30% HP; our team has zero priority of its own apart from Kingambit's Sucker Punch, so any chipped Pokemon of ours is a free KO for Kingambit/Rillaboom while we cannot reciprocate.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead vs Psychic Terrain again proved correct: it Protected through Pawmot's Will-O-Wisp turn 1, then Kowtow Cleave KO'd Pawmot and later one-shot Indeedee through its Sash. Drogon's turn-1 Mega + sun Heat Wave removed Mega Victreebel immediately. Milotic cleaned Zoroark-Hisui with Ice Beam.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed the psyterrain lead rule (Kingambit + Drogon), Mega-evolved Drogon on turn 1 for sun, and Protected the slot that was facing a guaranteed OHKO (Kingambit vs Pawmot Close Combat). The Weather Ball/Heat Wave calc-bug guard was respected (we trusted Heat Wave despite thin numbers).
analysis.whatFailed: The loss came from a single unseen mechanic: Victreebel-Mega's ability (Flower Veil-style contact/Fire reflect — actually Drogon fainted simultaneously from its own Heat Wave against a Mega Victreebel holding a damage-reflect ability/item, i.e. Rocky Helmet-equivalent or Mega ability). We never accounted for a Mega-evolving foe changing its defensive profile in the same turn, and we burned our Mega win-con on turn 1 for one KO. Worse: Turn 2 Garchomp Earthquake was fired with Kingambit beside it, which is an explicit team-rule violation — it took Kingambit from 207 to 85 HP and directly caused Kingambit to die to Dazzling Gleam chip on turn 3 (it finished at 12 HP and burned). Turn 3 we also ignored that a Zoroark-Hisui illusion board meant the 'Pawmot' we EQ'd was partly a disguise; and we split damage across two targets while Indeedee's Dazzling Gleam OHKO'd Garchomp. Finally Milotic was left alone 1v2 with a burn and no Recover plan.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Enforce the never-EQ-next-to-Kingambit rule as a hard block (it cost us the game outright here). 2) When Zoroark/Zoroark-Hisui is on the preview, treat every opposing slot as potentially disguised and prefer single-target reads over spread assumptions. 3) Do not fire Heat Wave into a freshly Mega-evolved unknown Grass/Poison when Weather Ball single-target already kills — spread moves into a Mega we have not scouted risk recoil/reflect abilities. 4) Milotic alone with a burn should Recover-cycle only if it out-damages the drain; otherwise it must have been preserved by switching earlier.

proposals.change: HARD BLOCK Earthquake/ Bulldoze / any Ground spread move from Garchomp whenever Kingambit (or any non-Flying, non-Levitate ally) is in the adjacent slot, regardless of the calc showing a double KO on the foes.
proposals.evidence: T2 Garchomp Earthquake dealt 122 damage to our own Kingambit (207->85); Kingambit then died on T3 at 12 HP to chip it would otherwise have survived, losing us the 2v2 endgame.

proposals.change: ILLUSION GUARD: if Zoroark or Zoroark-Hisui is on the opponent's preview and not yet revealed on field, add a note that one visible foe is a disguise; never commit both actions to a spread calc that assumes the displayed species' bulk.
proposals.evidence: T2 'Pawmot' in slot B was actually Zoroark-Hisui; our EQ calc of 71-136% on both Pawmots was fiction and the real spread left Zoroark at 4% while our own Kingambit took 59%.

proposals.change: UNKNOWN-MEGA CAUTION: on the turn an opposing Pokemon Mega-evolves for the first time in a game, prefer a single-target attack over a spread attack from our Mega when the single-target move already KOs, to avoid unknown contact/reflect/recoil abilities.
proposals.evidence: Drogon fainted on the same turn it KO'd Mega Victreebel with Heat Wave, losing our win condition on turn 1.

proposals.change: Give Milotic Icy Wind over Protect (now proposed five games running) so the back-line has a Fake-Out-proof, Dark-proof speed source once Whimsicott/Drogon are gone.
proposals.evidence: Milotic ended the game 1v1 with no speed control and lost a Giga Drain/burn race it could not outpace.

lessons: NEVER Earthquake with Garchomp while Kingambit, Milotic or Whimsicott is in the adjacent slot — this is a hard block, not a scoring preference; it cost the Bonkler game directly.

When Zoroark/Zoroark-Hisui is on the opposing preview, every displayed foe may be an Illusion: damage calcs on the visible species are unreliable, so prefer single-target attacks and expect the 'duplicate' Pokemon to be the disguise.
On the turn an opposing Pokemon Mega-evolves for the first time, its ability is unknown — prefer a single-target KO over a spread move from our Mega.
A burned Milotic cannot win a Giga Drain stall race; switch or Recover-cycle only while the opponent is not healing off us.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is at 49% over 45 games and its Earthquake keeps being the move that damages our own Kingambit; Sitrus gives Garchomp survivability to use Dragon Claw/Rock Slide single-target lines instead of relying on a spread move we must often block.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Illusion + Revival Blessing resource loop': they got a free extra Pokemon (Pawmot revived Victreebel) and a free turn of misinformation from Zoroark-Hisui. For us, the equivalent resource edge is durability on the back line — swap Milotic's Protect for Icy Wind and move Whimsicott's Focus Sash to Covert Cloak, so our last two Pokemon still have speed control and flinch/Will-O-Wisp immunity instead of a Sash that is already broken by then.
teamInspiration.reason: We lost a 2v2 and then a 1v1 purely to residual burn and speed; their team manufactured extra turns while ours had no answer once Drogon and Kingambit were gone.

change: STAMINA/DEF-BOOST GUARD: if a target's Defense rose from our previous attack and our move's predicted damage is under 15%, hard-block that move against that target next turn; redirect to the partner slot.
evidence: Garchomp clicked Rock Slide into Archaludon on T4, T5, T6 for 2-3% each, granting +1 Defense (Stamina) every single time — 6 free Defense boosts for ~7% total damage.

analysis.whatWorked: Very little. The only positive plays were Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum chipping Pincurchin (the Electric Terrain setter) to 10%, Kingambit's turn-3 Protect correctly dodging a lethal Rising Voltage, and Whimsicott's final Moonblast removing Pincurchin. The preview read that Pincurchin/Raichu were the terrain win-condition was directionally correct.
analysis.lessonsApplied: VIOLATED the single most important standing rule: 'Protect Drogon turn 1 when a faster foe likely OHKOs it.' The calc explicitly displayed 'Drogon threatened by Raichu-Alola Rising Voltage (86-159% OHKO 81%)' and we still Mega'd and attacked into it, losing our Mega and win condition on turn 1 for 10% chip. We also violated the 'do not spend both actions on a target you cannot KO' rule: the combined Moonblast + Weather Ball calc was 45-81% on Raichu, i.e. NOT a KO, while Raichu guaranteed-killed Drogon first. The turn-4 engine fallback is another known failure mode (rate limit/HTTP 429 earlier in the session) and it clicked Kowtow into a Mega Golisopod while Kingambit was in Rising Voltage KO range instead of Protecting or switching.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1: Drogon mega'd and attacked into a faster Alolan Raichu (Surge Surfer, 2x speed in Electric Terrain) that OHKO'd it with Volt Switch — our entire game plan died on turn 1 for 10% damage. The correct line was Drogon Protect (mega) + Whimsicott Moonblast or Tailwind. 2) We never once set Tailwind despite leading Whimsicott specifically for it; Whimsicott contributed one Moonblast and a late KO. 3) Golisopod-Mega's First Impression (+2 priority) and Sucker Punch (+1) made our whole team unable to win any speed race, yet we kept attacking with pieces inside priority KO range — Garchomp at 53/185 was clicking Stomping Tantrum into an active Sucker Punch user and got deleted. The PRIORITY-KO GUARD proposal already on file was ignored on the fallback turn. 4) Zero recognition that Electric Terrain + Rising Voltage doubles power on all our grounded mons (Kingambit, Garchomp, Whimsicott, Milotic) — Pincurchin was a genuine win condition and we gave it three free turns.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-code it: if the displayed threat calc shows any foe with an OHKO roll >=60% on Drogon and that foe is faster, Drogon's only legal action on the mega turn is Protect. Treat Electric Terrain + Pincurchin/Raichu-Alola exactly like Psychic Terrain + Indeedee: the terrain setter is the win condition, and Garchomp (Ground, immune to Electric) is the designated removal tool — lead Garchomp, not Whimsicott, into Electric Terrain teams. Add a hard block on attacking with any Pokemon whose current HP is below the max roll of an active revealed priority move (First Impression/Sucker Punch) — Protect or switch instead. And never leave the fallback engine to pick on a turn where our active is in priority-KO range.

proposals.change: TURN-1 MEGA PROTECT LAW: on the turn Drogon Mega-evolves, if any living foe is faster (including terrain/ability speed doublers like Surge Surfer in Electric Terrain, Chlorophyll, Swift Swim, Scarf) AND its displayed calc vs Drogon reaches >=90% max roll, Drogon MUST click Protect. No exceptions for 'we might KO it first' unless the combined calc is a guaranteed 100% OHKO.
proposals.evidence: T1 vs 0c3an m4n: calc read 'Drogon threatened by Raichu-Alola Rising Voltage (86-159% OHKO 81%)'; our combined offense on Raichu was only 45-81%. Drogon died turn 1 and we lost.

proposals.change: ELECTRIC TERRAIN PROTOCOL: treat Pincurchin/Raichu-Alola/Tapu Koko Electric Terrain as a priority matchup — Garchomp (Electric-immune) is a must-bring and should lead; Rising Voltage doubles on all four of our grounded mons so the terrain setter is the kill target, and Whimsicott (grounded, frail) must not lead.
proposals.evidence: Pincurchin's doubled Rising Voltage did 72% to Whimsicott T1 and KO'd Kingambit from 57/207 on T4; Garchomp took zero damage from it all game.

proposals.change: PRIORITY-KO GUARD (re-up, now as a hard block): if a foe with a revealed +1/+2 priority damaging move (First Impression, Sucker Punch, Grassy Glide, Aqua Jet, Extreme Speed) is active and our Pokemon's current HP is below that move's max roll, that Pokemon may not select an attacking move — only Protect or switch.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp at 53/185 attacked into Golisopod-Mega and was KO'd by Sucker Punch before moving on T4 (engine fallback turn).

proposals.change: FALLBACK SAFETY NET: when the pilot call fails (rate limit), the engine must apply the Protect/switch guardrails above rather than defaulting to a damage-maximizing attack.
proposals.evidence: T4 was a 'wolfe-fallback' turn and it chose Kowtow + Stomping Tantrum while both our mons were in guaranteed KO range; we lost two Pokemon that turn.

lessons: Alolan Raichu in Electric Terrain has Surge Surfer (2x Speed) — it outspeeds Drogon and its Volt Switch/Rising Voltage is a guaranteed OHKO; Protect Drogon on the mega turn, always.

Electric Terrain doubles Rising Voltage against ALL grounded targets: Kingambit, Garchomp, Whimsicott and Milotic all take doubled damage. Remove the terrain setter (Pincurchin) with Garchomp, which is Electric-immune.
Never spend both actions on a target the combined calc does not guarantee to KO when that target guarantees an OHKO on our Mega and moves first — Protect the Mega instead.
Golisopod-Mega has First Impression (+2) and Sucker Punch (+1): any of our Pokemon under ~45% cannot attack into it, only Protect or switch.
Engine fallback turns must still obey the Protect/switch guardrails; a fallback that clicks attacks with two mons in KO range loses the game outright.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp remains the correct variant: it was the only Pokemon immune to the Electric Terrain win condition and outsped everything. The loss was piloting, not items.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'terrain + double priority' shape: Pincurchin set the field and Golisopod-Mega held First Impression + Sucker Punch, so our speed control was irrelevant on every turn. For us, give Dragonite Extreme Speed over Heat Wave (our only +2 priority, lets a chipped Dragonite finish priority users) and swap Whimsicott's Focus Sash for Covert Cloak so it survives Fake Out/flinch chip and actually gets Tailwind off.
teamInspiration.reason: Both of our fast pieces died before acting (Drogon to a terrain-boosted Electric move, Garchomp to Sucker Punch). A team with zero priority of its own cannot contest a board where the opponent has +2 and +1 attackers; we need either our own priority or a bulkier speed setter that survives long enough to click Tailwind.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit under Trick Room moved first and cleanly KO'd Farigiraf with Kowtow Cleave, removing the Armor Tail priority blocker and TR setter. Whimsicott's Encore correctly locked +2 Golisopod-Mega into a move, and Protect on turn 6 blanked the Encored Sucker Punch on the Whimsicott slot.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Kingambit was correctly used as the Farigiraf answer and Sucker Punch was never clicked into Armor Tail. Tailwind was correctly never clicked into Trick Room. However the TURN-1 MEGA PROTECT LAW and the PRIORITY-KO GUARD were both violated: Drogon did not Protect on the mega turn against a Fake Out + Grassy Terrain Rillaboom/Farigiraf core, and Garchomp attacked at 52/185 and then 63/185 HP while a revealed +1 Sucker Punch / +2 First Impression Golisopod-Mega was active, dying to Sucker Punch twice over.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1: Drogon Mega-evolved into a known Fake Out user (Rillaboom) plus Farigiraf; it got Fake Out flinched, wasting half our action economy, and then died turn 2 to Thunderbolt + Wood Hammer having dealt 0 damage. Our best Pokemon contributed nothing. 2) Turn 2 was the losing turn: Drogon at 126/153 was threatened by both foes under incoming Trick Room, Heat Wave was clicked instead of Protect/switch, and Drogon died. 3) Turn 3 Kingambit traded 1-for-1 with Farigiraf but was then OHKO'd by Rillaboom Superpower — a predictable follow-up we did not hedge. 4) Turn 4: Golisopod-Mega used Swords Dance completely unpunished while we split attacks into a switched-in Azumarill (Dragon Claw was immune — a wasted action against a Fairy). 5) Turn 5-6: Garchomp attacked twice while below Sucker Punch's kill range instead of Protecting or switching — a direct violation of the priority guard.
analysis.howToImprove: Treat Rillaboom (Fake Out + Grassy Glide + Wood Hammer) + Farigiraf as an auto-Protect board for Drogon on the mega turn: the flinch costs the entire turn and the follow-up double OHKOs. Never leave Drogon in on turn 2 when both foes' calcs reach it under Trick Room — switch it to Milotic/Kingambit and bring it back after TR ends. Never click a Dragon move into an unknown/Fairy switch-in; check type immunities before committing both actions. When a foe uses Swords Dance, that slot becomes the kill target immediately. And enforce the hard priority guard: any of our mons under the max roll of a revealed Sucker Punch/First Impression may only Protect or switch.

proposals.change: HARD BLOCK: if our Pokemon's current HP is at or below the max roll of a revealed opposing +1/+2 priority damaging move (Sucker Punch, First Impression, Grassy Glide, Aqua Jet, Extreme Speed) from an active foe, that Pokemon may only select Protect or a switch. No attacking.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp at 52/185 and 63/185 clicked Dragon Claw twice into Golisopod-Mega Sucker Punch (72% hit) and died without the opponent ever having to out-speed it.

proposals.change: FAKE-OUT MEGA TURN: on the turn Drogon Mega-evolves, if any active foe has Fake Out available on its first turn out, Drogon must Protect (Protect blocks Fake Out and buys the terrain/TR read) unless a guaranteed OHKO on the Fake Out user is available from the ally slot.
proposals.evidence: Turn 1 Rillaboom Fake Out flinched Drogon; Drogon dealt 0 damage all game and died on turn 2.

proposals.change: SETUP PUNISH OVERRIDE: when a foe uses Swords Dance / Bulk Up / Dragon Dance / Calm Mind, both of our actions should target that slot next turn unless it is behind Protect; do not split damage into its freshly switched-in partner.
proposals.evidence: Golisopod-Mega Swords Dance on turn 4 went unpunished; at +2 it then two-shot our remaining team with Sucker Punch.

proposals.change: TYPE-IMMUNITY CHECK: block Dragon-type moves (Dragon Claw/Dragon Pulse) from targeting Fairy types, and block Normal/Fighting into Ghosts, at the move-selection layer.
proposals.evidence: Turn 4 Garchomp Dragon Claw hit Azumarill for -immune, wasting one of two actions on the key turn.

lessons: Rillaboom's Fake Out on the Drogon mega turn costs us the entire turn: Protect Drogon on turn 1 whenever a Fake Out user is active and unflinched.
Under the opponent's Trick Room, Drogon is the slowest-relevant target of every foe — switch it out on the turn TR goes up rather than attacking into a double KO.
Any of our Pokemon whose HP is below a revealed Sucker Punch / First Impression max roll must Protect or switch; attacking is strictly dominated because priority ignores our speed.
When a foe clicks Swords Dance, that slot becomes the only kill target next turn; splitting damage into its partner hands them a +2 sweeper.
Never aim Dragon Claw/Dragon Pulse at a Fairy type — always type-check before committing both actions on a turn.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp's speed was irrelevant in both of the last two losses (it died to +1/+2 priority, not to being outsped), while a Sitrus Berry would have let it survive one Sucker Punch and keep move freedom to pick Dragon Claw vs Earthquake vs the correct target instead of being locked.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'priority + Fake Out denial' shape: Rillaboom Fake Out blanked our Mega turn and Golisopod-Mega's First Impression/Sucker Punch made our speed control worthless. Give Dragonite Extreme Speed over Heat Wave (our only +2, lets a chipped Dragonite finish priority users first) and swap Whimsicott's Focus Sash for Covert Cloak so it is Fake-Out/flinch-proof and actually gets Tailwind or Encore off on turn 1.
teamInspiration.reason: Across the last four losses our two fastest pieces died before acting to either a flinch or a priority move. A team with no priority of its own cannot contest boards where the opponent holds +3, +2 and +1 brackets.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 vs serumahaja (snow): Protecting Whimsicott into a likely Blizzard while Mega Drogon's Drought instantly overwrote Snowscape — this both cancelled Aurora Veil (it literally failed: '|move|p1a: Ninetales|Aurora Veil|-fail') and let Heat Wave OHKO Ninetales-Alola through the now-absent veil, plus 59% chip onto the Clefable switch-in. Removing the weather setter on turn 1 against a snow team is exactly the Wolfe 'deny their field advantage before it exists' line, and the opponent forfeited immediately after. Lead choice (Whimsicott + Drogon, sun archetype) is our best-performing plan historically (sun 17-3).
analysis.lessonsApplied: The TURN-1 MEGA PROTECT LAW was consulted and correctly resolved: the threat display showed Jolteon Thunderbolt 72-135% (56% OHKO) on Drogon, but Drogon is the Mega and the proposal protects Drogon only when the foe is faster AND >=90% max roll — here the pilot instead Protected Whimsicott (OHKO'd by Blizzard 11%) and attacked with Drogon. That gamble paid off but was NOT clearly correct: Jolteon outspeeds Drogon and Volt Switch took 72% anyway. Rule 'remove the weather/terrain setter first' applied. No Tailwind into TR, no Sucker Punch into Armor Tail, no illegal Earthquake — all guardrails respected.
analysis.whatFailed: Nothing lost the game, but one real risk was taken: we left Drogon exposed to a faster Electric attacker on the Mega turn. Drogon ended the single turn at 43/153 (28%) after Volt Switch; had Jolteon clicked Thunderbolt instead, Drogon dies on turn 1 for the 5th time in recent games and the sun win-con evaporates. The threat line explicitly read 'Drogon threatened by Jolteon Thunderbolt (72-135% (OHKO 56%))' — a coin-flip OHKO on our win condition — and our existing coach note says an 83% OHKO roll is not a KO, but the inverse also holds: a 56% OHKO roll ON US is a coin flip we should not take with the Mega. Whimsicott's Protect was spent on an 11% OHKO threat while Drogon ate the 56% one. Correct allocation was Drogon Protect (Blizzard on Whimsicott with Focus Sash leaves it alive) or Whimsicott Tailwind. Also: we still have zero priority, so any chipped piece of ours is free for Sucker Punch/First Impression/Grassy Glide teams (three of the last four losses).
analysis.howToImprove: Protect allocation must be by OHKO probability, not by 'who looks frail': give Protect to the slot facing the highest OHKO chance, and prefer the Mega when the probabilities are close, because Focus Sash Whimsicott survives anything once while Drogon does not. Codify: if Drogon is Mega-evolving this turn and any faster foe's calc vs Drogon has >=40% OHKO chance, Drogon Protects (lowered from 90% max-roll). Also treat Electric-type fast specials (Jolteon, Raichu-A, Pincurchin, Zapdos, Iron Hands' allies) the same as Rock vs Drogon — they have killed Drogon on turn 1 repeatedly.

proposals.change: PROTECT ALLOCATION BY OHKO PROBABILITY: when exactly one Protect can be spent, assign it to the slot with the highest displayed OHKO% against it; ties and near-ties go to the Mega/win-con, never to a Focus Sash holder (Whimsicott survives one hit regardless).
proposals.evidence: T1 vs serumahaja: Whimsicott Protected vs Blizzard (11% OHKO, and Sash would have saved it anyway) while Drogon ate Jolteon's Electric move at 56% OHKO and ended at 28% HP.

proposals.change: DROGON ELECTRIC GUARD: add fast Electric special attackers (Jolteon, Raichu-Alola, Raichu-Mega-Y, Pincurchin+terrain, Zapdos, Regieleki) to the same Protect-mandatory list as Rock users on Drogon's Mega turn.
proposals.evidence: Raichu-Mega-Y Zap Cannon 10 KOs, Raichu-Alola Volt Switch, Pincurchin Rising Voltage 2, and this game's Jolteon Volt Switch 72% all hit Drogon on turn 1-2 in the killer table.

proposals.change: Swap Whimsicott's Focus Sash for Covert Cloak OR give Dragonite Extreme Speed over Heat Wave to gain a priority bracket; three of the last four losses were decided by opposing +1/+2 priority against our chipped pieces.
proposals.evidence: Golisopod-Mega Sucker Punch/First Impression and Rillaboom Grassy Glide/Wood Hammer accounted for 4 of our last 8 faints; we have no priority except Kingambit's Sucker Punch.

lessons: Protect belongs to the slot with the highest OHKO probability against it, not the frailest slot — a Focus Sash Whimsicott survives one hit anyway, Drogon does not.
Drogon's Drought overwrites Snowscape instantly and makes Aurora Veil FAIL on the same turn — leading Mega Charizard-Y into a snow team removes their entire defensive plan for free.
Fast Electric specials (Jolteon, Raichu-Alola, Pincurchin in terrain, Raichu-Mega-Y) are as lethal to Drogon on the Mega turn as Rock moves: Protect Drogon, not the partner.
A 56% OHKO chance against our Mega is a coin flip we must never accept when a Protect is available.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp: it is the only piece that outspeeds Jolteon/Raichu-A/Surge Surfer tiers without Tailwind, which is precisely the archetype that keeps deleting Drogon on turn 1.

teamInspiration.suggestion: They paired Snow Warning Ninetales-A (Aurora Veil) with fast Electric pivots (Jolteon Volt Switch) so that even a lost weather war still chipped our Mega 72% for free. Copy the 'pivot chip' idea: give Whimsicott Covert Cloak over Focus Sash (Fake-Out/flinch-proof so Tailwind actually lands) and consider Dragonite with Extreme Speed over Heat Wave so chipped foes that pivot out can still be punished through priority.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Mega keeps being traded away on turn 1 to a faster pivot move while our own board has zero priority to reclaim tempo; their build got value on a turn they lost outright.

analysis.whatWorked: Whimsicott's Focus Sash survived Flash Cannon at 1 HP and still produced 2 KOs (Archaludon finisher, Floette-Mega finisher) — it was our highest-value piece. Milotic walled Incineroar and KO'd it with Scald. Turn 2 Protect on the 1 HP Whimsicott was correct. Turn 4 switching Whimsicott out of Floette range was correct macro.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The Drogon-Protect guardrail was VIOLATED on the exact turn it was written for: Archaludon's Electro Shot was displayed as a 108-201% guaranteed OHKO on Drogon and we attacked anyway with a 7-12% Weather Ball. We also ignored the 'don't split damage / don't attack into a mon that outspeeds-and-OHKOs' rule. The anti-rain rule (burst Archaludon in one turn, never chip) was violated: 30-49% Moonblast + 7-12% Weather Ball is textbook chipping, and Stamina + Electro Shot snowballed exactly as predicted. One turn (T3) was a wolfe-fallback with no Protect guardrail applied.
analysis.whatFailed: T1: Drogon Mega-turn with an active Fake Out user (Incineroar) AND a foe showing a guaranteed OHKO (Archaludon Electro Shot) — Drogon should have Protected. Instead it got Fake Out flinched (wasted action economy entirely) and then died turn 2 to the exact move the calc flagged. T1 Drogon's Weather Ball into Archaludon (Steel resists Fire, sun doesn't help vs a Steel/Dragon) did 7-12% — effectively a wasted action; Heat Wave spread or Ancient Power would have been better, but Protect was best. T2: Drogon stayed in at 133 HP against a flagged 88-157% KO move rather than switching to Milotic/Garchomp; it died for zero value. Net result: our Mega contributed 0 damage and 0 KOs all game, and we still nearly won 1v2 — the game was lost on turn 1-2 alone.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Hard rule: on Drogon's Mega turn, if any active foe's displayed threat line contains a >=100% max-roll move against Drogon, Drogon MUST Protect regardless of KO opportunity elsewhere. 2) Never aim a Fire move at a Steel type as our 'KO contribution' — type-check base effectiveness before counting a move toward a focus-fire KO. 3) Against Archaludon specifically: only Garchomp (Earthquake/Stomping Tantrum) and Whimsicott Moonblast meaningfully damage it; Drogon should never be the second attacker into it. 4) If a flagged OHKO threat persists on turn 2 and Protect was already used, SWITCH the Mega out, don't trade.

proposals.change: MEGA-TURN OHKO LOCK: on the turn Drogon/Dragonite Mega-evolves, if the threat line shows any active foe with a max-roll >= 100% against that Mega, the Mega may ONLY select Protect or a switch. Attacking is hard-blocked.
proposals.evidence: T1 threat line read 'Drogon threatened by Archaludon Electro Shot (108-201% OHKO)'; we attacked for 7-12% and lost Drogon on T2 with zero damage contributed.

proposals.change: EFFECTIVENESS FLOOR FOR FOCUS FIRE: a move contributing less than 20% max-roll to a target may not be counted as part of a focus-fire KO plan; pick a different target or Protect instead.
proposals.evidence: Weather Ball (Fire, resisted by Archaludon's Steel) at 7-12% was spent as the 'second half' of a KO attempt that never materialised.

proposals.change: PERSISTENT OHKO = SWITCH: if our Mega survived turn N at reduced HP and the same foe still shows a >=100% max roll on turn N+1, and Protect was used on turn N, the Mega must switch out rather than attack.
proposals.evidence: T2 Drogon at 133/153 with 'Archaludon Electro Shot (88-157% KO)' flagged; stayed in, fainted, contributed nothing.

lessons: On the Mega-evolution turn, a displayed >=100% max-roll threat against our Mega overrides every offensive consideration: Protect, always.
Fire moves are resisted by Steel — Weather Ball/Heat Wave into Archaludon, Gholdengo or Metagross is not a damage contribution and must not be counted in a focus-fire plan.

Archaludon's Stamina raises Defense on every physical/contact hit and Electro Shot gains +1 SpA: it must be burst by Garchomp Ground moves or Whimsicott Moonblast in a single turn, never chipped from two sides.
A Mega that dies without dealing damage loses the game by itself: our 3 remaining mons still took 3 of their 4 KOs this game.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp remains the only piece that reliably outspeeds and bursts Archaludon/Pelipper; keep it while we fix the Mega-turn Protect discipline.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Fake Out + immediate OHKO threat' turn-1 shape: Incineroar denied our Mega's action while Archaludon set up a guaranteed kill. For us, give Dragonite Extreme Speed over Heat Wave (our only +2 to punish chipped setup mons) and move Whimsicott to Covert Cloak so Fake Out can't blank our Tailwind turn; additionally consider Milotic over Kingambit in rain matchups, as Milotic alone took 2 of their mons after our Mega died.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Mega contributed 0 damage in this loss purely because the opponent held both a Fake Out and a guaranteed OHKO on turn 1; the fix is either Protect discipline (code) or structural Fake Out immunity + priority (team).

analysis.whatWorked: Leading Kingambit into Psychic Terrain was correct: it was immune to Expanding Force and KO'd Indeedee on turn 1, removing the terrain setter and their Expanding Force win condition. Dragon Pulse breaking the presumed Sash was the right support action. Turn 3 Protect on Whimsicott + switching the 2% Kingambit out for healthy Drogon was a clean repositioning play.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: psyterrain lead rule (Kingambit lead, Sneasler home), setup/win-con denial (Indeedee removed turn 1), switching a near-dead Pokemon instead of attacking, Protect allocation on the slot about to die. Violated: the MEGA-TURN OHKO LOCK and the 'never let our Mega die without dealing damage' rule were effectively bypassed — Mega Dragonite was exposed on turn 2 to an untested Mega Garchomp-Z while already chipped by Expanding Force, and the PERSISTENT OHKO = SWITCH rule was not applied to Drogon on turn 5.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 2 was the game: Dragonite at 131/168 stayed in and fired Dragon Pulse at a Garchomp that was Mega-evolving (unknown ability/stats) — Garchomp-Mega-Z moved first and Draco Meteor OHKO'd our Mega for zero return value. Dragonite had Protect available; the Mega that was already chipped by Expanding Force had no Multiscale cushion. 2) Hisuian Arcanine's Flare Blitz got 3 free KOs (Kingambit to 5 HP, Whimsicott, Kingambit) and was never targeted until turn 5 when both our mons were at 2%/16%. We never applied focus fire to the actual damage dealer. 3) Turn 4 Whimsicott Moonblast chipped Garchomp to 26% but we never converted — Drogon Protected instead of attacking a 26% Garchomp on turn 5 (we instead split Kowtow Cleave + Ancient Power into Arcanine for a non-guaranteed KO while both our mons died). 4) Total damage output: 174% across the whole game, one KO. Our Mega contributed 78% and died turn 2.
analysis.howToImprove: On the turn an opposing Pokemon Mega-evolves while our chipped Mega is in a potential OHKO range, Protect or switch — never trade. Treat the un-Mega'd foe's Mega form stats as the worst case. Second: against Hisuian Arcanine (Rock Head Flare Blitz / Head Smash, no recoil), it is the primary damage dealer on these teams and must be the focus-fire target before the Psychic Terrain support piece's partner. Third: once a foe is below 30% (Garchomp-Mega-Z at 26%), finish it with a guaranteed single-target attack rather than Protecting and then splitting into a healthy foe.

proposals.change: OPPOSING MEGA TURN GUARD: if an active foe has an unused Mega stone (or Mega-evolves this turn) and our Mega/win-con is below 85% HP, our Mega may only Protect or switch — attacking is blocked. Worst-case stats of the Mega form must be assumed.
proposals.evidence: T2: Dragonite at 78% attacked into a Mega-evolving Garchomp; Garchomp-Mega-Z Draco Meteor OHKO'd it with zero damage traded back.

proposals.change: FOCUS-FIRE THE DAMAGE DEALER: rank foes by total displayed max-roll damage against our side, not by 'support value'. Hisuian Arcanine (Flare Blitz/Head Smash, Rock Head) scored 3 KOs untouched this game — it must be the primary target once the terrain/TR setter is gone.
proposals.evidence: Arcanine-Hisui Flare Blitz: 88% on Kingambit T1, 99% on Whimsicott T2, KO T4, KO T5 — it was never attacked until turn 5.

proposals.change: SUB-30% FINISH RULE: a foe below 30% HP that is not behind Protect must be finished with a guaranteed single-target attack before any Protect is spent on our side, unless that Protect prevents a certain OHKO on a healthy piece.
proposals.evidence: T4 Moonblast left Garchomp-Mega-Z at 26%; T5 we Protected/ignored it and it Power Gem'd Drogon for the KO.

proposals.change: Give Dragonite Extreme Speed over Heat Wave (or Protect over Heat Wave) — the recurring failure is our Mega dying before acting against faster/priority threats; we have zero priority outside Kingambit's Sucker Punch, which is blocked by Psychic Terrain in exactly these matchups.
proposals.evidence: 4 of the last 5 losses: our Mega died turn 1-2; in this game Psychic Terrain also blanked Sucker Punch as an option.

lessons: On the turn an opposing Pokemon Mega-evolves, assume worst-case Mega stats and coverage: our chipped Mega must Protect or switch, never trade attacks.
Hisuian Arcanine has Rock Head (recoil-free Flare Blitz / Head Smash) and is the top damage dealer on Psychic Terrain balance teams — focus-fire it immediately after the terrain setter dies.
A foe left at or below 30% HP must be finished with a guaranteed single-target attack before we spend a Protect elsewhere; chip that is never converted is a wasted action.
Expanding Force chip on our Mega (spread damage through the ally slot) removes Multiscale — after any spread hit, Mega Dragonite is no longer safe to leave in against a potential OHKO.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 24-27 and was not even brought in the last two psyterrain losses; Sitrus lets Garchomp survive one Light of Ruin / Power Gem and keeps move flexibility against Mega Garchomp-Z mirrors where Choice-lock into Dragon Claw is dead weight.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'two-threat, one-support' shape: Indeedee only had to live one turn while Arcanine-Hisui and Mega Garchomp-Z both held guaranteed OHKOs. For us, drop Heat Wave on Dragonite for Extreme Speed (our only +2 bracket; Psychic Terrain blocks Kingambit's Sucker Punch in exactly these games) and consider Milotic over Whimsicott in psyterrain matchups where Prankster Tailwind is blocked by Dark types and Whimsicott dies to any Fire/Fairy hit.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Mega died on turn 2 for 78% of damage and Whimsicott contributed 74% before fainting; we had no way to punish a 26% Mega Garchomp because every piece we had left was slower and had no priority.

whatWorked: Won 4-1 vs peterfur's Hippowdon sand/Trick Room-support team. The preview plan (Mega Charizard-Y + Whimsicott Tailwind lead, Garchomp/Milotic back) followed the confirmed anti-sand simulation result and delivered: Drought immediately overwrote nothing yet but gave Weather Ball 100 BP Fire, and focus-firing Oranguru (the Trick Room/Future Sight support) turn 1 with Moonblast + Weather Ball removed their speed-control enabler before it ever acted. Turn 2 Weather Ball OHKO'd Chandelure (Flash Fire never got to absorb a Fire move because we picked the non-Fire-immune target first). Switching the 1 HP Whimsicott out into Milotic instead of letting sandstorm chip-kill it preserved a body and brought in the correct sand-immune bulky wall. Scald burn on Hippowdon converted into the game-winning residual, and Scarf Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum (not Earthquake) correctly avoided hitting ally Milotic and OHKO'd Toxtricity through the Protect-fail turn.
lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) CONFIRMED anti-sand plan — Mega Charizard + Whimsicott Tailwind lead, not Dragonite+Milotic; (2) never Earthquake next to a grounded ally — Stomping Tantrum used both turns beside Milotic; (3) deny speed control first — Oranguru (Trick Room/Future Sight support) was the turn-1 focus-fire target, not the flashy Chandelure; (4) switch a Pokemon that is about to die rather than letting it faint for free (Whimsicott at 1 HP -> Milotic); (5) safe-play-when-ahead discipline — turns 3 and 4 were straight guaranteed-damage lines with no predictions while up on count; (6) repeated-Protect read — after Toxtricity Protected on T3 we correctly attacked it again on T4 (Protect cannot succeed twice reliably) and it failed. VIOLATED: the standing rule 'Protect Drogon vs active Hippowdon/Tyranitar Rock Slide in sand, even over securing a KO.' On turn 2 Hippowdon was already on the field with sand up and Drogon is 4x Rock weak; we clicked Weather Ball and Drogon died to Rock Slide immediately after getting the KO.
whatFailed: Only one real misplay: Drogon's death on turn 2. With Hippowdon freshly switched in under sandstorm, Rock Slide is the single most predictable move in the game against a 4x-weak Mega Charizard, and the threat line even listed Chandelure damage while the real killer (Hippowdon Rock Slide) was the newly arrived mon. We traded our Mega for Chandelure when Garchomp/Milotic already beat Chandelure comfortably — Drogon could have Protected (or switched to Garchomp, Ground-immune to nothing here but sand-immune and Rock-resistant) and still cleaned up later in sun. Secondary issues: the damage calc underestimated Milotic Scald vs Hippowdon by ~40 points (predicted 42-52%, actual 93%) and Moonblast vs Oranguru (22-38% vs 45%), meaning our focus-fire math is systematically too conservative against physically-bulky special-weak targets; and Tailwind was never set the entire game (0 turns), so the win came purely from raw matchup rather than speed control.
howToImprove: Hard-code the sand Rock-Slide guardrail: whenever Drogon (Charizard-Mega-Y) is on the field and ANY active foe is a Rock-move-capable Ground/Rock sand setter (Hippowdon, Tyranitar, Excadrill, Gigalith) that moves after us, Drogon may only Protect or switch — a KO on a different slot never justifies losing our Mega to a 4x hit. Additionally: when a foe switches in mid-turn, immediately re-rank threats around the NEW mon, not the one it replaced. Keep the sand lead plan and the Oranguru-style 'kill the support before it acts' habit; start clicking Tailwind on turns where neither of our slots is under immediate OHKO threat, since 0 Tailwind turns in a 4-turn win is luck, not a plan.

proposals.change: SAND 4x GUARD: if Drogon is active and an opposing Rock-capable sand mon (Hippowdon/Tyranitar/Tyranitar-Mega/Excadrill/Gigalith/Garchomp-Mega-Z) is active and faster or equal, Drogon may only select Protect or switch; attacking is hard-blocked that turn.
proposals.evidence: T2 vs peterfur: Drogon clicked Weather Ball to KO Chandelure and was immediately OHKO'd by Hippowdon Rock Slide (68% shown, actual kill) despite Garchomp and Milotic both beating Chandelure later.

proposals.change: NEW-SWITCH THREAT REFRESH: when an opposing Pokemon switched in on the previous turn, its threat damage must be recomputed and prioritized over the mon it replaced before choosing Protect targets.
proposals.evidence: The T2 threat line only listed Chandelure moves against Drogon while Hippowdon — the mon that actually KO'd it — had switched in at the end of T1.

proposals.change: Set Tailwind on any turn where neither active slot faces a >=70% max-roll threat and no foe is in guaranteed KO range; 0 Tailwind turns across a whole game means our primary speed control is never cashing in.
proposals.evidence: We won 4-1 but Tailwind turns were us 0, them 0; Whimsicott spent the game clicking Moonblast and then switching out at 1 HP.

lessons: In sandstorm, a Rock-capable sand setter that just switched in is a guaranteed OHKO on Drogon — Protect or switch the Mega even when a KO on the other slot is available.
Re-evaluate threats around a freshly switched-in foe, not the Pokemon it replaced; the mid-turn switch-in is usually the one that kills us next turn.
Flash Fire users (Chandelure) make Fire moves worthless — target the non-immune slot first with the Fire Mega and let Ground/Water teammates handle the Flash Fire mon.
Stomping Tantrum is the correct Garchomp move whenever a grounded ally (Milotic/Kingambit/Whimsicott) is beside it; it OHKO'd Toxtricity without touching Milotic.
After a foe Protects, attacking the same slot next turn is correct — consecutive Protect fails.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again produced a clean OHKO on Toxtricity and is the piece that functions without Tailwind; keep the current loadout while we fix the Mega-preservation bug rather than adding another variable.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'cheap support + weather chip' shape: Hippowdon traded 1-for-1 with our Mega just by existing under sand, and Yawn forced our Scarf mon into bad turns. For us, give Drogon Protect priority discipline in code and consider swapping Dragonite's Heat Wave for Protect/Extreme Speed so the second Mega is never a 3-move attacker that must trade; also test Milotic with a Scald-first spread (more SpD) since Scald hit 93% on a physically bulky Hippowdon and is our best anti-sand engine.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Mega died for a KO that two other teammates could have taken for free; the opponent's cheapest mon got the most valuable trade of the game purely through weather typing.

analysis.whatWorked: Won 4-1 vs pcrlbot12d159c39a. Turn 1 engine fallback (Whimsicott Protect + Drogon Heat Wave) removed Gholdengo outright and left Mega Staraptor at 21% — a spread move into two frail foes is exactly the right turn-1 action when the Fire Mega is in sun. Turn 3 double-target (Garchomp Dragon Claw on Basculegion at 37%, Whimsicott Moonblast on Staraptor at 21%) converted both chipped foes in one turn and swung the game to 4v1. Turn 4 switching Choice-locked Garchomp (locked into Dragon Claw, useless into Fairy Whimsicott) out to Milotic correctly reset the Choice lock and respected the 'never aim Dragon moves at a Fairy' rule. Damage calcs were accurate (3/3 inside predicted ranges).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) never Dragon Claw a Fairy — Garchomp switched instead; (2) Choice-lock reset by switching; (3) safe-play directive when ahead 4v1 — Turn 5 double-attacked the last foe with 100% accurate moves instead of predicting; (4) focus-fire chipped targets to convert them. VIOLATED: the standing 'Protect Drogon turn 1 when a faster OHKO threat exists' rule was not the issue — the issue was Turn 2. Drogon at full HP faced a displayed Basculegion Wave Crash of 87-142% (77% OHKO) and we attacked anyway into a near-certain Protect from a 21% Staraptor. That is precisely the '>=100% max-roll threat against our Mega = Protect' rule being ignored, and Drogon died having nothing left to do.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 2 was the only real misplay and it cost us the Mega. Board: Staraptor-Mega at 21% (obvious Protect — it was in KO range from either of our attacks and had already lost its partner) and a freshly switched-in Basculegion at 100% with a displayed 77% OHKO roll on Drogon. We spent BOTH actions (Moonblast + Heat Wave) on the 21% Staraptor slot, it Protected, and the only damage dealt was Heat Wave's spread chip onto Basculegion — then Wave Crash deleted Drogon. Correct line: Drogon Protect (its own rule), Whimsicott Moonblast or Heat Wave into Basculegion / or Whimsicott Tailwind. Also, Tailwind was never set in this game (0 Tailwind turns for the 9th game running) despite turn 4-5 being completely free; the opponent's Whimsicott got Tailwind up and we never did. Finally, the NEW-SWITCH THREAT REFRESH proposal was violated: Basculegion switched in on turn 1 and was never recomputed as the primary threat on turn 2.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Hard rule: when a foe is at or below 25% HP and is the ONLY member of its slot that can be KO'd, assume Protect and do NOT commit both actions to it — split, or Protect the threatened Mega. 2) A foe that switched in LAST turn at full HP with a >=70% max roll on our Mega outranks a 21% chipped foe as the target/threat for Protect allocation. 3) Tailwind must be clicked on any turn where Whimsicott is healthy, no slot faces a guaranteed OHKO, and no KO is being converted — we have now gone 9 games with 0 Tailwind turns while opponents routinely get theirs. 4) Keep the spread-move turn-1 pattern vs two frail foes in sun; it is our highest-value opening.

proposals.change: OBVIOUS-PROTECT GUARD: if a foe is at <=25% HP, has an unused Protect, and its partner slot presents a >=70% max-roll threat to one of our actives, we may not spend BOTH actions on the low-HP slot. One action must go to the threatening slot or to Protect on the threatened piece.
proposals.evidence: T2 vs pcrlbot: both Moonblast and Heat Wave aimed at 21% Staraptor-Mega; it Protected and Basculegion then OHKO'd Drogon with Wave Crash (displayed 87-142%, 77% OHKO).

proposals.change: MEGA PROTECT ENFORCEMENT: Drogon/Dragonite must select Protect or switch on any turn where the displayed max roll against it is >=100% from a foe that is faster or has equal speed, with no exception for 'our partner can KO the other slot'.
proposals.evidence: Drogon attacked into a displayed 87-142% Wave Crash and died; our Mega has now been the first faint in 5 of the last 6 logged games.

proposals.change: TAILWIND CONVERSION: on any turn with Whimsicott healthy (>50%), no guaranteed OHKO threat on either of our slots, and no foe currently in KO range of our other action, Tailwind is mandatory.
proposals.evidence: 0 Tailwind turns in this game and in all 5 of the last logged games; the opposing Whimsicott set Tailwind freely on T4.

lessons: A foe at <=25% HP whose partner just switched in healthy is an obvious Protect bait: never spend both actions on it — one action belongs to the new threat or to Protect on our Mega.
Heat Wave spread chip is not a substitute for targeting the real threat: 23-44% onto Basculegion did not stop a 100% Wave Crash.
Our Mega must Protect whenever the displayed max roll against it is >=100% from a faster foe, even if that means skipping a KO attempt on the other slot.
After a mid-turn switch-in, recompute threats around the NEW foe before allocating Protect — the Pokemon that replaced the fainted one is usually the one that kills us next turn.
When Choice-locked into a move the active foe is immune/resistant to (Dragon Claw into Fairy), switching is strictly better than clicking it.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again out-sped and converted a chipped Basculegion for a clean KO on T3; the loadout is at 49% and the losses trace to Mega Protect discipline, not the item. Keep it stable for more sample.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'chip-and-Protect' tempo: Mega Staraptor at 21% bought a whole free turn with Protect while Basculegion switched in and took our Mega. Give Drogon strict Protect priority in code, and consider swapping Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so a chipped foe behind Protect can still be finished the following turn through priority rather than requiring a second full-commitment turn.
teamInspiration.reason: Both of our last three Mega deaths came on turns where the opponent held a free Protect on a chipped mon plus a healthy OHKO threat; priority is the only tool that punishes that structure.

analysis.whatWorked: Leading Kingambit into Farigiraf Trick Room was correct and paid off instantly: Kowtow Cleave + Garchomp chip KO'd the Trick Room setter on turn 1 before it ever moved, so Trick Room never came up all game. Kingambit also traded itself for Sylveon (Iron Head OHKO) and Defiant turned Staraptor's Intimidate into +2. Dragonite + Garchomp cleaned up Torkoal, removing sun/Eruption. We won the speed-control war on paper (6 Tailwind turns to 0).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Speed-control-setter denial was executed perfectly (Farigiraf dead turn 1). We correctly avoided Tailwind while Trick Room was a possibility and only set it once Farigiraf was gone. We correctly switched Kingambit-type low-HP pieces out in earlier games, but here Kingambit at 25/207 was left in on turn 4 to trade. Garchomp Choice-lock discipline was violated: it stayed locked into Stomping Tantrum and spent turns 4, 7, 8 (and more) clicking a Ground move at a Flying-type Staraptor for literally 0 damage.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Garchomp spent at least four full actions clicking Stomping Tantrum into a Flying-type Staraptor (0 damage, repeated immunity messages). That is half our action economy donated for multiple turns and is exactly the 'Choice-locked into a useless move -> switch out' rule we already have written down. 2) We never punished Mega Staraptor's Close Combat Defense/SpD... actually it boosted def/spd (Contrary-like via Close Combat? No — it boosted, meaning Contrary Staraptor), and we kept trading into it instead of focusing it down or switching to Milotic, which we never even brought. 3) We burned turns 5-6 chipping a 44% Torkoal through two Protects while Staraptor Mega-evolved for free and started snowballing. 4) The endgame was a 20-turn grind where a +Def/+SpD Contrary Mega Staraptor had both speed (after our Tailwind lapsed) and power — exactly the board state we are told never to allow. 5) Whimsicott contributed only 47% damage and never got a second Tailwind out before dying.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: a Choice-locked Pokemon whose locked move is an immunity against every live foe must switch out immediately — no exceptions, no 'but it's our fastest mon'. Second: when a foe boosts from its own Close Combat (Contrary), it is the single win condition on the board — focus both actions onto it immediately or stall it out with Protect cycling while chipping; never let it accumulate turns. Third: against a Contrary/boosting flier, Milotic (Ice Beam, bulk, Recover) should have been brought over Whimsicott once Farigiraf died; plan the back-two for the post-setter board, not just the lead board. Fourth: do not spend two actions on a 3% Torkoal behind a Protect pattern — one action is enough, the other belongs to the freshly Mega-evolved threat.

proposals.change: CHOICE-LOCK IMMUNITY SWITCH: if our Choice-locked Pokemon's locked move has zero effect (type immunity) against every non-fainted active foe, switching is mandatory that turn; attacking is hard-blocked.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp clicked Stomping Tantrum into Flying Staraptor on turns 4, 7, 8 and beyond — 'immune' four times, ~4 wasted actions in a 20-turn loss.

proposals.change: CONTRARY/BOOSTING-FOE FOCUS: if a foe gains stat boosts from its own attacking move (Close Combat raising def/spd, Overheat raising SpA), that slot becomes the mandatory target for both of our actions until it is KO'd or we are forced to Protect.
proposals.evidence: Mega Staraptor used Close Combat and gained +1 Def/+1 SpD on turn 6, then took 14 more turns and both our remaining mons.

proposals.change: PROTECT-PATTERN OVERKILL GUARD: never commit both actions to a foe below 50% HP that has Protected on the previous turn; one action must go to the other slot or to our own Protect.
proposals.evidence: Turns 5-6 both actions went into a 44% Torkoal; turn 5 both were blocked by a double Protect, letting Staraptor Mega-evolve for free.

proposals.change: Bring Milotic over Whimsicott in Trick Room matchups where the TR setter dies turn 1 — Milotic's Ice Beam/bulk answers the Flying/Normal cleanup mons (Staraptor, Sylveon) that these teams back up with.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott dealt 47% all game and died to Close Combat; Milotic sat on the bench while a boosted Flying type ground us out.

lessons: A Choice-locked Pokemon whose move is an immunity against every live foe must switch out that turn — clicking it is a guaranteed zero-value action.
Staraptor with Contrary gains +1 Def/+1 SpD from its own Close Combat: it must be focus-fired or walled by Milotic, never traded with over many turns.
Never commit both actions to a sub-50% foe that Protected last turn while a fresh Mega-evolving threat sits in the other slot.
After the Trick Room setter dies on turn 1, re-plan the back two around their cleanup mons, not the setter.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice Scarf cost us ~4 full actions this game by locking Garchomp into Stomping Tantrum against a Flying type; Sitrus Garchomp keeps coverage flexibility (Rock Slide vs Staraptor) and survives longer in grind-out endgames.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'cheap setter + boosting cleanup Mega' shape: Farigiraf was expendable, and Contrary Mega Staraptor won by accumulating free boosts. For us, bring Milotic (Ice Beam/Recover) as the default fourth in Trick Room matchups instead of Whimsicott once the TR setter is likely to die turn 1, and consider Dragonite with Extreme Speed over Heat Wave to punish chipped boosting fliers through priority.
teamInspiration.reason: Our loss came entirely after turn 6 against one boosted Flying type we had no way to pressure: Garchomp was Ground-locked, Whimsicott was frail, and Dragonite had no priority.

analysis.whatWorked: Milotic was the only piece that earned value: it KO'd Raichu and Abomasnow and stalled Mega Blastoise for 6 turns with Protect/Recover cycling. Turn 1 Weather Ball into Raichu was the right target identification (Mega Raichu-Y Zap Cannon is a listed Drogon killer). Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave into +2 Blastoise on T2 was the correct win-con target even though the Pelipper switch blanked it.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Mega Protect enforcement was followed on T2 and attempted on T3 (Surf max 259% on Drogon).
