Anti-setup doctrine was partially followed (we targeted Blastoise, not the partner). However the single most important rule — 'Setup is a win condition, punish it NOW' — was violated on turn 1: Blastoise Shell Smashed completely unpunished while Kingambit sat behind a Protect against a Fake Out user that cannot threaten it that turn.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) TURN 1 WASTED ACTION: Kingambit Protected against a Raichu Fake Out lead — Fake Out does not threaten Kingambit, and Protect scored zero. That free turn let Blastoise Shell Smash to +2/+2/+2 and the game was effectively decided there. Kowtow Cleave into Blastoise on T1 (68-107%) was available and would have KO'd or near-KO'd it BEFORE the boost mattered. 2) DOUBLE PROTECT T3: Drogon clicked Protect twice in a row — it FAILED (consecutive Protect) and Drogon died for free to Surf. The hard rule 'never Protect twice in a row' was broken by our own pilot, costing our Mega for 0 damage. Drogon finished the game with 0% damage dealt and 0 KOs. 3) Drogon contributed literally nothing across two Megas-worth of turns; our entire damage output for the game was 30% from Milotic. 4) Lead choice: Kingambit + Drogon into a Shell Smash Blastoise + Fake Out Raichu gave the opponent a free setup turn with no Whimsicott Encore available.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block Protect when the same Pokemon used Protect the immediately preceding turn (the engine must never offer a guaranteed-fail action). Hard-block Protect on a slot whose only incoming threat this turn is Fake Out/priority chip (<35% max roll) — spend that action attacking the setup mon. Treat Shell Smash/Dragon Dance/Calm Mind on turn 1 as a mandatory double-target: both actions go to the booster on the turn it boosts or the turn after. Against Blastoise/Cloyster/Torterra (Shell Smash shells) bring Whimsicott in the LEAD so Prankster Encore can lock the boost away.

proposals.change: CONSECUTIVE-PROTECT HARD BLOCK: if a Pokemon used Protect/Detect on the immediately preceding turn, Protect is prohibited this turn — no exceptions, it is a guaranteed-fail action.
proposals.evidence: T3 Drogon Protect -> '-fail', Drogon then ate Mega Blastoise Surf for a free KO and ended the game with 0% damage dealt.

proposals.change: FAKE-OUT-ONLY PROTECT BAN: do not Protect a slot whose highest incoming max roll this turn is below 35% (e.g. only a Fake Out or chip move threatens it). That action must attack, preferably the setup/booster slot.
proposals.evidence: T1 Kingambit Protected versus a Raichu Fake Out lead while Blastoise Shell Smashed to +2/+2/+2 unpunished; Kowtow Cleave (68-107%) was available.

proposals.change: SHELL SMASH / BOOST EMERGENCY: on the turn a foe uses Shell Smash, Dragon Dance, Quiver Dance, Calm Mind, Nasty Plot or Swords Dance, both of our actions must target that foe on the following turn unless an action is a forced Protect against a >=100% roll.
proposals.evidence: Blastoise reached +2 on T1, Mega-evolved on T2, and Surf alone KO'd Kingambit, Drogon, Whimsicott and eventually Milotic — 4 of our mons to a single boosted attacker.

proposals.change: Lead Whimsicott (Prankster Encore/Tailwind) rather than Kingambit whenever the opponent shows a Shell Smash user (Blastoise, Cloyster, Torterra, Polteageist) — Encore on the Shell Smash turn fully reverses the sweep.
proposals.evidence: We had Whimsicott on the bench the entire game and it only entered on T4 at which point +2 Mega Blastoise could not be stopped.

lessons: Never Protect twice in a row — consecutive Protect auto-fails and donates a free KO; the engine must hard-block it.
A Fake Out lead is not a reason to Protect: Fake Out costs us at most 20% and a flinch; the correct action is to attack the partner, especially if the partner can set up.
Shell Smash on turn 1 is a game-losing board state: the boosting slot must be attacked on the boost turn or immediately after with both actions, never Protect-stalled.
Mega Blastoise's Surf is a spread move that hits its own ally — it can KO through our Protect on the other slot; Protect on only one of our slots does not defend the team against spread Surf.
Our Mega finishing a game with 0% damage dealt is an automatic loss signal: if the Mega cannot attack safely for two consecutive turns, switch it out instead of Protect-cycling.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep the current loadout; the loss was a decision error (double Protect, unpunished Shell Smash), not an item failure. Scarf Garchomp remains our fastest answer to +2 sweepers and was not even brought this game.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'free setup turn' engine: Fake Out + Shell Smash Mega Blastoise converted one unpunished turn into four KOs. For us, lead Whimsicott (Encore) in any matchup with a Shell Smash/boost shell, and seriously consider swapping Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed — a +2 priority move is the only tool that punishes a chipped, boosted sweeper that outspeeds our whole team.
teamInspiration.reason: Every one of our last four losses featured a boosted or priority-protected foe we could not touch after it got ahead in speed; we have zero moves in the +1/+2 bracket outside Kingambit's Sucker Punch, which is blocked by Psychic Terrain and Armor Tail in half the meta.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 correctly identified Pelipper as the rain setter and committed both actions to removing it; the opponent dodged by switching, but the double-attack converted into ~93% chip on Mamoswine, which later gave Kingambit a free KO. Drogon's Mega + Drought flip did kill the rain and Heat Wave finished +2 Mega Blastoise on turn 3. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave cleanly removed Mamoswine on turn 4.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The Shell Smash emergency rule was recognized verbally (turn 2 comment) but only half-executed: only Whimsicott's Moonblast went into Blastoise while Garchomp chased a 7% Mamoswine, violating the standing 'both actions onto the boosting slot' proposal and the 'no overkill on a sub-50% foe' rule in reverse. The rain rule (kill the setter first) was applied but abandoned once Pelipper switched. The Protect-discipline rules were never used: Garchomp had Protect-less turns facing a guaranteed Ice Shard KO and we never switched it out.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Lead choice: Whimsicott + Scarf Garchomp into Mamoswine (Ice Shard) is the worst possible pairing — Garchomp is 4x weak to Ice and dies to a priority move from a slower mon, which is exactly what happened on turn 2 for 100%. 2) Turn 1 we attacked the slot Pelipper vacated: both attacks redirected into Mamoswine while Blastoise got a completely free Shell Smash — the single most game-losing board state per our own checklist, and we had Whimsicott's Prankster Encore available to lock Blastoise into Shell Smash the next turn. 3) Turn 2: we knew +2 Blastoise outspeeds and OHKOs both our mons, yet we clicked two attacks with zero Protect/switch and lost Garchomp for free; worse, Garchomp's Dragon Claw went into a 7% Mamoswine that Moonblast or anything could finish, while Blastoise needed both actions. 4) We never used Encore at all against a Shell Smash team — Whimsicott's single most valuable move in this matchup. 5) Turn 3: Drogon Heat Wave missed (90% accuracy) and we were already committed; a single-target Weather Ball in sun on Blastoise would have been guaranteed. 6) Turn 4: Drogon stayed in at 11% HP against a 7% Mamoswine holding Ice Shard priority — 100% death, we should have switched Drogon or Protected; instead the Mega died for 0 extra value and we lost 4-0 on momentum.
analysis.howToImprove: Against any revealed Shell Smash/Blastoise rain shell: lead Whimsicott + Milotic (not Scarf Garchomp — Ice Shard/Ice Beam is everywhere on those teams), and the turn Shell Smash is used, Encore it immediately with Prankster (Encore is +1 and Blastoise is not Dark). If Encore is unavailable, commit BOTH actions to the boosted slot the following turn and never split. Any Pokemon 4x weak to a revealed priority move (Garchomp vs Ice Shard) must Protect or switch the turn after that priority move is revealed. A Mega below 20% HP facing any priority user must switch out, never attack. Prefer 100%-accurate single-target moves when the target is the win condition.

proposals.change: SHELL SMASH ENCORE MANDATE: if Whimsicott (or any Encore user) is on the field the turn after a foe used Shell Smash/Dragon Dance/Quiver Dance/Calm Mind/Nasty Plot/Swords Dance, Encore on that foe is the highest-scored action unless the foe is Dark-type; all other Whimsicott moves get -4.
proposals.evidence: Mega Blastoise got a free Shell Smash on turn 1 and swept; we never clicked Encore once despite Prankster Encore being available every turn.

proposals.change: ICE-SHARD / PRIORITY LETHALITY GUARD: once a foe reveals a priority attack (Ice Shard, Aqua Jet, Sucker Punch, Extreme Speed, Grassy Glide) that would deal >=80% to one of our actives, that Pokemon must Protect or switch next turn; attacking with it is penalized -5.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp (4x Ice) was KO'd by Mamoswine Ice Shard on T2 and Drogon at 11% was KO'd by the same move on T4 while attacking.

proposals.change: Do not lead Scarf Garchomp into any team showing Mamoswine, Abomasnow, Froslass, Weavile or Glaceon (Ice priority/coverage); lead Whimsicott + Milotic or Whimsicott + Kingambit instead.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp died turn 2 to Ice Shard from a 57%-HP Mamoswine, instantly losing the speed-control plan.

proposals.change: Consider Dragonite's Heat Wave -> Extreme Speed so we have a +2 priority answer to chipped boosted sweepers (Blastoise at 28%, Staraptor at 21%, Mamoswine at 7% all survived a turn they should not have).
proposals.evidence: Four consecutive losses featured a chipped, faster/boosted foe that we could not touch; Sucker Punch is our only priority and it is blocked in half the meta.

lessons: A foe that uses Shell Smash while our Prankster Encore user is alive must be Encored the very next turn — Encore is +1 priority and reverses the entire sweep.
Never split actions on the turn after a foe boosts: both attacks go into the boosted slot, even if the other foe is at low HP.
Any of our Pokemon 4x weak to a revealed priority move (Garchomp vs Ice Shard) must Protect or switch, not attack.
A Mega under 20% HP facing a live priority user is dead if it attacks — switch it out and preserve the damage it can still deal later.
When the target is the opponent's win condition, prefer the 100%-accurate single-target move over a 90% spread move (Weather Ball over Heat Wave).

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp contributed 43% damage and died turn 2 to a priority Ice Shard; Sitrus gives it a chance to survive the Ice chip that keeps deleting it in rain/snow matchups and frees it from the Choice lock that made Dragon Claw into a 7% Mamoswine mandatory.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'priority insurance behind a setup Mega' shape: Mamoswine's Ice Shard cleaned up three of our Pokemon that were all faster than it. For us, swap Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (STAB +2 priority, hits every chipped sweeper) and strongly consider Milotic over Garchomp in rain/Ice matchups — Competitive + Scald + Recover walls Blastoise and Palafin far better than a 4x-Ice-weak Scarf attacker.
teamInspiration.reason: Every recent loss ended with a chipped foe at <=30% HP that out-prioritized or outsped our whole remaining team; we own exactly one priority move and it is Dark-typed and blockable.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Protect on Drogon was correct (Aerodactyl Rock Slide/Dual Wingbeat would have OHKO'd) and Whimsicott's Tailwind went up cleanly. Kingambit's Iron Head KO'd Sylveon through its bulk and the damage calcs were accurate on that line. Identifying Aerodactyl as the Rock-Slide threat to our 4x-weak Mega was right.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Protect-the-Mega-turn-1-vs-Rock discipline was applied correctly. However the two most important active proposals were violated: the SETUP-PUNISH MANDATE (Charizard-X used Dragon Dance on turn 1 completely unpunished — Whimsicott clicked Tailwind and Drogon Protected, so BOTH of our actions ignored the booster) and the SUCKER PUNCH DISCIPLINE rule (Turn 4 Sucker Punch was clicked into an obvious switch slot and failed, wasting half the turn on the turn Drogon died).
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1: Charizard-X Dragon Danced for free. A +1 DD Mega Charizard X is their win condition and it then 2-shot our team; Whimsicott had Encore available and we never used it, and never attacked the booster. 2) Turns 2-3 were engine fallbacks (API rate limit) that burned Whimsicott's Protect then let it die to Flare Blitz chip + Rock Slide, and let Drogon Protect twice in the span of three turns while Aerodactyl got a second free Tailwind. 3) Turn 4: Sucker Punch into a Charizard-X that was being swapped out — guaranteed fail, and Drogon died to Rock Slide on the same turn with no Protect. 4) Turns 5-6: we attacked Aerodactyl with Dragon Claw twice while it Protected/Detected behind and Sylveon Detected; we burned four actions into Protects. We also let them have BOTH speed (two Tailwinds) and power the whole game. 5) We never used Encore once in a game featuring a Dragon Dance and two Protect-spamming foes.
analysis.howToImprove: Lead Whimsicott into a Dragon Dance / setup-shell and Encore the booster on the turn after it boosts — Encore is +1 priority and would have locked Charizard-X into Dragon Dance for 3 turns, winning the game outright. Never click Sucker Punch on a turn a foe is likely to switch or Protect; prefer Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head unless the foe is visibly committed to attacking. After a foe Protects, attack THAT slot next turn (consecutive Protect fails) — we did the opposite and attacked into fresh Protects twice. Finally, when our Mega is 4x weak to an active foe's STAB spread Rock move and the foe is faster even without Tailwind, Drogon should be switched out, not Protect-cycled; Drogon ended the game having dealt 62% total damage.

proposals.change: DRAGON DANCE / BOOST ENCORE MANDATE (expanded): if Whimsicott is on the field and any foe used a boosting move last turn and is NOT Dark-type, Encore targeting that foe is forced (score +6, all other Whimsicott moves -5). Applies to Dragon Dance, Shell Smash, Swords Dance, Calm Mind, Nasty Plot, Quiver Dance, Bulk Up, Coil, Work Up, Agility, Rock Polish.
proposals.evidence: Turn 1 booknerd07's Charizard-X Dragon Danced; Whimsicott used Tailwind and Drogon Protected. The +1 Mega-X then Flare Blitzed through Whimsicott and dictated the whole game.

proposals.change: SUCKER PUNCH SWITCH/PROTECT GUARD: block Sucker Punch when (a) the target is at <=20% HP with healthy bench available (obvious switch bait), or (b) the target Protected/Detected last turn, or (c) the target is a Mega that just took a near-lethal hit — prefer Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head.
proposals.evidence: Turn 4 Sucker Punch into 14% Charizard-X failed because they switched to Sylveon; Kingambit's action was wasted and Drogon died the same turn.

proposals.change: ANTI-PROTECT TARGETING: if a foe used Protect/Detect on the immediately previous turn, boost attacks targeting that foe by +2 and penalize attacks targeting the OTHER foe by -1 (consecutive Protect auto-fails).
proposals.evidence: Turn 5 Sylveon Detected and Aerodactyl Tailwinded; turn 6 we attacked Aerodactyl (which Protected) instead of the already-Protected Sylveon slot with Garchomp, wasting the action.

proposals.change: Give Drogon a switch-out rule rather than Protect-cycling vs Aerodactyl/Tyranitar-class Rock users: if the active foe has a Rock STAB and outspeeds, switch Drogon to Milotic/Kingambit instead of Protecting twice in four turns.
proposals.evidence: Drogon Protected T1, attacked T2, Protected T3, and died T4 to Rock Slide having dealt only 62% damage all game.

lessons: A foe that uses Dragon Dance on turn 1 must be Encored or double-attacked on turn 2 — setting Tailwind while they boost hands them speed AND power simultaneously.
Sucker Punch fails on switches: never click it at a sub-20% foe with a healthy bench, that slot is the one they swap out.
After a foe Protects, attack THAT slot next turn; attacking the other slot lets them Protect again for free.
Our Mega must not spend 2 of 4 turns Protecting against a faster Rock user — switch it out and bring it back when the Rock user is gone.
Encore is the single most under-used move on this team: in 7 turns with a Dragon Dance and three enemy Protects, we never clicked it once.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is at 46% over 57 games and keeps dying to priority/spread before contributing; Sitrus lets Garchomp survive Hyper Voice/Rock Slide chip and click the right move (Protect/EQ) instead of being locked into Dragon Claw into Protect spam.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'double speed control + setup Mega' shape: Aerodactyl clicked Tailwind twice (and Protected to preserve it) while Mega Charizard-X Dragon Danced behind it. For us, that means Whimsicott must be a disruption lead (Encore first, Tailwind second) rather than an autopilot Tailwind bot, and Dragonite should trade Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so a chipped +1 sweeper (Charizard-X at 14%) can be deleted through priority instead of whiffing Sucker Punch.
teamInspiration.reason: Their win came entirely from one unpunished Dragon Dance plus repeated Protect/Detect turns; we had exactly zero tools that punish Protect-cycling (no priority outside blockable Sucker Punch, and Encore never used).

analysis.whatWorked: Garchomp's turn-2 Earthquake was the single best action of the game: it double-KO'd Indeedee (removing Psychic Terrain and the Expanding Force engine) and Sneasler at once, and it was legal because Dragonite (Flying) was the ally. Turn-4 Moonblast + the forced KO on Mega Meowstic was correct focus-fire in a 2v2. Identifying Indeedee as the win condition in preview was right.
analysis.lessonsApplied: We correctly avoided Sucker Punch into Psychic Terrain, correctly Earthquaked only while a Flying ally was out, and correctly never clicked Tailwind into a Trick Room team. However the core rule 'Protect the slot that will be OHKO'd by a faster foe' was violated on turn 1 with Kingambit, and 'do not split actions when one of our mons is guaranteed dead' was violated too.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 1 is the whole game. The calc explicitly displayed 'Kingambit threatened by Sneasler Close Combat (153-222% OHKO)' — a guaranteed OHKO from a faster foe — and we still clicked Iron Head with Kingambit instead of Protect. Kingambit died before acting, so we spent a full Pokemon for ZERO damage and surrendered half our action economy on turn 1. Worse, the chosen plan was to focus-fire Indeedee with BOTH slots; since Kingambit never moved, Dragon Pulse alone left Indeedee at 39% and Psychic Terrain stayed up another turn. Second failure: the lead itself. Kingambit vs a revealed Sneasler (Close Combat, 4x-ish effective, faster) is a hard counter-lead; the preview logic chose Kingambit purely for 'Psychic immunity' and ignored the Fighting-type Sneasler sitting next to Indeedee. Third failure: turn 3, Dragonite Protected at 39% HP while Garchomp (which could not survive Dazzling Gleam + Expanding Force) attacked and died — we protected the mon that was already chipped instead of switching Dragonite out or Protecting the slot actually being focus-fired. We ended 0 KOs for Kingambit, Dragonite dealt 61%, and lost 4-2 in four turns.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Hard rule: if the engine's threat line shows a >=100% guaranteed OHKO on one of our actives from a FASTER foe and that mon has Protect, Protect is mandatory unless our other slot KOs that foe first. 2) Never lead Kingambit when the opponent's preview shows Sneasler, Great Tusk, Urshifu or any fast Fighting-type — Psychic immunity is worthless if it dies to Close Combat before moving. In that matchup lead Garchomp (immune to nothing but outspeeds, EQ hits both Psychic Terrain mons) + Dragonite/Charizard. 3) Don't commit both actions to a Focus-Sash-suspect Indeedee; one action should pressure or blank the Sneasler. 4) When our Mega is below 50% and both foes threaten it, switch it out rather than Protect — Protect only delays one turn and the partner dies instead.

proposals.change: GUARANTEED-OHKO PROTECT MANDATE: if the threat table shows a foe that moves before one of our actives dealing >=100% minimum damage to it, and that active has Protect, Protect is forced (score +6, all its attacking moves -6) unless our other active can KO that specific foe first.
proposals.evidence: T1: calc displayed 'Kingambit threatened by Sneasler Close Combat (153-222% OHKO)'. We clicked Iron Head anyway; Kingambit died without moving, Indeedee survived at 39%, and we lost the 2-action economy on turn 1 of a 4-turn loss.

proposals.change: ANTI-FIGHTING KINGAMBIT LEAD BAN: never lead Kingambit if the opponent's preview contains Sneasler, Urshifu, Great Tusk, Lucario, Breloom or Hariyama. Against Psychic Terrain teams with a fast Fighting-type, lead Garchomp + Mega Dragonite/Charizard instead (Garchomp EQ hits grounded Psychics and the Fighting type).
proposals.evidence: Kingambit was led into Indeedee+Sneasler and was OHKO'd by Close Combat before acting; the same Sneasler then died to one Garchomp Earthquake on turn 2.

proposals.change: CHIPPED MEGA SWITCH RULE: when our Mega is <=45% HP and BOTH opposing actives have a move that KOs it, switching it out scores higher than Protect (Protect only buys one turn and the partner absorbs the double-target).
proposals.evidence: T3 Dragonite at 39% Protected; Garchomp ate both Expanding Force and Dazzling Gleam and fainted, and Dragonite died on T4 anyway having dealt only 61% all game.

proposals.change: Consider Milotic over Kingambit as the default 4th vs Psychic Terrain teams that also show a Fighting-type: Milotic is not Psychic-immune but is not OHKO'd by Close Combat, gets Competitive value, and Ice Beam/Scald pressure Hatterene/Meowstic.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit has now been OHKO'd before acting in multiple psyterrain games (Sneasler Close Combat x2 this series); psyterrain record with Kingambit leads is 5-5 at best.

lessons: If the displayed threat line shows a guaranteed OHKO (min damage >=100%) from a foe that moves before us, that slot must Protect or switch — never attack and die without acting.
Kingambit's Psychic immunity is irrelevant next to a fast Fighting-type: never lead Kingambit into Sneasler/Urshifu/Great Tusk.
Do not commit both actions to one Focus-Sash-suspect support mon when the other foe will KO one of our slots first — one action must answer the immediate threat.
A Mega below ~45% HP threatened by both foes should switch out, not Protect; Protect just moves the KO onto the partner.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp was the only thing that worked this game (2 KOs in one Earthquake, outspeeding Sneasler); keep it while we fix the Kingambit lead problem.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'terrain setter + fast Fighting breaker' pairing: Indeedee's Psychic Terrain blanked our only priority while Sneasler's Close Combat deleted our Dark-type lead before it moved. For us that means Garchomp should be the designated psyterrain lead (EQ hits grounded Indeedee/Meowstic AND Sneasler), and Dragonite should trade Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so we keep a priority option that Psychic Terrain does NOT blank on Flying-type users... (Extreme Speed is still blocked for grounded targets, so alternatively run Milotic as the psyterrain fourth).
teamInspiration.reason: Our entire Psychic Terrain game plan is built on Kingambit, and Kingambit keeps dying to Close Combat before it acts; the opponent won by making our 'immunity' piece irrelevant.

analysis.whatWorked: Almost nothing. The only correct reads were identifying Maushold-Four's Population Bomb as the game-ending threat and finally removing it on turn 2 with Stomping Tantrum (correctly avoiding Earthquake next to Whimsicott), and Milotic's turn-4 Protect to burn the final Tailwind turn. Damage calcs were accurate (3/3 inside predicted range).
analysis.lessonsApplied: VIOLATED the single most important standing rule on this team: 'Protect Drogon turn 1 when a faster foe likely OHKOs it.' The threat table explicitly displayed Maushold-Four Population Bomb 159-222% OHKO on Drogon, and we still clicked Weather Ball (15-28% chip — a 4-turn kill) and lost the Mega on turn 1 having dealt 19% damage. We also violated 'never split actions when one foe threatens an OHKO on both our slots' by chipping Maushold for 15% with the Mega instead of either Protecting it or switching it. The tactics.js GUARANTEED-OHKO PROTECT MANDATE proposal existed but was never coded into adjustScore/shouldBlockMove, so it had zero effect.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1: Drogon fired a 15-28% Weather Ball into a Pokemon that OHKO'd it with a displayed 159-222% roll — the worst possible action economy trade; Mega gone on turn 1 for 19% chip, the fifth game in a row ending with our Mega contributing almost nothing. 2) Turn 2: after Drogon died, we double-committed into Maushold again while Whimsicott was displayed as 177-264% OHKO'd by that same foe — we should have switched Whimsicott out and let Garchomp Stomping Tantrum alone (which did 100% and KO'd anyway). We fed Whimsicott for free. 3) We never set Tailwind at all despite Volcarona giving THEM Tailwind on turn 1 — opponent had speed AND Population Bomb/Fiery Dance power simultaneously, exactly the Golden Rule violation. 4) Turn 3 we split damage onto Volcarona (31-38% + 17-26%) instead of recognizing Mega Pinsir (Aerilate Body Slam/Return) as the real sweeper; Garchomp died to it the same turn. 5) Lead choice: Drogon + Whimsicott into a team with Maushold-Four (Population Bomb, multi-hit, ignores Sash/Multiscale) and Pinsir is the worst possible pairing — both leads are OHKO'd by one Population Bomb.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-code the OHKO Protect mandate: whenever the threat table shows a foe that moves before one of our actives dealing >=100% minimum damage, that active MUST Protect or switch — attacking is forbidden unless our partner's action guarantees the KO of that exact foe first. Our partner's Moonblast at 30-57% does NOT guarantee it. Second: add Maushold/Population Bomb and other multi-hit spam to a 'frail-lead ban' list so Whimsicott (Focus Sash is useless vs multi-hit) and Drogon never lead against it. Third: when we lose our Mega turn 1, immediately shift to Milotic-based attrition rather than racing. Fourth: if the opponent sets Tailwind and we have not, the next Whimsicott action is Tailwind or Encore, never Moonblast chip.

proposals.change: HARD BLOCK: if the engine threat table shows any opposing active that moves before our Pokemon dealing >=100% MINIMUM damage to it, block all attacking moves from that Pokemon unless (a) our partner's action is a guaranteed (>=100% min roll) KO on that specific foe, or (b) no Protect/switch is legal. Force Protect or switch instead.
proposals.evidence: T1 Drogon fired a 15-28% Weather Ball into Maushold whose displayed Population Bomb was 159-222% OHKO; Drogon died having dealt 19% total. Same pattern T2 with Whimsicott (177-264% displayed).

proposals.change: MULTI-HIT FRAIL-LEAD BAN: if opponent preview contains Maushold/Maushold-Four, Cinccino, Greninja (Water Shuriken), or any Technician/Skill Link spammer, never lead Whimsicott (Focus Sash is consumed by hit 1) or Charizard-Y. Lead Milotic + Garchomp/Kingambit instead.
proposals.evidence: Both our leads were OHKO'd by a single Population Bomb across turns 1-2; Whimsicott's Sash provided zero value.

proposals.change: TAILWIND PARITY RULE: if the opponent has Tailwind active and we do not, and Trick Room is not up, Whimsicott's Tailwind gets +4 score and Moonblast -3 — never trade chip while they hold the speed advantage.
proposals.evidence: They had 3 Tailwind turns, we had 0; every subsequent turn we moved second and lost a Pokemon per turn.

proposals.change: Consider Milotic over Whimsicott as the default lead partner in snow/hail and multi-hit matchups: Competitive triggers on Intimidate, Recover outlasts chip, and it is not deleted by one spread or multi-hit move.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott has 149 faints vs 91 KOs across 235 games — by far our worst ratio — and died turn 2 here contributing 56% chip.

lessons: If the displayed threat shows a foe moving first with >=100% MINIMUM damage on our Pokemon, that Pokemon Protects or switches — chipping for 15-28% with a Mega is never an acceptable alternative.
Focus Sash is worthless against multi-hit moves (Population Bomb, Rock Blast, Icicle Spear): never rely on Whimsicott surviving a Skill Link/Technician spammer.
If the opponent sets Tailwind on turn 1 and we did not, matching speed control is the next Whimsicott action, not chip damage.
Mega Pinsir (Aerilate Body Slam/Return) is a higher-priority target than a +1 Volcarona once Pinsir has Mega Evolved — focus the physical sweeper that just gained a Mega stat boost.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 26-33 (44%) and in this game Scarf speed was irrelevant — Garchomp died to Mega Pinsir Body Slam at full HP after one turn. Sitrus Berry lets Garchomp survive a Body Slam/Rock Slide and fire twice, and removes the Choice lock that forces bad clicks after our Mega dies early.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'cheap turn-1 Tailwind from the support slot + two independent physical Mega/boosting threats' shape: Volcarona clicked Tailwind turn 1 (not an attack) and then boosted freely with Fiery Dance while Maushold forced both our leads to die. For us: run Milotic as the default partner to Charizard-Y in frail-lead matchups, and strongly consider replacing Whimsicott's Moonblast with Helping Hand or keeping Encore primed — Whimsicott's job is Tailwind/Encore, not 30% chip.
teamInspiration.reason: Their support mon spent turn 1 on speed control and still won the speed war; our support mon spent turn 1 on a 30% chip, got no Tailwind up all game, and both of our leads died to one move.

analysis.whatWorked: Scarf Garchomp was the MVP again: Stomping Tantrum OHKO'd Mega Raichu-Y through Lightning Rod on turn 1 (denying Zap Cannon, which has killed us 10 times), and broke Arcanine-H's Sash. Whimsicott's turn-1 Protect correctly dodged both Fake Out and the spread Make It Rain. Turn-2 Whimsicott->Kingambit pivot into Flare Blitz/Make It Rain was a textbook defensive repositioning switch. The game was won (3 KOs to 1) but the log ends with '|win|JJ1NE' — the result line is opponent-labelled; we ended ahead on board but Kingambit died to Make It Rain chip and our last switch was engine-driven.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: 'Protect when a faster foe likely OHKOs' (Whimsicott T1 vs Make It Rain), 'switch rather than die' (Whimsicott T2), 'never EQ next to Kingambit' (used Stomping Tantrum all game), 'KO the speed/power carrier first' (Mega Raichu-Y turn 1). Violated: on T3 we attacked a 1% HP Arcanine that had every reason to Protect — the coach note 'never waste turns attacking into an obvious Protect' and 'after a foe Protects, attack THAT slot next turn' were both ignored in spirit: Gholdengo Protected on T2, Arcanine Protected on T3, and our Garchomp action was fully wasted. Also we never brought Drogon into the field at all (Mega unused, 0 damage) — the standing 'Mega with 0% damage dealt is a loss signal' rule.
analysis.whatFailed: T3 was the only real misplay: Garchomp at 2% HP clicked Stomping Tantrum into a 1%-HP Arcanine that was overwhelmingly likely to Protect (it was at 1 HP, had already seen two Stomping Tantrums, and its partner Gholdengo had just Protected). The correct action was Garchomp -> Kowtow/Iron-Head-support target Gholdengo (double-target the non-Protect slot) or switch Garchomp to Drogon, who could then Drought+Weather Ball the field. Because the action was wasted, Make It Rain's spread chip killed Kingambit alongside the Gholdengo KO and left us with 2% Garchomp + unused Drogon instead of a clean 2v1. We also never Mega Evolved: Drogon sat on the bench the whole game with 0 damage.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Apply a hard anti-Protect-prediction rule: when a foe is at <=10% HP, has already been attacked by the same move twice, and its partner Protected the previous turn, redirect that attack to the OTHER slot. 2) When our attacker is at <=5% HP and the only remaining threat is spread chip, prefer switching it to the unused Mega (free Drought turn) over a low-value attack. 3) Deploy the Mega: if Drogon has not entered by the time we are up 2 KOs, bring it in as the cleanup piece rather than hoarding it. 4) Keep leading Scarf Garchomp vs Raichu-Y/Gholdengo cores — 2 for 2 now.

proposals.change: OBVIOUS-PROTECT REDIRECT: if a foe is at <=12% HP, is not Choice-locked, has a healthy partner, and either (a) it or its partner used Protect last turn, or (b) we have attacked it with the same move on each of the last two turns, block attacks targeting that slot and redirect to the partner slot (score -5 on that target, +3 on the other).
proposals.evidence: T3: Garchomp Stomping Tantrum into 1%-HP Arcanine that Protected; the action was fully wasted and Kingambit died to Gholdengo's chip.

proposals.change: UNUSED-MEGA DEPLOYMENT RULE: if our Mega has never been on the field and we are ahead by 2+ KOs or our active attacker is <=10% HP, switching to the Mega scores +3 over low-value attacks.
proposals.evidence: Drogon dealt 0 damage and never appeared; Garchomp attacked at 2% HP into a Protect instead of pivoting to the Mega for a free Drought turn.

proposals.change: LOW-HP ATTACKER PIVOT: our Pokemon at <=10% HP facing a spread move (Make It Rain, Hyper Voice, Rock Slide, Earthquake) should switch rather than attack, since the spread chip kills it regardless of target.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp at 2% survived only because Arcanine Protected; Make It Rain's spread chip nearly finished it and did finish Kingambit.

lessons: When a foe sits at 1-10% HP and its partner Protected the previous turn, it will Protect — redirect both actions to the partner slot instead of chasing the kill.
A Mega that never enters the field is a wasted sixth of the team: once ahead on KOs, bring the Mega in on a free turn (switch out a nearly dead attacker) rather than hoarding it.
Scarf Garchomp Stomping Tantrum is the correct turn-1 answer to Mega Raichu-Y (Lightning Rod does not redirect Ground) — keep this lead vs Raichu/Gholdengo cores.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp has now solo-answered Mega Raichu-Y twice (OHKO through Lightning Rod) and broke Arcanine-H's Sash; keep the current loadout while the Raichu/Gholdengo archetype is common.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Protect-cycling chip engine': Gholdengo Protected turn 2, Arcanine Protected turn 3, and their spread Make It Rain did 100% of their damage without ever winning a speed war. For us: give Kingambit a Safety Goggles/Clear Amulet-style chip-resistance slot or, better, run Milotic as Garchomp's partner vs Gholdengo cores — Milotic takes Make It Rain for ~25%, Recovers, and Scald burns Arcanine-H.
teamInspiration.reason: Our only loss condition in this game was spread chip damage from a Steel special attacker that we could not pressure; Kingambit at 207 HP was reduced to 12% purely by two Make It Rains.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 was executed correctly: Kowtow Cleave OHKO'd Indeedee through Follow Me redirection failing (Kingambit targeted it directly), instantly removing Psychic Terrain and the Trick Room/Expanding Force win condition, while Whimsicott Protected Sneasler's Dire Claw. Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum later KO'd Sneasler. The preview plan (Kingambit lead into psyterrain, Whimsicott for Protect/Tailwind) was sound in principle.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: Kingambit lead vs Indeedee, Kowtow Cleave over Sucker Punch in Psychic Terrain, Protect on the slot under lethal threat (Whimsicott T1). Violated: the standing coach rule 'Kingambit's Psychic immunity is irrelevant next to a fast Fighting-type: never lead Kingambit into Sneasler/Urshifu/Great Tusk' — Sneasler was visible in preview and OHKO'd Kingambit on T2. Also violated the HARD BLOCK proposal (foe moving first with >=100% MINIMUM damage must Protect or switch): the engine itself printed 'Kingambit threatened by Sneasler Close Combat (153-222% KO)' and we clicked Iron Head anyway, dying without the KO. Also violated 'never set Tailwind while the opponent holds the dangerous board' indirectly: Whimsicott set Tailwind at 137 HP into a live Pelipper Hurricane, got confused and died to self-hit.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T2 was the losing turn: Kingambit had a displayed 153-222% guaranteed-KO threat from Sneasler and still attacked (Iron Head, only 26% OHKO chance). Correct play was Kingambit Protect or switch Kingambit to Garchomp/Drogon, letting Sneasler's Close Combat whiff into Protect, keeping our best Dark attacker and the 2-action economy. 2) Whimsicott's Tailwind on T2 was redundant tempo: our Kingambit was about to die and Garchomp is already Scarfed; the Tailwind gave 3 turns that produced zero KOs and Whimsicott died to Hurricane confusion the next turn anyway. 3) T3 Stomping Tantrum into an obvious Sneasler Protect (Sneasler was at full HP, had just KO'd Kingambit, and knew it was the focus target) wasted a full action; Whimsicott's Moonblast was also spent into Protect/confusion. 4) T4 Drogon was Mega-Evolved and brought in directly in front of a Sneasler Rock Slide (4x) while Pelipper Weather Ball was also lethal — the Mega entered a board where both foes OHKO it, and it died dealing 0% damage, which is the documented auto-loss signal. 5) Endgame: Garchomp Choice-locked into Stomping Tantrum with Pelipper (immune) and Metagross Protect-cycling meant two completely wasted turns.
analysis.howToImprove: (a) Treat a displayed >=100% minimum-damage threat from a foe that moves first as a hard Protect/switch trigger — no exceptions for 'maybe we OHKO first'. (b) Never bring Charizard-Y onto the field while a live Rock Slide user (Sneasler/Aerodactyl/Tyranitar) is active — send Milotic/Garchomp instead and bank the Mega until the Rock user is gone. (c) Do not spend Whimsicott's turn on Tailwind when our only other active mon is about to die; preserve Whimsicott for Encore/Protect or set Tailwind the turn we actually have two healthy attackers. (d) Against a foe that just got a free KO and is clearly the focus target, expect Protect: attack the OTHER slot or Protect ourselves. (e) Vs psyterrain + Fighting cores, bring Milotic as the fourth instead of leading Kingambit, per the active proposal.

proposals.change: HARD BAN: never lead Kingambit when the opponent's preview contains Sneasler, Urshifu, Great Tusk, Koraidon, Lucario or any revealed Close Combat/Fighting attacker faster than 100 base Speed. Lead Garchomp (EQ hits grounded Indeedee/Meowstic AND Sneasler) + Whimsicott instead, Kingambit in the back as a late-game cleaner.
proposals.evidence: 3rd consecutive loss where Kingambit led into Sneasler and was OHKO'd by Close Combat before contributing more than one turn (khoikhoiisminisun T1, HIRLEGAN T2). Sneasler Close Combat is our #1 killer at 17 KOs.

proposals.change: MEGA ENTRY GATE: block switching Charizard-Y in (and block Mega-evolving it) on any turn where an opposing active has a revealed or likely Rock move (Rock Slide, Stone Edge, Head Smash, Power Gem, Ancient Power) or a 4x-effective move. Bring Milotic/Garchomp instead.
proposals.evidence: T4: Drogon switched in, Mega'd, and was deleted by Sneasler Rock Slide for 100% dealing 0% damage — the documented auto-loss signal; Drogon has now been killed by Rock moves in 6+ games.

proposals.change: TAILWIND GATING: Whimsicott's Tailwind scores -4 if our only other active Pokemon is facing a displayed guaranteed KO this turn (it will be 1v2 next turn) or if Whimsicott itself is below 30% HP. Prefer Protect/Encore/switch and set Tailwind once two healthy attackers are on the field.
proposals.evidence: T2 Tailwind went up while Kingambit died the same turn; the 3 Tailwind turns produced zero KOs and Whimsicott died the next turn to Hurricane confusion.

proposals.change: POST-KO PROTECT READ: a foe that just scored a KO on the previous turn and is now the obvious focus target should be assumed to Protect — redirect at least one of our two actions to the partner slot.
proposals.evidence: T3: both our actions (Stomping Tantrum + Moonblast) were aimed at Sneasler, which Protected; we lost a full 2-action turn while Pelipper freely set Tailwind.

lessons: If the engine threat line shows a foe moving first for >=100% MINIMUM damage, that Pokemon Protects or switches — a 26% OHKO chance in return is never worth the trade.
Never lead or keep Kingambit in front of a live Sneasler/Urshifu: Close Combat is a guaranteed OHKO and Kingambit's Psychic immunity is worthless there.
Never switch Charizard-Y into a board containing an active Rock Slide user; bank the Mega until the Rock user is gone.
Whimsicott should not spend a turn on Tailwind when our partner is about to faint — Tailwind with only one surviving attacker is wasted tempo.
A foe that just got a KO and is the obvious focus target will Protect: split actions or Protect instead of double-targeting it.
Choice-locked Garchomp facing a Ground-immune foe (Pelipper/Flying/Levitate) must switch, not click the locked move into immunity.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp ended two of the last three games Choice-locked into Stomping Tantrum against Ground-immune Pelipper/Flying foes, wasting whole turns. Sitrus Berry keeps move freedom (Dragon Claw/Rock Slide into Pelipper, EQ into grounded) and the extra HP lets Garchomp survive Pinsir Body Slam / Hatterene Dazzling Gleam chip that killed it in the last three losses.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'redirect + Fighting breaker + Flying-type weather pivot' shape: Indeedee's Follow Me bought Sneasler a free turn, and Pelipper (Ground-immune, Hurricane/Tailwind) hard-walled our Choice-locked Garchomp. For us: run Milotic as the default fourth vs psyterrain/Fighting cores (survives Close Combat, Scald burns Sneasler, Ice Beam hits Rillaboom/Salamence) and swap Garchomp to Sitrus Berry so it can click Dragon Claw/Rock Slide into Flying pivots instead of being locked into an immune Ground move.
teamInspiration.reason: Every loss in this set ended with our Dark/Ground core unable to touch the surviving foe: Kingambit died to Close Combat before acting, and Garchomp spent two final turns clicking Stomping Tantrum into a Ground-immune Pelipper and a Protect-cycling Mega Metagross.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Mega Charizard-Y overwrote Snowscape with Sun and Weather Ball OHKO'd Alolan Ninetales, denying Aurora Veil for the whole game — the single biggest tempo swing. Garchomp's Dragon Claw cleanly revenge-KO'd the chipped Baxcalibur, and Milotic's Competitive +2 from Salamence's Intimidate turned Ice Beam into a guaranteed OHKO that closed the game. Ancient Power into Pelipper put the rain setter into Hurricane-recoil KO range. Final 2v1 was played without unnecessary prediction.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed 'Mega Charizard-Y resets rain/snow weather' and 'deny the opponent's weather/veil win condition first'. Followed the ahead-on-count safe-play rule on turns 4-5 (no risky doubles, just the 100%-accurate Ice Beam line). Correctly avoided Earthquake next to a non-Flying ally. VIOLATED the durable rule 'any Pokemon 4x/priority-threatened that will be KO'd by a foe that moves first must Protect or switch': Whimsicott was at 29/137 after Ice Shard and the threat line showed Baxcalibur Ice Shard (priority, moves first) still lethal and Pelipper Hurricane 94-184% — we clicked Moonblast anyway and Whimsicott died without executing the KO. Also violated 'if the threat line shows a foe moving first for >=100% MINIMUM damage, Protect or switch': Drogon faced Pelipper Weather Ball 90-158% (86% OHKO) in rain and attacked instead of Protecting, dying for zero further value.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 2 was a double blunder costing both leads. (1) Whimsicott at 21% HP was in Ice Shard range from a +priority foe; Moonblast was never going to resolve, so the 'guaranteed KO on Baxcalibur' calc was fiction. (2) Drogon in enemy rain is a dead Pokemon against Pelipper Weather Ball — we knew the 86% OHKO number and still attacked. Protecting Drogon (or switching it to Milotic) that turn would have preserved a healthy Mega Charizard for the rest of the game; Pelipper was already at 20% and Hurricane recoil/Scald would have removed it anyway. Turn 5 Garchomp also attacked into a displayed Salamence Draco Meteor 81-146% (70% OHKO) when Milotic's Ice Beam alone was a guaranteed OHKO — Garchomp should have Protected or switched; we won anyway but traded a Pokemon for nothing. Also Turn 3 Milotic Scald was aimed at a Pelipper that fainted to its own Hurricane recoil, wasting an action (unavoidable ordering, but redirecting to Baxcalibur was the lower-variance call).
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Whenever our active's displayed incoming threat is from a PRIORITY move and current HP is below the max roll, that slot must Protect/switch — its attack will not resolve. 2) In enemy rain with a Water-type special attacker active, Charizard-Y attacks only if it KOs that turn; otherwise Protect or pivot to Milotic/Garchomp. Never trade a Mega for 50% chip. 3) When a teammate's move is already a displayed guaranteed OHKO on the only live foe, the partner should Protect, not add redundant chip into a 70% OHKO threat. 4) Keep leading Charizard-Y + Whimsicott vs weather, but consider Protect on Zard turn 1 when the opposing lead carries a 4x or weather-boosted OHKO.

proposals.change: PRIORITY-RANGE GUARD: if the displayed incoming threat on one of our active Pokemon comes from a priority move (Ice Shard, Sucker Punch, Grassy Glide, Aqua Jet, Extreme Speed, Bullet Punch) and our current HP is at or below that move's max roll, block all attacking moves for that slot (score -6) and force Protect or switch — the attack will never resolve.
proposals.evidence: T2: Whimsicott at 29/137 clicked Moonblast for a 'guaranteed KO' on Baxcalibur and was deleted by Ice Shard before moving; the action was worth zero.

proposals.change: MEGA-IN-ENEMY-RAIN GUARD: while opposing rain is active and an opposing Water-type special attacker (Pelipper/Politoed/Archaludon/Basculegion) is on the field, Charizard-Y may only attack if the attack is a displayed KO on that foe; otherwise Protect/switch scores +4.
proposals.evidence: T2: Drogon attacked Pelipper (53-102%, only 6% OHKO) while facing Pelipper Weather Ball at 90-158% (86% OHKO) and died; Pelipper then fainted to its own Hurricane recoil anyway.

proposals.change: REDUNDANT-CHIP PROTECT: when one of our actions is already a displayed guaranteed OHKO (min damage >=100%) on the last remaining foe, the partner slot should Protect instead of adding chip if that partner faces a >=50% OHKO chance.
proposals.evidence: T5: Milotic Ice Beam was 123-226% guaranteed OHKO on Salamence; Garchomp attacked into Draco Meteor 81-146% (70% OHKO) and fainted for nothing.

lessons: If the incoming threat on our Pokemon is a PRIORITY move and our HP is within its damage range, that slot must Protect or switch — attacking is a guaranteed wasted action.
Charizard-Y in enemy rain facing a Water special attacker must Protect or pivot unless its attack is a displayed KO; never trade the Mega for partial chip.
When a partner's move is already a guaranteed OHKO on the last live foe, the other slot Protects instead of attacking into a high OHKO chance.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'weather setter + priority breaker' pairing: Baxcalibur's Ice Shard punished every frail support mon regardless of speed, and Pelipper re-set rain instantly after Zard's Drought. For us: give Whimsicott more effective HP (its Focus Sash is dead weight vs chip/priority once it has taken any damage) — switch Whimsicott to Covert Cloak or keep Sash but lead it only when a Fake Out/priority user is NOT present; and strongly consider Dragonite's Heat Wave slot becoming Extreme Speed so we own a priority answer to chipped sweepers like Baxcalibur and Volcarona.
teamInspiration.reason: Both of our leads died to a combination of priority and weather-boosted Water damage while our team has zero priority outside blockable Sucker Punch; the opponent won every speed war they needed without any Tailwind.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Whimsicott Protect correctly dodged Sneasler-style pressure... actually in this game it dodged nothing since Gengar used Perish Song, but Heat Wave chipping Gengar and breaking Vivillon's Focus Sash was reasonable. Garchomp's Earthquake chip on Politoed and Incineroar generated real damage, and Milotic eventually removed Vivillon. Mega Charizard's Drought correctly overwrote rain on entry.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The Perish Song / Shadow Tag rule was known but applied far too late: we never switched anything out at perish 1, and we never prioritized a fast KO on Mega Gengar on turn 1-2 (the only turns it was killable). We also violated the explicit rule 'Prankster moves fail against Dark types' by clicking Encore into a freshly switched-in Incineroar — a wasted action in a 2-action economy with a perish clock running. We did correctly avoid Tailwind into no-threat turns, but Whimsicott never set Tailwind at all.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 2 Encore targeted Incineroar (Dark) = guaranteed fail, and it was aimed at a Pokemon that had just SWITCHED IN (Encore needs a last move). Two separate reasons it could never work. 2) We let the Perish clock run on both our mons without ever switching: Drogon fainted to perish0 having done nothing after turn 1 (slept, flinched, then perished). 3) Mega-evolving Charizard on turn 1 into a Mega Gengar + Vivillon lead was a win-con donation — Zard got Sleep Powdered immediately and never acted again; the Mega was effectively thrown away on turn 1. 4) We never focused Gengar down on turn 1 when both actions were available (Heat Wave did 34-49%, a Weather Ball + Moonblast would have been ~95-130%). 5) Turn 5/6 Earthquake into a Flying-type Vivillon while damaging our own Milotic for 45 and then 100 HP — a self-inflicted KO-level error; Garchomp should have clicked Dragon Claw/Rock Slide or switched. 6) Endgame had zero bench so Perish Song was lethal; we traded 4 mons for 2.
analysis.howToImprove: Against Perish Song + Shadow Tag cores: do not Mega on turn 1 into Gengar; focus BOTH actions on Gengar immediately (Moonblast + Weather Ball/Heat Wave) to break Shadow Tag before perish 2, and keep a bench so perish counts can be reset. Never click Prankster status at a Dark type or a Pokemon that just switched in. Never click a spread Ground move when our own partner is grounded and the only foe target is Flying/Levitate — it is pure self-damage. Treat Sleep Powder users (Vivillon, Amoonguss) as priority targets for our fastest KO because a slept Mega is a dead Mega.

proposals.change: HARD BLOCK: Prankster status moves (Encore, Taunt, Thunder Wave) targeting a Dark-type foe, and Encore targeting any foe that has no lastMove (just switched in) — both are guaranteed wasted actions.
proposals.evidence: T2 Whimsicott Encore -> freshly switched Incineroar: '-immune|p1b: Incineroar' with the Dark/Prankster hint, a full wasted action while Perish Song counted down.

proposals.change: SELF-DAMAGE SPREAD GUARD: block Earthquake when every living foe is immune (Flying/Levitate/Air Balloon) or Protected-likely AND our partner is grounded — the only guaranteed damage is to our own ally.
proposals.evidence: T5 EQ did 45 to Milotic and 0 to Vivillon; T6 EQ did 100 to Milotic, 0 to Vivillon (Politoed Protected) — self-KO'd our own last healthy mon.

proposals.change: PERISH/SHADOW TAG PROTOCOL: when an opposing Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) is on the field with Perish Song, score double-targeting Gengar +4 on the first two turns and forbid Mega-evolving Charizard that turn.
proposals.evidence: Gengar survived at 81% after one Moonblast; it never had to be removed and the perish clock killed Drogon for free.

proposals.change: Consider Covert Cloak or Safety Goggles on Charizard-Y/Milotic slot vs Powder cores; Sleep Powder from Vivillon disabled our Mega for the entire game.
proposals.evidence: Drogon slept T1, flinched T3, perished T4 having used exactly one move after Mega-evolving.

lessons: Never target a Dark-type foe with a Prankster status move (Encore/Taunt/Thunder Wave) — it is immune and the action is lost.
Encore fails on a foe that just switched in (no last move): check that the target actually used a move last turn.
Never click Earthquake when all living foes are Flying/Levitate-immune and our own partner is grounded — the only damage dealt is to our ally.
Against Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag) + Perish Song: do not Mega-evolve on turn 1; commit BOTH actions to KOing Gengar in the first two turns, because we cannot switch to reset perish counts.
Sleep Powder / Spore users are priority KO targets — a slept Mega is a dead Mega and donates the whole game.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice Scarf Garchomp repeatedly gets locked into Ground moves against Flying/Levitate foes (Pelipper, Vivillon, Gengar) and then damages our own partner; Sitrus lets it switch moves to Dragon Claw/Rock Slide and survive chip.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'trap + clock + powder' shape: Mega Gengar denied all switching while Perish Song and Sleep Powder removed our two best pieces without a single KO being earned. For us, add Safety Goggles to Milotic (or swap Whimsicott's Focus Sash to Covert Cloak) and consider Dragonite's Heat Wave slot becoming Extreme Speed so we have an unblockable finisher on trapped boards.
teamInspiration.reason: We lost 4 Pokemon and only 2 of their mons died to actual damage — the rest of our losses came from status and a perish clock we could not escape, which items (Goggles/Cloak) and priority directly answer.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 double-targeting Toxtricity with Moonblast + Mega Weather Ball removed the only foe that could OHKO both our leads, and it worked even through Light Screen. Mega-evolving Charizard turn 1 set Sun, which halved Blaziken's Fire output later. Kingambit Iron Head OHKO'd Grimmsnarl before it could finish its screen/terrain setup, denying the opponent the 'speed+power' board. Turn 5 double-targeting the 43% Garchomp (instead of chasing Mega Blaziken) was correct: it cleared the slot so Scarf Garchomp could revenge-kill Blaziken on turn 6. Turn 6 Stomping Tantrum (not Earthquake) next to Kingambit respected the never-EQ-beside-Kingambit rule, and Kingambit Protect covered Close Combat.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: never EQ beside Kingambit (used Stomping Tantrum T6); Protect the slot facing a displayed >=100% min-damage threat (Kingambit T6); punish/remove the support setter immediately (Grimmsnarl Iron Head); bring the Mega in early rather than hoarding it; safe-play discipline when ahead at the end. Violated: the POST-KO/REPEAT-PROTECT read — on T4 Garchomp had already Protected on T2, and we committed BOTH actions into it; it Protected again and we lost a full 2-action turn while Mega Blaziken evolved and got a free Speed Boost.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 4 was a total 2-action waste: both Whimsicott and Kingambit attacked Garchomp, which Protected for the second time in three turns, while Blaziken Mega-evolved, clicked Upper Hand (failed) and banked a Speed Boost. That turn also let Blaziken reach the board at full HP. Turn 2 was an engine fallback (API 429) that switched Kingambit into a Garchomp Protect turn — acceptable but unplanned. Whimsicott died again (its 153rd faint across the dataset) because it had no Tailwind value left and was chipped by Overdrive + Earthquake; Focus Sash never mattered. We also let Grimmsnarl get Light Screen AND Misty Terrain up for free on turns 1-2.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Encode a hard anti-Protect-chase rule: if a foe used Protect within the last two turns and is the obvious focus target, never commit both actions to it — split, or hit the partner that just Mega-evolved. 2) When an opposing Mega evolves on the field (Blaziken/Metagross/Salamence), it becomes the primary target the moment it is in range, especially if it has Speed Boost. 3) Keep leading Whimsicott only when Tailwind actually matters; against screens/terrain support leads, Moonblast chip + partner KO is correct but Whimsicott should pivot out before it drops below ~40%.

proposals.change: PROTECT-CHASE BLOCK: if a foe used Protect on either of the last two turns and is currently the lowest-HP foe, forbid committing BOTH of our actions to that slot (score -5 on the second action targeting it); at least one action must hit the partner or Protect/set up.
proposals.evidence: T4 vs aC-Carrot: Whimsicott Moonblast + Kingambit Kowtow Cleave both hit Garchomp's second Protect in three turns; the whole turn was wasted while Mega Blaziken evolved and gained Speed Boost.

proposals.change: FRESH-MEGA PRIORITY: when an opposing Pokemon Mega-evolves this turn or last turn and has a snowballing ability (Speed Boost, Contrary, Stamina, Moxie), raise its target priority +2 over a chipped non-Mega foe unless the chipped foe is a guaranteed KO this turn.
proposals.evidence: Mega Blaziken got two free Speed Boosts (T4 and T5) while we spent both turns on Garchomp; only a Scarf Garchomp revenge kill saved the game.

proposals.change: Give Whimsicott Covert Cloak over Focus Sash on spread-damage boards (Overdrive/Earthquake/Make It Rain cores); Sash has now failed to matter in 3 of the last 5 games because chip arrives before the lethal hit.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott took Overdrive (49) then Earthquake (54) and died to Close Combat with Sash long since broken; it is our most-fainted Pokemon (153 faints).

lessons: Never commit both actions to a foe that has already Protected within the last two turns — it will Protect again; split actions or hit the partner.
A foe that Mega-evolves with Speed Boost (Blaziken) gains a stat every turn we ignore it: treat a freshly Mega-evolved snowballing foe as the primary target once it is in KO range.
Grimmsnarl/support leads that get both a screen and a terrain up for free cost us two turns of damage — pressure the support slot with the hard-hitting partner on turn 1, not turn 3.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again converted the game: it outsped and OHKO'd a +2 Speed Mega Blaziken on the final turn. Keep the loadout while the sample grows.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Protect-cycling second slot' discipline: their Garchomp Protected twice to burn our actions while Blaziken boosted. For us, add Protect usage discipline on Garchomp-equivalent slots and consider swapping Whimsicott's Focus Sash to Covert Cloak (immune to Fake Out flinch/secondary chip) so our speed-control piece survives to set a second Tailwind.
teamInspiration.reason: They won two full turns of tempo with a single Protect-cycling Pokemon while their Mega boosted; our Sash Whimsicott, by contrast, dies to incidental spread chip before its Sash is ever relevant.

whatWorked: Turn 1 Weather Ball KO'd Sneasler (the single most dangerous foe for Kingambit and Whimsicott) before it could act again, and Moonblast correctly broke Scrafty's Focus Sash. Kingambit's Defiant converted both opposing Intimidates into +2 Attack, and Kowtow Cleave/Iron Head traded well. Garchomp's Dragon Claw correctly avoided Sylveon (Fairy resists Dragon) and kept pressure on Scrafty.
lessonsApplied: We did NOT Protect Drogon on turn 1 despite a visible 4x Rock threat (Sneasler Rock Slide) — a direct violation of the standing rule 'Protect Drogon turn 1 when a faster foe likely OHKOs it.' We also violated the rule 'a Mega at 1% HP threatened by Fake Out/priority must switch or Protect' on turn 2: Drogon at 1 HP was left in and deleted by Rillaboom Fake Out, wasting the Mega entirely. Conversely, the 'don't double-commit into a foe that Protected last turn' rule was respected on T4, and the Prankster/Dark rule was respected (no Encore into Scrafty).
whatFailed: 1) Turn 1: chose to attack with Drogon into a board with an unrevealed-but-obvious Rock Slide Sneasler; Drogon ended at 1 HP and never used its Mega value (only 100% damage all game). 2) Turn 2: with Drogon at 1 HP and an active Fake Out user (Rillaboom just switched in, first turn out), we clicked Heat Wave instead of switching Drogon out — a free Fake Out deleted our Mega. 3) Turn 3: we Protected Whimsicott AND clicked Iron Head into Sylveon, which Protected — a full wasted turn (both actions produced zero), exactly the 'don't attack into an obvious Protect' error. 4) Turn 4: Tailwind was set with only Kingambit alive-and-healthy as an attacker and Whimsicott about to die — wasted tempo (violates 'Whimsicott should not Tailwind when the partner is about to faint'). 5) Endgame: Choice-locked Garchomp into Dragon Claw with a Fairy (Sylveon) on the field meant one of two slots was permanently dead damage; we never switched to reset the lock.
howToImprove: Hard rule: if Drogon is at <=15% HP and ANY opposing Pokemon on the field is on its first active turn (Fake Out eligible) or has priority, Drogon must switch out, not attack. Turn 1 with a live Rock Slide user (Sneasler/Tyranitar/Excadrill/Garchomp), Drogon Protects or we lead a different pair. When a foe Protected the previous turn and is the obvious KO target, do not fire the KO move into it again; hit the partner instead. Only click Tailwind when at least two healthy attackers will still be on the field next turn. With Choice-locked Garchomp facing an immune/resistant last foe, switch to reset the lock rather than clicking a 0-14% move for two turns.

proposals.change: LOW-HP MEGA EVACUATION: if any of our Pokemon is below 15% HP and an opposing active Pokemon is on its first turn out (Fake Out eligible) or carries priority, force a switch (or Protect if no switch) instead of attacking.
proposals.evidence: Drogon at 1/153 HP clicked Heat Wave on T2 and was erased by Rillaboom Fake Out before moving, deleting our Mega for 0 further value.

proposals.change: ROCK-SLIDE LEAD GUARD: on turn 1, if any opposing active Pokemon has Rock Slide/Stone Edge/Power Gem in its possible set, Charizard-Y must Protect (or not be led) rather than attack.
proposals.evidence: Sneasler Rock Slide took Drogon 153->1 on turn 1 even though we got the KO; the Mega was functionally dead from that point.

proposals.change: PROTECT-MEMORY BLOCK: forbid targeting a foe that used Protect last turn with our single highest-value KO move when a second live foe exists; redirect to the partner slot.
proposals.evidence: T3 Iron Head into Sylveon hit Protect; both of our actions produced zero while Rillaboom was free.

proposals.change: TAILWIND VIABILITY GATE: block Tailwind if fewer than two of our Pokemon will plausibly survive the turn (partner threatened by a displayed >=70% KO chance).
proposals.evidence: T4 Tailwind went up as Whimsicott died to Wood Hammer, leaving only Kingambit to benefit; we never used the speed.

lessons: If Charizard-Y (or any Mega) is below ~15% HP and an opposing Pokemon is on its first active turn, switch it out — Fake Out will delete it before it moves.
Turn 1 with a live Rock Slide user on the field, Drogon Protects; getting the KO while dropping to 1 HP is not a win, it is losing the Mega.
Never fire the turn's key KO move into a foe that Protected last turn while a healthy partner foe is untouched.
Tailwind is only worth a turn if two attackers will still be alive to use it.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice-locked Garchomp spent the last three turns clicking Dragon Claw into a Fairy (Sylveon) it could not damage; Sitrus Berry lets Garchomp change moves (Earthquake/Rock Slide) and survive an extra Moonblast in the endgame.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Fake Out redundancy' shape: they ran TWO Fake Out users (Scrafty and Rillaboom) and used them to delete a 1-HP Mega and flinch our last Pokemon on the winning turn. For us: swap Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (unblockable priority finisher) and consider Covert Cloak on Drogon so Fake Out cannot flinch/finish our Mega.
teamInspiration.reason: Both of our key losses this game came from priority: Rillaboom Fake Out KO'd Drogon at 1 HP, and Rillaboom Fake Out flinched Garchomp on the final turn so Sylveon could Moonblast it. We have zero unblockable priority of our own.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Heat Wave through Sneasler's Protect KO'd Rillaboom and removed Grassy Terrain support immediately. Turn 3 Protect on the 7% Whimsicott while Scarf Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum KO'd the Unburden Sneasler was a clean, correct safe play (Ground ignores Unburden speed because Scarf Chomp still outran it). Turn 4 switching the 12% Whimsicott out instead of letting it die for free preserved a body.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: 'Scarf Garchomp Stomping Tantrum is the correct answer to the fast snowball threat'; 'low-HP piece should switch/Protect rather than attack'. VIOLATED the single most important standing rule: 'Never switch/keep Charizard-Y on a board containing an active Rock Slide / Power Gem user — Charizard-Y is 4x Rock weak and must Protect turn 1 vs Rock coverage.' Opposing Garchomp switched in on turn 1 and we let Drogon stand and attack on turn 2 with the engine-displayed threat line reading 'Drogon threatened by Garchomp Rock Slide (75-125%, OHKO 51%)'. Drogon died before dealing a point of damage on that turn. Also violated the ROCK-SLIDE LEAD GUARD proposal already in the active queue.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 2 was the game: with Drogon facing a freshly-switched Garchomp (Garchompite Z on team sheet = Power Gem/Rock coverage guaranteed) we clicked Weather Ball into Sneasler instead of Protecting the Mega. Drogon fainted doing 0 damage and we lost our only KO engine. 2) We double-targeted Sneasler with Whimsicott+Drogon when Drogon alone was already a 71% OHKO — a split action (Protect Drogon / Moonblast Sneasler) wins the same KO odds minus the Mega. 3) Rate-limit fallbacks on preview, T1, T5 and T6 handed four of seven turns to the engine; T6 the engine clicked Stomping Tantrum into a 16% Swampert instead of Protecting Kingambit, and Kingambit died to High Horsepower. 4) Endgame: Kingambit (Ground 4x-ish weak via Dark/Steel vs Swampert's High Horsepower) was the wrong body to keep opposite a Ground attacker; Milotic was left home against a Swampert/Garchomp Ground core. 5) Whimsicott's Focus Sash was again irrelevant — Dire Claw left it at 1 HP and chip finished it.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: once an opposing Pokemon with Rock-type coverage (Rock Slide/Stone Edge/Power Gem/Ancient Power) is ACTIVE, Charizard-Y either Protects or switches — never attacks — unless its attack is a displayed guaranteed OHKO on that specific Rock user. Against a Ground-heavy core (Garchomp + Swampert + Rillaboom) bring Milotic over Kingambit: Scald/Ice Beam answers both Ground types and Kingambit is Ground-neutral-but-slow bait for High Horsepower. Stop double-targeting a foe already at >=70% displayed OHKO; use the spare action to Protect the piece under a displayed OHKO threat.

proposals.change: ROCK-COVERAGE ZARD LOCK: whenever an opposing ACTIVE Pokemon has any Rock move in its known/possible set, block all non-Protect, non-switch actions for Charizard-Y unless the chosen move is a displayed >=95% OHKO on that Rock user itself.
proposals.evidence: T2: engine line read 'Drogon threatened by Garchomp Rock Slide (75-125%, OHKO 51%)' and we attacked Sneasler instead; Power Gem deleted Drogon for 0 value.

proposals.change: NO-OVERKILL DOUBLE: if one of our actions is already a displayed >=70% OHKO on a target, forbid the second action from also targeting that same foe when any of our active Pokemon is under a displayed >=50% OHKO threat — that slot must Protect or switch.
proposals.evidence: T2 Moonblast + Weather Ball both aimed at Sneasler (Weather Ball alone was 71% OHKO) while Drogon sat in a 51% OHKO threat line.

proposals.change: Against Ground-stacked cores (Garchomp + Swampert/Rillaboom High Horsepower), bring Milotic as the fourth over Kingambit.
proposals.evidence: Swampert High Horsepower hit Kingambit three times (65%, 47%, KO) while Kingambit never landed a relevant hit; Milotic's Ice Beam/Scald threatens both Garchomp and Swampert.

lessons: Once any opposing active Pokemon has Rock coverage (Rock Slide / Stone Edge / Power Gem / Ancient Power), Charizard-Y only Protects or switches — attacking is a 4x-weakness coin flip we cannot afford.
Never spend both actions on a foe that one action already OHKOs at >=70%; the second action must protect the piece that is itself under a displayed OHKO threat.
Do not bring Kingambit as the fourth into a Ground-stacked core (Garchomp + Swampert/Rillaboom); bring Milotic, which answers both Ground types with Ice Beam/Scald.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp again produced the game's only clean KOs (Sneasler through Unburden, repeated Stomping Tantrum pressure on Swampert); the loss was a piloting error on Charizard, not an item failure. Keep the loadout stable for more data.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Rock/Ground coverage on a Mega Dragon' shape: Garchomp-Mega-Z with Power Gem single-handedly deleted our Mega Charizard turn 2 and later Draco Meteor'd our Garchomp. For us: give Drogon Covert Cloak or simply stop leading it into Rock users, and swap Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so we own an unblockable finisher that does not require Drogon to survive; also consider Milotic as the default fourth vs Ground cores.
teamInspiration.reason: Every point of damage we lost this game came from coverage moves hitting a 4x weakness (Power Gem x2) and from Ground spam on Kingambit; we have no priority finisher and no Rock-resistant pivot to absorb those hits.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead was theoretically correct vs Indeedee Psychic Terrain and Kowtow Cleave did KO Indeedee-F through Follow Me later. Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum cleanly removed Houndoom. Whimsicott's Moonblast finally KO'd the +2/+2 Quaquaval. Drogon's turn-1 Protect correctly dodged Aqua Step.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The Protect-the-Mega directive was followed on turn 1 (Drogon Protect vs Quaquaval). The 'never Sucker Punch into a possible Protect/Psychic Terrain' rule was respected. However, the core Wolfe directive 'punish setup immediately' was violated: Quaquaval gained Speed from Aqua Step and Attack from Triple Axel across four turns and was never targeted until turn 4, and by then it was a +2 speed, +1 attack sweeper that KO'd three of our Pokemon.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) LEAD ERROR: Kingambit was led into Quaquaval (Close Combat / Triple Axel / Aqua Step), a displayed 156-229% OHKO threat — the exact 'never lead Kingambit in front of a Fighting-type' rule. 2) Drogon was not switched out on turn 2 at 57/153 HP into an unprotectable Heat Wave from Houndoom (Fire Mega into a Fire-type foe with Heat Wave, plus Quaquaval chip) — it died turn 2 and the Mega was wasted. 3) The real win condition (Quaquaval, an Aqua Step/Moxie-style snowballer) was ignored for three full turns while we traded with Houndoom and Indeedee. 4) Turn 3 we switched Kingambit out AND let Garchomp eat Triple Axel at 185 HP with a displayed 380-1554% OHKO — Garchomp should have been the switch, not Kingambit. 5) Turns 4 and 5 both slots attacked the same target while both of our Pokemon were under displayed OHKO threats, giving zero defensive value.
analysis.howToImprove: Treat any foe with a self-boosting attack (Aqua Step, Triple Axel's Moxie-like chains, Scale Shot, Fell Stinger) as a setup sweeper and focus-fire it on the turn it first boosts. Never lead Kingambit when the opponent's sheet shows Quaquaval/Golisopod/any Fighting or Water-Fighting. With open team sheets, the lead should have been Whimsicott (Tailwind/Encore on the Trick Room/boost slot) + Charizard, with Kingambit in back for Indeedee. Charizard must switch out, not attack, the turn its HP is below the displayed incoming damage from two live attackers.

proposals.change: SELF-BOOSTING ATTACKER PRIORITY: if any opposing active Pokemon has gained a Speed or Attack boost from its own attacking move (Aqua Step, Moxie/Chilling Neigh chains, Scale Shot), mark it as the primary focus target and apply a large score bonus to all moves aimed at it until it is KO'd; forbid spending a turn on any other foe unless that foe is at <=20% HP.
proposals.evidence: Quaquaval boosted Speed on T2 and T5 and Attack on T3 while we attacked Houndoom and Indeedee; it personally KO'd Drogon (indirectly), Garchomp, Kingambit and Whimsicott's partner.

proposals.change: KINGAMBIT FIGHTING-LEAD BAN: block Kingambit from the lead pair whenever the opponent's team (open sheet or preview) contains a Fighting-type or a Water/Fighting (Quaquaval, Urshifu, Sneasler, Scrafty, Golisopod with Close Combat).
proposals.evidence: Kingambit led into Quaquaval with a displayed 156-229% Close Combat OHKO on turn 1 and spent the whole game at <30% HP.

proposals.change: MEGA SURVIVAL SWITCH: if Charizard-Y's current HP is below the sum of the two displayed incoming threat minimums and a healthy bench Pokemon exists, force a switch instead of any attack.
proposals.evidence: Drogon at 57/153 took Aqua Step + Heat Wave on turn 2 and fainted having dealt 0 damage all game.

lessons: Treat Aqua Step / Triple Axel users (Quaquaval) as setup sweepers: they gain Speed and Attack every turn they are ignored — focus-fire them the turn they first boost.
Never lead Kingambit when the opponent's sheet shows any Fighting-type or Quaquaval; a displayed 156%+ Close Combat means it dies before contributing.
Charizard-Y whose HP is below the combined minimum of both displayed incoming threats must switch, not attack — a Mega that deals 0 damage all game is a forfeited resource.
Do not spend both actions on one foe while both of our Pokemon are under displayed OHKO threats; one slot must Protect or switch.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 29-38 over 67 games (43%) and this game it died to a Triple Axel it could not survive; Sitrus adds a turn of survivability against multi-hit Ice coverage and still outspeeds after Tailwind.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'self-boosting physical sweeper behind a redirector' shape: Quaquaval (Aqua Step speed snowball) + Indeedee-F (Follow Me) won them the game with zero speed control. For us: replace Garchomp's Rock Slide slot thinking with Dragonite running Extreme Speed over Heat Wave so we have an unblockable finisher on boosted sweepers, and consider Covert Cloak on Whimsicott so it survives chip to Encore the boosting slot on turn 2.
teamInspiration.reason: We had no way to answer a +2 speed Quaquaval once it got going — every answer we had was slower, and Whimsicott's Encore (the actual counter to a boosting attacker) was never used because Whimsicott was in the back.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 vs nishi44 (JJ1NE) was correct macro: identify the rain setter as the single most valuable win condition denial target and focus-fire it. Whimsicott Moonblast + Drogon Ancient Power removed Pelipper before Hurricane ever fired, instantly flipping the weather to sun with Mega Charizard-Y and cutting Swampert's Water damage in half. The game was recorded as a WIN (opponent forfeited/disconnected after turn 2). Turn 2's read that Drogon at 8% must leave the field rather than attack was also correct per the MEGA SURVIVAL SWITCH principle.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) 'KO the rain setter first' — Pelipper died turn 1 before it could Hurricane; (2) 'Charizard-Y in enemy rain facing a Water special attacker must Protect or pivot' — we pivoted Drogon out at 8% instead of trading the Mega for chip; (3) focus-fire rather than splitting actions when a single removal wins the macro. Violated/risky: we Mega-evolved Drogon into a board where Swampert-Mega Wave Crash was a displayed 152-247% OHKO on it. The displayed threat was an unavoidable OHKO and we still exposed the Mega — Drogon ended turn 1 at 8% HP and was effectively dead weight for the rest of the game. We also clicked Tailwind on turn 2 with only one healthy attacker (Milotic incoming, Drogon fleeing at 8%), which brushes against the TAILWIND VIABILITY GATE proposal.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 1: Drogon was under a displayed 152-247% OHKO from Swampert Wave Crash and we attacked anyway rather than Protecting or leading differently. It survived only because Wave Crash rolled low-ish and Drogon's Charizard-Y bulk absorbed 92% — pure luck. A Mega at 8% HP on turn 1 is a forfeited resource; the NO-OVERKILL DOUBLE and MEGA SURVIVAL rules both point to Drogon Protecting on T1 while Whimsicott Moonblasts Pelipper, then finishing Pelipper on T2 at full HP. Secondary: Pelipper was already down to 37% after Moonblast — Ancient Power was partially redundant; an alternative was Moonblast + Drogon Protect, losing one turn but keeping the Mega at 100%. Turn 2 Tailwind into an incoming Snow/Swampert board with Drogon fleeing was low-value tempo; Milotic entering wanted a resist, not speed.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Codify a MEGA-EVOLVE SAFETY CHECK: do not Mega-evolve Charizard-Y on a turn where a displayed >=100% OHKO threat exists on it from an active foe we cannot remove this turn — Protect instead and Mega the following turn (Mega still triggers Drought at the start of a Protect turn). 2) Against rain cores with a second heavy physical Water (Swampert-Mega Wave Crash), the correct T1 is Whimsicott Moonblast the setter + Drogon Protect/Mega, not double-attacking the setter. 3) Never set Tailwind on the turn our only healthy board piece is a defensive pivot switching in — Protect or switch and set Tailwind once two attackers are alive. 4) Keep the focus-fire-the-weather-setter rule; it worked.

proposals.change: MEGA EVOLVE SAFETY GATE: if Charizard-Y (or Dragonite) is about to Mega-evolve and any active foe has a displayed >=100% OHKO threat on it that we cannot remove with our other action this turn, force Protect on that slot (Mega still happens and Drought still sets) instead of an attack.
proposals.evidence: T1 vs nishi44: Drogon Mega'd and attacked into a displayed Swampert Wave Crash 152-247% OHKO, ending turn 1 at 8% HP. Whimsicott's Moonblast alone had already put Pelipper to 37%; Protect would have kept the Mega at full and still killed Pelipper on T2.

proposals.change: REDUNDANT-FOCUS GUARD: when our first action's displayed roll already leaves the target at <=40% and a second foe threatens one of our slots with a displayed OHKO, the second slot must Protect/switch rather than pile onto the same already-dying target.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott Moonblast (34-66%) on Pelipper plus Drogon Ancient Power (40-77%) was overkill risk; Drogon's action was worth more as Protect against the displayed 152-247% Wave Crash.

proposals.change: TAILWIND INCOMING-PIVOT GATE: block Tailwind on any turn where our partner slot is switching out a Pokemon (i.e. the incoming mon cannot attack this turn) AND no other healthy attacker is on the field.
proposals.evidence: T2: Whimsicott set Tailwind while Drogon fled to Milotic at 8% — the Tailwind had zero attackers to accelerate that turn and only ~1 usable turn remaining before the board stabilised.
