lessons: Mega-evolving does not require attacking: Drought/Multiscale apply even on a Protect turn — when the Mega is under a displayed OHKO on turn 1, Mega + Protect is strictly better than Mega + attack.
Against rain cores, kill the drizzle setter but check the SECOND foe: a Mega Swampert / Basculegion behind Pelipper means our Charizard must Protect turn 1, not double into the setter.
Do not stack a second attack onto a target the first attack already leaves below ~40% when the other slot is facing a displayed OHKO.
Tailwind is worthless on a turn where our only other action is a switch — set it after the pivot has landed and two attackers are live.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep the current loadout; Scarf Garchomp remains our only answer to fast rain/electric threats and the loss pattern this window is Mega-Charizard exposure, not Garchomp speed.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'double weather + Mega bruiser' shape: Pelipper Drizzle into Mega Swampert Wave Crash (Swift Swim-adjacent pressure) plus Alolan Ninetales to re-set weather after we flip to sun. For us: give Drogon a Covert Cloak or consider Milotic as the default fourth vs rain, and strongly consider swapping Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so we own an unblockable finisher that does not require Drogon to survive the turn-1 Water hit.
teamInspiration.reason: Their Mega Swampert put Charizard-Y to 8% on turn 1 through an un-Protected Mega evolution, and their Ninetales immediately overwrote our sun — our whole game plan hinges on a Mega that dies to one Water move, so we need either a Protect-first discipline rule (now coded) or a priority finisher that works without the Mega.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead was correct into a Grassy Terrain/Rillaboom + Wyrdeer board (resists Grassy Glide, Kowtow Cleave removed Wyrdeer by T2). Drought overwrote Grassy Terrain and later Politoed's rain cycle was broken by killing Politoed with Moonblast. Protect discipline on Drogon T3 (blanking Rillaboom Fake Out) and Kingambit T4/T6 was individually correct, and the Whimsicott Moonblast finish on an 8% Politoed was clean.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed 'Protect Drogon in enemy rain vs a Water special attacker' (T3), 'switch a Pokemon about to be KO'd' (Kingambit T5), and 'KO the drizzle setter' as the macro plan. Violated the deeper rule: we spent four separate actions chipping Politoed instead of bursting it in one turn, and we never once clicked Tailwind despite Whimsicott being alive from T5 — against a rain team with Raichu-Mega-Y in the back, speed control was the actual win condition and we gave it up entirely (Tailwind turns: us 0).
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Mega-evolving Drogon on turn 1 into a known Fake Out user (Rillaboom) plus Wyrdeer Psyshield Bash cost 64% of the Mega before it ever acted — Drogon should have Protected on T1 (Mega still applies) or Heat Wave should have gone to Rillaboom's slot first. 2) Drogon then never dealt meaningful damage (52% total, 0 KOs) and died to the exact Politoed Weather Ball we had already identified as a displayed OHKO on T3 and T4 — on T4 we attacked with it for 19-28% while under a 61-107% displayed OHKO; that is the REDUNDANT/MEGA-SURVIVAL rule being broken. 3) Kingambit was slowly deleted by Earth Power (Wyrdeer + Politoed both carried Ground) while we kept it in; we had Milotic on the bench and never brought it despite rain + two Ground users. 4) Zero Tailwind the whole game: Whimsicott lived from T5 to T8 and used Moonblast/Protect only, so Raichu-Mega-Y Zap Cannon outsped and killed our last two mons. 5) Garchomp was sent in to a free Wood Hammer from Rillaboom and died in one turn with 36% damage dealt.
analysis.howToImprove: Against rain cores with a Fake Out user on the field: Drogon's turn-1 action is Protect (Mega + Drought still resolve), not an attack. Once Drogon is below the displayed incoming OHKO minimum, it switches out — it must not fire a 19-28% chip into a 61-107% OHKO. Burst the weather setter in a single turn with both actions (Weather Ball + Kowtow Cleave on the switch-in turn) rather than chipping it across four turns while it heals and Icy Winds us. And with a live faster electric/special threat in the back (Raichu-Mega-Y), Whimsicott's first action once it is on the field is Tailwind, not Moonblast, whenever two attackers remain alive.
analysis.teamComposition: Milotic should have been the fourth over Garchomp into a rain team with Politoed Icy Wind/Weather Ball and Rillaboom; Scarf Garchomp contributed 36% and died to one Wood Hammer.

proposals.change: MEGA CHIP-INTO-OHKO BAN: if Charizard-Y's displayed damage on its best target is <35% and any active foe has a displayed >=90% OHKO on it, force Protect (if unused last turn) or a switch instead of attacking.
proposals.evidence: T4: Drogon fired Weather Ball for 19-28% into Politoed while under a displayed 61-107% Weather Ball OHKO and died, having dealt 52% all game.

proposals.change: TURN-1 MEGA PROTECT VS FAKE OUT: if Drogon/Dragonite is Mega-evolving on turn 1 and any opposing active Pokemon has Fake Out on its sheet or is a known Fake Out user (Rillaboom, Incineroar, Scrafty, Mienshao), that slot must Protect — the Mega and Drought still resolve.
proposals.evidence: T1 Rillaboom Fake Out flinched Drogon, then Wyrdeer Psyshield Bash took it to 36%; the Mega never got a single attack off at full HP.

proposals.change: WEATHER-SETTER BURST RULE: never commit more than one turn of chip to an opposing weather setter — if both actions cannot bring it below 0% this turn, prefer removing its partner or setting Tailwind instead of a partial chip that it heals back.
proposals.evidence: Politoed took Weather Ball (25%), Kowtow Cleave (54%), Weather Ball (19%), Dragon Claw (31%) across four turns while Leftovers/Grassy heal gave HP back and it KO'd Drogon and Garchomp in the meantime.

proposals.change: TAILWIND MANDATE: once Whimsicott is on the field with at least two of our Pokemon alive and no Trick Room active, its first action is Tailwind unless Moonblast is a displayed KO on the last live foe.
proposals.evidence: Tailwind turns us 0; Raichu-Mega-Y outsped and Zap-Cannoned our last two Pokemon in the endgame.

proposals.change: Against rain cores (Politoed/Pelipper + Rillaboom/Archaludon), bring Milotic as the fourth over Garchomp.
proposals.evidence: Garchomp dealt 36% and died to a single Wood Hammer; Milotic would have absorbed Weather Ball/Icy Wind and Ice Beamed Rillaboom.

lessons: If Charizard-Y is Mega-evolving on turn 1 while a Fake Out user is active, Protect — the Mega evolution and Drought still happen, and the Fake Out is blanked.
Never fire a sub-35% chip attack with Charizard-Y while it is under a displayed 90%+ OHKO; Protect or switch instead.
Do not chip an opposing weather setter across multiple turns — it heals and keeps its weather up; burst it in one turn with both actions or ignore it and remove its partner.
Whimsicott's first action after entering the field is Tailwind whenever two of our attackers are alive and no Trick Room is up; Moonblast chip is worth less than 4 turns of speed.
Against rain with Politoed + Rillaboom, bring Milotic over Garchomp: Garchomp folds to Wood Hammer and Icy Wind while Milotic walls the core.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp has produced 30W-39L and in this game died in a single Wood Hammer after contributing 36%; Sitrus gives it a turn of survivability against rain/Grassy Terrain chip and lets it switch moves to answer both Politoed and Rillaboom.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'pivot + weather reset' shape: Rillaboom U-turn brought Raichu-Mega-Y in for free on the exact turn their Politoed died, converting a losing board into a sweep. For us: swap Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (unblockable finisher that does not need Drogon alive) and give Drogon Covert Cloak so Rillaboom/Incineroar Fake Out cannot blank our Mega's first turn.
teamInspiration.reason: Both of Drogon's lost turns this game came from priority denial (Fake Out flinch T1, then a rain-boosted Weather Ball), and our endgame lost because Raichu-Mega-Y was faster than everything we had left with zero Tailwind up.

analysis.whatWorked: The Milotic + Mega Dragonite lead handled the Sinistcha/Raichu-Y front: Ice Beam + Heat Wave chip set up a clean double KO on turn 3 (Dragon Pulse removed Sinistcha through Rage Powder redirect failure, Scald finished the burned Raichu-Mega-Y). We went 2-0 up on KOs by turn 3 and correctly identified Raichu-Mega-Y (Zap Cannon) as the primary threat. Turn 4's pivot (Milotic at 9% para out, Dragonite Protect vs Kingambit Kowtow Cleave) was also correct repositioning.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: switching a nearly-dead paralyzed Milotic instead of letting it die; Protect discipline on the threatened slot turn 4; Whimsicott Tailwind once it was on the field. VIOLATED: (1) Turn 1 we Mega-evolved Dragonite into a known Fake Out user (Raichu with Fake Out) without Protect — the exact 'TURN-1 MEGA PROTECT VS FAKE OUT' proposal — and lost the whole turn plus the Multiscale shield. (2) Turn 5 we double-attacked with both slots while BOTH of our Pokemon were under displayed OHKO threats (Sneasler Dire Claw on Drogon, Kowtow Cleave on a paralyzed Dragonite) — directly against the 'do not spend both actions on one foe while both slots face displayed OHKOs' rule — and lost both Pokemon in one turn. (3) Drogon was switched in on turn 4 into an active Sneasler with Dire Claw and never Protected.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 1: Mega Dragonite ate Fake Out (flinch = half the turn's action economy gone) and then Zap Cannon paralysis on turn 2 — paralysis is what actually lost the game, because Dragonite was fully paralyzed on turn 5 and died without acting. Turn 2 was a wolfe-fallback (API failure) that chose Milotic Protect + Dragonite Heat Wave into Rage Powder, donating a free Zap Cannon. Turn 5 was the fatal misplay: at 2v2 with Drogon at 47% facing a displayed Dire Claw OHKO and a paralyzed Dragonite at 24%, we clicked double Heat Wave (spread, neither a guaranteed KO) instead of Protecting the piece under the displayed OHKO or switching. Sneasler moved first and deleted Drogon; Kingambit deleted Dragonite. From there it was Whimsicott (1 HP) + a paralyzed Milotic vs a healthy Sneasler/Kingambit — unwinnable. Net: we traded a Mega + our Mega-Y for two of their mons but handed them the endgame with zero live attackers.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Enforce the turn-1 Fake Out Protect rule mechanically: if we are Mega-evolving and any foe has Fake Out on its sheet, that slot Protects. 2) Never double-attack when both of our slots are under displayed OHKO threats and neither attack is a guaranteed KO — at minimum one slot Protects or switches. 3) Treat paralysis as a 'switch trigger' on a Mega: a paralyzed Mega Dragonite at <40% should be swapped, not kept in to fire spread moves. 4) Against Rage Powder/Follow Me redirectors, spread moves (Heat Wave) are the right answer, but only when the partner is not being redirected into a free KO; prefer KOing the redirector first. 5) Vs Sneasler, Dire Claw is a displayed OHKO on Whimsicott and near-OHKO on Drogon — remove Sneasler with Garchomp/Milotic before it gets a free turn.

proposals.change: DOUBLE-OHKO SPLIT RULE: if both of our active Pokemon are under displayed >=90% OHKO threats and neither of our candidate attacks is a >=90% KO on the foe that moves first, at least one slot MUST Protect or switch; block the double-attack line.
proposals.evidence: T5: Drogon (47%) under Dire Claw OHKO and paralyzed Dragonite (24%) under Kowtow Cleave KO; we clicked double Heat Wave (50-92% / 40-73%, no guaranteed KO) and lost both Pokemon in one turn, converting a 2-0 KO lead into a loss.

proposals.change: PARALYZED MEGA PIVOT: a paralyzed Mega (Dragonite/Charizard) below 45% HP must switch or Protect rather than attack — full-paralysis risk plus halved speed means its action is unreliable.
proposals.evidence: T5 Dragonite was fully paralyzed and died without acting; its Heat Wave was counted in our plan as a KO contribution that never happened.

proposals.change: FAKE OUT MEGA GATE (hard block): when Mega-evolving on turn 1 and any opposing active has Fake Out on its open sheet, the Mega slot's only legal choices are Protect or switch.
proposals.evidence: T1 Raichu Fake Out flinched Mega Dragonite, wasting our Mega's first turn and leaving it at 96% into Zap Cannon paralysis.

proposals.change: Swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (or add Covert Cloak to Drogon) so we hold an unblockable priority finisher that works through Fake Out, paralysis speed loss and Rage Powder-adjacent turns.
proposals.evidence: Three of the last five games ended with us having chip-range foes we could not finish because every attacker was slower or flinched; Heat Wave was redirected/flinched twice this game.

lessons: If both of our active Pokemon are under displayed OHKO threats and neither of our attacks is a guaranteed KO, one slot must Protect or switch — never double-attack into a double-OHKO board.
A paralyzed Mega below ~45% HP is not a reliable attacker: switch it or Protect, do not bank its damage into the turn plan.
When Mega-evolving on turn 1 against a sheet-confirmed Fake Out user, the Mega slot Protects; the Mega and its weather still resolve.
Zap Cannon (Raichu-Mega-Y) is a game-defining paralysis threat, not just damage — remove Raichu before it lands one, even at the cost of chip elsewhere.
Against Rage Powder/Follow Me, KO the redirector first; spread moves are the backup, not a reason to leave the partner's single-target KO on the table.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 30-40 (43%) and our last five losses were decided by survivability and Protect discipline, not raw speed; Sitrus adds a turn of life against the Dire Claw / Kowtow Cleave chip that keeps deleting our pieces, and removes the Choice lock that stops Garchomp from answering two different threats.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'status-first Mega' shape: Raichu-Mega-Y led with Fake Out then Zap Cannon paralysis behind a Rage Powder redirector, effectively removing two of our Pokemon's turns without KOing anything. For us: give Mega Dragonite Extreme Speed over Heat Wave (unblockable finisher that ignores paralysis speed loss and redirection) and consider Covert Cloak on Drogon to blank Fake Out entirely.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Mega Dragonite lost turn 1 to Fake Out, turn 2 to Zap Cannon paralysis, and turn 5 to full paralysis — three dead turns from a single opposing Pokemon. A priority move and a Fake Out immunity item directly answer that pattern.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Protect on Mega-evolving Drogon vs Aerodactyl Rock Slide was correct and saved the Mega that turn while Whimsicott still landed Tailwind. Turn 3 focus-fire (Moonblast to break Sash + Iron Head) removed Aerodactyl cleanly. Turn 5 double-targeting their Whimsicott removed their Tailwind setter and got the KO.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The 'Mega + Protect on turn 1 under a displayed OHKO' rule was applied correctly. The 'once a foe shows Rock coverage, Charizard only Protects or switches' rule was then VIOLATED on turn 2 — Drogon attacked into a live Aerodactyl Rock Slide and died. 'Never let the opponent have both speed and power' was violated: they got Tailwind up on turn 1 and we never denied it.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 2 was the game: Aerodactyl was fully healthy with a confirmed 4x Rock Slide that had already been aimed at Drogon on turn 1. The correct action was Drogon Protect again (or switch to Milotic/Kingambit) while Whimsicott attacked; instead Whimsicott double-Protected (no real threat to it behind Drogon's Protect being spent) and Drogon fired a 29-55% Heat Wave into the exact move that OHKOs it. We lost our Mega for ~30% chip. Secondary failure: turn 4 Whimsicott Protected a second time while Kingambit at 55/207 was left exposed to Moonblast and died; we had the slot order backwards (the dying piece should have Protected/switched). Turn 6 Tailwind with only Milotic + a 1-hit Whimsicott left violated 'Tailwind is only worth a turn if two attackers will still be alive'. Endgame: Milotic alone vs Mega Charizard + Tsareena was unwinnable.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: if a foe used a 4x-super-effective move at our Mega last turn and is still alive and faster, that Mega may not click an attack — Protect or switch, every turn, until the foe is dead. Second: never spend the Protect on the slot that is NOT the primary target; the threatened slot Protects, the safe slot attacks. Third: do not stack a second consecutive Protect on the same Pokemon while the partner is in KO range. Fourth: Tailwind requires two live attackers after this turn.

proposals.change: ROCK-LOCK RULE (hard block): if any living opposing active used a Rock move (Rock Slide / Stone Edge / Power Gem / Ancient Power) against Charizard-Y, or has one on its open sheet and outspeeds, Charizard-Y's legal actions are Protect or switch only — attacking is blocked until that foe is KO'd.
proposals.evidence: T1 Aerodactyl Rock Slide aimed at Drogon (blocked by Protect); T2 Drogon clicked Heat Wave into the same Aerodactyl and was OHKO'd (100%) for only 29-55% chip in return. Mega lost on turn 2.

proposals.change: PROTECT-THE-THREATENED-SLOT RULE: the Protect must go on the Pokemon under the highest displayed incoming damage. Block Protect on a slot whose displayed worst-case incoming damage is below 60% when the partner is above 90%.
proposals.evidence: T2 Whimsicott (behind Sash, not the Rock Slide target) Protected while Drogon, under a displayed 268-367% OHKO, attacked. T4 Whimsicott Protected again while Kingambit at 26% HP was KO'd by Moonblast.

proposals.change: NO CONSECUTIVE PROTECT while the partner is in displayed KO range: if a Pokemon Protected last turn, its Protect is blocked this turn unless it is itself under a >=90% displayed OHKO and the partner is not.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott Protected T2 and again T4; Kingambit died on T4 with Protect available in its own slot.

proposals.change: TAILWIND VIABILITY GATE: block Tailwind unless at least two of our Pokemon (including the setter) will plausibly be alive next turn and at least one is an attacker with a non-status move.
proposals.evidence: T6 Whimsicott set Tailwind at 69/137 under a Heat Wave OHKO with only Milotic behind; Whimsicott died the same turn and the Tailwind was wasted.

proposals.change: Against Rock-coverage leads (Aerodactyl, Tyranitar, Garchomp-Z, Barbaracle), bring Mega Dragonite instead of Mega Charizard-Y and keep Drogon home entirely; Dragonite only takes neutral Rock damage and still provides Tailwind.
proposals.evidence: Drogon has now been first-blooded by Rock moves repeatedly (Aerodactyl, Tyranitar, Power Gem x2 in logs); ourFaints shows Drogon 122 faints, the most of any attacker, and 'Aerodactyl Rock Slide' OHKO'd it through 153 HP.

lessons: If a foe already aimed a 4x-super-effective move at our Mega and is still alive, that Mega never attacks again until the foe is dead — Protect or switch only.
The Protect goes on the slot with the highest displayed incoming damage, not the slot that is convenient; a Protect on the safe slot is a wasted action in the 2-action economy.
Never Protect with the same Pokemon on consecutive turns while the partner is sitting in displayed KO range with Protect available.
Tailwind is forbidden unless two of our Pokemon will still be alive next turn and one of them can attack.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 30-41 (42%) over 71 games and the Scarf lock repeatedly leaves us without a flexible answer; Sitrus Garchomp gives a bulkier Rock-resist pivot that can switch into the Rock Slide users (Aerodactyl/Tyranitar) that keep deleting Drogon, and can change moves across turns.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'fast Rock lead + mirror Mega Charizard behind a Tailwind setter' shape: Aerodactyl threatened our Mega into permanent Protect while their own Whimsicott matched our speed control. For us: give Drogon a Covert Cloak or Focus Sash is not enough — instead swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (unblockable finisher) and make Milotic the mandatory fourth versus any Rock-coverage lead, so losing Drogon does not end the game.
teamInspiration.reason: Our entire game plan collapsed the moment Aerodactyl's Rock Slide connected on turn 2; we had no priority, no Rock-resist pivot on the field, and our remaining three Pokemon dealt only 188% total damage across five turns.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 Mega + Protect on Dragonite against Aerodactyl's Rock Slide was correct and saved Multiscale for a turn. Dragon Pulse eventually removed Aerodactyl, and Heat Wave cleaned Absol-Mega-Z late. The preview read (Kingambit vs Hatterene/Absol) was sound in isolation.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The 'Mega + Protect when under a displayed OHKO on turn 1' rule was followed correctly on Dragonite. However the 'never lead Kingambit when the opponent's sheet shows Fighting-type / Ground pressure' spirit was violated: Excadrill High Horsepower did 88% to Kingambit on turn 1 and Aerodactyl Rock Slide finished it on turn 3 having contributed ZERO damage all game. The Rock-lock rule was also effectively violated in reverse — we knew Aerodactyl had Rock Slide from turn 1 yet still kept Kingambit (a Rock-neutral but frail-to-Ground slot) exposed instead of pivoting.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Kingambit lead into Aerodactyl + Excadrill: Excadrill High Horsepower (4x effective vs the Dark/Steel typing's Ground weakness) deleted 88% on turn 1; Kingambit dealt 0% damage in the entire game and died turn 3 — a complete forfeited resource. 2) Turn 3 we spent Kingambit's last action on Iron Head into Aerodactyl but Dragonite attacked Absol instead, splitting; Aerodactyl survived and killed Kingambit and chipped Dragonite. 3) Dragonite was burned on turn 3 by Will-O-Wisp and then spent turns 4 and 6 Protecting at 17%/9% — a burned 9% Mega Protecting twice is not a win condition, it is a stalled corpse; it should have attacked or been switched. 4) Turn 4 Whimsicott Moonblast was aimed at a switched-in Excadrill for 24% instead of being Tailwind/Encore value; Whimsicott dealt 75% total and never set Tailwind this game (the Tailwind came from Dragonite on turn 2, wasting Dragonite's offensive turn). 5) Two rate-limit fallbacks handed turns to the engine at critical moments (T2, T5). 6) Endgame: Drogon alone vs Excadrill with Rock Slide — we attacked into a displayed 97-159% OHKO instead of Protecting; it was lost anyway but it confirms the Rock-lock discipline is not firing.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: never lead Kingambit when any opposing active/sheet Pokemon has a Ground move (Excadrill, Garchomp, Landorus, Rillaboom High Horsepower) — Kingambit is 4x-adjacent dead to Ground and contributes nothing. Against an Aerodactyl + Excadrill (Rock + Ground) front, the correct four is Milotic + Whimsicott + Dragonite + Drogon, leading Whimsicott (Tailwind) + Milotic (Scald/Ice Beam answers both Ground types and resists nothing-relevant). Second: a burned Mega below 25% HP must switch or attack, never Protect twice — Protect only delays and we lose the attacker. Third: Tailwind belongs to Whimsicott; never spend the Mega's turn setting it when Whimsicott is alive in the back.

proposals.change: HARD BAN: Kingambit may not be brought (and absolutely never led) when the opponent's sheet contains any Ground-move user (Excadrill, Garchomp, Rillaboom, Landorus, Swampert, Hippowdon). Bring Milotic as the fourth instead.
proposals.evidence: Excadrill High Horsepower did 88% to Kingambit on turn 1; Kingambit dealt 0 damage and died turn 3 having been a dead slot the entire game.

proposals.change: BURNED/LOW MEGA RULE: a Mega at or below 25% HP with a burn or other residual damage may not use Protect — it must attack or switch. Protect only guarantees residual death.
proposals.evidence: Dragonite Protected at 17% (T4) and 9% (T6); it died anyway on T6 and never used its remaining offensive turns.

proposals.change: TAILWIND OWNERSHIP: block Tailwind on Dragonite/Charizard whenever Whimsicott is alive on our bench or field; the Mega's turn is damage.
proposals.evidence: Dragonite spent turn 2 setting Tailwind while Whimsicott sat in the back; Dragonite then had only 2 attacking turns all game.

proposals.change: FOCUS FIRE RULE vs the confirmed killer: once a foe has landed a KO or a >50% hit on us and is still alive, both of our actions that turn must target that foe unless one slot is under a displayed OHKO requiring Protect.
proposals.evidence: T3 Kingambit Iron Head hit Aerodactyl while Dragonite hit Absol; Aerodactyl survived, KO'd Kingambit and chipped Dragonite twice more before dying on T5.

lessons: Never lead or bring Kingambit when the opponent's sheet shows any Ground-move user — Excadrill/Garchomp High Horsepower or Earthquake deletes it before it acts.
A burned or residual-damaged Mega at 25% HP or less must attack or switch; Protect just hands the turn away and it dies to chip anyway.
Tailwind is Whimsicott's job: never spend a Mega's action on Tailwind while Whimsicott is alive.
When one foe has already KO'd or >50%-chipped one of our Pokemon and is still alive, both actions focus that foe — splitting damage lets it kill twice more.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 30-42 (42%) and the Choice lock keeps producing dead turns in Rock/Ground-heavy boards like this one; Sitrus Garchomp can switch moves to answer both Excadrill (EQ) and Aerodactyl (Rock Slide/Dragon Claw) and survives chip to keep attacking.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'fast Rock lead + Ground partner' squeeze: Aerodactyl (Rock Slide + Taunt) alongside Excadrill (High Horsepower/Iron Head) attacked both of our Megas' weaknesses simultaneously. For us: make Milotic the mandatory fourth versus any Rock+Ground front (it answers Excadrill with Scald and Aerodactyl with Scald/Ice Beam), and swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so a chipped/burned Dragonite still converts its last turns into damage instead of Protecting.
teamInspiration.reason: Our Kingambit died contributing 0% and our Dragonite spent 2 of its 5 turns Protecting at single-digit HP; both failures come from having no Ground-resistant fourth and no priority finisher.

analysis.whatWorked: Won vs 6leen. Turn 1 Heat Wave + Moonblast into Gallade/Scolipede immediately pressured the Trick Room/setup pair and the spread hit Ditto's switch-in for 48%, so Ditto died on T2. Recognizing Wide Guard after T3 and swapping to single-target Weather Ball on T4 to delete the +2 Atk/+3 Spe Scolipede was the key play of the game — exactly the 'after Wide Guard, don't spread into it' rule. The endgame was clean: Whimsicott at 1 HP Protected, Encored Mega Aggron into Iron Defense (denying Body Press/Head Smash entirely), then Moonblast finished it. Encoring a setup move is a textbook win-con denial.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) after Wide Guard, stop spreading — switched to Weather Ball; (2) punish setup — Encore locked Aggron into Iron Defense instead of Protect-stalling; (3) never Earthquake next to an ally — used Stomping Tantrum with Garchomp beside Whimsicott; (4) switched Whimsicott out at 1 HP rather than letting it die for free. Violated: Drogon attacked into Mega Aggron on T5 (wolfe-fallback turn) when Head Smash was a displayed OHKO — the 'Mega under displayed OHKO must Protect or switch' rule was skipped because the LLM call fell back to the engine. Kingambit was also brought/sent in against an Aggron showing Body Press (Fighting coverage) and died contributing 0 damage, violating the Kingambit-vs-Fighting ban.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T5 fallback: Drogon fired Heat Wave into a freshly Mega-evolved Aggron that had Wide Guard support AND Head Smash — the spread was blocked by Wide Guard and Drogon was OHKO'd. Two straight turns of Wide Guard were already visible; this was a 100% avoidable loss of our Mega. 2) Kingambit entered against Mega Aggron with Body Press and died in one hit for 0% damage — a second confirmation that Kingambit must not be deployed against Fighting coverage. 3) Garchomp did a miserable 54% total over four turns because Stomping Tantrum into a +4 Def Iron Defense Aggron is near-worthless; the game was won by Whimsicott's Encore, not by damage. 4) Two rate-limit fallbacks again cost us the single most important turn of the game (T5).
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-code the Wide Guard memory: once a foe uses Wide Guard, block all spread moves (Heat Wave, Rock Slide, Dazzling Gleam) for the next two turns and force the single-target option. Hard-code the Mega-under-OHKO rule into shouldBlockMove rather than relying on the LLM, so fallback turns can't throw the Mega. Add an explicit Kingambit deployment ban vs Body Press/Close Combat/Aura Sphere users. Also, against an Iron Defense/Bulk Up snowballer, prioritize Encore the turn the boost appears rather than chipping with resisted Ground moves.

proposals.change: WIDE GUARD MEMORY: if any opposing active Pokemon used Wide Guard within the last 2 turns, hard-block all spread moves (Heat Wave, Rock Slide, Dazzling Gleam, Blizzard) and force single-target damage.
proposals.evidence: T3 Heat Wave fully blocked by Wide Guard; T5 Heat Wave blocked again and Drogon was OHKO'd by Head Smash on the wasted turn.

proposals.change: MEGA SURVIVAL GUARD (engine-level, not LLM-level): block any attacking move from Charizard-Y/Dragonite when a foe on the field has a displayed >=90% OHKO threat on it and Protect is available — force Protect or switch, even on wolfe-fallback turns.
proposals.evidence: T5 fallback had Drogon attack into Mega Aggron Head Smash and lose our Mega for zero damage; the same pattern killed Drogon vs Aerodactyl two games ago.

proposals.change: Extend the Kingambit ban: never bring Kingambit when the opponent's sheet shows Body Press, Close Combat, Aura Sphere, Drain Punch or any Fighting-type.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit died to Mega Aggron Body Press at full HP (100% damage) having dealt 0% this game; same pattern as Lucario/Absol games.

proposals.change: ENCORE PRIORITY: when a foe uses any defensive setup move (Iron Defense, Cosmic Power, Bulk Up, Calm Mind) and Whimsicott is alive, Encore it that same turn instead of chipping with a resisted attack.
proposals.evidence: Encore on T8 locked Mega Aggron into Iron Defense and won the game; one turn earlier would have saved Garchomp 20% of chip.

lessons: Wide Guard seen once means every spread move is dead for the next two turns — switch to single-target immediately and keep it switched.
A Mega facing a displayed 90%+ OHKO never attacks; this must hold even when the pilot falls back to the engine.
Never deploy Kingambit against Body Press / any Fighting coverage — it dies at full HP for zero damage.
Encore on a defensive setup move (Iron Defense) is a full win condition: it converts an unkillable wall into a free target.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp; this loss pattern was Mega preservation and Wide Guard, not Garchomp's item. Stay on the current variant to finish the trial window.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Wide Guard pivot + unkillable Mega wall' shape: Gallade's Wide Guard blanked two of our Charizard turns while Mega Aggron set Iron Defense behind it. For us, swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (spread, Wide-Guardable) for Extreme Speed — an unblockable single-target priority finisher that ignores Wide Guard, redirection and paralysis speed loss.
teamInspiration.reason: Across the last five games our spread moves were blocked three times (Wide Guard x2, Protect) and Dragonite/Drogon repeatedly had no way to convert a last turn into damage; a priority single-target move fixes both failure modes at once.

whatWorked: Won the game vs antumin's Trick Room/bulky-balance team. Turn 1 Weather Ball removed Meowstic (the Thunder Wave/Trick Room support) immediately, denying their speed-control and follow-up status. Turn 2 recognizing a 1% Whimsicott is a dead action and pivoting to Kingambit rather than Protect-stalling was correct. Focus-firing Toxapex with both actions over turns 3-5 (instead of chipping it across many turns while it Regenerates/Recovers) killed it cleanly. Milotic closed the game out as the bulky late-game win-con, KOing Sinistcha and Mega Dragonite with Ice Beam.
lessonsApplied: Followed: 'burst a bulky healer in one turn, do not chip across turns' (Toxapex double-targeted); 'a low-HP Pokemon that dies to anything should switch rather than Protect' (Whimsicott T2); 'KO the speed-control/status support first' (Meowstic T1); 'do not Tailwind into a Trick Room team with no attackers live'. Violated: the BURNED/LOW MEGA rule — Drogon at 13/153 with burn-equivalent residual (Infestation partial trap + paralysis) used Protect on T6 instead of attacking or switching, and it died on T7 anyway having contributed nothing after T5. Also violated the Mega-turn-1 discipline: the engine fallback fired Moonblast/Weather Ball into a confirmed Thunder Wave user instead of protecting the Mega, and Drogon spent the rest of the game paralyzed (2 full-para turns lost).
whatFailed: 1) Turn 1 was a wolfe-fallback (rate limit) that let Meowstic Thunder Wave the Mega — paralysis cost Drogon two complete turns (T2 and T3 'cant|par') and ultimately the Pokemon. 2) Drogon was trapped by Infestation while paralyzed at low HP and we kept it in for 4 turns instead of recognizing it was a dead asset; the T6 Protect was pure residual suicide. 3) Kingambit was burned by Matcha Gotcha and died to its own Life Orb + burn at 18 HP having scored 0 KOs despite 131% damage — the damage was spread across a Regenerator wall rather than converted. 4) Whimsicott again took a turn-1 OHKO-range hit (Air Slash to 1%) and then contributed 80% damage but no KOs; it has now fainted 160 times across the dataset.
howToImprove: Treat Thunder Wave/status support (Meowstic, Klefki, Amoonguss spore) on the opposing sheet exactly like Fake Out: the Mega Protects on its evolution turn rather than attacking, because a paralyzed Mega loses more total turns than one spread move gains. Add a trapped-and-crippled rule: a Pokemon that is partially trapped (Infestation/Whirlpool) AND statused AND below 25% HP may not Protect — it must fire its highest-damage attack every remaining turn. Against Regenerator/Recover walls (Toxapex, Milotic, Sinistcha) keep the focus-fire burst but accept that one of our Pokemon must be expendable; do not let Kingambit sit in Infestation with Life Orb recoil. Keep Milotic as the designated late-game closer — it has now won two of the last three games from the back.

proposals.change: STATUS-SUPPORT PROTECT RULE: if the opponent's sheet/active shows Thunder Wave, Will-O-Wisp, Spore, Yawn or Glare and our Mega is evolving this turn, the Mega slot Protects — the Mega evolution and weather still resolve, and we deny the status that costs 2+ future turns.
proposals.evidence: T1 Meowstic Thunder Wave paralyzed Drogon through a wolfe-fallback attack turn; Drogon then lost T2 and T3 entirely to full paralysis and died at 8% on T7.

proposals.change: TRAPPED-CRIPPLE RULE: block Protect for any Pokemon that is partially trapped (Infestation/Whirlpool/Bind) AND below 30% HP — it dies to residual regardless, so it must deal damage every turn it has left.
proposals.evidence: T6 Drogon (13/153, paralyzed, Infestation) used Protect, took residual to 8%, and was KO'd on T7 by Extreme Speed having dealt zero damage in its last two turns.

proposals.change: LIFE ORB + BURN STOP: once Kingambit is burned, block Life-Orb-recoil attacks when the combined recoil+burn chip would KO it this turn unless the attack is a guaranteed KO on the target.
proposals.evidence: T6 Kingambit at 18/207 burned fired Kowtow Cleave for 47% on Sinistcha and killed itself to Life Orb recoil; Sinistcha survived and had to be finished by Milotic anyway.

lessons: Thunder Wave support (Meowstic/Klefki) on the opposing sheet is a Protect trigger for our Mega on its evolution turn, exactly like Fake Out — paralysis costs more turns than a spread move gains.
A Pokemon that is partially trapped (Infestation) and below 30% HP must attack every remaining turn; Protect only guarantees it dies to residual with zero damage dealt.
Burned Kingambit with Life Orb must not fire a non-KO attack when recoil plus burn will faint it — switch or use Sucker Punch/Protect-free damage only if it secures the KO.
Against Regenerator/Recover walls (Toxapex/Sinistcha), burst with both actions in a single turn; Milotic is the designated closer and should be preserved to clean up.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'status-support behind a bulky trapper' shape: Meowstic Thunder Wave + Toxapex Infestation neutralized our Mega for four turns without ever KOing it. For us, give Drogon a Covert Cloak (blanks Fake Out, Infestation's trap chip stays but secondary flinch/Thunder-Wave-via-contact pressure drops) or, better, swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so a paralyzed or chipped Mega still converts turns into damage at +2 priority.
teamInspiration.reason: Drogon lost T2, T3 and T6 to paralysis/Protect and died contributing 97%; a priority move and a status-blanking item directly answer the repeated 'our Mega has no usable turns' failure mode seen in the last five games.

analysis.whatWorked: Garchomp was the only functional piece: 239% damage and a double KO (Glimmora-Mega + Incineroar) with one Earthquake on T6. The T3 read to pivot a 6% Dragonite out to Kingambit was correct in isolation, and the T5 Kingambit Protect correctly blanked Incineroar's Fake Out while Earthquake chipped Incineroar to 8%.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Violated several standing rules. (1) Our own team rule 'Never Earthquake with Garchomp while Kingambit is beside it' was broken on T4, T5 and fatally on T6 — our own Earthquake, not the opponent, KO'd Kingambit at 102/207. (2) 'Protect Mega Dragonite's Multiscale from chip' failed: on T1 the fallback engine led Dragonite into a sheet-visible Glimmora Power Gem (Rock, 4x-ish threat) + Garchomp Rock Slide and it was at 6% after one turn, never recovering. (3) The double-Protect on T2 with no real threat remaining wasted a full turn of the 2-action economy. (4) Four of nine turns were API-rate-limited fallbacks, meaning the pilot rules were simply not applied on the most important turns (T1, T2, T4).
analysis.whatFailed: T1 lead (Whimsicott + Dragonite into Glimmora/Garchomp) was the game-losing decision: Glimmora Power Gem and Garchomp Rock Slide both hit Dragonite super-effectively; Dragonite flinched from Rock Slide and fell to 10/168 on turn one, contributing 0% damage all game and dying to Grassy Glide. T2 double Protect gave a free turn. T4-T6: Garchomp spammed Earthquake next to Kingambit, hitting Kingambit for 105 then 77 then killing it — Kingambit contributed 0 KOs and effectively died to friendly fire. T7 Protect on a 6% Dragonite that then died anyway on T8 to Grassy Glide (priority ignores our Protect timing) wasted our last real action. We never set Tailwind despite leading Whimsicott.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Hard-block Earthquake whenever Kingambit (or any non-Flying/Levitate ally) is in the adjacent slot — this must be an engine-level block, not advice. 2) Against any sheet showing Rock coverage (Power Gem / Rock Slide / Stone Edge) do not lead Mega Dragonite; lead Whimsicott + Garchomp or Whimsicott + Drogon with Protect, and keep the Mega in the back. 3) Never double-Protect when neither slot is under a displayed KO. 4) A Pokemon below 10% HP with no Multiscale and a priority attacker (Rillaboom/Grassy Glide) on the field must attack or switch, never Protect. 5) Whimsicott's first action is Tailwind.

proposals.change: ALLY-DAMAGE HARD BLOCK: block Earthquake / Bulldoze / any spread Ground move whenever the ally slot is a grounded Pokemon (Kingambit, Milotic, Whimsicott, Garchomp). Force Dragon Claw / Stomping Tantrum / Rock Slide instead.
proposals.evidence: T4/T5/T6: our own Earthquake dealt 105 then 25 then the lethal blow to Kingambit (207 HP -> 0) while Kingambit contributed 0 damage and 0 KOs.

proposals.change: ROCK-COVERAGE MEGA RULE: if the opponent sheet shows two or more Rock-type moves (Power Gem, Rock Slide, Stone Edge, Ancient Power), neither Mega leads — lead Whimsicott + Garchomp/Milotic and bring the Mega in on turn 3+.
proposals.evidence: Glimmora Power Gem + Garchomp Rock Slide reduced Mega Dragonite to 6% on turn 1; it contributed 0% damage for the whole game.

proposals.change: SUB-10% NO-PROTECT RULE: block Protect for any ally at <=10% HP when an opposing active has a priority attacking move (Grassy Glide, Extreme Speed, Sucker Punch, Aqua Jet) — it dies next turn regardless, so it must attack or switch.
proposals.evidence: T7 Dragonite at 6% Protected, then died on T8 to Rillaboom Grassy Glide having dealt 0 damage all game.

proposals.change: NO DOUBLE PROTECT WITHOUT DOUBLE THREAT: block the second Protect in a turn unless both slots show a displayed >=80% incoming hit.
proposals.evidence: T2 both Whimsicott and Dragonite Protected against a 21%-HP Garchomp and Glimmora with nothing lethal queued; a full turn of the 2-action economy was surrendered.

lessons: Garchomp's Earthquake must be hard-blocked whenever a grounded ally (Kingambit, Milotic, Whimsicott) shares the field — our own spread move KO'd Kingambit this game.
If the opponent's sheet shows two or more Rock-type moves, do not lead either Mega; the Mega enters on turn 3+ after the Rock user is chipped or dead.
A Pokemon at or below 10% HP never Protects while a priority attacker (Grassy Glide, Extreme Speed, Sucker Punch) is on the field — it must attack or switch.
Never double-Protect unless both slots face a displayed 80%+ incoming hit.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is locked into Earthquake, which is exactly the move that killed our own Kingambit across T4-T6; Sitrus lets Garchomp pick Dragon Claw/Rock Slide next to grounded allies and survive the Rock-coverage leads that keep deleting our Megas.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Rock-coverage lead + priority cleaner' shape: Glimmora Power Gem + Garchomp Rock Slide deleted our Mega on turn 1, and Rillaboom Grassy Glide cleaned up two low-HP Pokemon at +1 priority. For us: swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (an unblockable +2 finisher that converts chipped Pokemon into KOs and gives a crippled Dragonite a usable turn), and give Drogon a Covert Cloak to blank Fake Out/flinch (Rock Slide flinched our Dragonite on T1 and cost the game).
teamInspiration.reason: Across the last five games our Megas have repeatedly ended at single-digit HP with zero damage contributed, and flinch/priority was the deciding mechanic in three of them; a priority finisher and a flinch-blocking item attack both failure modes directly.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Moonblast + Heat Wave into Staraptor was the right focus-fire target (it fell on T2 to Brave Bird recoil + chip). Charizard-Y's Drought correctly overwrote Snow and denied Aurora Veil for two turns. T3 Moonblast-to-break-Sash + Iron Head cleanly removed Ninetales-Alola, the snow/veil engine, in one turn.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Mega evolved turn 1 and the Whimsicott+Charizard lead vs snow followed the confirmed plan. Focus-firing the speed-control setter (Staraptor Tailwind) was correct Wolfe doctrine. However the SUB-10% NO-PROTECT RULE was violated on T4 (Whimsicott at 7% Protected while Grassy Glide was live on the field, and it still died on T5 having contributed nothing), and the 'Protect goes on the slot with the highest displayed incoming damage' rule was violated — Kingambit at 37% was the one in displayed KO range from Basculegion Wave Crash + Grassy Glide, not the already-dead-to-anything Whimsicott.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T1: we did NOT Protect Drogon against a sheet-confirmed Fake Out user (Rillaboom) while Mega-evolving — Drogon flinched, lost its whole turn, and the 2-action economy went to 1. That is the exact codified rule 'when Mega-evolving turn 1 against a sheet-confirmed Fake Out user, the Mega slot Protects.' 2) T2 was an engine fallback (rate limit) that clicked Tailwind into an already-active opposing Tailwind while Drogon sat at 110/153 in displayed Brave Bird KO range with Protect available — Drogon died on turn 2 with 0 damage dealt, in a matchup where Drogon is the entire win condition. 3) T4: Kowtow Cleave into Basculegion was a 95% OHKO line but Kingambit at 37% was guaranteed to be hit first by Aqua Jet+Grassy Glide priority and died before moving; the correct line was Kingambit Protect / Whimsicott attack, or simply accept that Kingambit had to move first which it could not. 4) Basculegion's Last Respects grows with each of OUR faints — by T5 it was a guaranteed OHKO on Garchomp; we never accounted for that scaling and still split damage (Moonblast + Dragon Claw) instead of killing it or switching. 5) Rate-limit fallbacks decided 1 of 5 turns and that turn lost the game.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-code the turn-1 Fake-Out Protect for the Mega slot. Never click Tailwind when the opponent already has Tailwind up and our Mega is in displayed OHKO range — Protect instead. Treat Basculegion as a scaling threat: its Last Respects power rises per our faint, so it must be removed before we lose our third Pokemon, and never leave it alive at 40% hoping to split chip. Put the Protect on the piece that is both (a) in displayed KO range and (b) still capable of dealing damage next turn — not on a 7% Focus-Sash-spent Whimsicott that dies to any residual/priority.

proposals.change: TURN-1 MEGA FAKE-OUT PROTECT (hard rule): if it is turn 1, our Mega slot is Mega-evolving, and any opposing active has Fake Out on the sheet, the Mega slot must Protect. Block all other moves for that slot.
proposals.evidence: T1 vs nwoidn: Rillaboom Fake Out flinched Drogon through the Mega evolution; Drogon lost its only healthy turn and died T2 with 0 damage dealt.

proposals.change: NO TAILWIND WHEN BEHIND ON SPEED CONTROL AND A MEGA IS IN KO RANGE: block Tailwind if the opponent already has Tailwind active AND one of our actives is in a displayed >=70% incoming hit with Protect available; Protect that slot instead.
proposals.evidence: T2 engine fallback set our Tailwind while Drogon sat at 72% HP in displayed Brave Bird KO range; Drogon died instantly and the Tailwind mattered for one turn.

proposals.change: LAST RESPECTS / SCALING-THREAT RULE: flag Basculegion (Last Respects) and Kingambit (Supreme Overlord) as threats whose power scales with faints; prioritize removing them while our faint count is low and never split damage across two foes when one of them is a scaling threat below 50% HP.
proposals.evidence: T5: Basculegion Last Respects OHKO'd full-HP Garchomp after 3 of our faints; we split Moonblast + Dragon Claw and left it at 43%.

proposals.change: Consider Extreme Speed over Heat Wave on Mega Dragonite (fifth consecutive game where a chipped Mega had no way to convert a turn into damage and priority decided the game).
proposals.evidence: Rillaboom Grassy Glide got 2 KOs this game; our Megas and Garchomp repeatedly died before acting.

lessons: On turn 1, if we are Mega-evolving and the opposing sheet shows Fake Out, the Mega slot Protects — the Mega and its weather still resolve, and the flinch is denied.

Never click Tailwind on a turn where our Mega is in displayed OHKO range and Protect is available, especially when the opponent already has Tailwind up — speed control is worthless if the win condition dies on the same turn.
Basculegion's Last Respects and Kingambit's Supreme Overlord scale with faints: remove them early, and once we are down 2+ Pokemon treat them as guaranteed OHKOs on anything.
The Protect belongs on the slot that is in KO range AND can still deal damage next turn, never on a sub-10% Pokemon that dies to any residual or priority anyway.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp: the loss was caused by turn-1/2 Mega mismanagement and priority, not by Garchomp's item; changing items now would add noise to the 30-game window.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Fake Out + priority cleaner behind Tailwind' shape: Rillaboom Fake Out denied our Mega's turn 1 and Grassy Glide closed two KOs at +1. For us, swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (unblockable +2 finisher, ignores Wide Guard/redirection/paralysis) and give Drogon a Covert Cloak to blank Fake Out flinches on its Mega turn.
teamInspiration.reason: Fake Out or flinch cost Drogon its turn-1 action in three of the last five games, and opposing +1/+2 priority scored the final KOs in four of them; a priority finisher and a flinch-blanking item attack both recurring failure modes directly.

analysis.whatWorked: Win vs unsupervised702 (Trick Room archetype, Kingambit + Mega Dragonite lead). Turn 1 focus-fire on Sneasler with Iron Head + Dragon Pulse was the correct Wolfe play: Sneasler Close Combat OHKOs Kingambit, so removing it before it could act was win-condition denial. Turn 3 Heat Wave scored a clean double KO on burned Rillaboom and Protect-healed Sneasler — the turn-2 Heat Wave burn on Rillaboom is what converted that into a 2-for-1. Turn 4 Kowtow Cleave deleted Farigiraf, removing both Armor Tail (priority block) and the Trick Room setter in one action. Endgame 2v1 was closed with the safe double-target (Moonblast + Ice Beam) rather than a prediction, exactly per the 'ahead in count = no reads' directive.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) No Tailwind into a Trick Room team with Farigiraf on sheet — Whimsicott never clicked it. (2) Kingambit used Iron Head/Kowtow Cleave instead of Sucker Punch into Armor Tail Farigiraf — the hard block worked. (3) Focus fire on the single foe that KOs our piece (Sneasler) instead of splitting. (4) Safe closing line when ahead. Violated/at risk: Kingambit was led into a sheet containing Rillaboom High Horsepower — the standing rule 'never lead Kingambit when the opponent's sheet shows a Ground move' was broken, and High Horsepower took Kingambit from 207 to 58 across two turns, which is why it died to Hyper Voice at 7% instead of surviving to clean. Also Fake Out flinched Kingambit on turn 1, costing a full action in the 2-action economy.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Lead choice: Kingambit into Rillaboom (Fake Out + High Horsepower) lost turn 1's Kingambit action to flinch and lost 60% of its HP to Ground chip. 2) Turn 2 double-attack into an obvious Protect: Sneasler at 28% HP was the single most predictable Protect on the board, and we aimed BOTH Iron Head and Heat Wave at it; Iron Head was fully wasted and Heat Wave only landed on Rillaboom by spread splash. The correct line was Iron Head/attack the Rillaboom slot and let Heat Wave's spread chip Sneasler. 3) Turn 4 we let Mega Salamence enter and Hyper Voice for a double KO (Dragonite + Kingambit in one move) — we had no Protect on the 60/168 Dragonite despite Draco Meteor/Hyper Voice being displayed as a KO threat. That nearly threw a won game; Milotic cleaned up only because Whimsicott's Moonblast rolled high. 4) Damage calc was off twice on Dragonite's hits (Dragon Pulse 78% vs predicted 61% max, Heat Wave 62% vs 56% max), suggesting our calc under-rates sun-boosted/Mega Dragonite output — we are leaving KOs on the table by assuming we can't kill.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Enforce the Ground-move lead rule for Kingambit as a hard block, not a soft preference: with Rillaboom/Garchomp/Excadrill on the sheet, Kingambit comes in on turn 3+ after the Ground user is chipped or dead. 2) Add an anti-Protect-bait rule: never aim BOTH actions at a foe that is below 35% HP and has Protect on its sheet and has not yet Protected this cycle — put one action on the partner slot or use a spread that hits both. 3) When a known Mega sweeper (Salamence/Hyper Voice, Floette/Dazzling Gleam) switches in beside a support mon, the slot in displayed KO range must Protect or switch — spread-move double KOs are the #1 way we lose two pieces in one action. 4) Trust higher damage rolls on Mega Dragonite: it out-rolled the calc twice, so treat its 'likely KO' thresholds as reachable and prefer the KO line over the chip line.

proposals.change: ANTI-PROTECT-BAIT: block the second action aimed at the same foe when that foe is <=35% HP, has Protect available, and did not Protect last turn. Redirect the second action to the partner slot or a spread move.
proposals.evidence: T2 vs unsupervised702: both Iron Head and Heat Wave were aimed at 28% Sneasler, which Protected; Iron Head was a fully wasted action in the 2-action economy.

proposals.change: SPREAD-MEGA ENTRY PROTECT: when an opposing Mega with a spread special move (Hyper Voice, Dazzling Gleam, Blizzard, Earth Power) is newly on the field and one of our actives is in displayed >=70% incoming range, that slot must Protect or switch.
proposals.evidence: T4: Mega Salamence Hyper Voice KO'd both Dragonite (60/168) and Kingambit (7 HP after) in one action; a Protect on Dragonite keeps our Mega alive for the endgame.

proposals.change: Hard-block Kingambit from the LEAD pair whenever the opposing sheet shows Rillaboom, Garchomp, Excadrill, Landorus or any High Horsepower/Earthquake user; bring it in at position 3-4.
proposals.evidence: Rillaboom High Horsepower did 110 and 50 damage across T2-T3, leaving Kingambit at 58/207 before the decisive turn.

lessons: Never aim both actions at a sub-35% foe that still has Protect — spread one action onto the partner slot so a Protect costs us nothing.
When an opposing Mega with a spread move enters beside a support mon, the ally in displayed KO range Protects or switches; spread double-KOs are how we lose two pieces to one action.
Kingambit never leads into a sheet with any High Horsepower/Earthquake user (Rillaboom, Garchomp, Excadrill) — it arrives turn 3+ after the Ground user is handled.
Burning a Grass/physical attacker with Heat Wave is real value: the burn turned Rillaboom into a Heat Wave KO one turn later.

itemExperiment.reason: Kingambit keeps arriving chipped and dying with low damage contributed; Clear Amulet also blanks Rock Tomb/Icy Wind speed drops and opposing Intimidate while we test whether Defiant's +2 is actually being realized (it was not this game — the Intimidate came only after Rillaboom fainted).

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Helping Hand + spread Mega' shape: Farigiraf Helping Hand into Mega Salamence Hyper Voice KO'd two of our Pokemon in a single action. For us, swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed as a +2 unblockable finisher, and consider Safety Goggles/Covert Cloak on Kingambit so Fake Out cannot steal its turn-1 action (it was flinched on T1 and contributed only one KO).
teamInspiration.reason: Spread + support doubling is the highest-value action economy play in the format, and our Megas repeatedly lose turns to Fake Out/flinch; a priority finisher plus a flinch-blanking item attacks both of our recurring failure modes.

analysis.whatWorked: Mega Charizard-Y Drought + Heat Wave was the entire engine of this win: 394% total damage and 2 KOs in 5 turns. Turn 1 Heat Wave hit both foes (Whimsicott to 1%, Kangaskhan to 17%) and immediately put their Tailwind setter and their Fake Out pivot into one-shot range. Turn 2 Heat Wave converted that into a Kangaskhan KO plus Baxcalibur to 21%; Turn 3 Heat Wave finished Baxcalibur and chipped Sneasler to 5% while Milotic correctly Protected through Sneasler Rock Slide + Baxcalibur Glaive Rush. Milotic as the designated closer (Scald KO on Sneasler, Ice Beam cleanup) is exactly the role the playbook assigns it, and sheltering Mega Dragonite in the back meant we always had a healthy answer. We also never clicked Tailwind into their Tailwind-advantage board where it would have wasted a turn.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) Milotic designated closer preserved — it finished two Pokemon; (2) win-con sheltered in back (Dragonite never exposed); (3) Protect used only on the slot facing a displayed KO-range hit (T3 Milotic vs Close Combat/Rock Slide), never a double Protect; (4) no Tailwind clicked while behind on speed control with a Mega in KO range; (5) spread damage focused to deny the opponent BOTH speed and power — their Tailwind went up but their two power pieces (Kangaskhan, Baxcalibur) were dead by turn 3. Violated: the active proposal 'TURN-1 MEGA FAKE-OUT PROTECT' — goatgovaa's sheet showed Kangaskhan (Fake Out) and the engine fallback on T1 clicked Heat Wave with Whimsicott, not Protect; we got lucky the Fake Out went into Whimsicott instead of Drogon. Also violated the Drogon-protection principle on T4: Drogon at 17% HP with a displayed Sneasler Rock Slide (71-115% KO) and an opposing Whimsicott Moonblast on board was sent to attack and died.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T1 was a rate-limit fallback (HTTP 429) — the pilot made no decision on the single most important turn of the game; this is now the 5th straight game with 1+ fallback turns. 2) Drogon died on T4 at 17% HP. The board was 2 foes at 1% and 5% HP; Heat Wave was not needed from Drogon at all — Milotic Scald alone KO'd Sneasler, and Drogon could have Protected (or we could have switched it) and survived to close the game at full value. We traded our 394%-damage win condition for zero marginal value because both targets were already dead to one action. 3) Whimsicott died on T2 at 1% HP without contributing (Moonblast into Kangaskhan was fine, but it was already a dead piece from T1 Heat Wave friendly-fire-less chip + Last Resort). 4) We never got Tailwind up at all (us 0 turns, them 3) and still won — but only because Drought/Heat Wave outpaced their board; against a bulkier team this is a losing pattern.
analysis.howToImprove: (a) Hard rule: when BOTH remaining opposing actives are at or below 10% HP and a single one of our actions already KOs both/either, the Mega in <=25% HP must Protect or switch rather than attack — overkill with our win condition on the field is a free loss of the Mega. (b) Enforce the turn-1 Fake Out Protect rule in code, not just as a proposal, so engine fallbacks still obey it. (c) When a sub-10% Pokemon (Whimsicott at 1%) is on our side and the opponent has any attacker, switch it rather than clicking a non-KO attack — it bought one Moonblast and then died for free. (d) Keep leading Drogon + Whimsicott vs standard offense: Drought Heat Wave double-chip on T1 is the highest-EV opening we have in this matchup.

proposals.change: NO-OVERKILL MEGA SAFETY: if our Mega is at <=30% HP and the combined KO math shows our PARTNER's action alone already removes every opposing active that can act this turn, block all attacking moves for the Mega slot — it must Protect or switch.
proposals.evidence: T4: Sneasler 5%, Whimsicott 1%. Milotic Scald alone KO'd Sneasler. Drogon at 17% attacked anyway and was KO'd by Whimsicott Moonblast, losing our 394%-damage win condition for zero marginal value.

proposals.change: SUB-10% PIVOT RULE: any of our Pokemon at <=10% HP that is not securing a KO this turn must switch (if a switch exists) rather than attack or Protect.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott sat at 1% on T2, clicked a non-KO Moonblast, and died to Last Resort; a switch would have preserved Tailwind access for the rest of the game (we finished with 0 Tailwind turns).

proposals.change: FALLBACK-PROOF TURN-1 RULES: codify the turn-1 Fake Out Protect rule inside shouldBlockMove so it applies even when the Claude call rate-limits and the engine fallback picks the move.
proposals.evidence: T1 was a 429 fallback; Kangaskhan Fake Out was on the sheet and flinched our Whimsicott. Five consecutive games now contain at least one fallback turn.

lessons: When both opposing actives are in one-shot range of a single partner action, our Mega must not attack — it Protects or switches; overkill is how we lose the win condition.
A Pokemon at <=10% HP that cannot secure a KO should switch out, not click a chip move — it dies for free otherwise.

Drought + Heat Wave double-chip on turn 1 vs standard offense (Whimsicott/Kangaskhan/Baxcalibur style) puts two foes into KO range at once and is our highest-EV opening; keep the Drogon + Whimsicott lead there.
Turn-1 guardrails must live in shouldBlockMove, not only in the prompt, because rate-limit fallbacks bypass the pilot entirely.

itemExperiment.reason: Clear Amulet Kingambit is 1-2 and Kingambit was not even brought this game; Scarf Garchomp (33-44) remains the only loadout with a meaningful sample and gives us the natural speed insurance the playbook demands when we keep ending games with 0 Tailwind turns.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Fake Out + immediate Tailwind' opening: Kangaskhan Fake Out flinched our lead while Whimsicott set Tailwind unopposed. For us, give Drogon a Covert Cloak (blanks Fake Out flinch, Rock Slide flinch, and Dire Claw secondaries on its Mega turn) and swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so a chipped Mega can still convert a turn into damage at +2 priority instead of dying with the attack unused.
teamInspiration.reason: Drogon ended this game at 17% HP and died clicking an unnecessary attack; across the last five games our Megas have repeatedly either lost their turn to Fake Out/flinch or had no safe way to deal damage while chipped. Covert Cloak and a priority finisher address both failure modes directly.

analysis.whatWorked: Drogon + Whimsicott lead into a Trick Room archetype was correct and decisive: Drought instantly removed any weather plan, Heat Wave spread chip burned Farigiraf on T1 (burn did the heavy lifting — it dropped Farigiraf from 40% to 34% and halved its physical threat), and T2 Heat Wave KO'd Mega Heracross through the Encore lock. Whimsicott's Encore onto Heracross after it clicked Protect on T1 was the textbook play from the playbook: Encore a Protect-happy Mega and it loses every subsequent turn (it immediately failed its forced Protect, eating the full Heat Wave). Identifying Heracross-Mega as the single win condition and focusing both actions at it won the game in 2 turns.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) never Tailwind into Trick Room — Whimsicott did NOT click Tailwind on T2 after Farigiraf set TR, it used Encore instead; (2) punish/neutralize a setup or Protect-cycling foe immediately rather than stall; (3) spread Heat Wave to put two foes in range at once (the confirmed highest-EV Drogon opening); (4) Mega evolved on T1 and the win-condition Mega still got full value; (5) focus-fire the single most dangerous foe (Mega Heracross) rather than splitting. Violated/at risk: on T1 Whimsicott's Moonblast was aimed into the slot most likely to Protect (Heracross, a newly Mega'd Protect user) and was fully wasted — half our action economy burned on a predictable Protect, exactly the 'anti-Protect-bait' proposal already on the board.
analysis.whatFailed: Only one real error: T1 Moonblast into Heracross. Heracross had just Mega-evolved on its first turn facing a Drought Charizard-Y — a Protect read there is near-free, and the current ANTI-PROTECT-BAIT proposal (don't point a second action at a foe likely to Protect) says to redirect. Moonblast into Farigiraf instead would have added ~25-30% plus the burn chip, likely putting Farigiraf in Heat Wave KO range on T2 before it could switch to Skeledirge, and would have given the Trick Room setter real pressure rather than a free TR turn. Secondary: our damage-calc model under-read Heat Wave on Farigiraf (predicted 25-35%, actual 60%), meaning our calc assumptions about opposing bulk in this format remain too generous — we are leaving KOs on the table by assuming foes are bulkier than they are. Also, Farigiraf got Trick Room up uncontested; the game ended fast enough that it didn't matter, but had Skeledirge + Pinsir come in under TR that would have been a live problem.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Codify the Protect-bait rule: when an opposing Pokemon is on its FIRST turn out, just Mega-evolved, and has Protect on its sheet, do not aim a second single-target action at it — spread moves still hit it for free, so the partner should instead hit the OTHER slot (especially a Trick Room setter). 2) Treat an un-moved Trick Room setter as the priority chip target for single-target moves when our spread move already covers the other slot. 3) Encore is a win condition against Protect-cyclers and should be scored very highly as soon as a foe's last move was Protect/Detect/Spiky Shield — generalize the existing Encore-on-TR rule to Encore-on-Protect. 4) After the T1 burn lands on a physical TR setter, keep pressure instead of letting it pivot — expect the switch and keep spread damage flowing.
analysis.wholeGame: Clean 2-turn win; the only leak was one wasted Moonblast into an obvious Protect.

proposals.change: PROTECT-BAIT GUARD: never aim a single-target move at an opposing Pokemon that is on its first active turn, has just Mega-evolved, and has Protect/Detect/Spiky Shield known or likely. Redirect that action to the partner slot (prefer an un-moved Trick Room / Tailwind setter). Spread moves are exempt.
proposals.evidence: T1 Whimsicott Moonblast -> Heracross was fully blocked by Protect on Heracross's Mega turn; the same Moonblast into Farigiraf would have stacked with burn and likely enabled a double KO on T2 instead of letting Trick Room go up for free.

proposals.change: GENERALIZE ENCORE: score Encore at maximum priority whenever any opposing active's lastMove was Protect/Detect/Spiky Shield/Baneful Bunker, not just Trick Room. Encoring a Protect converts a dangerous Mega into a free target for the rest of the game.
proposals.evidence: T2 Whimsicott Encore locked Mega Heracross into Protect; the forced Protect failed and Heat Wave KO'd it outright, winning the game on turn 2.

proposals.change: CALC CONFIDENCE: when the engine's predicted damage band has been exceeded in a previous turn against the same foe, widen the KO threshold downward (treat predicted 50-69% as a likely KO on a burned/chipped target) so we do not pass on game-ending spread moves.
proposals.evidence: Heat Wave -> Farigiraf predicted 25-35%, actual 60% — a 2x under-read; across the last 5 games 4 of 15 checked attacks landed above the predicted band.

lessons: Encore is not only a Trick Room answer: Encoring a foe that just clicked Protect locks a Mega out of the entire game — click it the turn after any Protect.

Never aim a single-target move at a foe on its Mega-evolution turn that has Protect on its sheet; send that action into the partner (especially an un-moved Trick Room setter) and let the spread move handle the Protect user.
Heat Wave's burn on a physical Trick Room setter (Farigiraf/Hatterene) is worth as much as the damage — it halves their offense and stacks residual while we Encore-lock their partner.
Our damage model under-reads opposing bulk/power in Reg M-C; when a previous hit exceeded the predicted band on a foe, treat later predicted ranges as optimistic-low and take the KO line.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their Heracross-Mega + Farigiraf shell shows the value of a Protect-first Mega that stalls a turn while the partner sets the field. For us, keep Protect on Drogon but swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed: a +2 finisher ignores Protect timing games, Wide Guard and redirection, and gives a chipped Dragonite a usable turn (five straight games where our Mega had no way to convert). Also consider Covert Cloak on Drogon to blank Fake Out/flinch on its Mega turn.
teamInspiration.reason: We won here because Encore removed their Protect cycling; in the losses our Megas lost their turn to Fake Out/flinch or were walled by Protect timing. A priority finisher plus a flinch-blanking item attacks both recurring failure modes directly.

analysis.whatWorked: Won 4-0 in Pokémon remaining... actually a clean win vs LLCDoubleOG's Trick Room/offense shell. The Whimsicott + Drogon lead was correct: turn-1 Protect on Whimsicott dodged a lethal Dire Claw/Make It Rain and let Drogon Mega-evolve and set Sun. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave one-shot Gholdengo (Dark hits Ghost/Steel for the KO, and Kingambit is immune to nothing relevant but tanks Make It Rain for only 21-33%). Tailwind on turn 2 was correctly set BEFORE any Trick Room appeared and gave us the speed lead for the rest of the game. The closing turn was textbook: Dragonite's sun-boosted Heat Wave hit both sub-10% foes for a double KO while Kingambit Protected through Volcarona Heat Wave — Rage Powder could not redirect the spread move, so the game ended with zero risk.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) Protect the Mega-adjacent frail slot on turn 1 against a known Fake Out/Dire Claw lead — Whimsicott survived by Protecting. (2) Never Tailwind into Trick Room — Farigiraf was on the sheet but never came, and Tailwind went up on a clean board. (3) Focus-fire the biggest immediate threat (Gholdengo) rather than splitting. (4) Protect belongs on the slot in displayed KO range that can still act next turn (Kingambit vs Volcarona Heat Wave 67-100%). (5) Spread move finishes two sub-10% foes — no overkill, no 50/50. Violated/questionable: on turn 1 we left Drogon unprotected into a sheet showing Sneasler Fake Out; the coach note says 'if we are Mega-evolving and the opposing sheet shows Fake Out, the MEGA slot Protects.' We Protected Whimsicott instead and Drogon ate Fake Out + poison + Shadow Ball, falling to 20% and dying on turn 2 having scored zero KOs. Also turn 3 Moonblast was aimed at a freshly switched-in Volcarona for 15% instead of finishing the 2% Sneasler that had already been revealed as a Fake Out user.
analysis.whatFailed: Drogon again contributed 98% damage and zero KOs before dying on turn 2 — the fifth straight game where our Mega Charizard is removed early. Specific chain: T1 Sneasler Fake Out (flinch + Dire Claw poison) plus Gholdengo Shadow Ball put Drogon at 20% before it ever moved; T2 Gholdengo Protected our Heat Wave so the spread only hit Sneasler, and Dire Claw finished Drogon. The Gholdengo Protect was predictable — it was the obvious KO target after a 53-85% Heat Wave the prior turn, and we fired a spread move into it anyway rather than accounting for the 50% damage loss. T4 we chose Moonblast into Volcarona (non-lethal chip) while Sneasler at 2% was free to Fake Out — Whimsicott got flinched and then died to Volcarona Heat Wave. Had we Moonblasted the 2% Sneasler (it was the active slot p1b) we would have removed the Fake Out and kept Whimsicott. The damage model was again optimistic-low: Kowtow Cleave predicted 52-61% on Volcarona and dealt 77%.
analysis.howToImprove: 1. On turn 1 versus any sheet with Fake Out AND a second attacker that threatens our Mega, the MEGA slot takes Protect — the Mega and its weather still resolve, the flinch is denied, and the partner can Tailwind/attack. Drogon at full HP is worth more than one Heat Wave. 2. Never aim a spread move's value calculation at a foe that is the obvious KO target and has Protect shown or likely on its sheet (Gholdengo). Either hit the partner with a single-target move or accept the Heat Wave as chip only. 3. Always finish a sub-5% foe that has a disruption move (Fake Out, Rage Powder, Follow Me, Taunt) before chipping a fresh switch-in — the 2% Sneasler cost us Whimsicott. 4. Treat our predicted damage bands as 15-20% low; when a predicted roll is 50-69% on a chipped/burned target, assume KO.

proposals.change: SUB-5% DISRUPTOR PRIORITY: if any opposing active is at <=10% HP and its known moveset includes Fake Out, Rage Powder, Follow Me, Taunt, Encore or Protect, our fastest action must target that slot. Block chip moves aimed at a freshly switched-in healthy foe while a sub-10% disruptor is alive.
proposals.evidence: T4: we Moonblasted a fresh Volcarona for 15% while 2% Sneasler Fake Out flinched Whimsicott; Whimsicott then died to Volcarona Heat Wave.

proposals.change: MEGA-SLOT TURN-1 PROTECT: on turn 1, if we are Mega-evolving and the opposing lead pair shows Fake Out on any sheet, the Mega slot clicks Protect (weather/Mega still resolve); the partner takes the attacking or Tailwind action.
proposals.evidence: Drogon was Fake Out flinched + poisoned + Shadow Balled to 20% on T1 and died T2 with zero KOs; Whimsicott Protected instead and was never the target.

proposals.change: PROTECT-DISCOUNT ON SPREAD: when scoring a spread move, zero out the damage credited to any opposing active that used Protect/Detect/Spiky Shield in the last 2 turns or is the single most obvious KO target at <=50% HP; choose the action by the remaining credited damage only.
proposals.evidence: T2 Heat Wave was chosen on predicted 102-168% on Gholdengo; Gholdengo Protected and the real output was one Sneasler hit while Drogon died.

lessons: On turn 1, when the opposing lead shows Fake Out and a second attacker, the MEGA slot Protects — not the support slot; the Mega's weather and Mega-evolution still resolve and the flinch is denied.
A foe at <=10% HP that still has Fake Out / Rage Powder / Follow Me must be KO'd before any chip damage is spent on a healthy switch-in.
When scoring a spread move, credit zero damage to a foe that Protected recently or is the obvious focus-fire target — Gholdengo Protect halved our Heat Wave and cost us Drogon.
Rage Powder does not redirect spread moves (Heat Wave) — a spread finisher is the safe closing action against a redirector.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep the current loadout one more game; the loss pattern is Mega survivability and turn-1 Fake Out, not Garchomp's item. Scarf Garchomp's speed was never the failure point this game.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Give Drogon a Covert Cloak in place of its current item slot consideration is impossible (Charizardite Y is mandatory) — instead swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed and bring Dragonite as the primary Mega against any sheet with two Fake Out users. Alternatively, lead Kingambit (Fake Out-resistant bulk, Defiant) alongside Whimsicott and bring Drogon in on turn 3 after the Fake Out is spent.
teamInspiration.reason: Their whole opening was Sneasler Fake Out + Gholdengo Shadow Ball to delete our Mega before it acted — the same pattern that has killed Drogon in five straight games. We cannot run Covert Cloak on a Mega Stone holder, so the fix is either a priority finisher on Dragonite or delaying Drogon's entry past the Fake Out turn.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 Whimsicott Protect blanked the Fake Out + Hyper Voice double-up on the support slot, and Tailwind went up safely on turn 2. Scarf Garchomp was the MVP: Stomping Tantrum removed Primarina and then one-shot Mega Blaziken the turn it evolved, denying their sweeper win condition. Milotic absorbed Hyper Voice and traded fine until Last Respects scaled.
analysis.lessonsApplied: We did follow 'Protect the slot in KO range' on T2 (Drogon) and 'switch rather than die' on T3 (Whimsicott out for Milotic). We correctly refused to Earthquake next to Milotic (used Stomping Tantrum instead). We correctly prioritized the Mega Blaziken KO over chipping Basculegion. However the coach rule 'on turn 1, if the opposing sheet shows Fake Out and we are Mega-evolving, the MEGA slot Protects' was VIOLATED — Whimsicott Protected while Drogon ate Fake Out + Hyper Voice for 69% and was dead by turn 3 having dealt 58% total. Also the known lesson 'Basculegion Last Respects scales with faints — remove it early' was ignored: we never once targeted Basculegion with a real attack until turn 6.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Lead/protect assignment: Drogon was the OHKO target (Primarina Hyper Voice displayed 69-129%) yet Whimsicott got the Protect. Drogon lost its Mega turn to Fake Out, then took Hyper Voice, and contributed almost nothing before fainting — the win condition died by turn 3 for the fifth game running. 2) Bringing Drogon into a sheet with Primarina (Hyper Voice spread special) and Incineroar (Fake Out + Intimidate) at all — the whole lead was into their best pair. 3) Last Respects management: once Primarina fainted on T4 Basculegion's Last Respects got stronger with every one of our deaths; we let it KO Milotic, Garchomp and Whimsicott unanswered. The T4 action (Milotic Ice Beam into Basculegion for 12%) was pure waste — Milotic should have Protected or Scald-burned it, or we should have doubled Basculegion. 4) T5 double-targeted Mega Blaziken on its Detect turn (Protect-bait guard violated: fresh-in Mega with Detect on sheet) — both actions whiffed and Milotic died for free. 5) Endgame 1v2 with Whimsicott at 55% clicking Moonblast into a Fake Out Incineroar — dead action.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: the Protect goes on the Mega/slot with the highest displayed incoming damage, period — a support mon at 100% HP never takes the Protect over a Mega in 69-129% range. Against sheets with Primarina/Hyper Voice + Incineroar Fake Out, lead Milotic (Competitive +2 off Intimidate, resists Hyper Voice) + Whimsicott and hold Drogon for turn 3. Treat Basculegion like a boosting sweeper: the turn their first mon faints, every action targets Basculegion until it is dead. Never aim both actions at an opposing Mega on its first active turn when Detect/Protect is on the sheet — split one action onto the partner.

proposals.change: PROTECT-GOES-TO-THE-BIGGEST-THREATENED-SLOT: when both our actives have a Protect-capable move, Protect must be assigned to the slot with the highest displayed incoming damage percentage. Block Protect on a slot whose displayed incoming max is below 60% while the ally's displayed incoming max is 90%+.
proposals.evidence: T1 Whimsicott (threatened 90-166%) Protected but Drogon (threatened 69-129% + Fake Out) did not; Drogon lost its Mega turn and died on T3 having dealt 58% total damage.

proposals.change: LAST RESPECTS / SUPREME OVERLORD ESCALATION: once any Pokemon on the board has fainted, treat Basculegion/Kingambit as the single highest-priority target — forbid chip moves (<20% predicted) aimed at it and require at least one action per turn to target it until it is KO'd.
proposals.evidence: Milotic Ice Beam did 12% to Basculegion on T4; Basculegion then KO'd Milotic, Garchomp and Whimsicott with escalating Last Respects for the loss.

proposals.change: Do not lead Drogon into any sheet containing Primarina or another Hyper Voice/spread-special user alongside Incineroar Fake Out. Lead Milotic + Whimsicott; Drogon enters turn 3+ after the Fake Out is spent.
proposals.evidence: Drogon took Fake Out flinch + Hyper Voice on T1 and was at 31% before acting usefully; it dealt 58% all game.

proposals.change: Swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed to give the core a +2 finisher that ignores Detect timing, Protect cycling, and faster priority sweepers like Basculegion's Aqua Jet.
proposals.evidence: Six straight games where our Mega either lost its turn to Fake Out or had no way to convert while chipped; T5 both actions whiffed into Mega Blaziken's Detect.

lessons: The Protect belongs to the slot with the largest displayed incoming damage — never to a healthy support mon while the Mega is in displayed OHKO range.
Basculegion is a scaling sweeper, not a normal attacker: from the moment the first Pokemon on either side faints, every turn must land real damage on it or it wins the endgame.
Never aim both actions at an opposing Mega on its first active turn when Detect/Protect appears on its sheet — split one action to the partner slot.
Against Incineroar Fake Out + Primarina Hyper Voice leads, Drogon stays in the back; lead Milotic (Competitive) + Whimsicott instead.
