itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp was the only piece that performed: it outsped and removed Primarina and one-shot Mega Blaziken on its evolution turn. Keep the variant while we fix lead/Protect assignment issues.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Fake Out + spread special + faint-scaling cleaner' shape: run Mega Dragonite with Extreme Speed over Heat Wave as a +2 unblockable finisher, and consider Milotic as the default lead partner for Whimsicott against Incineroar/Primarina sheets so Drogon never eats the Fake Out turn.
teamInspiration.reason: Incineroar Fake Out into Primarina Hyper Voice deleted 69% of Drogon before it moved, and Basculegion's Last Respects closed three KOs through our Protects — a priority finisher plus delaying our Mega's entry attacks both failure modes directly.

whatWorked: Turn 1 focus-fire on Toucannon (the faster attacker) with Dragon Claw + Mega Dragon Pulse secured an immediate KO before it could act, which was the correct application of 'remove the faster threat first'. Kingambit under Trick Room moved first every turn and Kowtow Cleave + Moonblast cleanly removed Conkeldurr on T4. Damage-calc accuracy was perfect (5/5 inside predicted range), so the engine model was not the problem here.
lessonsApplied: The 'never Tailwind into Trick Room' rule was correctly honored (Whimsicott never clicked Tailwind after TR went up). Kingambit was correctly valued as the Trick Room abuser and was brought in to move first. However, the core Trick Room directive — 'focus fire the setter BEFORE it goes up' — was violated: we knew Reuniclus was the only slow Psychic on the board and spent turn 1 on Toucannon, giving Reuniclus a completely free Trick Room. We also violated 'switch a Pokemon out when it is about to be KO'd' on turn 3: both Garchomp (29/185, 16%) and Dragonite (31/168, 18%) were in displayed OHKO range from Conkeldurr/Reuniclus and both attacked anyway, losing two Pokemon in a single turn.
whatFailed: 1) LEAD/PLAN ERROR: Mega Dragonite + Garchomp lead into a sheet containing Reuniclus, Conkeldurr and Drampa (an obvious Trick Room shell) — our two FASTEST Pokemon were led into the one team archetype that punishes speed, and the plan 'Dragonite|zg' is 0-1 all-time. The preview call was a rate-limit fallback (HTTP 429), so no human-level preview reasoning happened at all. 2) TURN 1 TARGETING: Toucannon was already going to be outsped and KO'd later; Reuniclus was the win condition. Both actions should have gone into Reuniclus to deny Trick Room entirely — we had 65-118% combined into it. Instead Reuniclus got TR up for free and the whole game inverted. 3) TURN 3 DOUBLE-DEATH: with Garchomp at 16% and Dragonite at 18% under enemy Trick Room, both of which were in 100%-displayed-KO range from Conkeldurr Ice Punch, we clicked two attacks and lost both. One of them had to Protect or switch (Dragonite had Protect available; Garchomp was Choice-locked but could have switched). That single turn turned a 4-3 into a 2-3. 4) ENDGAME: Kingambit was left alone at 14% vs a +1/+1 Quaquaval with no outs — the 50/50 Sucker Punch was correct only because the game was already lost.
howToImprove: Treat any sheet containing Reuniclus/Conkeldurr/Drampa/Hatterene/Indeedee as trickroom BEFORE the engine labels it, and never lead our two fastest Pokemon (Scarf Garchomp + Mega Dragonite) into it. Correct lead is Whimsicott (Encore the TR setter the turn after it goes up) + Charizard-Y or Kingambit. On the turn a Trick Room setter is on the field and TR is NOT yet up, both actions must target the setter if combined damage can plausibly KO — denying TR is worth more than any other KO on the board. Under enemy Trick Room, any of our Pokemon below ~25% HP facing a displayed 90%+ incoming hit must Protect or switch, never attack; we should never lose two Pokemon in one turn to that. Finally, rate-limit fallbacks on the preview call must not be allowed to produce an anti-archetype lead — the fallback lead for an unknown/Trick Room board should default to Whimsicott + Charizard.

proposals.change: TRICK ROOM SETTER DENIAL: while an opposing Trick-Room-capable Pokemon (Reuniclus, Hatterene, Farigiraf, Porygon2, Dusclops, Indeedee, Bronzong, Oranguru, Cresselia, Mimikyu, Drampa, Sinistcha, Armarouge) is on the field and Trick Room is NOT yet active, both of our actions must target that slot if combined predicted damage reaches 85%+; block attacks aimed at the partner slot in that case.
proposals.evidence: T1 we double-targeted Toucannon for a KO while Reuniclus set Trick Room completely unopposed; combined Dragon Claw + Dragon Pulse into Reuniclus was 65-118% and would have denied the entire opposing game plan.

proposals.change: LOW-HP UNDER-TR SURVIVAL RULE: under opposing Trick Room, any of our actives at <=30% HP facing a displayed incoming max >=90% must Protect (if available) or switch; block pure attack choices from that slot unless the attack is a guaranteed KO on the threatening foe.
proposals.evidence: T3 Garchomp (16%) and Dragonite (18%) both attacked into displayed 'Conkeldurr Ice Punch 73-134% KO' and both fainted on the same turn, converting a 4-3 lead into a 2-3 deficit.

proposals.change: Never lead Scarf Garchomp + Mega Dragonite (our two fastest) into any sheet with two or more of {Reuniclus, Conkeldurr, Drampa, Hatterene, Indeedee, Porygon2, Dusclops, Farigiraf, Sinistcha, Torkoal, Ursaluna}. Default to Whimsicott (Encore) + Charizard-Y, with Kingambit in the back as the Trick Room abuser.
proposals.evidence: 'Dragonite|zg' preview plan is 0-1 and this game's loss was decided by leading our two fastest Pokemon into a Reuniclus Trick Room shell while the preview call fell back from rate limiting.

proposals.change: Keep the proposed Extreme Speed over Heat Wave on Mega Dragonite but note it is ALSO a Trick Room liability (priority is reversed-neutral, still moves at +2) — it would have let a 18% Dragonite finish a 12% Reuniclus on T3 instead of dying with a spread move unused.
proposals.evidence: T3 Dragonite clicked Heat Wave for 19-35% on a 12% Reuniclus and died before Reuniclus; +2 priority Extreme Speed would have taken that KO first.

lessons: If an opposing Trick Room setter is on the field and Trick Room is not yet up, denying Trick Room outranks any other KO on the board — send both actions into the setter.
Never lead our two fastest Pokemon (Scarf Garchomp + Mega Dragonite) into a Trick Room sheet; lead Whimsicott (Encore) + Charizard and keep Kingambit in the back.
Under enemy Trick Room, a Pokemon at <=30% HP facing a displayed 90%+ incoming hit must Protect or switch — never click an attack and lose two Pokemon in one turn.
A preview rate-limit fallback must never produce an anti-archetype lead; the safe default lead is Whimsicott + Charizard-Y.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'slow bulky setter + two slow heavy hitters' redundancy: they had Reuniclus set TR and still won after it died because Conkeldurr and Quaquaval both snowballed. For us, swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (a +2 finisher that works in and out of Trick Room and converts chipped Megas into KOs), and consider Milotic's Recover-based longevity as the preferred Trick Room partner for Kingambit instead of Garchomp.
teamInspiration.reason: Our two fastest mons were dead weight once Trick Room went up and died with attacks unused; a priority finisher and a bulky TR-neutral pivot would have kept us in the game after the setter resolved.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice Scarf Garchomp is actively harmful under Trick Room (moves last AND is locked into one move, so it cannot Protect or pivot). Sitrus Berry restores Garchomp's ability to Protect/switch on the turn it is in KO range, which is exactly the turn we lost here.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 was a textbook anti-Psychic-Terrain opening: Kingambit (Psychic-immune, Defiant) + Mega Charizard-Y lead against an Indeedee sheet. Heat Wave finished Indeedee through its switch-in and simultaneously chipped the incoming Garchomp, while Kowtow Cleave cleaned the Garchomp — a double KO on turn 1 that denied Psychic Terrain, Expanding Force and Trick Room in one action pair. Mystical Fire into Defiant gave Kingambit +2 Atk, which is exactly why Kingambit is the designated Psychic-Terrain lead.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: Kingambit leads into Psychic Terrain sheets (immune to Expanding Force, blocks Prankster-irrelevance), focus the terrain/TR setter first, and never Sucker Punch under Psychic Terrain (Kowtow Cleave was used instead). Violated: the standing rule 'never aim a single-target action at a slot that has Protect on its sheet on the turn it is the obvious focus-fire target' — on T2 both of our actions were spent into a Gholdengo whose Protect had already been revealed in a prior scouting game and which was the single obvious target; both actions were blanked. Also violated the 'Kingambit at <=10% should switch, not Protect twice' discipline: Kingambit Protected on T2 and then was forced into a switch on T3 anyway, wasting the slot two turns running.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 2: Drogon clicked Weather Ball into Gholdengo, the only foe on the board that had a reason to Protect (it had just switched in next to a fresh Arcanine-H and was in displayed OHKO range). Gholdengo Protected, Drogon's action was wasted, and with Kingambit also Protecting we spent an entire 2-action turn for zero. Turn 3 repeated the exact same move into the same Gholdengo. The real error is macro: with Arcanine-Hisui on the field, Head Smash was displayed as a 235-384% OHKO on Drogon — our win condition was standing in front of a guaranteed OHKO while we aimed at the slot behind it. Drogon should have either Protected on T2 (with Kingambit switching) or attacked Arcanine-H, the piece that actually threatens us. Spending two turns ignoring the only foe that can KO our Mega is how a 4-2 lead becomes a loss. (The game is logged as a win by score/forfeit but the board state going into T3 was deteriorating fast.)
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Never send an action into a foe that has a revealed/sheet Protect on the turn it is the single obvious focus-fire target — split the action onto the partner slot. 2) When a foe on the field has a displayed OHKO (>=100%) on our Mega, the Mega's action must be Protect, a switch, or an attack aimed at THAT foe — never a chip/KO attempt on the other slot. 3) After the opponent Protects with a slot, the next turn must target the OTHER slot (anti-double-blank rule). 4) A Pokemon at <=10% HP that already Protected last turn must switch, not Protect again.

proposals.change: ANTI-BLANK RULE: block any single-target move aimed at a foe that (a) used Protect/Detect on the immediately preceding turn, or (b) has Protect on its sheet AND is the only foe in displayed KO range this turn while a partner slot exists. Redirect the action to the partner slot or use a spread move.
proposals.evidence: T2 and T3 both spent Drogon's Weather Ball on Gholdengo; Gholdengo Protected on T2 and the same move was re-selected on T3, blanking 2 of 4 actions over two turns.

proposals.change: MEGA-UNDER-OHKO RULE: if any live foe's displayed max damage on our Mega is >=100%, the Mega may only Protect, switch, or attack that specific foe. Block attacks from the Mega aimed at any other slot.
proposals.evidence: Arcanine-Hisui Head Smash displayed 235-384% OHKO on Drogon for two consecutive turns while Drogon attacked Gholdengo instead.

proposals.change: NO-REPEAT-PROTECT-AT-LOW-HP: a Pokemon at <=15% HP that used Protect last turn must switch (if a switch exists) rather than Protect or attack.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit at 9% Protected T2 then had to switch T3 anyway, losing two turns of action economy.

lessons: Never aim an action at the one foe everybody expects to be focused when that foe has Protect — send it to the partner slot or use a spread move.
If a foe on the field displays a 100%+ hit on our Mega, the Mega's only legal actions are Protect, switch, or attacking that foe.
After an opposing slot Protects, the following turn must target the other slot.
Kingambit leading into Psychic Terrain/Indeedee sheets is confirmed correct: Psychic immunity + Defiant turns Mystical Fire into +2 Attack and Kowtow Cleave removes the setter's partner.

For us, swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed so a chipped Mega has a +2 action that still converts when the obvious target Protects, and consider bringing Milotic over Whimsicott into Arcanine-H/Gholdengo sheets (Scald + Recover answers Flare Blitz and Head Smash recoil).

whatWorked: Very little. The only correct decisions were Whimsicott Protecting on T1 and T3 (Primarina Hyper Voice/Dazzling Gleam were in KO range) and Garchomp using Stomping Tantrum instead of Earthquake to avoid hitting the ally. Drogon did Mega-evolve on turn 1 and set Sun, which halved Primarina's Water damage.
lessonsApplied: Mostly violated. (1) The preview plan was correct per our own simulation data (Mega Charizard + Whimsicott Tailwind vs sand = 70.7%), but the first two turns were rate-limit FALLBACKS to the engine, which immediately threw the game: the engine clicked Ancient Power into a Volcarona that Protected (a wasted Mega action on turn 1), and on T2 clicked Encore into Tyranitar — a Dark type, which is explicitly in our rules as immune to Prankster — plus Ancient Power into Tyranitar for 17% instead of Protecting Drogon who was in displayed KO range from Hyper Voice. (2) Our own rule 'Protect Drogon vs Tyranitar/strong special attackers' was ignored by the fallback and Drogon died on T2 with 0 KOs. (3) Tailwind was never set in a sand matchup where the entire plan is built around Tailwind. (4) On T5 Milotic clicked an 8-13% Scald into a 23% Primarina while Rillaboom (displayed 139-183% OHKO on us) was the only Pokemon that mattered — a pure wasted action in a lost 1v2.
whatFailed: 1) RATE-LIMIT FALLBACKS LOST THE GAME. Turns 1 and 2 were both engine fallbacks. T1: Ancient Power into a Protecting Volcarona (0 damage) when Heat Wave would have spread-chipped both foes and burned. T2: Encore into Tyranitar — a hard-coded illegal play (Dark is Prankster-immune) that our prompt lists but the engine does not enforce — and Drogon attacking instead of Protecting while displayed in KO range. That is three wasted actions out of four across two turns, and Drogon died on T2 having dealt 17% total. 2) NO TAILWIND. The entire sand game plan is 'Tailwind then burst'; Whimsicott spent the game Protecting and Encoring into immunity and never clicked it. 3) We never identified the real win condition on their side: Primarina was the carry (killed Drogon, killed Whimsicott, dealt ~250% across the game), not Tyranitar. We spent our Drogon turns chipping Tyranitar for 17% and let Primarina free-fire Hyper Voice three times. 4) T4: splitting Moonblast + Stomping Tantrum into a 65% Primarina when Rillaboom's Grassy Glide was going to KO Garchomp first (priority under Grassy Terrain) was a misordered focus-fire; Primarina survived at 23% and still got the Whimsicott KO. 5) 0 KOs the entire game — we were swept 4-0.
howToImprove: 1) Harden the fallback path: Prankster-move-into-Dark and attacking-into-a-foe-that-Protected-last-turn must be blocked in shouldBlockMove so the engine fallback cannot make them. 2) Add a hard rule that Drogon must Protect or switch when a live foe's displayed damage reaches KO range and we are not removing that foe this turn — this is the single most repeated loss pattern (Drogon first-faint in 4 of the last 5 games). 3) Whimsicott must click Tailwind by turn 2 at the latest in any non-Trick-Room matchup; it is the team's only speed control and we won 0 Tailwind turns. 4) Identify the CARRY not the weather setter: vs sand, Primarina/Rillaboom spread damage killed us, not Tyranitar. Focus fire the spread special attacker first. 5) Under Grassy Terrain, treat Rillaboom's Grassy Glide as +1 priority in KO-threat evaluation — Garchomp died before it could fire.

proposals.change: PRANKSTER-INTO-DARK HARD BLOCK: block any Prankster-boosted status move from Whimsicott (Encore, Tailwind is side-targeting so exempt, Moonblast is an attack) aimed at a Dark-type foe. Encore/Taunt/status into Dark must return true from shouldBlockMove so engine fallbacks cannot waste the action.

proposals.evidence: Drogon spent both its turns on Tyranitar for 17% total while Primarina dealt 250%+ and killed three of ours.

proposals.change: Consider Milotic over Whimsicott into sheets with Primarina + Rillaboom + Tyranitar: Milotic's Competitive and bulk answer the Hyper Voice/Moonblast spam that Whimsicott folds to, and Whimsicott's Prankster is dead vs Tyranitar.

lessons: Prankster status moves (Encore/Taunt/Thunder Wave) FAIL against Dark types — never click Encore at Tyranitar, Kingambit, Incineroar or Scrafty.
Rate-limit engine fallbacks are a real loss source: every rule we rely on (Protect Drogon, no Prankster into Dark, no attack into a fresh Protect) must live in shouldBlockMove, not just the prompt.
Vs sand, the killer is usually the spread special attacker (Primarina Hyper Voice / Dazzling Gleam), not Tyranitar — focus the carry, not the weather setter.
Under Grassy Terrain, Rillaboom's Grassy Glide is +1 priority: any of our Pokemon in Glide KO range will die before it acts, so splitting damage into a different target is a wasted turn.
If Whimsicott is alive and Trick Room is not threatened, Tailwind must be clicked by turn 2 — the team has no other speed control.

analysis.whatWorked: Focus-firing Pelipper on turn 2 with Kowtow Cleave + Moonblast removed the Drizzle enabler and was the only clean piece of play in the game. analysis.lessonsApplied: Rain plan (Mega Charizard to override Drizzle) was correct on paper, and the pilot did KO the weather setter early. However the critical turn-1 decision was a wolfe-fallback (HTTP 429 rate limit) that sent Drogon into Archaludon with an attack instead of Protect — exactly the 'Protect Drogon turn 1 against a strong special attacker' rule, and exactly the documented failure mode that fallbacks produce anti-rules leads. Tailwind was also set on turn 3 into an already-active enemy Tailwind and with Whimsicott in a guaranteed-OHKO window, wasting the move entirely.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 1 fallback: Drogon attacked Archaludon (predicted 86-139%, actual 27% — Archaludon's bulk + Stamina Def boost) and was immediately OHKO'd by Electro Shot, which charges instantly in rain. Our Mega died on turn 1 for the sixth time in recent games. 2) Weather Ball into Archaludon was the wrong target/move entirely: the sun had already been reverted to rain by Pelipper's switch-in, so Weather Ball was a 50 BP Normal move, not a 100 BP Fire move — a catastrophic technical error. 3) Turn 3: Whimsicott clicked Tailwind while facing a displayed 159-307% Flash Cannon; it died with Tailwind having zero value (we were already down our Mega and the opponent had Tailwind too). It should have Protected or we should have accepted the loss of tempo. 4) Turn 4 Garchomp Stomping Tantrum into a Dragonite switch-in was a Ground move into a Flying type — total immunity, a wasted action. 5) Archaludon snowballed exactly as the knowledge base warns: Stamina +Def on every contact hit, Electro Shot +SpA, never burst down in one turn.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block Weather Ball when our side's Drought has been overridden by opposing rain and the move would be Normal-type. Hard-block Ground moves aimed at Flying/Levitate targets. Force Drogon to Protect on turn 1 whenever a foe with a displayed >=90% hit is on the field (Archaludon, Inteleon, Primarina). Never set Tailwind when opposing Tailwind is already active AND our setter faces a displayed OHKO — Protect instead. Against Archaludon specifically: it must be burst in ONE turn with both actions or ignored; chip damage feeds Stamina. And the rate-limit fallback path must itself contain the Protect-Drogon rule.

proposals.change: WEATHER BALL TYPE CHECK: block Weather Ball from Charizard when battle.field.weather is rain/sand/snow (i.e. our Drought was overridden) — it becomes a 50 BP Normal/Water/Rock/Ice move; use Heat Wave or Ancient Power instead, or re-establish sun by switching.

Never click a Ground move at a Flying-type or Levitate foe; check the switch-in's type before committing Earthquake/Stomping Tantrum.
Archaludon in rain fires Electro Shot the same turn (no charge) and gains Stamina Def on every contact hit — it must be burst with both actions in one turn or left alone entirely.
Tailwind has zero value when the opponent already has Tailwind and our setter is in a displayed OHKO window — Protect the Focus Sash body instead.

analysis.whatWorked: Lead Whimsicott + Mega Charizard-Y into a standard sheet was correct: turn 1 Moonblast broke Noivern's Sash and the Heat Wave chip finished the Tailwind setter before it could do anything else, removing their speed control on turn 1. The NO-ATTACK-INTO-FRESH-PROTECT proposal was VIOLATED on turn 3: Gholdengo Protected on turn 2 and we still aimed Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave at it on turn 3, and it Protected again — a fully wasted action from our strongest attacker, which then died to Pawmot Close Combat having done nothing. analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 3 Kingambit Kowtow Cleave into Gholdengo, which had Protected the previous turn — it Protected again, so Kingambit contributed zero damage all game and died. The right target was Pawmot (the foe that actually threatened the OHKO on Kingambit), or Sucker Punch, which beats the Protect timing when Pawmot clicks Close Combat. 2) Turn 2 we left Drogon exposed to Mega Glalie: Glalie had already Protected on turn 1 (a classic Explosion-setup Protect) and we put both of our bodies next to it without Protecting Drogon — Explosion killed our Mega and left Whimsicott at 1 HP. A Mega Glalie that Protects turn 1 is a telegraphed Explosion; Drogon should have Protected or we should have KO'd Glalie with a single-target move while Whimsicott Protected. 3) We ended the game with only Garchomp alive at 36%; four of our pieces died, which is far closer than a 4-turn win should be.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-code the fresh-Protect rule: never aim a single-target attack at a foe that used Protect/Detect on the immediately previous turn when a different foe exists. Add a Mega Glalie / Explosion-user rule: if a foe with Explosion/Self-Destruct (Glalie-Mega, Electrode, Gengar with Destiny Bond) Protected last turn or is at low HP, the slot it can kill must Protect. Against a Pawmot/fast Fighting attacker, Kingambit's Sucker Punch outplays the Protect/attack mixup. Keep leading Whimsicott + Drogon into standard sheets — that plan is 18-14 and remains our best standard line.

proposals.change: EXPLOSION GUARD: if any opposing active Pokemon has Explosion/Self-Destruct/Misty Explosion on its sheet and is either below 50% HP or Protected on the previous turn, the ally slot that would be OHKO'd by it must Protect or switch; never leave both of our bodies adjacent with no Protect.

Mega Glalie / any Explosion user that Protects turn 1 is telegraphing Explosion: Protect the Pokemon it would KO on the following turn.
Tailwind clicked on turn 2 won this game: Whimsicott at 1 HP still outsped and KO'd Pawmot. Keep the turn-2 Tailwind rule.

analysis.whatWorked: Win vs xtero in 3 turns. Turn-1 Whimsicott Tailwind + Mega Charizard Heat Wave was the correct standard-archetype lead and immediately established speed control that held the whole game. Turn-3 focus-fire on the freshly Mega-Evolved Salamence (Moonblast + Ancient Power) removed their win condition before it could fire Draco Meteor/Hyper Voice — a textbook 'deny speed AND power' play, and Ancient Power (single-target) was correctly chosen over Heat Wave because Toxapex had already shown Wide Guard twice.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed the turn-2 Tailwind rule (set turn 1). Followed 'after Wide Guard, don't spread into it' — after Toxapex blanked Heat Wave on T2, T3 used single-target Ancient Power and Moonblast instead of another spread move. Followed 'focus the carry, not the support' by killing Mega Salamence rather than chipping Toxapex. Did not Protect-stall, did not click Prankster into a Dark type, did not Earthquake next to an ally.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 2 was a wasted half-action in the 2-action economy: Heat Wave was fired into Toxapex's Wide Guard (Wide Guard was already a known Toxapex staple and the engine had no guard against first-use). Rillaboom survived at 31% and U-turned out for free. Drogon was also left trapped by Infestation all game (19 HP/turn chip plus the Fake Out flinch), losing ~60% of our Mega's HP without a switch option — we never considered that Infestation locks the Mega into the slot. Whimsicott also ate a free U-turn because we committed Moonblast into a target that a spread move was already going to kill.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Treat Wide Guard as a live threat the moment a Toxapex/Mandibuzz/Aegislash/Kommo-o/Gastrodon-style bulky support is on the field: when a foe with Wide Guard on its sheet is active and healthy, prefer single-target moves unless the spread KOs BOTH slots. 2) When our Mega is partially trapped (Infestation/Whirlpool/Bind), account for the fact it cannot pivot and that a Protect turn is more valuable than a chip turn. 3) Don't duplicate damage: if Heat Wave already KOs Rillaboom, send Whimsicott's action at the other slot or at Tailwind/Encore utility.

proposals.change: WIDE GUARD GUARD: if any active foe has wideguard on its revealed sheet (or is Toxapex/Aegislash/Kommo-o/Mandibuzz/Kingambit-style known WG user) and is at >0 HP, apply a heavy penalty to our spread moves (Heat Wave, Dazzling Gleam, Rock Slide, Earthquake) unless the spread move KOs both foes; hard-block the spread move if that foe used Wide Guard on any previous turn.
proposals.evidence: T2 vs xtero: Toxapex used Wide Guard and blanked Drogon's Heat Wave entirely, leaving Rillaboom alive at 31% to U-turn out for free — a full wasted Mega action.

proposals.change: TRAPPED-MEGA RULE: when our Pokemon has the partiallytrapped volatile (Infestation/Whirlpool/Bind/Sand Tomb), mark it as unable to switch in the prompt and raise the value of Protect on that slot (it is taking guaranteed residual chip and cannot pivot out of an incoming KO).
proposals.evidence: Drogon lost 92 of 153 HP across 3 turns to Fake Out + Infestation residual with no switch option available.

proposals.change: NO-DUPLICATE-DAMAGE RULE: penalize aiming a second action at a target our first action already KOs with >=95% probability; redirect to the other slot or a utility move.
proposals.evidence: T2 Whimsicott Moonblast went into Rillaboom which Heat Wave was projected to OHKO (111-131%); the spread was blocked, but the principle cost us a free action on the Toxapex slot.

lessons: Wide Guard blanks ALL spread moves (Heat Wave, Dazzling Gleam, Rock Slide, Muddy Water) — once a bulky support like Toxapex is on the field, assume Wide Guard and use single-target damage unless the spread KOs both slots.
Partial-trapping moves (Infestation/Whirlpool) remove our switch option entirely: a trapped Mega must either Protect or kill, it cannot reposition.
Killing the opposing Mega on its first active turn with two single-target actions is correct when Wide Guard is on the board — Ancient Power into Mega Salamence closed this game.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Wide Guard + trapping chip' support shell: Toxapex blanked our Mega's entire offense for two turns with Wide Guard and Infestation while costing them nothing. Our analogue is Milotic — but Milotic has no spread-denial. Consider swapping Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant with Charizard's Heat Wave and blanked by Wide Guard) for Extreme Speed: a +2 single-target finisher that ignores Wide Guard, Protect timing, Grassy Glide and Trick Room, and converts our chipped Mega into KOs on Sash/1-HP foes.
teamInspiration.reason: Our two recurring wasted-action patterns are spread moves into Wide Guard and slow attackers unable to finish chipped foes; a priority single-target move on Dragonite solves both, and Heat Wave on Dragonite overlaps entirely with Charizard-Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead into the Psychic Terrain / Indeedee-F Trick Room sheet was exactly right: Defiant converted Salamence's Intimidate into +2 Atk, Psychic immunity made Expanding Force dead, and Kowtow Cleave OHKO'd Indeedee-F on turn 1, deleting both the Trick Room setter and the terrain before it could matter. Drogon Mega-evolved turn 1 and Ancient Power into Salamence (pre-Mega, 4x-relevant Rock) rolled high (93%), setting up a turn-2 Weather Ball KO on Mega Salamence. Sun-boosted Heat Wave then double-KO'd Torkoal and Sylveon for the win in 4 turns. Overall: win-condition denial (TR setter) first, then focus-fire the opposing Mega, then spread cleanup.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: 'Kingambit leads into Psychic Terrain/Indeedee sheets' (confirmed again), 'denying Trick Room outranks any other KO' (both turn-1 actions pressured the TR pair), 'Charizard-Y Mega sheltered in the back' at preview, 'no Tailwind into a Trick Room sheet' (Whimsicott was correctly kept off the lead), and 'no overkill with stat-drop moves'. Violated/at-risk: turn 2 we did NOT account for Mega Salamence (Speed 150+ after Mega) moving before Kingambit — Kingambit at 146/207 was in Flamethrower KO range (71% displayed... actually full KO) and had Protect available; we clicked Iron Head into Sylveon and lost Kingambit for free. One turn was again a rate-limit fallback (T3), which is a recurring structural risk.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 2 Kingambit died to Salamence-Mega Flamethrower. The displayed threat list only showed 'Sylveon Hyper Voice (32-48%)' for Kingambit — the engine failed to list Mega Salamence Flamethrower (4x into Kingambit's Steel/Dark? no — Fire is 2x on Steel, and Kingambit was already at 70%) as a KO threat. Kingambit had Protect; Drogon alone OHKO'd Salamence with Weather Ball anyway, so Protect was the free, strictly-better action. That is a real -1 Pokemon from an avoidable action-economy loss. 2) Turn 3 was a rate-limit fallback again (1 of 5 calls); the fallback happened to be fine, but this path has previously lost Megas. 3) Ancient Power damage prediction was badly off (predicted 30-56%, actual 93%) — our Salamence bulk model is wrong, which could just as easily under-predict an incoming hit.
analysis.howToImprove: Add an explicit 'residual Fire/Fighting threat on Kingambit' check: Kingambit below ~80% HP facing any active foe with a Fire or Fighting attacking move that moves before it must Protect or switch unless our other slot's action alone wins the turn — and in this game Drogon's Weather Ball alone DID win the turn, so Protect cost nothing. More generally: when one of our two actions already secures the only KO that matters this turn, the second slot should default to Protect/reposition rather than a second KO that doesn't change the board. Also: when a foe Mega-evolves, recompute its Speed and its coverage before assuming our move order; treat 'threat list omitted a foe' as unknown-dangerous, not safe.

proposals.change: FREE-PROTECT RULE: if one of our two slots already has a >=90% KO on the only foe that threatens us this turn, and the other slot is at <=85% HP with Protect available and faces any foe move that is super-effective on it, that second slot must Protect instead of attacking a non-threatening target.
proposals.evidence: T2: Drogon Weather Ball alone KO'd Mega Salamence (the only real threat). Kingambit instead clicked Iron Head into Sylveon and was KO'd by Salamence Flamethrower before moving — a free Protect would have kept a 4th Pokemon alive.

proposals.change: MEGA-RECOMPUTE RULE: when an opposing Pokemon Mega-evolves, flag it in the prompt as 'speed/coverage unknown — assume it moves first and has STAB + 2 coverage types' until proven otherwise; never rely on a threat list that omits it.
proposals.evidence: T2 threat line for Kingambit listed only Sylveon Hyper Voice; Salamence-Mega Flamethrower (which actually OHKO'd Kingambit from 70%) was absent from the displayed threats.

proposals.change: KINGAMBIT FIRE/FIGHTING GUARD: block Kingambit non-Protect actions when it is <=80% HP and an active foe has a revealed Fire or Fighting move and outspeeds it (no Trick Room), unless that action KOs that specific foe.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit at 146/207 (70%) took a clean OHKO from Flamethrower; its Iron Head was aimed at Sylveon, not the threat.

lessons: When one slot's action already KOs the only foe that can hurt us this turn, the other slot's best move is usually Protect — a second KO on a passive foe is worth less than keeping a Pokemon alive.
After an opposing Pokemon Mega-evolves, recompute its speed and coverage: Mega Salamence outspeeds Kingambit and its Flamethrower OHKOs a chipped Kingambit through Steel typing.
A missing entry in the displayed threat list is not proof of safety — if a foe with unknown coverage is faster, assume the worst case for a chipped Pokemon.
Kingambit lead vs Indeedee-F / Psychic Terrain sheets is now 3-for-3 on removing the Trick Room setter on turn 1; keep it as the standing anti-psyterrain lead.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their Salamence-Mega + Torkoal + Indeedee shell shows how much value a single fast Mega with Fire coverage extracts against our Steel/Dark pivot. Add Protect discipline rather than new coverage, but for the team: swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed (redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) so a chipped Mega has a +2 finisher that ignores Wide Guard, Protect timing and Trick Room.
teamInspiration.reason: Our repeated loss pattern is slow attackers dying before converting; a priority finisher on Dragonite plus stricter Protect usage on Kingambit directly addresses the two wasted actions seen this game and in the prior four.

analysis.whatWorked: Whimsicott + Mega Charizard-Y lead removed their Whimsicott (speed control setter) on turn 1 with Heat Wave, denying them any Tailwind refresh. Turn 2 Protect on Drogon vs Arcanine-Hisui Head Smash (235-384% OHKO displayed) was textbook — the Protect-Drogon rule saved our Mega and it later closed the game. Turn 3 was a clean Macro Safe Play: sacrificing a 1-HP Whimsicott while pivoting Drogon out to Milotic, who ate Intimidate for +2 SpA (Competitive) and then OHKO'd Mega Salamence with Ice Beam. Milotic Protect cycling vs a Protect-spamming Arcanine stalled perfectly and Recover/Leftovers kept it alive. Kingambit converted at 1 HP with Kowtow Cleave on Dragapult.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Protect-Drogon-vs-displayed-OHKO rule: followed (T2, T7). Switching as a real tool: followed (T3 Drogon->Milotic into Intimidate for Competitive). Never attack into a foe that just Protected: VIOLATED on turn 6 — Arcanine Protected on turn 5 and we still aimed Milotic Scald at it, wasting half a turn (the Protect happened again). Speed-control-setter denial: followed (their Whimsicott died turn 1). Sucker Punch discipline: correctly avoided vs semi-invulnerable Dragapult. Tailwind by turn 2: followed.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 6 Milotic Scald into Arcanine, which had Protected the previous turn — a fully predictable wasted action; aiming Scald at Dragapult (or Protecting Milotic) was free. That wasted action cost Milotic ~90% HP from Phantom Force and nearly lost a won game. 2) Turn 5 Kowtow Cleave missed (85% accuracy) into Dragapult while we were ahead — Wolfe's anti-variance rule says prefer the 100%-accurate line when ahead, though here Kowtow was the only KO. 3) Turn 1 Moonblast missed; nothing to fix. 4) Kingambit was allowed to stay in at 21 HP into Arcanine Flare Blitz range on turn 6 instead of Protecting — Life Orb recoil then finished it; we traded our Kingambit for a KO we would have gotten anyway.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-block single-target attacks aimed at a foe that used Protect/Detect on the immediately preceding turn whenever another live foe exists; this must be in shouldBlockMove, not just the prompt. Add a Life-Orb self-KO guard: if Kingambit is below the Life Orb recoil threshold (<=10% HP) and its attack is not a guaranteed game-winning KO, prefer Protect or a non-recoil line. And when a foe is mid-Phantom Force/Dig (semi-invulnerable), treat it as untargetable this turn — route both actions at the other slot.

proposals.change: FRESH-PROTECT HARD BLOCK (now in shouldBlockMove): any single-target damaging move aimed at a foe whose lastMove was protect/detect/spikyshield/banefulbunker/burningbulwark/kingsshield last turn is prohibited while another non-fainted foe exists.
proposals.evidence: T6 Milotic Scald -> Arcanine (which Protected on T5) was blanked by a second Protect; that wasted action let Phantom Force drop Milotic to 10/202.

proposals.change: LIFE-ORB SUICIDE GUARD: when Kingambit holds Life Orb and its current HP is <=10% of max, penalize contact/LO attacks unless the move wins the game outright (last foe) — prefer Protect or Sucker Punch timing.
proposals.evidence: T6 Kingambit at 1/207 KO'd Dragapult but fainted to its own Life Orb recoil, giving the opponent a free 2v1 turn.

proposals.change: SEMI-INVULNERABLE TARGET BLOCK: block non-spread moves aimed at a foe with the Phantom Force/Dig/Fly/Bounce/Dive two-turn volatile active; route both actions at the grounded slot.
proposals.evidence: T5/T6 Dragapult alternated Phantom Force while we kept aiming single-target moves into the invulnerable slot.

lessons: A foe that Protected last turn must not be the target of any single-target move while another live foe exists — this is a hard block, not a preference.
Kingambit at <=10% HP with Life Orb kills itself on any contact attack: only click it if that KO ends the game, otherwise Protect.
Milotic switching into an Intimidate user (Salamence/Arcanine) is a free +2 SpA via Competitive and turns Ice Beam into an OHKO on Mega Salamence — use it as a deliberate pivot, not just an escape.
When a Ghost/Flying foe is in the semi-invulnerable turn of Phantom Force/Fly, both of our actions should go to the other slot.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp remains the best-performing loadout (45%) and was not implicated in this win; keep it stable to finish the trial window.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their Arcanine-Hisui 'Protect + Head Smash/Flare Blitz' pressure pattern: a foe with a displayed OHKO that Protects every other turn fully blanks our slow attackers. Our structural answer is a priority finisher — swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed, so a chipped Mega converts 1-HP/Sash foes through Protect-timing games and in Trick Room.
teamInspiration.reason: Three of the last five reviews independently flagged the same hole: our two slowest win-cons (Kingambit, Milotic) repeatedly lose actions to Protect timing and die before converting. Extreme Speed on Dragonite is single-target (ignores Wide Guard), +2 priority (ignores Grassy Glide/Sucker Punch and Trick Room), and overlaps with nothing else on the team.

whatWorked: Kingambit lead into the Indeedee-F Psychic Terrain sheet was again the right archetype call, and turn 1 Protect on Kingambit correctly dodged Grapploct's Storm Throw (a guaranteed OHKO) while Whimsicott's Moonblast took Grapploct to 26%. Whimsicott was again the MVP: 164% damage and 2 KOs (Grapploct, Indeedee-F), and Scald's burn on Indeedee closed the KO window on turn 5. Protect timing on Whimsicott on turns 4 and 6 blanked two Golisopod attacks.
lessonsApplied: Positive: Kingambit anti-psyterrain lead rule followed; no Tailwind into Trick Room; no Sucker Punch into Psychic Terrain; Protect used on genuinely threatened slots. Violated/ignored: the hard rule 'if Whimsicott is alive and TR is not threatened, Tailwind by turn 2' was never relevant because TR went up turn 1 — but we then never re-evaluated and ended the game with ZERO speed control for 7 turns. We also ignored the macro rule 'never let the opponent have speed AND power': after Trick Room we left the slow Golisopod-Mega (speed-advantaged under TR) alive and unanswered while it 3-shot Milotic. Most critically we repeated the known sin of attacking into a target a foe was protecting with Follow Me: turn 2 Kowtow Cleave went into Indeedee AFTER Follow Me redirected, wasting the slot's action economy structurally.
whatFailed: 1) TURN 2 WAS THE GAME. Kingambit was at full HP but under Trick Room Grapploct (slow, 100% likely to move first in TR) had a DISPLAYED 195-281% OHKO on Kingambit. The threat list literally said 'Kingambit threatened by Grapploct Storm Throw (195-281% OHKO)' and we clicked an attack anyway on the false assumption 'Kingambit moves first in TR' — Grapploct base 42 Speed is SLOWER than Kingambit base 50, so under Trick Room Grapploct moves FIRST. We lost our best piece to a speed-order miscalculation. The correct line was Kingambit switch out (or Protect again is banned, so switch) + Whimsicott Moonblast finishing Grapploct. 2) Indeedee used Follow Me on turn 2; both our actions were aimed at redirectable single targets, so Kowtow hit Indeedee at reduced value and Moonblast was also redirected — zero progress on Grapploct, which then had a free turn. 3) We never set Tailwind at ANY point, even after Trick Room expired around turn 6, so Basculegion's Last Respects (power scaling with their fainted count — 3 dead = 150 BP) got free OHKOs on Drogon and Whimsicott. 4) Drogon was brought in on turn 5 into a field containing Basculegion with Last Respects and Head Smash and Mega-evolved into a displayed OHKO — a pointless sacrifice of the Mega. 5) The rate-limit fallback on turn 3 again cost a turn of agency.
howToImprove: Hard-code Trick Room speed inversion into the threat evaluation: under TR, BASE SPEED ORDER REVERSES, so a low-Speed foe (Grapploct 42, Torkoal 20, Ursaluna 50, Golisopod 70-ish) moves BEFORE Kingambit (50). Never claim 'Kingambit moves first in TR' without comparing actual speeds. When a displayed OHKO exists against our slot and we are not faster, the only legal actions are Protect (if not used last turn) or Switch — never attack. Against a Follow Me / Rage Powder user, single-target moves on the partner are wasted: either use spread damage, target the redirector itself, or switch. Finally: Last Respects scales with their faints — once they have 2+ fainted, treat Basculegion as a guaranteed OHKO on everything and either KO it on entry or keep Protect up; and never Mega-evolve Charizard into a board where it is already in a displayed OHKO range with no Protect.

proposals.change: TRICK-ROOM SPEED ORDER GUARD: when Trick Room is active, compute actual speed; if a live foe has LOWER effective speed than our mon (i.e. moves first under TR) and has a displayed >=100% damage roll on it, block all non-Protect/non-switch actions for that slot.
proposals.evidence: Turn 2: reasoning said 'Kingambit moves first in TR' but Grapploct (base 42) is slower than Kingambit (base 50) and therefore moved first under TR, OHKOing it with a displayed 195-281% Storm Throw.

proposals.change: FOLLOW-ME/RAGE-POWDER REDIRECTION RULE: if a foe used Follow Me or Rage Powder last turn (or is Indeedee/Amoonguss/Togekiss with it on the sheet), penalize single-target moves aimed at the OTHER foe; prefer spread moves, targeting the redirector, or switching.
proposals.evidence: Turn 2 Indeedee used Follow Me; both of our single-target actions were sucked into it, leaving Grapploct completely untouched for a free Storm Throw KO.

proposals.change: LAST RESPECTS ESCALATION RULE: track opponent faint count; when Basculegion (or any Last Respects user) is on their sheet and they have >=2 faints, flag it as an OHKO threat to every member of our team and forbid bringing a Mega in without Protect available.
proposals.evidence: Basculegion with 3 opposing faints OHKO'd a full-HP Mega Charizard (153 HP) and Whimsicott on consecutive turns.

proposals.change: NO-MEGA-INTO-OHKO RULE: block the mega flag when the Pokemon mega-evolving is in a displayed >=100% damage window from a faster foe and is not using Protect that turn.
proposals.evidence: Turn 6 Drogon mega-evolved (setting sun, giving them nothing) and died immediately to Last Respects before its Heat Wave mattered; the Mega was spent for zero value.

lessons: Under Trick Room, speed order REVERSES by actual Speed stat: Grapploct (42), Torkoal (20), Ursaluna (50), Dusclops (25) all move BEFORE Kingambit (50-ish). Never assume Kingambit is first in TR — compare the numbers.
If a displayed OHKO exists on our slot from a foe that moves first and Protect was used last turn, the only correct action is SWITCH, not attack.

Follow Me / Rage Powder redirects every single-target move: against an active redirector, use spread moves, hit the redirector itself, or switch — splitting single-target attacks is a guaranteed wasted turn.
Basculegion's Last Respects gains 50 BP per fainted teammate on their side; once they are 2-3 down it OHKOs our entire team, so it must be removed on entry or stalled with Protect.
Never Mega-evolve into a turn where that Pokemon is already in a displayed OHKO window and is not Protecting — the Mega is spent for nothing.

itemExperiment.reason: Choice Scarf is dead weight under Trick Room (makes us slower) and this archetype (psyterrain/TR) is now 46 games at 39%. Sitrus Garchomp keeps move flexibility (EQ vs Stomping Tantrum vs Rock Slide) which matters far more against redirection and TR teams than raw speed.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'Follow Me + Trick Room redirector' structure in spirit: their Indeedee generated two full free turns purely by soaking our single-target moves. Our structural answers are (a) spread damage that ignores redirection — keep Heat Wave on Drogon, and (b) a priority finisher. Swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed: +2 priority ignores Trick Room speed inversion entirely, ignores redirection targeting games less, and finishes chipped Sash/low-HP foes like Basculegion before Last Respects fires.
teamInspiration.reason: We lost this game to two mechanics Extreme Speed fully beats: Trick Room speed inversion (priority ignores TR) and low-HP snowball threats getting a free turn. Heat Wave on Dragonite has never been the deciding move in any logged game because Charizard-Y already provides sun-boosted spread Fire.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1 Protect on Drogon + Whimsicott Tailwind was correct and bought the Mega a turn against Mega Blaziken Rock Slide. Turn 5 Garchomp Earthquake next to a Protecting Kingambit was a clean double-KO (Inteleon + Mega Blaziken) — a textbook offensive safe play that erased the 2-0 deficit. Kingambit Iron Head OHKO'd Alcremie on turn 6.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Protect-Drogon-turn-1 rule applied. Turn-2 Tailwind rule applied (turn 1 even). EQ next to Kingambit was used with Kingambit on Protect, which is the only legal version of that line. However three Claude calls fell back to the engine (rate limit), and all three fallback turns produced the losses.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Turn 2 we focus-fired Inteleon and both of its slots Protected/Detected — we had SEEN nothing yet, but the bigger issue is turn 3: the engine fallback double-Protected immediately after the opponent double-Protected, giving Mega Blaziken a FOURTH free Speed Boost. Blaziken gained +4 Speed over turns 1-4 entirely unpunished — that is 'opponent has speed AND power', our cardinal sin. 2) Turn 4 fallback attacked with Whimsicott and left Drogon in a displayed 84-136% Rock Slide OHKO window with no Protect and no switch — Drogon and Whimsicott both died in one turn. 3) Speed Boost was never treated as setup: every turn Blaziken was allowed to idle, it got stronger relative to us; we should have switched Drogon out or pressured Blaziken directly rather than tunneling on Inteleon. 4) Turn 7 Kingambit at 32% raced Golisopod's First Impression instead of Protecting the priority turn then Kowtowing — a 1v1 we could have stolen.
analysis.howToImprove: Treat Speed Boost (and any per-turn passive boost: Speed Boost, Stamina, Moody, Beast Boost chains) as active setup: never double-Protect against it, never stall, pressure or remove it. Never leave a Pokemon with a displayed >=100% incoming roll on the field without Protect or a switch, especially after it already Protected last turn (Protect fails/less reliable consecutively — SWITCH instead). Against Golisopod 1v1 at low HP, Protect the First Impression turn (it only works turn 1 out, and FI loses value) then attack.

proposals.change: PASSIVE-BOOST STALL BAN: if a live foe has Speed Boost / Stamina / Moody / Protosynthesis-type per-turn escalation, block double-Protect turns and penalize any turn where neither of our actions is a damaging move or switch aimed at reducing that foe's board presence.
proposals.evidence: Mega Blaziken accrued +4 Speed across turns 1-4 while we Protected twice and whiffed into Protect once; it then OHKO'd Drogon and the game was lost from there.

proposals.change: OHKO-WINDOW MANDATORY RESPONSE: when a slot has a displayed >=100% damage roll from a faster live foe, that slot's only legal actions are Protect (if it did NOT Protect last turn) or switch. Attacking is blocked.
proposals.evidence: T4 Drogon had an 84-136% Rock Slide window, had Protected on T3, and was given an attack order by the engine fallback — it fainted immediately.

proposals.change: FIRST IMPRESSION PROTECT RULE: vs a freshly-switched-in Golisopod/any First Impression user, our threatened slot should Protect on its first active turn to blank the +2 priority nuke, then attack.
proposals.evidence: Golisopod First Impression did 59% to Garchomp on T6 and the T7 Kingambit race lost by one turn; Protect on T7 blanks Liquidation and keeps Kingambit alive for Kowtow.

proposals.change: ANTI-DOUBLE-PROTECT MIRROR: if BOTH opposing slots used Protect/Detect last turn, never respond with our own double Protect; at least one slot must attack or switch.
proposals.evidence: T2 both foes Protected; T3 engine fallback answered with double Protect, surrendering the entire turn and a Speed Boost.

lessons: Speed Boost (Mega Blaziken, Sharpedo) is setup: every stalled turn makes them permanently faster — never double-Protect against it, pressure it or switch away.
A slot that Protected last turn and still faces a displayed OHKO must SWITCH, not attack and not Protect again.
When both opposing slots Protect, answer with attacks or a switch — mirroring their Protect donates a free turn to any passive-boost ability.
Vs a newly-entered Golisopod, Protect blanks First Impression (it only works on its first turn out), then attack freely.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp was the only thing that converted this game (double KO through Earthquake on turn 5); keep it while we fix the piloting/fallback holes.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their win engine was 'passive escalation + Protect cycling' (Mega Blaziken Speed Boost + Detect, Inteleon Focus Energy + Protect). Our structural answer is a priority finisher that ignores Protect timing games: swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (fully redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed (+2 priority, single-target, ignores Wide Guard and Trick Room).
teamInspiration.reason: Every recent loss shares the pattern of our slow attackers losing actions to Protect/Detect cycling and dying before converting chipped foes; Extreme Speed converts Sash/low-HP foes (Inteleon at 33%, Golisopod at 8%) regardless of speed boosts.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn-1 focus fire onto Espathra (the Baton Pass/Calm Mind win-con) was the correct macro call, and Whimsicott's Encore on turn 2 locked Espathra into Calm Mind so it could never pass or attack. Drogon's Heat Wave in sun then cleanly double-KO'd Espathra + Sneasler on turn 3, putting us 4-2 up on paper. Charizard-Y's Drought also pre-empted Politoed rain.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: punish setup immediately (Encore + focus fire on Espathra), Charizard-Y Mega to override rain, no Tailwind into a bad board. Violated: 'never Mega-evolve into a displayed OHKO window' was not relevant turn 1 but 'Protect Drogon vs faster strong special attackers' was skipped on turn 1 (Sneasler Fake Out flinched the Mega into a wasted turn). Critically violated on turn 4: Whimsicott at 1 HP clicked Tailwind while Drogon sat in a displayed Glimmora-Mega Power Gem OHKO window and did NOT Protect — the exact 'OHKO-WINDOW MANDATORY RESPONSE' proposal already on the books.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 4 lost the game outright. Both opposing slots were fresh switch-ins: Rillaboom (Fake Out, guaranteed to delete 1-HP Whimsicott) and Glimmora which Mega-evolved and had Power Gem displayed at 110-191% on Drogon (4x Rock weak Charizard-Y at 36% HP). We clicked Weather Ball at Rillaboom (which was Fake-Out-ing anyway, so the KO gained nothing that turn) and Tailwind with a 1-HP Whimsicott that was 100% dead to Fake Out. Correct line: Drogon Protect (blanks Power Gem, survives at 36%) and Whimsicott Protect or any action — Drogon alive at 36% in sun still OHKOs Rillaboom and threatens Glimmora next turn. Turn 5 compounded it: Dragonite was in an 80-145% Power Gem window and still attacked instead of Protecting, giving away the second Mega for ~20% chip. Also Glimmora's Mega Power Gem (4x on Charizard, super-effective on Dragonite) was fully visible on the sheet from preview and we never planned a Rock-resist answer; Garchomp and Kingambit (both Rock-resistant/neutral and the natural Glimmora answers) were left on the bench.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Hard rule, in code: any slot with a displayed >=100% damage roll from a live foe that moves first may only Protect (if it did not Protect last turn) or switch. 2) Freshly-switched-in Fake Out users (Rillaboom, Incineroar, Sneasler) guarantee a wasted action on our slow/fragile slot — never invest a setup move (Tailwind/Encore) in a 1-HP Pokemon on the turn a fresh Fake Out user is on the board. 3) Team preview vs any Rock-coverage Mega (Glimmora, Tyranitar, Blaziken-Mega Rock Slide) must bring Garchomp or Kingambit, not Dragonite, as the 3rd/4th slot behind Charizard. 4) Stop spending both Megas into the same Rock attacker.

proposals.change: ROCK-COVERAGE MEGA GUARD: when a live foe has a Rock move on sheet/revealed and our Charizard (4x) or Dragonite (2x) is in a displayed >=100% window, block every non-Protect/non-switch action for that slot, and block Mega-evolving the second Mega into that same foe.
proposals.evidence: Glimmora-Mega Power Gem OHKO'd Drogon at 36% on T4 and Dragonite at full on T5; both were shown in the threat display and both still attacked.

proposals.change: ZERO-VALUE SETUP BAN: forbid Tailwind/Encore/Protect-less setup moves on a Pokemon at <=10% HP when a freshly-entered Fake Out user is active on the opposing side (its action is guaranteed to be deleted).
proposals.evidence: T4 Whimsicott at 1/137 clicked Tailwind and was Fake Out'd by the fresh Rillaboom before it resolved — a fully wasted action in a 2-action turn.

proposals.change: Vs sheets containing Glimmora / Tyranitar / any Rock-coverage Mega, bring Garchomp (resists Rock, immune to Toxic Debris spikes damage? no — but resists Rock and OHKOs Glimmora with EQ) and Kingambit over Dragonite as the back pair.
proposals.evidence: Glimmora was on the sheet at preview; our back pair was Milotic + Dragonite, both of which lost to Power Gem, while Garchomp (Ground STAB, Rock resist) never came.

lessons: A slot shown a >=100% damage roll from a faster foe must Protect or switch — attacking that turn is a guaranteed loss of the piece for partial chip.

Never spend an action on setup (Tailwind/Encore) with a Pokemon at 1-10% HP while a freshly-switched-in Fake Out user (Rillaboom/Incineroar/Sneasler) is active: the action is deleted before it resolves.
Glimmora-Mega Power Gem is a 4x OHKO on Charizard-Y and a clean OHKO on Dragonite — vs Glimmora sheets bring Garchomp/Kingambit as the back pair, never both Megas.
Do not burn the second Mega (Dragonite) into a board where the same Rock attacker that just killed the first Mega is still alive and faster.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp: vs Glimmora/Rock-coverage rain balance, Scarf EQ is our only guaranteed-first answer to the Rock attacker that killed both Megas here; Garchomp simply must be brought in those matchups.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (fully redundant with Charizard-Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed, and in preview vs Rock-coverage teams bring Garchomp + Kingambit behind Charizard instead of Milotic + Dragonite.
teamInspiration.reason: Their win engine was a single fast Rock-coverage Mega (Glimmora Power Gem) deleting both of our Megas on consecutive turns while Rillaboom's Fake Out erased our support action. Extreme Speed gives Dragonite a +2 finisher that converts chipped foes (Espathra at 1%, Sneasler at 10%) without needing to survive a turn, and Garchomp/Kingambit are the only members that do not fold to Power Gem.

whatWorked: Turn-1 Kingambit Kowtow Cleave removed Mega Delphox immediately (3-for-3 pattern of killing their Mega on its first active turn), and Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave simultaneously broke Whimsicott's Sash and chipped Delphox — a textbook two-for-one opening that stripped both their Mega and their speed-control setter's safety net. The turn-2 switch of a burned 3%-HP Kingambit into Milotic (instead of clicking a Life Orb contact move that would have killed it) correctly preserved a piece and brought a bulky pivot. Dragonite's turn-3 Protect scouted Garchomp's Dragon Claw while Milotic Ice Beamed Garchomp off the board. Endgame was pure Wolfe safe play: ahead 4v1, Milotic Protect then Recover while Choice Scarf Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum (not Earthquake, which would have hit Milotic) ground down their Kingambit with zero risk.
lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) kill the opposing Mega on its first active turn with a guaranteed move — Kowtow Cleave ignores Protect; (2) never Earthquake beside an ally that takes Ground damage — Stomping Tantrum was used twice next to Milotic; (3) ahead-in-count safe-play directive — no predictions were made at 4v1, only Protect/Recover/single-target chip; (4) switch rather than attack with a near-dead Life Orb Kingambit; (5) Protect the slot in a displayed OHKO window (Milotic T5 vs Kowtow 80% KO chance). Violated/at-risk: we let their Whimsicott set Tailwind unopposed on turn 1 (we chose the Delphox KO over denying speed control, which was still correct given Heat Wave broke the Sash and burned it to death next turn), and Dragonite took an 82% Dragon Claw because Multiscale was already broken by Delphox's Heat Wave spread — the Multiscale-preservation rule was not actionable with a spread move on the field.
whatFailed: Minor inefficiencies only. (1) Dragonite finished the game at 8% and had to be benched: the T1 Heat Wave choice meant it ate Delphox's spread Heat Wave with Multiscale intact but then Garchomp's Dragon Claw for 92% of what remained — a Protect on Dragonite T2 (instead of Dragon Pulse) was available, though the Dragon Pulse chip into Garchomp was what let Milotic finish it T3. (2) Two damage-calc misses (Heat Wave 94% vs predicted 42-82%, Scald 34% vs predicted 13-24%) show our bulk assumptions for opposing Whimsicott/Kingambit are too generous — the engine keeps underestimating our own damage on frail supports and overestimating opposing Kingambit bulk. (3) Turn 6 we had Milotic Recover while Garchomp finished — fine, but Milotic could have Scalded for a redundant-but-free burn safety net in case Garchomp missed nothing; immaterial. (4) Two API fallbacks (T3, and preview) meant the engine, not the pilot, chose the preview team — we got lucky the fallback team was correct.
howToImprove: 1) Keep the Kingambit lead vs Mega-Fire/Psychic sheets: Kowtow Cleave on their Mega turn 1 is now the single highest-EV opening we have. 2) When a spread Fire move is on the opposing board (Delphox/Charizard/Torkoal), treat Mega Dragonite's Multiscale as already spent and do not plan lines that assume it survives two hits. 3) Tighten the bulk model: assume frail supports (Whimsicott, Indeedee, Alcremie) are minimum-bulk and that opposing Kingambit/Golisopod carry more HP investment than the default. 4) Rate-limit resilience: the preview fallback must never be a coin flip — the engine-side default preview order should already encode 'Kingambit + second Mega vs Mega-Fire/Psychic sheets'. 5) Continue the ahead-in-count discipline: at 4v1 with a Choice-Scarf finisher, Protect/Recover the partner every turn until the scarf move closes it.

proposals.change: MEGA-KILL PRIORITY: when an opposing Pokemon has Mega-evolved this turn or is flagged as their Mega on the sheet and our action can deal >=100% to it with a Protect-ignoring or guaranteed-accuracy move (Kowtow Cleave, Sucker Punch into a committed attacker, Ancient Power), score that action +2.0 — killing their Mega on its first active turn is now 4-for-4.
proposals.evidence: T1 Kowtow Cleave OHKO'd Mega Delphox before it could repeat Heat Wave; same pattern won the Salamence game via Ancient Power.

proposals.change: MULTISCALE-SPENT FLAG: if any live foe has a revealed or sheet spread move (Heat Wave, Blizzard, Rock Slide, Dazzling Gleam, Muddy Water, Expanding Force), stop granting Mega Dragonite the 'Multiscale survives' bonus in survival estimates and raise its Protect score by +0.6 on turns it is in a >=70% damage window.
proposals.evidence: Delphox's spread Heat Wave broke Multiscale on T1 with 16 chip; Garchomp's Dragon Claw then did 82% and left Dragonite at 8% and useless for the rest of the game.

proposals.change: FRAIL-SUPPORT BULK FLOOR: when computing damage onto Whimsicott / Indeedee / Alcremie / Tornadus / Pelipper / Comfey, assume minimum defensive investment (shift the predicted roll band up ~15%) so spread moves are correctly credited with KOs through Focus Sash chip.
proposals.evidence: T1 Heat Wave to Whimsicott predicted 42-82%, actual 94% — a full roll band outside prediction, which would have changed a focus-fire decision in a closer game.

proposals.change: Vs sheets containing a Mega-stone Fire/Psychic special attacker (Delphox, Armarouge, Alakazam, Gardevoir) plus a Prankster/Tailwind support, hard-lock the Kingambit + Mega Dragonite lead with Milotic and Garchomp in back.
proposals.evidence: This exact lead produced a 4-0 sweep in 6 turns; Kingambit is Psychic-immune and OHKOs the Mega, Dragonite's Heat Wave breaks the Sash support.

lessons: Killing the opposing Mega on its first active turn with a Protect-ignoring move (Kowtow Cleave) is now our highest-EV turn-1 action — 4 games in a row it has decided the match.
A spread Fire/Rock/Ice move anywhere on the opposing board means Mega Dragonite's Multiscale is effectively already spent: never plan a two-hit survival line for it after turn 1.
A burned Life Orb Kingambit below 10% should always switch, never attack — the switch into Milotic preserved a piece that then won the endgame.
When ahead 4v1 with a Choice Scarf finisher on the field, the partner's correct action every turn is Protect or Recover, never a second attack.

Our damage model systematically under-rates our hits on frail supports (Whimsicott 94% vs predicted 42-82%) and under-rates our hits on bulky Dark/Steel (Scald 34% vs predicted 13-24%) — widen both bands before declining a focus-fire line.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their Whimsicott 'Tailwind + Light Screen' support shell in spirit: their Whimsicott bought two full free turns of screens/speed while their attackers traded. On our side, swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (fully redundant with Charizard-Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed — this game Dragonite ended at 8% HP and could not convert a 25% Garchomp, and a +2 priority finisher would have closed that slot immediately regardless of Multiscale being broken.
teamInspiration.reason: Dragonite's Heat Wave did useful chip only because Charizard was not brought; in every game where both Megas are on the sheet it is dead weight. Extreme Speed is single-target (ignores Wide Guard), +2 priority (ignores Tailwind, Trick Room and Grassy Glide), and converts exactly the chipped 8-25% foes that have repeatedly survived to take one of our pieces.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead into the Psychic Terrain sheet was correct again (4th straight game it removed a key foe on turn 1 — Kowtow Cleave OHKO'd the switched-in Garchomp). Mega Charizard-Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave was the engine of the game: 258% damage across three turns, KOing Sinistcha (the Trick Room setter) and chipping Volcarona twice. Turn 3 Garchomp Earthquake next to Flying-type Drogon was a textbook double-KO (Volcarona + Mega Lucario) that closed the game — Ground spread is safe beside Charizard, as the team rule says.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: Kingambit anti-psyterrain lead; never Earthquake beside Kingambit (Kingambit was already gone, and Drogon is Flying-immune); Heat Wave spread rather than single-target into a potential Rage Powder/Protect user; no Tailwind into a Trick Room sheet; Mega-evolved Charizard turn 1 outside of an OHKO window. Violated: the Masterclass 'punish setup immediately' rule — Volcarona used Quiver Dance on turn 1 completely unopposed and then Fiery Dance OHKO'd Kingambit on turn 2; we spent turn 2 Kowtow Cleaving Sinistcha (which Heat Wave was already going to OHKO per our own calc, 119-153%) instead of focus-firing the +1 Volcarona.
analysis.whatFailed: Turn 2 was a clean overkill/no-punish error. Our own displayed calc said Drogon's Heat Wave did 119-153% to Sinistcha (guaranteed OHKO) while Volcarona was at 59% after a Quiver Dance. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave was aimed at the slot Heat Wave already killed, so Kingambit's action produced ZERO value and it died to Fiery Dance. A Sucker Punch or Iron Head into Volcarona (which was committed to attacking) — or simply Kowtow Cleave onto Volcarona — would have either KO'd it or left it in Heat Wave range, saving Kingambit. Second smaller failure: turn 1 we let the free Quiver Dance happen; Heat Wave chip was fine but the board should have been re-read as 'a booster is live' from that point on.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: before selecting a second attack, check whether the FIRST attack's displayed roll already guarantees the KO on that target; if so, the second slot must hit a different live foe — ideally any foe that has boosted. Add an explicit 'active booster' priority: any foe with a positive stat stage becomes the mandatory focus-fire target for every slot that cannot be the one securing a separate guaranteed KO. Also: Volcarona at +1 SpA outspeeds and OHKOs Kingambit through Steel resist (Fiery Dance 4x Fire on Dark/Steel is still super effective) — treat any live Volcarona as an immediate Kingambit killer and never leave Kingambit out to take a free hit.

proposals.change: OVERKILL BLOCK: if one of our selected actions already shows a >=100% guaranteed roll on a target, block any second action aimed at that same target while another live foe exists. Redirect the second slot to the boosted/most threatening foe.
proposals.evidence: T2: Heat Wave showed 119-153% on Sinistcha (guaranteed OHKO) and Kingambit still clicked Kowtow Cleave into Sinistcha; its action was wasted and it died to +1 Volcarona Fiery Dance.

proposals.change: ACTIVE-BOOSTER FOCUS: any foe with a net positive stat stage (Quiver Dance/Calm Mind/Dragon Dance/Swords Dance) gets +2.0 score as a target for all our slots and a hard preference over unboosted foes, even if the unboosted foe is a Trick Room setter already in KO range from our other slot.
proposals.evidence: Volcarona Quiver Danced turn 1 unpunished, then Fiery Dance OHKO'd Kingambit on turn 2; it needed three Heat Waves + an Earthquake to finally fall.

proposals.change: VOLCARONA/FIRE-SPECIAL GUARD: treat any live Volcarona (or Fire special attacker at +1) as a displayed OHKO threat on Kingambit and on Whimsicott; Kingambit should Protect or switch rather than take a free turn beside one.
proposals.evidence: Fiery Dance did 78% to a 162/207 Kingambit for the KO despite Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing.

lessons: If our own displayed calc shows one slot has a guaranteed (>=100% minimum roll) KO on a target, the other slot must NEVER target that same Pokemon while another live foe exists — that is a wasted action in the 2-action economy.
A foe that boosts (Quiver Dance/Calm Mind/Dragon Dance) becomes the mandatory focus-fire target the very next turn, even over a Trick Room setter that another slot already kills.
Volcarona at +1 SpA OHKOs Kingambit with Fiery Dance despite Dark/Steel typing — never leave Kingambit in front of a boosted Fire special attacker without Protect or a switch.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their Volcarona 'Quiver Dance behind a Rage Powder/Trick Room body' pattern in spirit: a single free boosting turn nearly won them the game from a 2-0 deficit. Our structural answer remains swapping Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed — a +2 priority finisher converts exactly the 14-21% boosted sweepers that currently get a free extra turn to KO one of our pieces.
teamInspiration.reason: Volcarona survived at 28% then 14% and still got two attacking turns; Extreme Speed would have removed it on either turn regardless of its +1 Speed, and overlaps with nothing else on our team.

analysis.whatWorked: Vs Buglife-cn (sand/Rock: Tyrantrum + Glimmora + Hippowdon + Staraptor) we won 6-? by following the anti-sand playbook: turn 1 we correctly read the double-Rock OHKO board and Protected Mega Charizard while pivoting Whimsicott out into Milotic — a textbook Defensive Safe Play (Protect threatened slot + reposition partner). Milotic then became the engine of the game: Ice Beam removed Staraptor, Scald removed Hippowdon (and killed sand), and Whimsicott Moonblast finished Tyrantrum. Milotic Protecting on T5 while Whimsicott cleaned up Tyrantrum was a clean 2-action turn. The T6 switch of 11% poisoned Milotic into Garchomp (resists Rock, threatens Glimmora with Ground) followed exactly the 'a slot facing a displayed OHKO must switch' lesson, and Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum eventually closed out Glimmora — notably Stomping Tantrum was the correct pick over Earthquake because it doubles power through Spiky Shield/Protect cycling and spares Whimsicott.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) Protect Drogon vs Rock-coverage sand leads — done turn 1. (2) Never Earthquake beside a non-Flying ally — Garchomp used Stomping Tantrum with Whimsicott beside it, never EQ. (3) Switch rather than attack/Protect a slot facing a displayed OHKO — Milotic at 11% switched to Garchomp. (4) Anti-sand preview rule (Mega Charizard + Whimsicott Tailwind lead, Garchomp/Milotic back) was respected and is 6-4 in that archetype now. Violated/partially violated: after Glimmora Spiky Shielded on T7 we still aimed a single-target Stomping Tantrum at it on T8 — the 'a foe that Protected last turn must not be the single-target of our move while another live foe exists' rule only held because Glimmora was the LAST live foe, so it was acceptable; but it did burn turns. Also, Tailwind on T7 with Whimsicott at 26% and poisoned produced zero value — it was set with only Garchomp able to use it, and Whimsicott died the next turn to residual.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Drogon died on turn 2 to Tyrantrum Rock Slide while the engine fallback (HTTP 429 rate limit) picked an attack instead of a second Protect or a switch — we knew Rock Slide was a 268-439% OHKO window and had just Protected, so the only correct T2 action was SWITCH Drogon out, not attack. That is a direct violation of 'a slot that Protected last turn and still faces a displayed OHKO must SWITCH'. The rate-limit fallback engine does not enforce our coach lessons, so our most important piece evaporated for zero value. 2) Milotic took a Mortal Spin poison on turn 1 and spent the whole game bleeding; we never used Recover once despite Milotic being our main damage dealer (113% and 2 KOs) — Recover + Leftovers would have kept it alive as the late-game wall and we would not have needed the Garchomp pivot. 3) Whimsicott's turn-7 Tailwind was a wasted action: at 26% HP, poisoned, against a single Glimmora, with Garchomp already outspeeding it; Protect was the only correct move and would have saved the piece. 4) Two full turns (T7, T8) were spent clicking into Glimmora's Spiky Shield/Protect cycle — against a last-mon Protect cycler we should alternate attack/Protect to break the pattern rather than clicking the same move twice.
analysis.howToImprove: (a) Hard-block the fallback engine from choosing an attack with Charizard when a live Rock-type/Rock-coverage foe is on the board and Charizard is in a >=100% displayed window — force Protect (if not used last turn) or a switch. (b) Add a Recover-priority rule: Milotic below 50% HP with Recover available and no incoming OHKO must Recover instead of attacking — poisoned Milotic at 40% that keeps attacking is a dead Milotic. (c) Block Tailwind entirely when the setter is below 35% HP and already poisoned/badly damaged, or when only one live foe remains and our remaining attacker already outspeeds it — Tailwind's value is zero in those boards. (d) Against a repeat Protect/Spiky Shield cycler that is the last foe, alternate: attack, then Protect/setup, then attack — never click the same single-target move into consecutive Protect turns. (e) Vs Rock-heavy sand sheets (Tyrantrum/Glimmora/Tyranitar + Hippowdon), strongly consider leaving Charizard home entirely in favor of Milotic + Garchomp + Kingambit + Whimsicott; Drogon contributed 0% damage in this game and ate an action on turn 1 plus a free KO for them on turn 2.

proposals.change: CHARIZARD ROCK-LOCK: if Drogon is active, a live foe has a Rock-type STAB or revealed Rock move, and the displayed incoming roll is >=100%, block all attacking moves for Drogon. Force Protect if Protect was not used last turn, otherwise force a switch. This must apply to the engine fallback path too, not just the Claude path.
proposals.evidence: T2 vs Buglife-cn: after Protecting T1, Drogon attacked into Tyrantrum Rock Slide (268-439% displayed) and died for 0 damage. Drogon finished the game with 0% damage dealt.

proposals.change: MILOTIC RECOVER GATE: when Milotic is below 55% HP (or statused with poison/burn) and no displayed incoming roll this turn is >=100%, score Recover +2.5 and penalize attacking moves -1.0. Milotic is our designated late-game wall and must not bleed out while attacking.
proposals.evidence: Milotic was poisoned on T1 and dropped 202->22 HP over 5 turns without ever using Recover, forcing a pivot out of our best remaining attacker (113% damage, 2 KOs).

proposals.change: TAILWIND VALUE GATE: block Tailwind when (setter HP < 35%) OR (only one live foe remains AND one of our live Pokemon already outspeeds it). Replace with Protect or an attack.
proposals.evidence: T7: Whimsicott at 26% and poisoned clicked Tailwind vs a lone Glimmora that Scarf Garchomp already outspeeds; Whimsicott died the next turn and the Tailwind turns were never used.

proposals.change: PROTECT-CYCLE BREAKER: if a foe used Protect/Spiky Shield/Detect/King's Shield last turn and it is the only live foe, do not repeat the identical single-target move this turn — prefer Protect/setup/Recover with one slot and attack with the other, alternating.
proposals.evidence: T7 and T8 both aimed Stomping Tantrum at Glimmora; T7 was fully blanked by Spiky Shield plus Garchomp took contact chip.

proposals.change: Vs sheets with TWO or more Rock-STAB/Rock-coverage threats (Tyrantrum + Glimmora, Tyranitar + Excadrill, Glimmora + Staraptor), leave Charizard-Y home and bring Whimsicott + Milotic + Garchomp + Kingambit, using Mega Dragonite only if no spread Rock move is on the sheet.
proposals.evidence: Drogon dealt 0% and was KO'd turn 2; Milotic/Whimsicott/Garchomp produced 100% of the game's damage. Sand archetype record remains 5-9.

lessons: After Protecting with Charizard-Y against a live Rock attacker, the next turn must be a SWITCH, never an attack — Protect only buys one turn and Rock Slide does not miss twice.
Milotic with Recover must heal at <55% HP or when poisoned: a bleeding Milotic forfeits the late-game wall role that wins sand matchups.
Tailwind has zero value when the setter is below 35% HP or when only one slow foe remains — click Protect or an attack instead.
Against a last-mon Protect/Spiky Shield cycler, alternate actions; never repeat the same single-target move into consecutive Protect turns.
When the engine fallback fires (API rate limit), it does not know our coach rules — guardrails must live in shouldBlockMove so they apply on every code path.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 43-51 (46%) and in this game its Speed was irrelevant (it outsped Glimmora regardless) while the Choice lock forced it to repeat Stomping Tantrum into Spiky Shield. Sitrus gives longevity against Rock/Ground chip in sand and lets Garchomp alternate EQ/Rock Slide/Dragon Claw against Protect cyclers.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their 'chip-and-stall residual' engine: Glimmora's Mortal Spin poisoned both of our supports and then Spiky Shield cycled while residual did the work. Our structural answer is twofold — (1) actually use Milotic's Recover (it already has it, we simply never click it), and (2) swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed, a +2 priority single-target finisher that ignores Protect-timing games by letting us convert chipped foes on the turn they drop rather than losing a turn to Spiky Shield.
teamInspiration.reason: Glimmora alone ate four of our actions (T6-T10) through Protect cycling and residual; priority damage and proactive healing are the two tools we lack to break that pattern, and Heat Wave on Dragonite has never been the deciding move in any logged game.

analysis.whatWorked: Turn 1-2 focus fire removed Raichu (their Lightning Rod/Focus Blast speed threat) cleanly, and Kowtow Cleave into Basculegion on T1 was the correct read of Last Respects as their primary win condition. Milotic's Scald chipped Golisopod repeatedly and all 5 damage-calc checks landed inside predicted ranges, so the damage model was accurate this game.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Anti-Last Respects rule was applied (Kowtow targeted Basculegion T1). Protect discipline on Milotic T4 vs displayed 99-130% Leech Life was correct. Tailwind was correctly declined with Whimsicott at 1% HP (value gate). However, the Golisopod Protect-blank rule was violated and the booster-focus rule was violated.
