analysis.whatFailed: 1) SWORDS DANCE UNPUNISHED: Golisopod used Swords Dance on T2 and we never focus-fired it; from T3 onward a +2 Mega Golisopod with Leech Life OHKO'd Kingambit, Milotic and 2HKO'd Drogon — it single-handedly won the game. 2) T3 we split damage into Pelipper (a 19% leftover) while +2 Golisopod sat untouched with a displayed 99-130% OHKO on Milotic and 79-113% on Kingambit; that was the losing turn. 3) T4-T6 Whimsicott at 1 HP burned three actions (Moonblast into a switch, Protect, Encore) and died; Encore on T6 came 4 turns too late and locked an already-spent Swords Dance. 4) Drogon Mega'd on T7 into a board where +2 Golisopod (faster, Liquidation 231-376% displayed OHKO) was alive — direct violation of 'never Mega into a displayed OHKO window' and 'never burn the second Mega into the attacker that killed the first pieces'. 5) T7 Heat Wave MISSED (90% acc) on the one turn it mattered, and we had no 100%-accurate option because Drogon was alone.
analysis.howToImprove: Treat any foe that uses a boosting move as the mandatory double-target the very next turn, overriding 'remove speed control' when the setter is already chipped — on T3 the correct play was Kowtow Cleave + Scald both into Golisopod (and Milotic should have Protected or switched given the displayed OHKO). Against Emergency Exit/Mega Golisopod, Protect blanks First Impression but Swords Dance must still be answered with damage. Never send a lone Mega into a board where a faster foe shows a >=100% roll on it; switch to Garchomp/Kingambit instead. And a Pokemon at 1 HP should either Protect once to absorb a hit for the partner or be used immediately for its highest-value action on the first turn it is at 1 HP, not three turns later.

proposals.change: BOOSTED-ATTACKER OVERRIDE: if any foe has >=+2 in Atk or SpA, it becomes the mandatory target for BOTH our slots (unless one slot must Protect/switch against a displayed >=100% roll). Block all attacking moves aimed at any other foe while a +2 foe is alive and not at KO-range from a single hit.
proposals.evidence: Golisopod got Swords Dance off on T2 and was never double-targeted; it then KO'd Kingambit (T3), Whimsicott (T4 chip), Milotic (T6) and Drogon (T9).

proposals.change: LONE-MEGA GUARD: block Mega Evolution on a turn where the Mega's own slot shows an incoming >=100% roll from a faster foe and the Mega is not Protecting/switching. Prefer switching in Garchomp/Kingambit instead of burning the second Mega.
proposals.evidence: T7 Drogon Mega'd with Golisopod-Mega Liquidation displayed at 231-376% OHKO; the Mega was spent for two Heat Waves, one of which missed.

proposals.change: 1-HP ACTION GATE: a Pokemon at <=5% HP that faces any live foe with a non-priority attack must either Protect (once) or use its single highest-value action immediately — never spend consecutive turns on chip attacks or late Encore.
proposals.evidence: Whimsicott sat at 1/137 from T2 to T6 and produced one 56% Moonblast and a wasted Encore before dying to Shadow Ball.

lessons: A foe that clicks Swords Dance / Calm Mind / Quiver Dance becomes the mandatory DOUBLE-target the very next turn, even if a speed-control setter (Pelipper) is sitting at low HP beside it — chipping the setter while the booster snowballs loses the game.
Never Mega-evolve a lone Pokemon into a board where a faster foe already shows a >=100% damage roll on it; switch to a resist instead and save the Mega.
Mega Golisopod with Leech Life at +2 heals back every chip we deal — it must be removed in one turn or avoided entirely; Scald chip lines are strictly negative against drain moves.
A Pokemon at 1 HP has exactly one useful action: use it on the first turn it is at 1 HP (Tailwind/Encore/finisher), not three turns later.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp: the loss was a boosted-sweeper focus-fire failure, not an item issue, and Scarf Garchomp remains our only answer that outspeeds +2 Mega Golisopod after Tailwind expires.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed, and consider Milotic's Scald -> Haze is NOT needed; instead give Whimsicott Light Screen over Moonblast is rejected — keep Moonblast. The single highest-value change remains Extreme Speed on Dragonite as a +2 priority finisher.
teamInspiration.reason: grynpup's engine was 'boost behind a bulky body, then drain-heal through our chip' (Swords Dance Mega Golisopod + Leech Life). Our team has zero way to finish a boosted foe before it moves once Tailwind is gone; Extreme Speed on Dragonite converts chipped boosted sweepers (Golisopod at 31%, Basculegion at 44%) regardless of their speed, and overlaps with nothing else since Charizard-Y already provides sun Heat Wave.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit + Charizard-Y lead into Psychic Terrain was the correct 'must-come' pairing: Kowtow Cleave ignored Indeedee's Follow Me redirection target choice (we hit it directly) and OHKO'd the terrain setter on turn 1, while Weather Ball chipped it through Follow Me. Kingambit's Psychic immunity blanked two Expanding Forces outright (T2 and T3), making Hatterene's only real attacking option useless. Heat Wave in sun OHKO'd Sinistcha through Rage Powder redirection, and Kowtow Cleave removed Hatterene under their own Trick Room. Defiant converted Salamence's Intimidate into +2 Attack (T2 end), which turned Kowtow Cleave into an 84% hit on Mega Salamence. Protecting Drogon at 24% on T3 and then switching it out on T4 followed the 'Protected last turn and still threatened = switch' rule exactly. Result: 3-0 sweep with zero of our Pokemon fainted (log shows a mislabeled |win| line, but board state was 4 alive vs 1 at 16%).
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) 'Killing the opposing Mega/setter on its first active turn with a Protect-ignoring move (Kowtow Cleave) is our highest-EV turn-1 action' — done on Indeedee. (2) Kingambit lead vs Psychic Terrain per getLeadPreference('psyterrain'). (3) No overkill: T2 used Iron Head (100% accurate, no drops) on Hatterene instead of stacking spread damage, and Heat Wave was aimed so Sinistcha died while Hatterene took residual. (4) 'A slot that Protected last turn and still faces a displayed OHKO must SWITCH' — Drogon Protected T3, switched T4. (5) No Tailwind clicked into Trick Room. (6) Milotic Protect rather than a second redundant attack when Kingambit had a guaranteed KO (ahead-4v1 discipline).
analysis.whatFailed: Minor only. T1: Weather Ball was aimed at Hatterene in the stated reasoning but resolved into Indeedee because of Follow Me — that was a lucky non-error; the engine/Claude did not account for Follow Me redirection in its displayed calc, which is a systematic blind spot (Follow Me/Rage Powder makes any single-target move at the partner a wasted action). T2: Iron Head was declared vs Hatterene (101-149% OHKO) but Rage Powder redirected it into Sinistcha for only 49% — a half-wasted action; Kowtow Cleave or targeting through the redirect was never considered, and we got bailed out because Heat Wave (spread, ignores redirection) finished Sinistcha anyway. So two consecutive turns our single-target calcs were invalid because of an active redirector. Also Drogon dropped to 24% on T2 from an Expanding Force it could have avoided had we recognized Kingambit's immunity meant Hatterene would aim at the Charizard slot.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard-code redirection awareness: when any live foe has Follow Me / Rage Powder / Storm Drain / Lightning Rod active or on its sheet, all single-target moves must be scored as if they hit the redirector, and spread moves (Heat Wave, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Dazzling Gleam) get a large bonus because they ignore redirection. Second: when our Kingambit is Psychic-immune on the board, assume the opposing Psychic attacker will aim its Expanding Force at the OTHER slot — that slot should Protect or be the one that switches, not the immune one. Third: keep sheltering Drogon behind Kingambit vs Psychic Terrain; the Kingambit|Charizard psyterrain plan is now 9-6 and should be the default.

proposals.change: REDIRECTION GUARD: if any live foe used Follow Me/Rage Powder last turn or has it on its sheet and is not fainted, block single-target attacking moves aimed at the NON-redirector foe (they will be redirected), and give spread moves (Heat Wave, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Dazzling Gleam, Make It Rain) +2.0 score since spread moves ignore redirection.
proposals.evidence: T1 Weather Ball declared vs Hatterene hit Indeedee (Follow Me); T2 Iron Head declared vs Hatterene (101-149% OHKO) hit Sinistcha for 49% (Rage Powder). Two of five turns had invalid damage calcs.

proposals.change: IMMUNE-SLOT INFERENCE: when one of our actives is immune to the foe's primary STAB (Kingambit vs Psychic/Expanding Force, Flying vs Ground, Dark vs Prankster), treat the OTHER slot as the designated target for that attacker and bias it toward Protect/switch rather than attacking into a displayed >=70% roll.
proposals.evidence: T2 Hatterene's Expanding Force bounced off Kingambit and still took Drogon from 100% to 24% (76%), forcing a Protect turn and a switch on T3-T4.

proposals.change: Lock Kingambit|Charizard (zk) as the default psyterrain plan over Dragonite|zw and Charizard|zw.
proposals.evidence: Learned plan table: psyterrain Charizard|zk 8-6 (now 9-6) vs Dragonite|zw 2-7 and Dragonite|zk 0-3.

lessons: Follow Me / Rage Powder invalidates every single-target damage calc on the board: against an active redirector, click spread moves (Heat Wave, Earthquake, Rock Slide) or attack the redirector itself — never a declared single-target KO on its partner.

When one of our actives is immune to the foe's main attack (Kingambit vs Expanding Force), the foe will aim at the other slot: that slot, not the immune one, is the one that needs Protect or a switch.
Kingambit + Charizard-Y is the confirmed default lead vs Psychic Terrain: Kowtow Cleave OHKOs Indeedee through Follow Me positioning and Psychic immunity blanks the whole turn.
Defiant turning an opposing Mega Salamence Intimidate into +2 Attack is a real win condition — do not switch Kingambit out just because an Intimidate user arrives.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Copy their redirection shell in spirit: Indeedee Follow Me + Sinistcha Rage Powder bought two full turns of action denial. Our structural counter is spread damage, so keep Heat Wave on Charizard-Y, but swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant) for Extreme Speed as a +2 priority single-target finisher that converts chipped foes without caring about speed; and consider Garchomp's Rock Slide staying over Stomping Tantrum since spread moves ignore Follow Me/Rage Powder entirely.
teamInspiration.reason: Both turns where our single-target calc was invalid this game were caused by redirection; our only clean answers were spread moves (Heat Wave KO'd Sinistcha through Rage Powder) and priority. Extreme Speed also closes the recurring pattern of chipped sweepers (Salamence at 16%, Volcarona at 14%, Espathra at 1%) surviving to take a piece.

analysis.whatWorked: Won 3-1 in 3 turns. Preview read was correct: vs a Torkoal/Sinistcha/Slowbro Trick Room + Pyroar sun shell, bringing Whimsicott + Kingambit + Garchomp + Milotic and holding both Megas back was fine. Turn 1 Whimsicott Moonblast OHKO'd Pangoro (Fake Out/Parting Shot disruptor) and Kingambit Iron Head took their Whimsicott to 1 HP through Focus Sash, pre-empting Tailwind. Turn 2 the switch of 36% Whimsicott into Milotic (Fire resist) was a textbook defensive safe play vs Mega Pyroar Heat Wave. Turn 3 Garchomp Earthquake was correct spread usage next to Milotic (no Kingambit on field), finishing the 1% Whimsicott and leaving Pyroar at 8% for Scald to close.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: never EQ next to Kingambit (Kingambit was already fainted, Milotic took only partial spread damage which was acceptable); switched a threatened piece rather than attacking into a displayed >=100% roll (Whimsicott -> Milotic on T2); did not click Tailwind into a Trick Room team; removed the opposing speed-control setter (their Whimsicott) before it could refresh Tailwind. Violated/at risk: the T1 engine fallback left Kingambit on the field against a freshly-Mega'd Pyroar with spread Heat Wave shown at 41-59% + residual, and we did not Protect or reposition it — Kingambit died to a 90% Heat Wave roll, our only loss of the game. Also, the T1 fallback (rate limit) chose Iron Head into a Focus Sash Whimsicott rather than finishing it with the spread-safe option, meaning their Tailwind still went up on T2.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) Kingambit lost for free on turn 2: a Mega Pyroar with a spread Fire move was revealed on the board and Kingambit was listed at 41-59% from Heat Wave, but it had already taken 20 Life Orb recoil and 99 damage was pending; the displayed roll plus chip made it a realistic KO and we neither Protected nor switched the slot we were NOT saving. We saved Whimsicott (36%) and let the Life-Orb-chipped Kingambit eat the spread. 2) Turn 1 fallback fired because of API rate limiting — the engine-only line let their Whimsicott survive on 1 HP via Sash and set Tailwind, handing the opponent speed control for a turn. 3) Minor: Garchomp Earthquake on T3 clipped Milotic for 70 HP when Dragon Claw/Rock Slide alternatives existed; it was still correct because EQ hit both live foes, but the ally damage should be priced in. 4) Damage model again under-rated our hit (EQ -> Pyroar predicted 55-86%, actual 92%).
analysis.howToImprove: Treat a revealed Mega Fire/spread attacker exactly like a revealed Rock attacker: every slot of ours that is already chipped (Life Orb recoil counts) must Protect or switch on the turn the spread move can roll into KO range, not just the slot with the lower raw HP. When two of our slots are both inside the spread's KO band, prefer the switch on the one with a resist available and the Protect on the other instead of attacking with both. Second, when a Focus Sash support (Whimsicott/Glimmora) is at 1 HP, the following turn's cheapest action — any residual, any spread, any priority — must close it before it sets Tailwind; do not let a 1 HP Prankster setter get a free turn. Third, keep ahead-in-count discipline: at 3v2 with Scarf Garchomp live, prefer the 100% accurate line (we did).

proposals.change: SPREAD-FIRE KO BAND: when any live foe has a spread Fire/Rock/Ice/Ground move and our active slot's current HP is below (max displayed roll + 15% chip buffer), that slot must Protect or switch — apply to BOTH slots independently, including Life-Orb-chipped Kingambit, not just the visibly lowest-HP slot.
proposals.evidence: T2 Kingambit at 187/207 with Heat Wave shown at 41-59% took 90% and fainted; we only repositioned Whimsicott.

proposals.change: SASH-SETTER FINISHER: if an opposing Prankster/support Pokemon is at <=5% HP and has Tailwind/Trick Room/Follow Me on its sheet, at least one of our actions must target it (any damage, including spread) until it faints — block pure Protect/setup turns while it is alive.
proposals.evidence: Their 1 HP Whimsicott got a free Tailwind on T2 and then Moonblasted Garchomp for 85% on T3.

proposals.change: ALLY-SPREAD PRICE: subtract a small score penalty from Earthquake/Heat Wave when it hits a living ally for >25% unless it KOs two foes or is the only KO line; favour single-target when one foe is already in range of the partner's move.
proposals.evidence: T3 Earthquake clipped Milotic for 70 HP; Milotic ended the game at 122/202 in a 2v0.

lessons: A revealed Mega with a spread Fire/Rock/Ice move puts BOTH our slots in the KO band — Life Orb recoil counts as chip, so a 90% HP Kingambit is already inside a 41-59% Heat Wave roll plus residual and must Protect or switch.
An opposing Focus Sash support at 1 HP must be finished with any available action (spread/residual/priority) the very next turn — never let a 1 HP Prankster Tailwind setter act.
When a spread attacker threatens both slots, save the chipped attacker (Protect) and switch the one with a type resist — do not spend both actions on offense.

itemExperiment.reason: Kingambit has now died 132 times and in this game Life Orb recoil (20 HP) is literally the difference between surviving and fainting to a 90% Heat Wave roll; Clear Amulet removes self-chip pressure and blocks Intimidate stat games, worth a short trial given scarf_garchomp sits at 46%.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their Whimsicott + Focus Sash guaranteed a Tailwind turn even at 1 HP — the same pattern that keeps burning us. Mirror the lesson by swapping Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed: a +2 priority single-target finisher closes 1-HP Sash setters, chipped Megas (Pyroar at 8%) and boosted sweepers before they act, and it ignores Tailwind/Trick Room entirely.
teamInspiration.reason: Across the last six games the deciding pattern has been a foe surviving at 1-20% and getting one more action (Whimsicott Tailwind, Pyroar Heat Wave, Golisopod Leech Life, Volcarona Fiery Dance). Our team has zero priority outside Kingambit's Sucker Punch, which fails against status/Protect and Psychic Terrain.

analysis.whatWorked: Heat Wave as a spread move correctly ignored Rage Powder/redirection fears and KO'd Rillaboom on T2; Milotic's Ice Beam cleanly finished the chipped Dragapult on T3. Preview reasoning (Kingambit immune to Farigiraf Psychic, Charizard-Y torches Volcarona) was sound in the abstract.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The redirection-guard lesson (prefer spread moves) was applied. The 'foe that boosts becomes mandatory focus-fire' rule was partially applied — Kowtow Cleave went at Volcarona T1. However the durable lesson 'Volcarona at +1 OHKOs Kingambit with a Fire special move — never leave Kingambit in front of a boosted/strong Fire special attacker without Protect or a switch' was VIOLATED on turn 1 at 0 boosts: Volcarona Overheat OHKO'd a 207 HP Kingambit from full. The SPREAD-FIRE KO BAND proposal (any live foe with a spread Fire move puts our slot in the KO band) was also violated for the Rillaboom slot on T2.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) LEAD ERROR: we led Kingambit (Dark/Steel, 4x weak to Fire) directly into a revealed Volcarona on a team sheet that also held Rillaboom. Volcarona Overheat OHKO'd it turn 1 before it ever attacked — our entire turn-1 damage plan assumed Kingambit would act. Our own threat display even failed to list Volcarona Overheat as a threat to Kingambit, so the engine never saw the OHKO. 2) T2: we sacrificed Rillaboom into the same Overheat (it had just OHKO'd a 207 HP Steel type; a 207 HP Grass type was a guaranteed corpse) for 21-24% of chip. That is a whole Pokemon traded for nothing — Rillaboom should have switched or Protected. 3) T3: Drogon at 96/153 with a live Dragapult (Draco Meteor 52-92%) plus a live Volcarona Overheat was inside the combined KO band and attacked instead of Protecting; it died. 4) We never set Tailwind or Trick-Room-denial at all; 0 speed control the whole game while they outsped every turn. 5) Net: 4-0 loss in 4 turns, all four of our Pokemon died to Fire/Grass attacks we had already measured.
analysis.howToImprove: Hard rule: if ANY opposing team-sheet Pokemon is a Fire-type special attacker (Volcarona, Pyroar, Torkoal, Camerupt, Chi-Yu, Armarouge), Kingambit must NOT be a lead and must never be on the field unprotected while that Fire attacker is active — Kingambit is 4x weak and dies through its 207 HP. Against Volcarona specifically, Charizard-Y + Milotic (Fire resist + Scald/Ice Beam) or Garchomp (Rock Slide) are the correct leads. Second: when a foe one-shots a 207 HP Steel type, treat every subsequent slot as in the OHKO band — Protect or switch, never feed a second body for 20% chip. Third: fix the threat model so 4x type multipliers are always computed from the sheet, not only from revealed moves.

proposals.change: FIRE-WEAK LEAD BAN: never lead or keep Kingambit on the field while any opposing Fire-type special attacker (Volcarona, Pyroar, Torkoal, Chi-Yu, Armarouge, Camerupt, Charizard) is active or on the sheet unless Kingambit is Protecting or the Fire mon is already KO'd. Block attacking moves from a 4x-weak slot when that foe is active and faster.
proposals.evidence: T1: Volcarona Overheat OHKO'd a full-HP 207 HP Kingambit before it acted; our threat list did not even display the threat, so the engine led into a guaranteed 0-for-1.

proposals.change: OHKO-PRECEDENT RULE: once a foe has KO'd one of our Pokemon from full HP in a single hit, every one of our actives that is neutral-or-worse to that move type must Protect or switch on the following turn — never attack into it for sub-30% chip.
proposals.evidence: T2: Rillaboom (207 HP) was sent into the same Volcarona Overheat that just OHKO'd Kingambit and died while dealing 21-24%.

proposals.change: Drop Rillaboom from the bring list against any Fire-heavy/sun/Trick-Room board; Milotic is the correct Fire sponge and we already own it.
proposals.evidence: Rillaboom was brought into a board with Volcarona + Charizard-Y-class Fire pressure and contributed 0 damage before dying.

lessons: Volcarona Overheat OHKOs a full-HP 207 HP Kingambit at 0 boosts — Kingambit is 4x weak to Fire and must never lead into or stand in front of any Fire special attacker.
When a foe OHKOs one of our Pokemon from full HP, the next Pokemon we send into that same attack dies too: Protect or switch, never trade a body for sub-30% chip.
If a game reaches turn 3 with zero speed control set and zero foes KO'd by us, we are already losing — prioritise Tailwind or a removal KO over chip.
Our threat display must compute 4x weaknesses from the opposing team sheet, not only from revealed moves; an undisplayed OHKO caused this entire loss.

itemExperiment.reason: Clear Amulet Kingambit is 1-3 (25%) and died turn 1 to a Fire move that Clear Amulet does nothing about; Scarf Garchomp (45-52) gives us the Rock Slide speed answer to Volcarona/Pyroar that this loss exposed.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Their win condition was a single 4x-coverage special move (Volcarona Overheat) deleting our Steel/Dark and Grass bodies regardless of their bulk. Mirror this: swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) for Extreme Speed as a +2 priority finisher, and prefer Garchomp's Rock Slide as the dedicated Volcarona/Pyroar answer — Rock Slide 4x's Volcarona and ignores its Quiver Dance speed.
teamInspiration.reason: Volcarona at 31% and 25% HP got three free Overheats across the game because we had zero priority and zero faster answer; Extreme Speed or a Scarf Rock Slide removes it on any of those turns.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit + Mega Charizard-Y lead into Psychic Terrain (psyterrain / Charizard|zk) delivered a clean 4-0 win over Gellapo in 5 turns. Kingambit was immune to Expanding Force and Kowtow Cleave ignored Milotic's Protect-timing by pressuring every turn; Drogon's Drought turned Weather Ball into a 150 BP nuke that OHKO'd Indeedee, Hydrapple and Mega-bulk Golisopod. Turn 4's declared double-KO (Kowtow on Milotic at 42% + Weather Ball on Hydrapple at 33%) was textbook 2-action economy: two actions, two KOs, no overlap. Turn 5 Protect on a 25% HP Kingambit while Drogon took the guaranteed last KO was correct safe-play-when-ahead discipline.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: (1) psyterrain default plan Kingambit|Charizard (zk) — the locked preview proposal, now 9-6 lifetime; (2) focus-fire the Psychic Terrain setter immediately (Indeedee dead T2); (3) no double-target overlap — each slot always had its own target; (4) when ahead 4v1 the non-finisher slot Protected rather than attacking (coach note: 'when ahead with a finisher on the field, the partner's correct action is Protect'); (5) no Sucker Punch clicked into Psychic Terrain. Violated/soft: T3 Kowtow Cleave went into Milotic's Protect — Milotic had already shown Recover at T2 and was at 30% and obviously threatened, so Protect was highly predictable; that was a wasted action in the 2-action economy (the Protect-prediction rule says attack the OTHER slot when their Protect is obvious). Kingambit also ate a 59% Earth Power from Hydrapple that turn and fell to 45/207 — the immune-slot-inference proposal would have flagged Kingambit as the Ground-move target and biased it toward Protect/switch.
analysis.whatFailed: Only one real error, but a recurring one: T3 both of our actions were spent as if Milotic could not Protect. Milotic at 30% HP with Recover already revealed is the single most predictable Protect on the board; Kowtow Cleave hit the shield and we traded a full action for zero damage while Hydrapple removed 59% of Kingambit. The correct T3 line was Kingambit Protect (dodging Earth Power, it is 4x-relevant special pressure on a Life-Orb-chipped body) or Kingambit attacking Hydrapple alongside Weather Ball to delete the Ground attacker outright. We also never used Whimsicott/Milotic — fine given the speed of the win, but it means no Tailwind data. Macro-wise nothing was lost; the game was won on turn 4.
analysis.howToImprove: Codify a PREDICTABLE-PROTECT rule: when a foe is below ~45% HP, is in declared KO range of our move, and has Protect/Detect on its sheet or has already used Recover/Protect this game, do not aim a single-target KO at it two turns in a row — either spread into it, target the partner, or Protect the slot that is being threatened. Pair this with the immune-slot inference: when Kingambit is immune to one foe's STAB, the OTHER live foe (Hydrapple Earth Power) is the one aiming at Kingambit, so Kingambit's HP must be checked against that roll before attacking. Keep the zk lead vs psyterrain — it is now the best-performing psyterrain plan by a wide margin.

proposals.change: PREDICTABLE-PROTECT GUARD: if a foe is at <=45% HP, is in our displayed KO range, and has Protect/Detect/Recover revealed or already protected once this battle, penalize aiming a second consecutive single-target move at it; prefer spread damage, the partner slot, or Protect/switch on our threatened slot.
proposals.evidence: T3 vs Gellapo: Kingambit Kowtow Cleave (49-64% KO declared) into a 30% Milotic that had just used Recover — Milotic Protected, our action was wasted, and Hydrapple Earth Power took Kingambit from 167/207 to 45/207 on the same turn.

proposals.change: Extend IMMUNE-SLOT INFERENCE into a concrete HP check: when our slot is immune/resistant to foe A's STAB, compute foe B's best roll on that slot; if current HP < max roll, that slot must Protect or switch instead of attacking.
proposals.evidence: Kingambit was immune to Indeedee/Psychic but Hydrapple's Earth Power (declared 45-69%) was the real threat; Kingambit dropped to 12% HP on a turn where its own attack did nothing.

proposals.change: Keep Kingambit|Charizard-Y (zk) as the hard default for psyterrain and stop offering Dragonite|zk there (0-3).
proposals.evidence: psyterrain plans: Charizard|zk 9-6, Charizard|zw 10-12, Dragonite|zw 2-7, Dragonite|zk 0-3.

lessons: A foe at <=45% HP that has already revealed Recover or Protect will almost always Protect the turn we declare a KO on it — aim the second action at its partner or spread into both, never two consecutive single-target KOs at the obvious shield.

When one of our slots is immune to one foe's STAB, the OTHER foe's best roll is the number that decides whether that slot attacks, Protects, or switches — check it explicitly before clicking an attack.

Charizard-Y Weather Ball in self-made sun is our highest-value single-target button: it OHKO'd a Mega Golisopod, a full-HP Hydrapple and a chipped Indeedee in one game — prefer it over Heat Wave once only one relevant foe is left on that side.
Kingambit + Charizard-Y remains the confirmed best lead vs Psychic Terrain (9-6); Dragonite leads into psyterrain are 2-10 and should not be offered.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Gellapo's bulky Milotic (Recover + Protect) stalled two of our actions on 202 HP; mirror that durability tax by keeping Recover-Protect Milotic but shifting Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave (fully redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave) to Extreme Speed, giving us a +2 priority finisher that closes Protect-cycling bulky walls and 1-HP Sash setters the turn they drop.
teamInspiration.reason: Our only wasted action this game was a single-target KO attempt into a predictable Protect; priority damage ignores the Protect-timing game entirely and is the one tool this team still lacks (confirmed across the grynpup, Suttirak, Lawliet0 and appledragon3 reviews).

whatWorked: Milotic's Protect on turns 2 and 4 correctly blanked two guaranteed Wood Hammer OHKOs, and Whimsicott's Moonblast finished burned Mega Froslass on turn 4. Scald's turn-1 burn on Froslass was the single most valuable chip of the game — it did ~21% residual and set up the Moonblast KO. Tailwind was established turn 1 and gave us speed advantage for most of the game.
lessonsApplied: Protect discipline on the slot that was in a declared OHKO band was applied correctly twice. The 1-HP rule was applied (Whimsicott at 1 HP was given an action rather than Protect-stalling) — though it was then deleted by Fake Out before acting, which is the predictable failure mode of that rule against an Incineroar that had not yet been on the field. The Tailwind-vs-Trick-Room rule was irrelevant here. We violated the OHKO-PRECEDENT rule: after Wood Hammer showed a 139-183% roll on Milotic on turn 2, we left Milotic in on turn 5 to click Ice Beam and it died.
whatFailed: 1) Turn 1 was an API-fallback engine turn and it led Milotic+Dragonite into a snow/Aurora Veil board — the Mega was used turn 1 on the exposed slot and Multiscale was broken on turn 2 by Blizzard (82%). 2) Turn 3 Dragonite at 18% HP attacked instead of switching/Protecting into a declared Rillaboom Wood Hammer and died — direct OHKO-PRECEDENT violation and loss of our Mega for zero return. 3) Turn 5 Milotic clicked Ice Beam for 22-27% chip while sitting in a declared 139-183% Wood Hammer band: we traded our best wall for chip. Tailwind was re-set on the same turn with Whimsicott instead of Protecting the 1-HP-bound setter, and Tailwind had almost no remaining value (only Basculegion and a dying Rillaboom left). 4) Heat Wave missed on turn 2 (90% accuracy) — the known variance tax. 5) We never brought Charizard-Y to reset Snowscape to Sun, which would have halved Blizzard and disabled Aurora Veil pressure; against a Froslass snow team that is the structural answer. 6) Three of six damage calcs came in above predicted range (Rillaboom especially) — our Rillaboom bulk/offense model is too low.
howToImprove: Against Froslass/snow, Mega Charizard-Y must come: Drought overwrites Snowscape, kills Blizzard's accuracy boost and the Aurora Veil setup pressure. Never lead Mega Dragonite into a Blizzard board. Enforce the OHKO-PRECEDENT rule as a hard block: once a foe's move has a displayed >=100% roll on our slot, that slot may only Protect or switch. Stop re-clicking Tailwind when it is already up or when only one slow foe remains. Treat a 1-HP Pokemon as dead to any priority user on the board — if an unrevealed Incineroar/Fake Out user is on their sheet, assume it comes in and that the 1-HP slot gets zero actions; spend the turn elsewhere or switch it.

proposals.change: HARD OHKO-BAND BLOCK: if the displayed threat line shows a foe move with a max roll >= our slot's current HP, block all attacking moves from that slot — only Protect or switch are legal.
proposals.evidence: Dragonite at 18% attacked into a declared 139-183% Wood Hammer and died (T3); Milotic at 100% clicked Ice Beam into the same declared OHKO band and died (T5).

proposals.change: TAILWIND REDUNDANCY BLOCK: block Tailwind if our side already has Tailwind active with >=2 turns left, or if the only living foes are all slower than our active slots.
proposals.evidence: T5 Whimsicott re-set Tailwind (already active from T1, and only Rillaboom/Basculegion left) instead of Protecting; Whimsicott then died to Fake Out with Tailwind wasted.

proposals.change: Add a 'snow' lead override: vs Froslass/Abomasnow/Alolan-Ninetales always bring Mega Charizard-Y (Drought overwrites Snowscape) and never lead Mega Dragonite.
proposals.evidence: Snow record 4-8; this game Mega Dragonite was OHKO-ranged by veil-boosted Blizzard and died turn 3 without Charizard ever appearing.

proposals.change: Replace Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave with Extreme Speed (+2 priority finisher).
proposals.evidence: Fifth consecutive game decided by a foe surviving at low HP and acting (Rillaboom at 15%, Froslass at 31%, Basculegion); Heat Wave is fully redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave and missed at the critical moment on T2.

lessons: Against any Snowscape team (Froslass-Mega, Abomasnow, Ninetales-A), Mega Charizard-Y is mandatory: Drought overwrites snow, removing Blizzard's perfect accuracy and the Aurora Veil tempo.
Once a foe's displayed damage roll on our slot has a maximum >= our current HP, that slot must Protect or switch — attacking for chip is a strict loss (Dragonite T3, Milotic T5).
Never re-click Tailwind while our own Tailwind is still active, and never set it when every remaining foe is slower than our actives.
A Pokemon at 1 HP is worth zero actions if the opponent has any unrevealed Fake Out / priority user on their team sheet — assume it gets deleted and spend the turn elsewhere.
Our damage model systematically underrates Rillaboom (3 calcs high this game): treat Wood Hammer/Grassy Glide as ~20% stronger than displayed and Rillaboom as bulkier than assumed.

itemExperiment.reason: Scarf Garchomp is 46-53 and this game it was choice-locked into Stomping Tantrum against a Basculegion it could never beat; Sitrus gives survivability against Last Respects chip and lets Garchomp switch moves to Rock Slide/EQ as the board demands.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Mirror their Rillaboom + Basculegion 'chip-then-Last-Respects' engine: swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed as a +2 priority finisher, and consider Milotic's Protect -> Haze is NOT needed; instead keep Protect but shift Whimsicott's Encore usage earlier against Aurora Veil setters.
teamInspiration.reason: Their win condition was that every one of our chipped attackers got one more free turn while their Rillaboom/Basculegion closed. Last Respects scaled with our faints — we had no way to finish a 15% Rillaboom or a 44% Basculegion before it acted. Extreme Speed solves exactly that and overlaps with nothing since Charizard-Y already owns sun Heat Wave.

analysis.whatWorked: Won 4-1 in Pokémon count vs gogogadgetnuke's Alolan-Ninetales snow team. Turn 1 Prankster Tailwind landed before Ninetales acted, giving us 3 speed-control turns. Recognizing the Encore lock on Whimsicott and immediately switching it to Kingambit (T2) was the correct 'switch when Encored into a useless move' play from the standing rules. Kingambit Iron Head/Kowtow Cleave removed Rillaboom through Grassy Terrain recovery, and Milotic was the MVP: +2 SpA from Incineroar's Intimidate (Competitive) turned Ice Beam into a clean OHKO on Mega Dragonite and Scald into an OHKO on Incineroar. Milotic Protect on T4 blanked Rillaboom's Fake Out while Kingambit got the free Kowtow KO — a textbook 'Attack Slot A + Protect Slot B' turn. Endgame Moonblast finishing at 1 HP Whimsicott was correct use of the 1-HP action rule.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Applied: (1) Encore -> switch out rule executed perfectly on T2. (2) Milotic as Intimidate-punisher (Competitive) was honored and decided the game. (3) The 'Pokemon at 1 HP has one useful action — use it now' rule: Whimsicott at 1 HP attacked immediately on T7 and got the final KO. (4) Spread-vs-redirect/Protect discipline was fine. VIOLATED: the snow lead override from the active proposal list ('vs Froslass/Abomasnow/Alolan-Ninetales always bring Mega Charizard-Y, never lead Mega Dragonite') was ignored — we brought Mega Dragonite into Snowscape and it died on turn 2 to Draco Meteor without Charizard's Drought ever resetting the weather. Also the 'Protect Mega Dragonite's Multiscale from chip' rule was effectively violated: Heat Wave into a mirror Dragonite + Blizzard chip broke Multiscale and the mirror Mega one-shot ours.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) PLAN ERROR: brought Mega Dragonite vs an Alolan-Ninetales snow team. The standing snow rule says Charizard-Y is mandatory (Drought overwrites Snowscape, removing Blizzard's 100% accuracy and the Aurora Veil tempo). We lost our Mega for free on turn 2. 2) T1 Heat Wave spread chipped their Dragonite by 7% but, critically, revealed/committed our Mega into a mirror matchup where their Mega Dragonite outspeeds post-Tailwind and Draco Meteor OHKOs a Multiscale-broken Dragonite. The correct T1 was Tailwind + Protect (or Heat Wave aimed with Dragonite behind Protect) because Ninetales Blizzard showed a 79-136% OHKO roll on Dragonite — our own threat display literally printed 'OHKO 63%' and we attacked anyway. That is the HARD OHKO-BAND violation again. 3) T2 we stayed in with Dragonite at 168 HP into a board where Blizzard + Draco Meteor was lethal; the switch should have been Dragonite out, not Whimsicott out (Whimsicott Encored into Tailwind was harmless; it could have sat there). 4) T3 Milotic Ice Beam was fired into an obvious Protect from a Dragonite that had just taken a Mega-vs-Mega trade and was the only foe we threatened — exactly the PREDICTABLE-PROTECT pattern on our proposal list. 5) We burned 2 of 8 Claude calls on rate-limit fallbacks, including team preview, which is how the wrong Mega got brought at all.
analysis.howToImprove: 1) Hard-code the snow lead override: any Froslass / Abomasnow / Ninetales-Alola / Snow Warning on the opposing sheet => Mega Charizard-Y mandatory, Mega Dragonite never leads and preferably stays home. Drought replacing Snowscape is worth more than any single Heat Wave. 2) Enforce the OHKO-band block in code so even the engine fallback honours it: if a displayed foe move's max roll >= our slot's current HP, that slot may only Protect or switch. This would have saved Dragonite on T1/T2. 3) Add a Multiscale guard: Mega Dragonite at full HP facing any spread Ice/Rock move should prefer Protect over a 7-12% chip spread. 4) Add the predictable-Protect penalty: foe that just Mega-traded / is the lone threatened target and has Protect revealed => do not aim a second single-target KO at it. 5) Keep leaning on Milotic vs Intimidate teams — it is our highest-value piece against Incineroar cores and should be an auto-bring there.

proposals.change: SNOW HARD OVERRIDE: if the opposing sheet contains Ninetales-Alola, Abomasnow, Froslass, or any Snow Warning user, Mega Charizard-Y is mandatory and Mega Dragonite must not be brought as the Mega; lead Charizard + Whimsicott (Tailwind).
proposals.evidence: vs gogogadgetnuke we brought Mega Dragonite into Snowscape; it was OHKO'd on T2 by a mirror Mega Dragonite Draco Meteor after Blizzard chip broke Multiscale. Drought was never deployed, so Blizzard kept perfect accuracy all game.

proposals.change: HARD OHKO-BAND BLOCK (re-assert, now in shouldBlockMove so the engine fallback obeys it): when a displayed foe move's maximum roll >= our slot's current HP and we are slower, block attacking moves from that slot — Protect or switch only.
proposals.evidence: T1 threat display read 'Dragonite threatened by Ninetales Blizzard (79-136% (OHKO 63%))' and we clicked Heat Wave anyway; Dragonite died on T2.

proposals.change: MULTISCALE GUARD: Mega Dragonite at 100% HP facing a revealed spread Ice/Rock/Fairy move should weight Protect +1.2 rather than firing a <=15% spread chip.
proposals.evidence: T1 Heat Wave dealt 7-12% to their Dragonite and 32-59% to Ninetales but cost us Multiscale integrity the following turn.

proposals.change: Make Milotic an auto-bring against any team sheet with Incineroar, Salamence, Arcanine-H or Landorus (Intimidate users): Competitive +2 converted Ice Beam and Scald into back-to-back OHKOs this game.
proposals.evidence: T4 Incineroar switch-in gave Milotic +2 SpA; T5 Ice Beam OHKO'd Mega Dragonite (94%), T6 Scald OHKO'd Incineroar (85%).

lessons: Alolan Ninetales / Froslass / Abomasnow on the opposing sheet makes Mega Charizard-Y mandatory — Drought removes Snowscape, Blizzard's perfect accuracy and Aurora Veil tempo in one move; never spend the Mega slot on Dragonite there.
A mirror Mega (their Dragonite vs ours) is decided by who keeps Multiscale: never spend turn 1 on a 7-12% spread chip when the threat display shows an OHKO roll on our own Mega.
Encore on Whimsicott is a free switch signal, but check WHICH slot is actually dying — we switched the Encored-but-safe Whimsicott and left the OHKO-threatened Dragonite in.
Milotic + Competitive is a win condition against any Intimidate team: it converted a single Incineroar switch-in into two consecutive OHKOs.
Do not aim a single-target KO at the only threatened foe the turn after a Mega trade — Protect is their highest-value button there (T3 Ice Beam blanked).

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Choice Scarf Garchomp: snow/Tailwind matchups are decided by having one naturally fast revenge killer once speed control expires, and Garchomp was not brought this game — no evidence to change the active loadout.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Mirror their Ninetales-Alola 'weather + Encore' disruption: give Whimsicott more value by keeping Encore (it locked our Tailwind the same way theirs did) and swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed, since Charizard-Y already owns sun Heat Wave and we twice needed a priority finisher on a 3-10% Ninetales and a 1-HP setter.
teamInspiration.reason: Their Ninetales survived at 3% and 10% HP for two extra turns and got a Helping Hand Blizzard off that nearly took Whimsicott and Milotic; a +2 priority finisher on Mega Dragonite closes those exact windows and does not overlap with any existing move.

analysis.whatWorked: Kowtow Cleave OHKO'd the Mega Froslass on turn 3, removing Aurora Veil/Blizzard pressure, and the Protect discipline on Kingambit (T4, T7) correctly honored the OHKO-band rule against +2 Sneasler Close Combat. Turn-1 Whimsicott Protect blanked both a Blizzard and a Dire Claw. Tailwind went up turn 1.
analysis.lessonsApplied: The hard OHKO-band block was followed (Kingambit Protect T4, Dragonite Protect T6). Snow override was effectively ignored — Mega Dragonite was brought as the Mega into a Froslass snow team, directly violating the standing 'vs Snowscape, Mega Charizard-Y is mandatory (Drought overwrites snow)' rule, and Dragonite was immediately chunked to 29% by Blizzard and never recovered. The 'punish setup immediately' rule was violated: Sneasler used Swords Dance on T4 with zero pressure applied because both our slots were passive (Protect + flinched Garchomp).
analysis.whatFailed: 1) MEGA CHOICE: brought Mega Dragonite into Froslass snow; Snowscape kept Blizzard at 100% accuracy and Aurora Veil up, and Dragonite lost 71% on T1. Charizard-Y's Drought deletes snow, Blizzard accuracy and Aurora Veil in one action. 2) We clicked single-target attacks into Sneasler's Protect on BOTH T3 and T5 — four wasted actions out of eight. Sneasler had already Protected on T3; re-declaring a single-target KO at the same obvious shield on T5 is the exact coach rule we keep breaking. 3) After Sneasler hit +2 Swords Dance it was never removed; we had no answer and it closed the game. 4) Garchomp was left in front of a full-HP Rillaboom (Wood Hammer 58-101%) with no Protect and died on T5 while its attack whiffed into Protect. 5) We never had a clean turn where both actions produced damage after T3.
analysis.howToImprove: Enforce the snow override at preview: if the sheet contains Froslass/Abomasnow/Ninetales-A, Mega must be Charizard-Y, lead Charizard + Whimsicott. Build a Protect-tracker: a foe that used Protect last turn and is under an announced KO threat should NOT be the target of a second consecutive single-target attack — spread into it (Heat Wave/Earthquake/Rock Slide) or hit the partner. Against +2 Sneasler, Kingambit is physically immune to Dire Claw's Poison? No — it is not; instead focus Garchomp's Rock Slide (spread, ignores Protect-timing less but hits both) or simply hard-remove Rillaboom first so Grassy Glide/Wood Hammer stops killing our Ground slot.

proposals.change: SNOW HARD OVERRIDE (re-assert, enforce in getLeadPreference): any opposing sheet with Froslass, Abomasnow, Ninetales-Alola or Snow Warning forces Mega Charizard-Y and a Charizard+Whimsicott lead; Mega Dragonite is forbidden as the Mega.
proposals.evidence: Mega Dragonite lost 71% HP to a 100%-accurate Blizzard on T1 under Snowscape with Aurora Veil up and contributed 0 KOs; Drought would have removed snow, Blizzard accuracy and the Veil.

proposals.change: PROTECT-REPEAT BLOCK: if a foe used Protect/Detect on the immediately preceding turn AND our chosen move is single-target at that same foe, heavily penalize (-4) the move; prefer a spread move or target the partner.
proposals.evidence: Sneasler Protected on T3 and T5, eating Garchomp Stomping Tantrum twice plus Kingambit Iron Head — 3 wasted actions, and Garchomp died the same turn it whiffed.

proposals.change: SETUP PUNISH OVERRIDE: when a foe gains +2 Atk/SpA (Swords Dance/Nasty Plot/Quiver Dance), ban Protect on both of our slots for the following turn unless that slot is in the OHKO band, and force at least one spread move or focus attack at the booster.
proposals.evidence: Sneasler used Swords Dance on T4 while both our slots did nothing (Protect + flinch) and then closed out the game.

proposals.change: Replace Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave with Extreme Speed (+2 priority finisher).
proposals.evidence: Rillaboom sat at 16-29% for three turns and Sneasler Protect-cycled; a +2 priority finisher closes both windows and ignores Protect-timing on the follow-up turn.

lessons: Any opposing Froslass/Abomasnow/Alolan-Ninetales makes Mega Charizard-Y mandatory: Drought deletes Snowscape, Blizzard's 100% accuracy and Aurora Veil in one action — never spend the Mega slot on Dragonite there.
Never aim a second consecutive single-target attack at a foe that Protected last turn and is still the obvious KO target — use a spread move or hit the partner.
When a foe reaches +2 Attack (Swords Dance), both of our slots must not Protect that turn: at least one action has to pressure the booster or remove its partner.
Protect on one slot does not protect the other: leaving Garchomp in front of a full-HP Rillaboom Wood Hammer while Kingambit Protected was a free KO for the opponent.

itemExperiment.reason: Keep Scarf Garchomp: it is the only piece that outspeeds +2 Sneasler and Froslass without Tailwind; the loss came from Mega choice and Protect-whiffs, not the item.

teamInspiration.suggestion: Mirror Noobilio's Sneasler Protect-cycle + Swords Dance engine by giving ourselves a Protect-proof finisher: swap Mega Dragonite's Heat Wave for Extreme Speed, and keep Garchomp's Rock Slide as the designated anti-Sneasler/Froslass spread button (hits both slots so Protect only saves one).
teamInspiration.reason: Sneasler bought three free turns with Protect while Rillaboom Fake Out/Wood Hammer deleted our Ground slot; spread moves and +2 priority are the only two tools that do not lose value to Protect-timing, and Heat Wave on Dragonite is fully redundant with Charizard-Y sun Heat Wave.

analysis.whatWorked: Kingambit lead vs Farigiraf Trick Room was correct in principle; Mega Charizard-Y Heat Wave on T2 was the game-winning turn, double-KOing Farigiraf (the TR setter) and Tsareena (the Low Kick/Triple Axel threat) in one action — a perfect 2-for-1 under Trick Room. Milotic Protect on T2 and T3 correctly dodged Triple Axel/Eruption while the sun Heat Wave landed. The endgame 1v1 Milotic vs Clawitzer was played exactly right: Scald for the burn, then Recover-cycle attrition, converting a 1-mon deficit position into a win.
analysis.lessonsApplied: Followed: 'Protect Drogon when a foe that moves before us is likely to KO it' (T3 Protect vs Torkoal Eruption under TR). Followed: focus-fire the Trick Room setter (Farigiraf died T2). Followed: no Tailwind into Trick Room. Followed: Milotic bulky wall under TR. VIOLATED: the T1 engine fallback left Kingambit in front of Tsareena, which Low Kick OHKO'd (Kingambit is heavy = max Low Kick BP 120, and Fighting is 2x into Dark) — the threat display never flagged the Low Kick weight interaction. VIOLATED (T4): aimed a single-target Ancient Power at Torkoal while Drogon was inside Torkoal's Weather Ball OHKO band under Trick Room — the known 'OHKO-band block: Protect or switch, never trade' rule.
analysis.whatFailed: 1) T1 fallback (rate limit) chose Milotic Scald + Kingambit Kowtow into Farigiraf, ignoring that Tsareena's Low Kick OHKOs our 207-HP Kingambit; we lost our anti-TR piece on turn 1 for 30% chip. 2) T4: Drogon at 41% attacked instead of Protecting/switching into Torkoal's Weather Ball (sun-boosted Fire, 100 BP) under Trick Room — Torkoal moves first, so Drogon was dead before it could fire. The displayed threat only listed Clawitzer Dragon Pulse and omitted Torkoal Weather Ball entirely, even though Weather Ball had just been used. 3) T5: Garchomp was sent in and immediately died to Clawitzer Ice Beam (4x) — a known 4x matchup; Milotic should have been the lone body with Garchomp held back or we should have accepted the 1v2. We won anyway only because Milotic out-stalled Clawitzer. 4) Three rate-limit fallbacks/preview misses continue to cost whole turns.
analysis.howToImprove: a) Add a Low Kick/Heavy Slam weight rule: Kingambit (100 kg) takes max-BP Low Kick, so never leave Kingambit in front of a revealed/sheet Tsareena, Hariyama, Machamp or any Fighting user with Low Kick. b) Enforce the OHKO-band block using the foe's LAST USED move, not only sheet moves — Torkoal's Weather Ball had been used on T4's previous turn and still wasn't in the threat list. c) Under Trick Room, treat every slower-than-us foe as moving FIRST when computing the OHKO band; our Charizard at 41% was effectively 'slower' and had to Protect. d) Never switch Garchomp into an active Clawitzer/Ice-move user (4x); prefer Milotic or keep the slot empty-by-faint order. e) Sun Weather Ball from an opposing Torkoal is a 150-BP special Fire move — flag Charizard, Kingambit and Whimsicott as in-band immediately whenever Drought/Torkoal sun is up.

proposals.change: LOW KICK / HEAVY SLAM WEIGHT GUARD: never lead or leave Kingambit (100kg), Garchomp (95kg) or Drogon (100kg) in front of a revealed or sheet-listed Low Kick / Grass Knot user (Tsareena, Hariyama, Machamp, Rillaboom); treat Low Kick on Kingambit as a guaranteed OHKO and force Protect/switch.
proposals.evidence: T1 Tsareena Low Kick dealt 100% to a full-HP 207 HP Kingambit; the threat display did not list it and the engine fallback left Kingambit in.

proposals.change: LAST-USED-MOVE THREAT INCLUSION: any move a foe has actually used this battle must be included in the OHKO-band computation for every subsequent turn, even if the sheet/heuristics rank it low.
proposals.evidence: T4 Torkoal Weather Ball (used T4 after Eruption on T3) was absent from the displayed threats; Drogon at 41% attacked and was OHKO'd.

proposals.change: TRICK ROOM SPEED INVERSION IN THREAT MODEL: while Trick Room is active, every foe slower than our slot in raw Speed must be treated as moving FIRST for OHKO-band blocking purposes.
proposals.evidence: Torkoal (base 20 Spe) moved before Drogon (138) on T4 and T5 and KO'd both Drogon and chipped Milotic before they acted.

proposals.change: 4x SWITCH-IN BAN: never switch Garchomp into a field with an active revealed Ice-move user (Clawitzer, Froslass, Alolan Ninetales, Inteleon); prefer Milotic or Whimsicott.
proposals.evidence: T5 Garchomp entered and was OHKO'd by Clawitzer Ice Beam for zero value.

proposals.change: Keep Milotic as an auto-bring vs any Fire/Trick Room core: it solo-won the endgame via Scald burn + Recover vs Clawitzer and tanked Torkoal Eruption.
proposals.evidence: Milotic dealt 191% and took the last 8 turns of the game alone.

lessons: Low Kick / Grass Knot scale with OUR weight: Kingambit (100 kg) and Drogon (100 kg) take near-max BP — a Tsareena/Hariyama/Machamp Low Kick is a KO threat on Kingambit from full HP and must be in the threat display.
Any move a foe has already USED this battle must stay in the OHKO-band threat model for the rest of the game — Torkoal's Weather Ball was omitted on the turn it KO'd our Charizard.
Under Trick Room, compute the OHKO band assuming every slower foe moves FIRST; a 41% Charizard facing a sun-boosted Torkoal must Protect or switch, never attack for chip.
Never switch Garchomp in while an Ice-move user (Clawitzer, Froslass, Ninetales-A, Inteleon) is active — it is a free OHKO and a wasted body.
Milotic's Scald burn + Recover loop beats any single special attacker without recovery: in a 1v1 endgame, burn first, then alternate Recover and Scald.
